HP_0011599.label: mesocardia
HP_0011599.definition: Mesocardia is an abnormal location of the heart in which the heart is in a midline position and the longitudinal axis of the heart lies in the mid-sagittal plane.
HP_0011599.UMLS synonyms: Mesocardia | echocardiography: mesocardia | cardiac catheterization situs mesocardia

HP_0011600.label: abnormal direction of ventricular apex
HP_0011600.definition: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex. Left sided is normal.

HP_0011601.label: rightward direction of ventricular apex
HP_0011601.definition: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex towards the right. Left sided is normal.

HP_0011602.label: midline direction of ventricular apex
HP_0011602.definition: Abnormal plane of direction of the heart from the base to the apex in the midline. Left sided is normal.

HP_0011603.label: congenital malformation of the great arteries
HP_0011603.definition: Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the aorta and pulmonary arteries.
HP_0011603.UMLS synonyms: Congenitally uncorrected transposition of the great arteries with cardiac malformation

HP_0011604.label: aortopulmonary window
HP_0011604.definition: A congenital anomaly with an abnormal connection between the aorta and the main pulmonary artery resulting in an aortopulmonary shunt.

HP_0011605.label: congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries with ventricular septal defect
HP_0011605.definition: A congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries with a ventricular septal defect: a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart. The ventricular septal defect is centered around the most superior aspect of the ventricular septum.

HP_0011606.label: obsolete transposition of the great arteries with intact ventricular septum

HP_0011607.label: obsolete transposition of the great arteries with ventricular septal defect

HP_0011608.label: type ii truncus arteriosus
HP_0011608.definition: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) with each pulmonary artery arising separate from each other on the posterior or lateral aspect of the truncus.
HP_0011608.synonyms: persistent truncus arteriosus type ii | type 2 truncus arteriosus
HP_0011608.UMLS synonyms: Common arterial trunk and separate origin of pulmonary arteries

HP_0011609.label: type iii truncus arteriosus
HP_0011609.definition: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby one of the two pulmonary artery branched does not arise from the common pulmonary trunk, but instead from the ductus arteriosus or directly from the aorta.
HP_0011609.synonyms: persistent truncus arteriosus type iii | type 3 truncus arteriosus
HP_0011609.UMLS synonyms: Common arterial trunk and widely separate origin of pulmonary arteries

HP_0011610.label: type iv truncus arteriosus
HP_0011610.definition: Truncus arteriosus (single great artery leaving the base of the heart, giving rise to the coronary, pulmonary, and systemic arteries) whereby the aortic arch is hypoplastic or interrupted, and a large patent ductus arteriosus is present.
HP_0011610.synonyms: persistent truncus arteriosus type iv | type 4 truncus arteriosus

HP_0011611.label: interrupted aortic arch
HP_0011611.definition: Non-continuity of the arch of aorta with an atretic point or absent segment.
HP_0011611.synonyms: aortic arch obstruction | atretic transverse aortic arch

HP_0011612.label: interrupted aortic arch type a
HP_0011612.definition: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment at the level of the isthmus.
HP_0011612.UMLS synonyms: Interrupted aortic arch distal to left subclavian artery | Interruption of aortic arch distal to subclavian artery

HP_0011613.label: interrupted aortic arch type b
HP_0011613.definition: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the left carotid and subclavian arteries.
HP_0011613.UMLS synonyms: Interrupted aortic arch between left subclavian and left common carotid artery | Interruption of aortic arch between subclavian artery and common carotid artery

HP_0011614.label: interrupted aortic arch type c
HP_0011614.definition: Non-continuity of the aortic arch with an atretic point or absent segment between the innominate and left carotid arteries.
HP_0011614.UMLS synonyms: Interrupted aortic arch between left common carotid and brachiocephalic artery | Interruption of aortic arch between left common carotid artery and right common carotid artery

HP_0011615.label: abnormal pulmonary situs morphology
HP_0011615.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, which is defined by characteristics such as the number of lobes per lung and the relationship of the pulmonary arteries to their bronchi.

HP_0011616.label: pulmonary situs inversus
HP_0011616.definition: Mirror image arrangement of the mainstem bronchi with the right pulmonary artery posterior to the right upper lobe bronchus and the left pulmonary artery anterior to the left upper lobe bronchus.
HP_0011616.UMLS synonyms: cardiac catheterization pulmonary vein total anomalous pulmonary venous connection to left atrium, situs inversus

HP_0011617.label: pulmonary situs ambiguus
HP_0011617.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which the morphology of both left and right lungs is the same.

HP_0011618.label: pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic right lungs
HP_0011618.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a right lung.

HP_0011619.label: pulmonary situs ambiguus with bilateral morphologic left lungs
HP_0011619.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which both lungs have the morphology of a left lung.

HP_0011620.label: abnormality of abdominal situs
HP_0011620.definition: An abnormality of the abdominal situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the abdomen and its organs.

HP_0011621.label: gerbode ventricular septal defect
HP_0011621.definition: A type of ventricular septal defect communicating directly between the left ventricle and right atrium. This is anatomically possible because the normal tricuspid valve is more apically displaced than the mitral valve.

HP_0011622.label: inlet ventricular septal defect
HP_0011622.definition: A ventricular septal defect that involves the inlet of the right ventricular septum immediately inferior to the AV valve apparatus.
HP_0011622.synonyms: atrioventricular canal type ventricular septal defect | type 3 ventricular septal defect
HP_0011622.UMLS synonyms: Inlet ventricular septal defect | Perimembranous inlet ventricular septal defect | Muscular ventricular septal defect in inlet septum | Perimembranous inlet ventricular septal defect with atrioventricular septal malalignment | Muscular ventricular septal defect opening to right ventricular inlet | Perimembranous ventricular septal defect with extension to right ventricular inlet | Ventricular septal defect of inlet of right aspect of ventricular septum

HP_0011623.label: muscular ventricular septal defect
HP_0011623.definition: The trabecular septum is the largest part of the interventricular septum. It extends from the membranous septum to the apex and superiorly to the infundibular septum. A defect in the trabecular septum is called muscular VSD if the defect is completely rimmed by muscle.
HP_0011623.synonyms: type 4 ventricular septal defect | ventricular septal defect , muscular

HP_0011624.label: apical muscular ventricular septal defect
HP_0011624.definition: A muscular ventricular septal defect located at the apex of the heart.
HP_0011624.UMLS synonyms: Muscular ventricular septal defect in apical trabecular septum

HP_0011625.label: multiple muscular ventricular septal defects
HP_0011625.definition: A type of muscular ventricular septal defect characterized by the presence of multiple small defects in the ventricular septum.

HP_0011626.label: scimitar anomaly
HP_0011626.definition: Right pulmonary venous return to the inferior vena cava.
HP_0011626.UMLS synonyms: Scimitar Syndrome | Scimitar Anomaly, Multiple Cardiac Malformations, and Craniofacial and Central Nervous System Abnormalities

HP_0011627.label: aorto - ventricular tunnel
HP_0011627.definition: Aorto-ventricular tunnel is a congenital, extracardiac channel which connects the ascending aorta above the sinotubular junction to the cavity of the left, or (less commonly) right ventricle.
HP_0011627.UMLS synonyms: Closure of aorto-left ventricular tunnel | Aortico-Ventricular Tunnel | Aortico-Left Ventricular Tunnel | Aortico-Right Ventricular Tunnel

HP_0011628.label: congenital defect of the pericardium
HP_0011628.definition: A developmental defect of the pericardium with congenital onset.

HP_0011629.label: total absence of the pericardium
HP_0011629.definition: No pericardium around the heart, occurring as a congenital defect, not the result of a surgical pericardectomy.
HP_0011629.synonyms: absent pericardium | congenital absence of the pericardium

HP_0011630.label: complete diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
HP_0011630.definition: No pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.

HP_0011631.label: complete right sided absence of pericardium
HP_0011631.definition: No pericardium is present on the righthand side of the heart. It is a congenital absence of pericardium rather than the result of a pericardectomy.

HP_0011632.label: partial right sided absence of pericardium
HP_0011632.definition: A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the righthand side of the heart.

HP_0011633.label: complete left sided absence of pericardium
HP_0011633.definition: A congenital anomaly with complete lack of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.
HP_0011633.synonyms: absent lining around of left side of heart

HP_0011634.label: partial left sided absence of pericardium
HP_0011634.definition: A congenital anomaly with lack of part of the pericardium on the lefthand side of the heart.

HP_0011635.label: partial diaphragmatic absence of pericardium
HP_0011635.definition: Lack of a part of the pericardium over the diaphragmatic surface of the heart. It is a congenital defect, not the result of a pericardectomy. Pericardium is present on other parts of the heart.

HP_0011636.label: abnormal coronary artery origin
HP_0011636.definition: Isolated abnormalities of the coronary artery origins. This may be in associated with other structural heart malformations but not the patterns of complex structural heart malformations which result in abnormal course of the coronary arteries.

HP_0011637.label: anomalous origin of coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
HP_0011637.definition: A coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta.
HP_0011637.UMLS synonyms: Bland White Garland Syndrome | Anomalous origin of right coronary artery from pulmonary artery

HP_0011638.label: anomalous origin of left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
HP_0011638.definition: Left main coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the left cusp of the aortic valve.
HP_0011638.synonyms: anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery | bland - garland - white syndrome

HP_0011639.label: anomalous origin of right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery
HP_0011639.definition: Right coronary artery begins (branches off from) the pulmonary artery rather than as normal from the root of the aorta, above the right cusp of the aortic valve.
HP_0011639.UMLS synonyms: Anomalous origin of right coronary artery from pulmonary artery

HP_0011640.definition: The presence of a single coronary artery ostium from which both coronary arteries arise.

HP_0011641.label: coronary artery fistula
HP_0011641.definition: A congenital malformation with abnormal connection between one of the coronary arteries and a heart chamber or another blood vessel.

HP_0011642.label: abnormal coronary sinus morphology
HP_0011642.definition: An abnormality of the coronary sinus, which is formed by the union of the great cardiac vein and the left marginal vein and terminates in the right atrium. The coronary sinus functions to o collect deoxygenated blood from the myocardium of the heart and drain it into the right atrium.

HP_0011643.label: coronary sinus atrial septal defect
HP_0011643.definition: An atrial septal defect characterized by a deficiency in the tissue separating the coronary sinus from the left atrium (LA). This results in partial or complete unroofing of the coronary sinus leading to a predominantly left-to-right shunt through the coronary sinus (LA to coronary sinus to right atrium [RA]). The orifice of the ostium is frequently large because of the increased flow. From the RA side, the defect is located at the level of the coronary sinus ostium and may also include some deficiency in atrial tissue around the ostium. From the LA side, the size can be variable depending on the degree of unroofing of the coronary sinus.
HP_0011643.UMLS synonyms: Atrial septal defect through coronary sinus orifice | Patching of coronary sinus atrial septal defect | Closure of coronary sinus atrial septal defect | Repair of unroofed coronary sinus to create tunnel

HP_0011644.label: coronary sinus diverticulum
HP_0011644.definition: A venous pouch within the left ventricular wall, with a neck opening into the coronary sinus.

HP_0011645.label: dilatation of the sinus of valsalva
HP_0011645.definition: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation of one of the anatomic dilations of the ascending aorta, which occurs just above the aortic valve.
HP_0011645.synonyms: aneurysm of the aortic sinus | aortic sinus aneurysm | sinus of valsalva aneurysm

HP_0011646.label: juxtaductal coarctation of the aorta
HP_0011646.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized at the insertion of the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the juxtaductal region of aortic arch.

HP_0011647.label: postductal coarctation of the aorta
HP_0011647.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized distal to the ductus arteriosus, i.e., to the postductal region of aortic arch.

HP_0011648.label: patent ductus arteriosus after birth at term
HP_0011648.definition: Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus in postnatal life when birth was at 37 completed weeks of gestation or greater.

HP_0011649.label: patent ductus arteriosus after premature birth
HP_0011649.definition: Abnormal persistent patency of the ductus arteriosus when birth was at less than 37 weeks completed gestation.

HP_0011650.label: bilateral ductus arteriosus
HP_0011650.definition: The presence of both a left and a right ductus arteriosus.
HP_0011650.UMLS synonyms: Bilateral ductus arteriosus with closed left ductus arteriosus and patent right ductus arteriosus | Bilateral arterial duct | cardiac catheterization persistent bilateral ductus arteriosus | Bilateral closed arterial ducts | Bilateral patent arterial ducts | Bilateral arterial duct with patent left arterial duct and closed right arterial duct | Cardiovascular abnormality due to bilateral arterial ducts

HP_0011651.label: double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011651.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
HP_0011651.synonyms: dorv with doubly committed vsd and pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011651.UMLS synonyms: Double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis | Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis Fallot type

HP_0011652.label: double outlet right ventricle with doubly committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011652.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a subaortic ventritricular septal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that extends anterosuperiorly and are closely related to the pulmonary artery as well, are considered to be doubly committed. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
HP_0011652.synonyms: dorv with doubly committed vsd | double outlet right ventricle , doubly committed ventricular septal defect

HP_0011653.label: double outlet right ventricle with non - committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011653.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, and also has a pulmonary stenosis; abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
HP_0011653.synonyms: dorv with non - committed vsd and pulmonary stenosis

HP_0011654.label: double outlet right ventricle with non - committed ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011654.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a non-committed ventricular septal defect (VSD), which is a VSD that is anatomically related to, or close to, neither great vessel, being separated from both by considerable muscle, but there is not accompanying pulmonary stenosis; the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
HP_0011654.synonyms: dorv with non - committed vsd without pulmonary stenosis | double outlet right ventricle , noncommitted ventricular septal defect

HP_0011655.label: double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011655.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
HP_0011655.synonyms: dorv with subaortic vsd and pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011655.UMLS synonyms: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis Fallot type | Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic or doubly committed ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis Fallot type

HP_0011656.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the aortic origin. HP_0011657.label: double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect and pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011657.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
HP_0011657.synonyms: dorv with subpulmonary vsd and pulmonary stenosis

HP_0011658.label: double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary ventricular septal defect without pulmonary stenosis
HP_0011658.definition: A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect (a hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
HP_0011658.synonyms: dorv with subpulmonary vsd without pulmonary stenosis | taussig - bing anomaly

HP_0011659.label: tetralogy of fallot with absent pulmonary valve
HP_0011659.definition: Features of tetralogy of Fallot with either rudimentary ridges or the complete absence of pulmonic valve tissue.
HP_0011659.synonyms: tetralogy of fallot with absent pulmonary valve syndrome
HP_0011659.UMLS synonyms: Tetralogy of Fallot with absent pulmonary valve | Repair of tetralogy of Fallot with absent pulmonary valve

HP_0011660.label: anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from ascending aorta
HP_0011660.definition: Anomalous origin of one pulmonary artery from the ascending aorta with the contralateral pulmonary artery arising from the right ventricle.

HP_0011661.definition: The left pulmonary artery originates from the ascending aorta in the presence of a pulmonary valve and main pulmonary artery.

HP_0011664.label: left ventricular noncompaction cardiomyopathy
HP_0011664.definition: Left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC) is characterized by prominent left ventricular trabeculae and deep inter-trabecular recesses. The myocardial wall is often thickened with a thin, compacted epicardial layer and a thickened endocardial layer. In some patients, LVNC is associated with left ventricular dilatation and systolic dysfunction, which can be transient in neonates.

HP_0011665.label: takotsubo cardiomyopathy
HP_0011665.definition: Transient left ventricular apical ballooning syndrome or takotsubo cardiomyopathy is characterized by transient regional systolic dysfunction involving the left ventricular apex and/or mid-ventricle in the absence of obstructive coronary disease on coronary angiography. Patients present with an abrupt onset of angina-like chest pain, and have diffuse T-wave inversion, sometimes preceded by ST-segment elevation, and mild cardiac enzyme elevation.

HP_0011666.label: absent right superior vena cava
HP_0011666.definition: Absence of the right superior vena cava (RSVC). An absent RSVC is always associated with a persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC). During normal fetal development, the left-sided anterior venous cardinal system regresses, leaving the coronary sinus (CS) and the ligament of Marshall. Failure of the closure of the left anterior cardinal vein results in PLSVC. In general, PLSVC is associated with the right superior vena cava (RSVC) and drains into the RA via a dilated CS. When developmental arrest occurs at an earlier stage, the CS is absent and the PLSVC drains into the left atrium.
HP_0011666.UMLS synonyms: Absent right superior vena cava | cardiac catheterization absent right superior vena cava

HP_0011667.label: bilateral superior vena cava with bridging vein

HP_0011668.label: bilateral superior vena cava with no bridging vein

HP_0011669.label: left superior vena cava draining directly to the left atrium
HP_0011669.definition: A persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) that drains into the left atrium instead of the right atrium via the coronary sinus, resulting in a right to left sided shunt.

HP_0011670.label: left superior vena cava draining to coronary sinus
HP_0011670.definition: A persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) that drains into the right atrium via the coronary sinus. This is the case in 80-92% of cases of PLSVC and results in no hemodynamic consequence.

HP_0011671.label: interrupted inferior vena cava with azygous continuation
HP_0011671.definition: Interrupted inferior vena cava with azygous continuation is the result of connection failure between the right subcardinal vein and the right vitelline vein. Consequently, venous blood from the caudal part of the body reaches the heart via the azygous vein and superior vena cava.

HP_0011672.label: cardiac myxoma
HP_0011672.definition: A myxoma (tumor of primitive connective tissue) of the heart. Cardiac myxomas consist of stellate to plump, cytologically bland mesenchymal cells set in a myxoid stroma. Cardiac myxomas are of endocardial origin and general project from the endocardium into a cardiac chamber.
HP_0011672.UMLS synonyms: Myxoma of heart | Myxoma of the Endocardium | Cardiac myxoma resection | Embolism due to cardiac myxoma | CT scan of heart: cardiac myxoma | Atrial myxoma

HP_0011673.label: cardiac hemangioma
HP_0011673.definition: Abnormal proliferation of blood vessels within the cardiac cavities attached to the endocardium.
HP_0011673.UMLS synonyms: Cardiac Intramuscular Hemangioma | Cardiac Cavernous Hemangioma | Cardiac Capillary Hemangioma | Cardiac haemangioma benign | Posterior fossa brain malformation, hemangioma, arterial anomaly, cardiac defect and aortic coarctation, and eye abnormality syndrome | LYMPHATIC MALFORMATION 13

HP_0011674.label: cardiac teratoma
HP_0011674.definition: A teratoma within the heart. Most commonly, these tumors are detected in the pericardial cavity attached to the pulmonary artery and aorta. The tumor size within the heart varies from 2 to 9 cm in diameter, and intrapericardial tumors as large as 15 cm have been reported. Intracardiac tumors arise from the atrial or ventricular wall as nodular masses protruding into the cardiac chambers. Cardiac and pericardial teratomas are easily detected in the fetus and neonate by two-dimensional echocardiography as heterogeneous and encapsulated cystic masses. Histologically, cardiac teratomas contain multiple immature elements including epithelium, neuroglial tissue, thyroid, pancreas, smooth and skeletal muscle, cartilage and bone.

HP_0011675.label: arrhythmia
HP_0011675.definition: Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.

HP_0011703.definition: Heart rate of greater than 100 beats per minute.

HP_0011704.label: sick sinus syndrome
HP_0011704.definition: An abnormality involving the generation of the action potential by the sinus node and is characterized by an atrial rate inappropriate for physiological requirements. Manifestations include severe sinus bradycardia, sinus pauses or arrest, sinus node exit block, chronic atrial tachyarrhythmias, alternating periods of atrial bradyarrhythmias and tachyarrhythmias, and inappropriate responses of heart rate during exercise or stress.

HP_0011705.label: first degree atrioventricular block
HP_0011705.definition: Delay of conduction through the atrioventricular node, which is manifested as prolongation of the PR interval in the electrocardiogram (EKG). All atrial impulses reach the ventricles.

HP_0011706.label: second degree atrioventricular block
HP_0011706.definition: An intermittent atrioventricular block with failure of some atrial impulses to conduct to the ventricles, i.e., some but not all atrial impulses are conducted through the atrioventricular node and trigger ventricular contraction.

HP_0011707.label: mobitz i atrioventricular block
HP_0011707.definition: Progressive PR interval prolongation with the subsequent occurrence of a single nonconducted P wave that results in a pause. The pause that follows the nonconducted impulse is less than fully compensatory (less than the sum of two normal sinus intervals).

HP_0011708.label: mobitz ii atrioventricular block
HP_0011708.definition: A type of second degree atrioventricular (AV) block characterized by sudden failure to conduct an impulse through the AV node without a preceding change in the PR interval.

HP_0011709.label: atrioventricular dissociation
HP_0011709.definition: Atrioventricular (AV) dissociation is present if the atria and the ventricles are under the control of two separate pacemakers. AV dissociation can occur in the absence of a primary AV conduction disturbance.

HP_0011710.label: bundle branch block
HP_0011710.definition: Block of conduction of electrical impulses along the Bundle of His or along one of its bundle branches.

HP_0011711.definition: Conduction block in the anterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.

HP_0011712.label: right bundle branch block
HP_0011712.definition: A conduction block of the right branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a prolongation of the QRS complex (greater than 0.12 s) with delayed activation of the right ventricle and terminal delay on the EKG.

HP_0011713.label: left bundle branch block
HP_0011713.definition: A conduction block of the left branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a generalized disturbance of QRS morphology on EKG.

HP_0011714.label: libman - sacks lesions
HP_0011714.definition: Libman-Sacks valvular lesions are sterile fibrofibrinous vegetations that favor the left-sided heart valves and usually form on the ventricular surface of the mitral valve.

HP_0011715.label: trifascicular block
HP_0011715.definition: Abnormal conduction in all three divisions of the intraventricular conducting tissue.
HP_0011715.UMLS synonyms: Trifascicular block | Trifascicular block on electrocardiogram

HP_0011716.label: junctional ectopic tachycardia
HP_0011716.definition: Junctional ectopic tachycardia (JET) is a unique type of supraventricular arrhythmia defined by narrow QRS complex and atrioventricular (AV) dissociation or retrograde atrial conduction in a 1:1 pattern.
HP_0011716.UMLS synonyms: Tachycardia, Ectopic Junctional | Congenital junctional ectopic tachycardia | Idiopathic junctional ectopic tachycardia | Postoperative junctional ectopic tachycardia | Idiopathic chronic junctional ectopic tachycardia | Transient postoperative junctional ectopic tachycardia

HP_0011717.label: atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia
HP_0011717.definition: Accessory pathway-related atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia (AVRT) involves an abnormal electrical conduction of the accessory pathway. The accessory pathway connecting impulses between the atrium and the ventricle can be seen at any site in the AV groove.
HP_0011717.UMLS synonyms: Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia by ECG Finding | Tachycardia, Atrioventricular Nodal Reentry | Re-entrant atrioventricular tachycardia | Atrioventricular Nodal Reentry Tachycardia by ECG Finding | Arrhythmias induced by programmed electrical stimulation (atrial fibrillation, atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation)

HP_0011718.label: abnormality of the pulmonary veins
HP_0011718.definition: An abnormality of the pulmonary veins.

HP_0011719.label: supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
HP_0011719.definition: Type 1 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

HP_0011719.UMLS synonyms: Total anomalous pulmonary venous connection of supracardiac type | Correction of total anomalous pulmonary venous connection to supracardiac vessel

HP_0011721.label: infracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
HP_0011721.definition: Type 3 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

HP_0011721.UMLS synonyms: Total anomalous pulmonary venous connection of infracardiac type | Correction of total anomalous pulmonary venous connection to infracardiac vessel

HP_0011722.label: mixed total anomalous pulmonary venous connection
HP_0011722.definition: Type 4 total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

HP_0011723.label: congenital malformation of the right heart
HP_0011723.definition: Defect or defects of the morphogenesis of the right heart identifiable at birth.

HP_0011724.label: uhl 's anomaly
HP_0011724.definition: Uhl anomaly of the right ventricle refers to the almost complete absence of right ventricular myocardium, normal tricuspid valve, and preserved septal and left ventricular myocardium.

HP_0011726.label: persistent fetal circulation
HP_0011726.definition: Systemic desaturation of a liveborn baby resulting from persistent pulmonary hypertension with a patent ductus arteriosus and patent foramen ovale, such that the circulation in postnatal life follows the fetal course.
HP_0011726.UMLS synonyms: Persistent Fetal Circulation Syndrome | Other persistent fetal circulation

HP_0011727.label: peroneal muscle weakness
HP_0011727.UMLS synonyms: Peroneal muscle weakness and atrophy | Peroneal muscle weakness, transient, recurrent due to peripheral neuropathy

HP_0011728.label: elbow clonus
HP_0011728.definition: Clonus at the elbow joint, i.e., an exaggerated phasic stretch reflex characterized by repetitive, rhythmic contractions at the elbow, generated by rapid passive stretch at the elbow joint.

HP_0011729.label: abnormality of joint mobility
HP_0011729.definition: An abnormality in the range and ease of motion of joints across their normal range.

HP_0011730.label: abnormal central sensory function
HP_0011730.definition: An abnormality of sensation related to CNS function. Assuming the primary sensory modalities are intact and the patient is alert and cooperative, the presence of an abnormality of sensory function may indicate a lesion of a parietal cortex, the thalamocortical projections to the parietal cortex, or the spinal cord.

HP_0011731.label: abnormality of circulating cortisol level
HP_0011731.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of cortisol in the blood.

HP_0011732.label: abnormal adrenal morphology
HP_0011732.definition: Any structural anomaly of the adrenal glands.
HP_0011732.UMLS synonyms: Adrenocortical carcinoma | Adrenal Cortical Adenoma | Extra-Adrenal Paraganglioma | Adrenal Rest Tumor | Heavily Pigmented Adrenal Cortical Adenoma | Extra-adrenal paraganglioma, malignant | Mixed Cell Adrenal Cortical Adenoma | Clear Cell Adrenal Cortical Adenoma | Glomerulosa Cell Adrenal Cortical Adenoma | Compact Cell Adrenal Cortical Adenoma

HP_0011733.label: abnormality of adrenal physiology
HP_0011733.definition: A functional abnormality of the adrenal glands.

HP_0011734.label: central adrenal insufficiency
HP_0011734.definition: A form of adrenal insufficiency related to a lack of ACTH, which leads to a decrease in the production of cortisol by the adrenal glands. Aldosterone production is not usually affected.
HP_0011734.UMLS synonyms: Secondary Adrenal Insufficiency | IMMUNODEFICIENCY, COMMON VARIABLE, 10

HP_0011735.label: adrenocorticotropin deficient adrenal insufficiency
HP_0011735.definition: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in ACTH production.

HP_0011736.label: primary hyperaldosteronism
HP_0011736.definition: A form of hyperaldosteronism caused by a defect within the adrenal gland.
HP_0011736.UMLS synonyms: Conn Syndrome | Other primary hyperaldosteronism | Rare primary hyperaldosteronism | Primary hyperaldosteronism due to hyperplasia | Primary hyperaldosteronism, seizures, neurological abnormalities syndrome | Primary hyperaldosteronism due to adrenal adenoma | Primary hyperaldosteronism due to aldosterone-secreting malignant neoplasm of adrenal gland

HP_0011737.label: corticotropin - releasing hormone deficient adrenal insufficiency
HP_0011737.definition: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in corticotropin-releasing hormone production.
HP_0011737.synonyms: crh deficient adrenal insufficiency | tertiary adrenal insufficiency

HP_0011738.label: corticotropin - releasing hormone receptor defect
HP_0011738.definition: Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in the corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor.
HP_0011738.synonyms: corticotropin - releasing hormone receptor ( crhr ) resistance | crhr defect

HP_0011739.label: dexamethasone - suppressible primary hyperaldosteronism
HP_0011739.definition: A form of primary hyperaldosteronism in which the overproduction of aldosterone can be suppressed by the administration of dexamethasone.
HP_0011739.synonyms: familial primary hyperaldosteronism type 1 | glucocorticoid - remediable familial primary aldosteronism

HP_0011740.label: glucocortocoid - insensitive primary hyperaldosteronism
HP_0011740.definition: A form of primary hyperaldosteronism in which the overproduction of aldosterone cannot be suppressed by the administration of dexamethasone or similar glucocorticoids.

HP_0011741.label: secondary hyperaldosteronism
HP_0011741.definition: A form of hyperaldosteronism caused by abnormally increased renin levels.
HP_0011741.UMLS synonyms: Secondary hyperaldosteronism | Juxtaglomerular hyperplasia co-occurrent with secondary hyperaldosteronism

HP_0011742.label: ectopic adrenal gland
HP_0011742.definition: Abnormal anatomical location of the adrenal gland.

HP_0011743.label: adrenal gland agenesis
HP_0011743.definition: Absent development of the adrenal gland.

HP_0011744.label: secondary hypercortisolism
HP_0011744.definition: Hypercortisolemia associated with a overproduction of ACTH (often from a tumor), leading secondarily to overproduction of cortisol.

HP_0011745.label: non - secretory adrenocortical adenoma
HP_0011745.definition: An hormonally inactive adrenocortical adenoma, that is, an adenoma that does not secrete excessive amounts of adrenal hormones.

HP_0011746.label: secretory adrenocortical adenoma
HP_0011746.definition: An hormonally active adrenocortical adenoma, that is, an adenoma that secretes excessive amounts of adrenal hormones.

HP_0011747.label: abnormality of the anterior pituitary
HP_0011747.definition: An abnormality of the adenohypophysis, which is also known as the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland.

HP_0011748.label: adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency
HP_0011748.definition: A reduced ability to secrete adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), a hormone that stimulates the adrenal cortex to secrete of glucocorticoids such as cortisol.
HP_0011748.UMLS synonyms: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) deficiency (disorder) | Idiopathic adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency | Acquired Adrenocorticotropic Hormone Deficiency | Congenital isolated adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency | Late-onset isolated adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency | insulin tolerance panel for adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency | ACTH Deficiency, Isolated | Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation panel for 21-hydroxylase deficiency | Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation panel for 3 beta-hydroxydehydrogenase deficiency | Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation panel for 21- hydroxylase deficiency - Measurement of cortisol | Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation panel for 21-hydroxylase deficiency - Measurement of 17 hydroxyprogesterone | Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation panel for 3 beta-hydroxydehydrogenase deficiency - Measurement of cortisol | Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation panel for 3 beta-hydroxydehydrogenase deficiency - Measurement of 17 hydroxypregnenolone

HP_0011749.label: adrenocorticotropic hormone excess
HP_0011749.definition: Overproduction of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), which generally leads secondarily to overproduction of cortisol by the adrenal cortex.

HP_0011750.label: neoplasm of the anterior pituitary
HP_0011750.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the adenohypophysis, which is also known as the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland.
HP_0011750.synonyms: neoplasm of the adenohypophysis | neoplasm of the pars anterior
HP_0011750.UMLS synonyms: Recurrent Anterior Pituitary Gland Neoplasm | Anterior Pituitary Gland Neoplasm

HP_0011751.label: abnormal posterior pituitary morphogenesis
HP_0011751.definition: An abnormality of the neurohypophysis, which is also known as the posterior lobe of the hypophysis.
HP_0011751.synonyms: abnormality of the neurohypophysis | abnormality of the posterior pituitary

HP_0011752.label: neoplasm of the posterior pituitary
HP_0011752.definition: The presence of a neoplasm (tumor) in the neurohypophysis, which is also known as the posterior lobe of the hypophysis.

HP_0011753.label: posterior pituitary dysgenesis
HP_0011753.definition: Abnormal development of the neurohypophysis during embryonic growth and development.

HP_0011754.label: pituicytoma
HP_0011754.definition: A solid, low grade, spindle cell, glial neoplasm of adults that originates in the neurohypophysis or infundibulum. Clinical signs and symptoms include visual disturbance, headache and features of hypopituitarism. Pituicytomas are well-circumscribed, solid masses that can measure up to several centimeters. Histologically, they show a compact architecture consisting of elongate, bipolar spindle cells arranged in interlacing fascicles or assuming a storiform pattern.
HP_0011754.UMLS synonyms: Pituicytoma | Rat Pituicytoma | pituicytoma of pituitary gland | Experimental Organism Malignant Pituicytoma | Pituicytoma of posterior pituitary gland | Sellar ependymoma | Spindle Cell Oncocytoma of the Adenohypophysis | Granular Cell Tumor of the Neurohypophysis

HP_0011755.label: ectopic posterior pituitary
HP_0011755.definition: An abnormal anatomical location of the posterior lobe of the hypophysis, also known as the neurohypophysis. The posterior pituitary is normally present in the dorsal portion of the sella turcica, but when ectopic is usually near the median eminence. This defect is likely to be due to abnormal migration during embryogenesis.
HP_0011755.synonyms: ectopic neurohypophysis | ectopic posterior pituitary lobe
HP_0011755.UMLS synonyms: Ectopic posterior pituitary | Ectopic posterior pituitary gland | Ectopic or absent posterior pituitary

HP_0011756.label: posterior pituitary agenesis
HP_0011756.definition: Absence of the neurohypophysis owing to a developmental defect.

HP_0011758.label: pituitary acidophilic stem cell adenoma
HP_0011758.UMLS synonyms: Acidophil Stem Cell Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor

HP_0011759.label: pituitary gonadotropic cell adenoma
HP_0011759.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces gonadotropins.

HP_0011760.label: pituitary growth hormone cell adenoma
HP_0011760.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces growth hormone.

HP_0011761.label: pituitary null cell adenoma
HP_0011761.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that is of unknown cellular origin and that lacks immunocytochemical or fine structural markers. Null cell adenomas are not associated with hormone excess.
HP_0011761.synonyms: clinically silent pituitary adenoma | hormonally silent pituitary adenoma | non - functional pituitary adenoma | silent pituitary adenoma
HP_0011761.UMLS synonyms: Non-Functioning Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor | Null Cell Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor

HP_0011762.label: pituitary thyrotropic cell adenoma
HP_0011762.definition: A type of pituitary adenoma that produces thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH).

HP_0011763.label: pituitary carcinoma
HP_0011763.definition: A pituitary tumor with subarachnoid, brain, or systemic metastasis. The diagnosis of a pituitary carcinoma requires evidence of metastatic disease, either outside the central nervous system (CNS) or as separate noncontiguous foci within the CNS.
HP_0011763.UMLS synonyms: Pituitary carcinoma | Primary pituitary carcinoma | Hamster Pituitary Carcinoma | Pituitary Gland Basophil Carcinoma | Metastatic carcinoma to pituitary | Mouse Pituitary Carcinoma, NOS | anaplastic carcinoma of pituitary gland | chromophobe carcinoma of pituitary gland | undifferentiated carcinoma of pituitary gland | embryonal carcinoma of pituitary gland | pleomorphic carcinoma of pituitary gland | granular cell carcinoma of pituitary gland | Carcinoma in situ of pituitary gland | large cell carcinoma of pituitary gland | glassy cell carcinoma of pituitary gland | Acidophil carcinoma | large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of pituitary gland | Metastatic Unresectable Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor | large cell carcinoma of pituitary gland with rhabdoid phenotype | Locally Advanced Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor | Metastatic Thyrotroph Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor | Metastatic Lactotroph Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor | Metastatic Corticotroph Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor | Mixed acidophil-basophil carcinoma | Metastatic Somatotroph Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor

HP_0011764.label: pituitary spindle cell oncocytoma
HP_0011764.definition: A spindled-to-epithelioid, oncocytic, nonendocrine neoplasm of the anterior hypophysis that manifests in adults and follows a benign clinical course. Pituitary spindle cell oncocytomas are firm, fibrous, and adherent to surrounding structures and are highly vascular.
HP_0011764.UMLS synonyms: Spindle cell oncocytoma of posterior pituitary gland

HP_0011766.label: abnormal parathyroid morphology
HP_0011766.definition: A structural abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

HP_0011767.label: abnormality of the parathyroid physiology
HP_0011767.definition: A functional abnormality of the parathyroid gland.

HP_0011768.label: parathyroid dysgenesis
HP_0011768.definition: Abnormal embryonic development of the parathyroid gland.

HP_0011769.label: ectopic parathyroid
HP_0011769.definition: An abnormal anatomical location of the parathyroid gland.
HP_0011769.UMLS synonyms: Ectopic parathyroid adenoma | Accessory parathyroid gland | Ectopic parathyroid hormone-related protein secretion | removal of single ectopic parathyroid tumor | Aberrant parathyroid gland | radionuclide scan of parathyroid gland: ectopic uptake | computed tomography of neck: ectopic parathyroid gland | Ectopic hyperparathyroidism | Ectopic parathyroidectomy | radionuclide scan of parathyroid gland: ectopic uptake in mediastinum | Level IV surgical pathology with gross and microscopic examination

HP_0011770.label: tertiary hyperparathyroidism
HP_0011770.definition: A type of hyperparathyroidism that occurs following kidney transplantation, which is a treatment for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Although kidney transplantation leads to a normalization of serum calcium and parathyroid hormone in most patients. The state of persistent hypercalcemia and hyperparathyroidism is referred to as tertiary hyperparathyroidism.

HP_0011771.label: autoimmune hypoparathyroidism
HP_0011771.definition: A type of hypoparathyroidism with circulating antiparathyroid or anti-calcium sensing receptor antibodies indicative of autoimmunity.
HP_0011771.UMLS synonyms: Autoimmune hypoparathyroidism | Polyglandular Type I Autoimmune Syndrome

HP_0011772.label: abnormal thyroid morphology

HP_0011904.label: persistence of hemoglobin f
HP_0011904.definition: Hemoglobin F (HbF) contains two globin alpha chains and two globin gamma chains. It is the main form of hemoglobin in the fetus during the last seven months of intrauterine development and in the half year of postnatal life. In adults it normally makes up less than one percent of all hemoglobin. This term refers to an increase in HbF above this limit. In beta thalassemia major, it may represent over 90 percent of all hemoglobin, and in beta thalassemia minor it may make up between 0.5 to 4 percent.
HP_0011904.synonyms: increased haemoglobin f | increased hemoglobin f | persistence of haemoglobin f | persistence of hbf

HP_0011905.label: reduced hemoglobin a
HP_0011905.definition: Hemoglobin A (HbA) contains two globin alpha chains and two globin beta chains. HbA is normally the main adult hemoglobin, representing about 96-98 percent of all hemoglobin. This term represents a decreased in the proportion of HbA below this limit, and can be seen in various forms of thalassemia.

HP_0011906.label: reduced beta / alpha synthesis ratio
HP_0011906.definition: A reduction in the ratio of production of beta globin to that of alpha globin. This is the major abnormality in the various forms of beta thalassemia.

HP_0011920.label: transudative pleural effusion
HP_0011920.definition: A type of pleural effusion with a transudate (extravascular fluid with low protein content and a low specific gravity). Pleural effusions can be classified as transudates or exudates based on Light's criteria, which classify an effusion as exudate if one or more of the following are present: (1) the ratio of pleural fluid protein to serum protein is greater than 0.5, (2) the ratio of pleural fluid lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) to serum LDH is greater than 0.6, or (3) the pleural fluid LDH level is greater than two thirds of the upper limit of normal for serum LDH.

HP_0011921.label: exudative pleural effusion
HP_0011921.definition: A type of pleural effusion with a exudate (extravascular fluid that has exuded out of a tissue or its capillaries due to injury or inflammation). Pleural effusions can be classified as transudates or exudates based on Light's criteria, which classify an effusion as exudate if one or more of the following are present: (1) the ratio of pleural fluid protein to serum protein is greater than 0.5, (2) the ratio of pleural fluid lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) to serum LDH is greater than 0.6, or (3) the pleural fluid LDH level is greater than two thirds of the upper limit of normal for serum LDH.
HP_0011921.UMLS synonyms: Exudative pleural effusion | Pleurisy with effusion | PLEURAL EFFUSION, EXUDATE

HP_0011955.definition: The presence of multiple granulomas in the liver as based on pathological examination. Granulomas are small 0.5 to 2 mm collections of modified macrophages called epithelioid cells usually surrounded by lymphocytes.

HP_0011956.definition: A lymphoproliferative abnormality of the intestine characterized by numerous visible mucosal nodules measuring up to, and rarely exceeding, 0.5 cm in diameter Histologically, hyperplastic lymphoid follicles with large germinal centres are seen in the lamina propria and superficial submucosa. HP_0011957.label: abnormal pectoral muscle morphology
HP_0011957.definition: An abnormality of the pectoral muscle, comprising the pectoralis major, a thick, fan-shaped muscle of the anterior chest and the pectoralis minor, a thin, triangular muscle situated underneath the pectoralis major.

HP_0011962.label: obstructive azoospermia

HP_0012023.definition: Elevated concentration of galactose in the urine.

HP_0012024.label: hypergalactosemia
HP_0012024.definition: Elevated concentration of galactose in the blood.

HP_0012026.label: hyperornithinemia
HP_0012026.definition: Increased concentration of ornithine in the blood.
HP_0012026.UMLS synonyms: Hyperornithinemia | Gyrate Atrophy | hyperornithinemia gyrate atrophy of choroid | HHH syndrome | SLC25A15 gene

HP_0012029.definition: An abnormal concentration of a hormone in the urine.

HP_0012030.label: increased urinary cortisol level
HP_0012030.definition: Abnormally increased concentration of cortisol in the urine.

HP_0012032.label: lipoma
HP_0012032.definition: Benign neoplasia derived from lipoblasts or lipocytes of white or brown fat. May be angiomatous or hibernomatous.
HP_0012032.UMLS synonyms: Lipoma | Intramuscular lipoma | Pleomorphic Lipoma | Lipomatosis, Multiple | Subcutaneous lipoma | Cardiac Lipoma | Atypical Lipoma | Gastric Lipoma | Lipoma of skin | Excision of lipoma | Spindle cell lipoma | Intraosseous lipoma | Lipoma of breast | Intracortical lipoma | Chondroid lipoma | Mouse Lipoma | Intermuscular lipoma | Hepatic lipoma | Renal lipoma | Endobronchial lipoma | Intracranial lipoma | Lipoma arborescens | Parosteal lipoma

HP_0012033.label: sacral lipoma
HP_0012033.definition: Presence of a lipoma in the region of the sacrum.
HP_0012033.UMLS synonyms: Lipoma, anterior sacral | Lowry Yong syndrome

HP_0012034.label: liposarcoma
HP_0012034.definition: Malignant neoplasms which probably originate in primitive mesenchymal stem cell populations differentiating down a lipomatous pathway.

HP_0012035.label: steatocystoma multiplex
HP_0012035.definition: Multiple, localized or widespread, asymptomatic or inflammatory dermal cysts involving the pilosebaceous units. Lesions can appear anywhere on the body, but steatocystoma multiplex is more commonly involved with those areas of the skin with a high density of developed pilosebaceous units (e.g., the axilla, groin, neck, and proximal extremities).
HP_0012035.UMLS synonyms: Steatocystoma multiplex | Steatocystoma multiplex with natal teeth | Steatocystoma multiplex with natal tooth syndrome

HP_0012036.label: sternocleidomastoid amyotrophy
HP_0012036.definition: Wasting of the sternocleidomastoid muscle, the muscle in the anterior part of the neck that acts to flex and rotate the head.

HP_0012037.label: pectoralis amyotrophy
HP_0012037.definition: Wasting of the pectoral muscles, i.e., of the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor.

HP_0012038.label: corneal guttata
HP_0012038.definition: Corneal guttata are droplet-like accumulations of non-banded collagen on the posterior surface of Descemet's membrane. The presence of focal thickenings of Descemet's membrane histologically named guttae. Cornea guttata can be easily diagnosed in vivo and ex vivo by means of specular microscopy as it gives dark areas where no endothelial cells are visible.

HP_0012039.label: descemet membrane folds
HP_0012039.definition: Presence of folds in the Descemet membrane, which is the basement membrane of the endothelial (inner) cell layer of the cornea. Descemet membrane folds are generally a manifestation of inflammation or edema of the cornea.
HP_0012039.UMLS synonyms: Descemet's membrane fold | Left Descemet's membrane fold | Right Descemet's membrane fold | Bilateral Descemet's membrane fold | grade of folds of Descemet's membrane of left eye | grade of folds of Descemet's membrane of right eye | Folds in Descemet's membrane, unspecified eye

HP_0012040.label: corneal stromal edema
HP_0012040.definition: Abnormal accumulation of fluid and swelling of the stroma of cornea.

HP_0012042.label: aspirin - induced asthma
HP_0012042.definition: A type of asthma in which aspirin and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) that inhibit cyclooxygen-ase 1 (COX-1) exacerbate bronchoconstriction.
HP_0012042.UMLS synonyms: Asthma, Aspirin-Induced | ASTHMA, ASPIRIN-INDUCED, SUSCEPTIBILITY TO

HP_0012043.label: pendular nystagmus
HP_0012043.definition: Rhythmic, involuntary sinusoidal oscillations of one or both eyes. The waveform of pendular nystagmus may occur in any direction.
HP_0012043.UMLS synonyms: Pendular Nystagmus | Acquired pendular nystagmus | Disjunctive pendular nystagmus | Nystagmus, congenital horizontal pendular | Nystagmus, pendular (primarily in childhood) | Myoclonus, Oculopalatal

HP_0012044.label: seesaw nystagmus
HP_0012044.definition: Seesaw nystagmus is a type of pendular nystagmus where a half cycle consists of the elevation and intorsion of one eye, concurrently with the depression and extortion of the fellow eye. In the other half cycle, there is an inversion of the ocular movements.

HP_0012045.label: retinal flecks
HP_0012045.definition: Presence of multiple yellowish-white lesions of various size and configuration on the retina not related to vascular lesions.

HP_0012046.label: areflexia of upper limbs
HP_0012046.definition: Inability to elicit tendon reflexes in the upper limbs.
HP_0012046.UMLS synonyms: Areflexia of the upper and lower limbs

HP_0012047.label: hemeralopia
HP_0012047.definition: A visual defect characterized by the inability to see as clearly in bright light as in dim light. The word hemeralopia literally means day blindness.
HP_0012047.UMLS synonyms: Hemeralopia | Night Blindness, Congenital Stationary, Type 1A | vitamin A; deficiency, hemeralopia (manifestation) | Night blindness, congenital stationary | Heredopathia Atactica Polyneuritiformis | Goldmann-Favre syndrome (disorder)

HP_0012048.label: oromandibular dystonia
HP_0012048.definition: A kind of focal dystonia characterized by forceful contractions of the face, jaw, and/or tongue causing difficulty in opening and closing the mouth and often affecting chewing and speech.
HP_0012048.UMLS synonyms: Oromandibular dystonia | Isolated oromandibular dystonia | Meige Syndrome

HP_0012049.label: laryngeal dystonia
HP_0012049.definition: A form of focal dystonia that affects the vocal cords, associated with involuntary contractions of the vocal cords causing interruptions of speech and affecting the voice quality and often leading to patterned, repeated breaks in speech.
HP_0012049.UMLS synonyms: Laryngeal dystonia | Cranio-cervical dystonia with laryngeal and upper limb involvement

HP_0012050.label: anasarca
HP_0012050.definition: An extreme form of generalized edema with widespread and massive edema due to effusion of fluid into the extracellular space.
HP_0012050.synonyms: extreme generalised oedema | extreme generalized edema
HP_0012050.UMLS synonyms: Anasarca | Edema | Renal anasarca | anasarca; cardiac | ANASARCA TOTAL BODY | Hydrops Fetalis | anasarca; fetus or newborn | Immune Hydrops Fetalis | Hydrops Fetalis, Non-Immune | TAFRO syndrome

HP_0012051.label: reactive hypoglycemia
HP_0012051.definition: Hypoglycermia following a meal (or more generally, after intake of glucose).
HP_0012051.synonyms: low blood sugar after a meal | postprandial hypoglycemia
HP_0012051.UMLS synonyms: Reactive hypoglycemia | Postprandial reactive hypoglycemia | HYPOGLYCEMIA, REACTIVE FUNCTIONAL | Insulin reactive hypoglycemia due to type 2 diabetes mellitus

HP_0012052.label: low serum calcitriol
HP_0012052.definition: A reduced concentration of calcitriol in the blood. Calcitriol is also known as 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol or 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3.
HP_0012052.synonyms: low serum 1,25 - dihydroxycholecalciferol | low serum 1,25 - dihydroxyvitamin d3

HP_0012053.label: decreased circulating calcifediol concentration
HP_0012053.definition: A reduced concentration of calcifediol in the blood. Calcifediol is also known as calcidiol, 25-hydroxycholecalciferol and 25-Hydroxyvitamin D3.
HP_0012053.synonyms: decreased 25 - hydroxyvitamin d3 | low serum 25 - hydroxycholecalciferol | low serum calcidiol | low serum calcifediol

HP_0012054.label: choroidal melanoma
HP_0012054.definition: Malignant tumor of melanocytes of the choroid. The classic appearance of choroidal melanoma is a pigmented dome-shaped or collar button-shaped tumor with an associated exudative retinal detachment. Choroidal melanoma is usually pigmented, but can be variably pigmented and even amelanotic (non-pigmented).

HP_0012058.definition: A type of melanoma that starts as a raised area that is usually dark blackish-blue or bluish-red but may not have any color.

HP_0012059.label: lentigo maligna melanoma
HP_0012059.definition: A subtype of melanoma in situ that typically develops on sun-damaged skin. The lesion is typically a large, irregularly pigmented macule that has developed from an ordinary lentigo (a small pigmented spot on the skin with a clearly-defined edge). Change to a malignant lentigo typically takes place over 20 years or more, and many patients accept the change as a consequence of aging.

HP_0012060.label: acral lentiginous melanoma
HP_0012060.definition: A type of cutaneous melanoma localized to the palm, sole, or beneath the nail (subungual melanoma). Acral lentiginous melanoma starts as a slowly-enlarging flat patch of discoloured skin and usually displays a size above 6 mm and often several centimetres or more in diameter upon diagnosis and variable pigmentation with a mixutre of colors including brown, and blue-grey, black and red. The surface of the lesion is initially smooth but later in the course may become thicker and irregular, and may ulcerate or bleed.

HP_0012061.label: urinary excretion of sialylated oligosaccharides
HP_0012061.definition: Excretion of oligosaccharides conjugated to sialic acid in the urine.

HP_0012062.label: bone cyst
HP_0012062.definition: A fluid filled cavity that develops with a bone.

HP_0012063.label: aneurysmal bone cyst
HP_0012063.definition: Radiographic features include a dilated, radiolucent lesion typically located eccentrically within the metaphyseal portion of the bone, with fluid levels visible on magnetic resonance imaging.

HP_0012064.label: unicameral bone cyst
HP_0012064.definition: A benign fluid filled simple cyst of bone filled with serous fluid.

HP_0012065.label: multiple bony cystic lesions
HP_0012065.definition: Presence of multiple cystic changes in multiple areas or multiple bones.

HP_0012066.label: increased urinary disaccharide excretion
HP_0012066.definition: Increased concentration of disaccharide in the urine.

HP_0012067.label: glycopeptiduria
HP_0012067.definition: Increased excretion of glycopeptides in the urine. Glycopeptides are peptides with carbohydrate moieties covalently attached to the side chains of the amino acid residues.

HP_0012068.label: aspartylglucosaminuria
HP_0012068.definition: Excretion of excess amounts of aspartylglucosamine in the urine.
HP_0012068.UMLS synonyms: Aspartylglucosaminuria | ASPARTYLGLUCOSAMINURIA, FINNISH TYPE | Little to absent aspartylglucosaminuria activity

HP_0012069.label: keratan sulfate excretion in urine
HP_0012069.definition: An increased concentration of keratan sulfate in the urine.
HP_0012069.UMLS synonyms: Keratan sulfate excretion in urine that decreases with age

HP_0012070.label: chondroitin sulfate excretion in urine
HP_0012070.definition: An increased concentration of chondroitin sulfate (CHEBI:37397) in the urine.
HP_0012070.UMLS synonyms: Chondroitin 6-sulfate excretion in urine | Chondroitin 4-, 6-sulfate excretion in urine

HP_0012071.label: abnormal circulating acylcarnitine concentration
HP_0012071.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of an acylcarnitine, which is produced by reversible esterification of the 3-hydroxyl group of carnitine.
HP_0012071.synonyms: abnormal acetylcarnitine profile | abnormal circulating esterified carnitine concentration

HP_0012072.label: aciduria
HP_0012072.definition: Excretion of urine with an acid pH, i.e., having an increased hydrogen ion concentration.
HP_0012072.UMLS synonyms: Aciduria | Argininosuccinic Aciduria | Orotic aciduria | Malonic aciduria | Mevalonic Aciduria | Glutaric aciduria | Methylmalonic aciduria | Hydroxymethylglutaric aciduria | Fumaric aciduria | Propionic Aciduria | Methylcrotonic aciduria | arginosuccinic aciduria | 3-Methylglutaconic aciduria type 2 | Lactic aciduria | Methylsuccinic aciduria | Hyperglycolic aciduria | Glutamic aciduria | Methylglutaconic aciduria | Glycoamino aciduria | 3-Methylglutaconic Aciduria

HP_0012073.label: abnormal urinary acylglycine profile
HP_0012073.definition: An abnormal distribution of N-acylglycines in the urine. There are numerous different N-acylglycines, and this term refers to pathological alterations in their level or distribution.

HP_0012074.label: tonic pupil
HP_0012074.definition: An abnormality of the pupillary light reaction characterized by a marked slowing of the light reaction of usually just one pupil. The pupil tends to be relatively dilated, and there is reduced accommodation.
HP_0012074.UMLS synonyms: Tonic Pupil | Adie Syndrome | Tonic Pupil, Neuropathic | Tonic Pupil, Local | Tonic pupil, bilateral | Tonic pupil, left eye | Tonic pupil, unspecified eye | Tonic pupil, right eye | Adie's tonic pupil of left eye | Adie's tonic pupil of right eye | Adie's tonic pupil of both eyes | Tonic, sluggishly reacting pupil and hypoactive or absent tendon reflexes | Tonic pupillary reaction of left eye | Tonic pupillary reaction of right eye | Tonically dilated pupils | Bilateral tonic pupillary reaction

HP_0012075.label: personality disorder
HP_0012075.definition: A personality disorder is a deeply ingrained pattern of behavior of a specified kind that deviates markedly from the norms of generally accepted behavior. It is typically apparent by the time of adolescence and causes long-term difficulties in personal relationships or functioning in society.

HP_0012076.label: borderline personality disorder
HP_0012076.definition: A personality disorder characterized by impulsive behavior and unpredictable, capricious mood. Affected individuals show a tendency to have outbursts of emotion and an inability to control these behavioral explosions. They generally experience an intense fear of abandonment or instability and also struggle with feelings of emptiness.

HP_0012077.label: histrionic personality disorder
HP_0012077.definition: A personality disorder characterized by shallow and labile affectivity, self-dramatization, theatricality, exaggerated expression of emotions, suggestibility, egocentricity, self-indulgence, lack of consideration for others, easily hurt feelings, and continuous seeking for appreciation, excitement and attention.
HP_0012077.UMLS synonyms: Histrionic Personality Disorder | Other histrionic personality disorder

HP_0012078.label: motor conduction block
HP_0012078.definition: Blockade of impulses at a focal site along the course of a motor axon.

HP_0012079.label: abnormality of central motor conduction
HP_0012079.definition: Any anomaly of the conduction of motor nerve impulses in the central nervous system.

HP_0012080.label: cerebellar granular layer atrophy
HP_0012080.definition: Atrophy of the cerebellum affecting primarily the granular cell layer.

HP_0012081.label: enlarged cerebellum
HP_0012081.definition: An abnormally increased size of the cerebellum compared to other brain structures.

HP_0012082.label: cerebellar purkinje layer atrophy
HP_0012082.definition: Atrophy of the cerebellum affecting primarily the Purkinje cell layer.

HP_0012083.label: ubiquitin - positive cerebral inclusion bodies
HP_0012083.definition: Nuclear or cytoplasmic aggregates that show positive staining with antibodies against ubiquitin within cells of the brain.

HP_0012084.label: abnormality of skeletal muscle fiber size
HP_0012084.definition: Any abnormality of the size of the skeletal muscle cell.
HP_0012084.synonyms: abnormality of skeletal muscle fibre size

HP_0012628.synonyms: abnormality of the suspensory ligament of lens | abnormality of zinn 's membrane | ciliary zonule abnormality | zonule of zinn abnormality

HP_0012629.label: phakodonesis
HP_0012629.definition: Tremulousness (trembling) of the lens of the eye.

HP_0012630.label: abnormal trabecular meshwork morphology
HP_0012630.definition: An anomaly of the trabecular meshwork, which is the porelike structure surrounding the entire circumference of the anterior chamber at the base of the cornea and near the ciliary body. The trabecular mesh work is responsible for draining the aqueous humor into the canal of Schlemm.

HP_0012631.label: pigment deposition in the trabecular meshwork
HP_0012631.definition: Accumulation of abnormal amounts of pigment within the trabecular meshwork.

HP_0012632.label: abnormal intraocular pressure
HP_0012632.definition: An anomaly in the amount of force per unit area exerted by the intraocular fluid within the eye.
HP_0012632.synonyms: abnormal eye pressure | abnormal intraocular pressure
HP_0012632.UMLS synonyms: Abnormal intraocular pressure | Intraocular pressure test abnormal

HP_0012633.label: asymmetry of intraocular pressure
HP_0012633.definition: A difference in the amount of intraocular pressure in the right and left eye.

HP_0012634.label: iris pigment dispersion
HP_0012634.definition: Shedding of the pigment granules that normally adhere to the back of the iris into the aqueous humor.
HP_0012634.UMLS synonyms: Iris transillumination with pigment dispersion | Pigmentary iris degeneration, NOS

HP_0012635.label: iris hypoperfusion
HP_0012635.definition: Reduction in the amount of blood flow to the iris.
HP_0012635.UMLS synonyms: Iris hypoperfusion resulting from degenerated stromal vessels

HP_0012640.definition: A deviation from the norm of the intracranial pressure.

HP_0012641.label: decreased intracranial pressure
HP_0012641.definition: A reduction of the pressure inside the cranium (skull) and thereby in the brain tissue and cerebrospinal fluid.

HP_0012642.label: cerebellar agenesis
HP_0012642.definition: Cerebellar agenesis is defined by the near complete absence of cerebellar tissue with only remnants of the anterior vermis, flocculus, and/or middle cerebellar peduncles.

HP_0012643.label: foveal hypopigmentation
HP_0012643.definition: Decreased amount of pigmentation in the fovea centralis.

HP_0012644.label: increased caudate lactate level
HP_0012644.definition: An elevated concentration of lactate in the caudate nucleus. This finding can be elicited by magnetic resonance spectroscopy imaging.

HP_0012645.label: enlarged peripheral nerve
HP_0012645.definition: Increase in size of a peripheral nerve. This finding can be appreciated by palpation along the axis of the nerve.

HP_0012646.label: retractile testis
HP_0012646.definition: A testis that is located at the upper scrotum or lower inguinal canal and that can be made to descend completely into the scrotum without resistance by manual reduction but returns to its original position by the cremasteric reflex.
HP_0012646.UMLS synonyms: Retractile testis | Pain due to retractile testis | Encounter Due to Retractile Testis | Retractile testes (46XX)

HP_0012647.label: abnormal inflammatory response
HP_0012647.definition: Any anomaly of the inflammatory response, a response to injury or infection characterized by local vasodilation, extravasation of plasma into intercellular spaces and accumulation of white blood cells and macrophages.

HP_0012648.label: decreased inflammatory response
HP_0012648.definition: An abnormal reduction in the inflammatory response to injury or infection.

HP_0012649.label: increased inflammatory response
HP_0012649.definition: A abnormal increase in the inflammatory response to injury or infection.
HP_0012649.UMLS synonyms: Monitor for early signs of systemic inflammatory response syndrome (e.g., increased temperature, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypocarbia, leukocytosis, or leucopenia)

HP_0012650.label: perisylvian polymicrogyria
HP_0012650.definition: Polymicrogyria (an excessive number of small gyri or convolutions) that is maximal in perisylvian regions (the regions that surround the Sylvian fissures), which may be symmetric or asymmetric and may extend beyond perisylvian regions. HP_0012654.label: abnormal csf dopamine concentration
HP_0012654.definition: Abnormal concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP_0012655.label: elevated csf dopamine concentration
HP_0012655.definition: Increased concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP_0012656.label: reduced csf dopamine concentration
HP_0012656.definition: Decreased concentration of dopamine in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP_0012657.label: abnormal brain positron emission tomography
HP_0012657.definition: A functional brain anomaly detectable by positron emission tomography (PET). PET scanning is a method for functional brain imaging, and its measurements reflect the amount of brain activity in the various regions of the brain.

HP_0012658.label: abnormal brain fdg positron emission tomography
HP_0012658.definition: An anomaly detectable in [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) brain scans. Glucose uptake measured with FDG-PET is a marker of neuronal metabolic activity.

HP_0012659.label: prefrontal hypometabolism in fdg pet
HP_0012659.definition: Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the prefrontal cortex as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.

HP_0012660.label: thalamic hypometabolism in fdg pet
HP_0012660.definition: Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the thalamus as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.

HP_0012661.label: hypothalamic hypometabolism in fdg pet
HP_0012661.definition: Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the hypothalamus as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.

HP_0012662.label: parietal hypometabolism in fdg pet
HP_0012662.definition: Reduced uptake of [18F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) in the parietal cortex as measured by positron emission tomography (PET) brain scan.

HP_0012663.label: mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
HP_0012663.definition: A small reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle. The normal range in adults is at least 50 percent, and a mild reduction is defined as 40-49 percent.

HP_0012664.label: reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
HP_0012664.definition: A diminution of the volumetric fraction of blood pumped out of the ventricle with each cardiac cycle.
HP_0012664.UMLS synonyms: Markedly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction | Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, severe | Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (in young adulthood)

HP_0012665.label: moderately reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
HP_0012665.definition: A medium reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle, defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30-39 percent.

HP_0012666.label: severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
HP_0012666.definition: A large reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle. The normal range in adults is at over 50 percent, and a severe reduction is defined as less than 30 percent.
HP_0012666.UMLS synonyms: Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, severe

HP_0012667.label: regional left ventricular wall motion abnormality
HP_0012667.definition: An abnormal motion of a segment of the left ventricle during the cardiac cycle.

HP_0012668.label: vasovagal syncope
HP_0012668.synonyms: neurocardiogenic syncope | reflex syncope | situational syncope
HP_0012668.UMLS synonyms: Vasovagal syncope | Vasovagal syncope due to immersion | Familial neurocardiogenic syncope

HP_0012669.label: carotid sinus syncope
HP_0012669.definition: An exaggerated response to carotid sinus baroreceptor stimulation resulting in syncope from transient diminished cerebral perfusion.

HP_0012670.label: orthostatic syncope
HP_0012670.definition: Syncope following a quick change in position from lying down to standing.
HP_0012670.UMLS synonyms: Syncope due to orthostatic hypotension | Syncope due to autonomic failure

HP_0012671.label: abulia

HP_0012672.label: akinetic mutism
HP_0012672.definition: Akinetic mutism is essentially characterized by a total absence of spontaneous behavior and speech occurring in the presence of preserved visual tracking.

HP_0012673.label: aplasia of the upper vagina
HP_0012673.definition: A failure to develop of the upper vagina.

HP_0012674.label: aplasia of the lower vagina
HP_0012674.definition: A failure to develop of the lower part of the vagina.
HP_0012674.synonyms: absent lower vagina | agenesis of the lower vagina

HP_0012680.label: abnormality of the pineal gland

HP_0012683.label: pineal cyst

HP_0012684.label: abnormal pineal volume
HP_0012684.definition: An abnormal increase or decrease in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.

HP_0012685.label: decreased pineal volume
HP_0012685.definition: An abnormal reduction in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.

HP_0012686.label: increased pineal volume
HP_0012686.definition: An abnormal elevation in the quantity of three-dimensional space taken up by the pineal gland.

HP_0012687.label: agenesis of pineal gland
HP_0012687.definition: Failure to develop of the pineal gland, defined clinically as the absence of the pineal gland with no indication of the pineal gland even having been present.

HP_0012688.label: abnormality of pineal physiology
HP_0012688.definition: A functional abnormality of the pineal gland.

HP_0012689.label: abnormal pineal melatonin secretion
HP_0012689.definition: An anomaly in the amount or timing of melatonin secretion by the pineal gland. Note that melatonin is also synthesized by multiple tissues outside of the pineal gland.

HP_0012690.label: t2 hypointense thalamus

HP_0012694.label: enlarged thalamic volume

HP_0012695.label: decreased thalamic volume

HP_0012696.label: abnormal thalamic mri signal intensity

HP_0012697.label: small basal ganglia

HP_0020082.label: heinz bodies
HP_0020082.definition: A type of erythrocyte inclusion composed of denatured hemoglobin.

HP_0020083.label: furuncle
HP_0020083.definition: An infection of a hair follicle that extends subcutaneously, forming an abscess.

HP_0020084.label: carbuncle
HP_0020084.definition: A pustular lesion of the skin emerging from group of infected hair follicles, characterized by a deep location and dissecting through tissue planes. A carbuncle is larger and deeper than a furuncle.
