HP_0020171.definition: Low plasma concentration of a drug as compared to previously measured thresholds given the expected concentration for the applied dosage regime.
HP_0020171.synonyms: decreased plasma drug concentration | decreased serum drug concentration | reduced blood drug concentration | reduced plasma drug concentration | reduced serum drug concentrations
HP_0020171.UMLS synonyms: Decreased Peak Drug Blood Concentration | Decreased Concomitant Drug Peak Blood Concentration | Decreased Time To Peak Drug Blood Concentration | Decreased Time To Concomitant Drug Peak Blood Concentration

HP_0020172.label: adverse drug response
HP_0020172.definition: An unpleasant or harmful reaction resulting from treatment with a drug.
HP_0020172.synonyms: adverse drug reaction | drug - induced reaction | drug - induced response | toxic drug response
HP_0020172.UMLS synonyms: Adverse reaction to drug | Test for adverse drug reactions and drug response | Gene analysis of targeted sequences for adverse drug reactions and drug response | Drug metabolism (adverse drug reactions and drug response), genomic analysis panel, variant analysis of 25 genes with reported phenotypes | Drug metabolism (adverse drug reactions and drug response), targeted sequence analysis (ie, CYP1A2, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP3A4, CYP3A5, CYP4F2, SLCO1B1, VKORC1 and rs12777823) | Drug metabolism (adverse drug reactions and drug response), targeted sequence analysis, 20 gene variants and CYP2D6 deletion or duplication analysis with reported genotype and phenotype | genomic sequence analysis panel of 20 gene variants and CYP2D6 duplication or deletion analysis for adverse drug reactions and drug response | Drug metabolism (adverse drug reactions and drug response), buccal specimen, gene-drug interactions, variant analysis of 33 genes, including deletion/duplication analysis of cyp2d6, including reported phenotypes and impacted gene-drug interactions | Administer adjunct drugs and fluids necessary to manage the anesthetic, maintain physiological homeostasis, and correct adverse or unfavorable responses to anesthesia and surgery

HP_0020173.label: reduced drug efficacy
HP_0020173.definition: Decreased response to a drug intervention in comparison to the expected response.

HP_0020174.label: refractory drug response
HP_0020174.definition: Absent or significantly reduced efficacy of drug intervention characterized by lack of measurable benefit or deterioration of disease course.

HP_0020175.label: reduced cholinesterase level
HP_0020175.definition: A decreased amount of cholinesterase in the blood circulation.

HP_0020176.label: cholesterol crystalluria
HP_0020176.definition: The presence of cholesterol crystals in the urine.

HP_0020177.label: abnormal proportion of cd8 - positive , alpha - beta temra t cells
HP_0020177.definition: An abnormal proportion of CD8-positive, alpha-beta effector memory RA TEMRA T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These cells have the phenotype CD45RA-positive, CD45RO-negative, and CCR7-negative.
HP_0020177.synonyms: abnormal proportion of effector memory cd8 - positive , alpha - beta t cells , terminally differentiated

HP_0020178.label: abnormal dendritic cell count
HP_0020178.definition: A deviation from the normal count of dendritic cells in the peripheral blood circulation. Dendritic cells are of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation. These cells are lineage negative (CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD34-negative, and CD56-negative).

HP_0020179.label: abnormal circulating haptoglobin concentration
HP_0020179.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation.

HP_0020180.label: elevated haptoglobin level
HP_0020180.definition: An abnormally high concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation. Haptoglobin is an acute-phase reactant whose levels can become elevated in the presence of infection and inflammation.

HP_0020181.label: reduced haptoglobin level
HP_0020181.definition: An abnormally low concentration of haptoglobin in the blood circulation. Decreased haptoglobin in conjunction with increased reticulocyte count and anemia may indicate hemolysis. Decreased haptoglobin levels can also occur in the absence of hemolysis, due to cirrhosis of the liver, disseminated ovarian carcinomatosis, pulmonary sarcoidosis, and elevated estrogen state.

HP_0020182.label: abnormal circulating a - type atrial natriuretic peptide concentration
HP_0020182.definition: A measurable change in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.
HP_0020182.synonyms: abnormal a - type atrial natriuretic peptide level

HP_0020183.label: increased circulating a - type natriuretic peptide concentration
HP_0020183.definition: A measurable elevation in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.
HP_0020183.synonyms: increased circulating a - type natriuretic peptide level

HP_0020184.label: decreased circulating a - type natriuretic peptide concentration
HP_0020184.definition: A measurable reduction in circulating levels of Atrial natriuretic peptide hormone, a protein which plays an important role in the regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.
HP_0020184.synonyms: decreased circulating a - type natriuretic peptide level

HP_0020185.label: superior cerebellar dysplasia
HP_0020185.definition: Abnormal morphological development of the superior part of the cerebellum.

HP_0020186.label: multilobulated spleen
HP_0020186.definition: The fetal spleen is lobulated, and these lobules normally disappear before the birth. Lobulation of the spleen may persist into adult life and be typically seen along the medial part of the spleen. A persisting lobule results in a variation in shape of the spleen.

HP_0020187.label: thick pachygyria
HP_0020187.definition: Pachygyria with a very thick cerebral cortex measuring 10-20 mm. Note that cortical thickness cannot be measured reliably on scans done between 3 and 24 months of age.
HP_0020187.synonyms: pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm | pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm

HP_0020188.label: anterior predominant pachygyria with 5 - 10 mm cortical thickness
HP_0020188.definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness between 5 and 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically over 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.

HP_0020189.label: posterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
HP_0020189.definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.
HP_0020189.synonyms: occipital predomimant classic pachygyria | pachygyria with cortical thickness over 10 mm posterior predominant

HP_0020190.label: perisylvian predominant thick cortex pachygyria
HP_0020190.definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm and a perisylvian predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Perisylvian predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.
HP_0020190.synonyms: pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm perisylvian predominant

HP_0020191.label: anterior predominant thick cortex pachygyria
HP_0020191.definition: Pachygyria with cortical thickness greater than 10 mm and an anterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Anterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe over the frontal and temporal lobes.
HP_0020191.synonyms: pachygyria with cortical thickness > 10 mm anterior predominant

HP_0020192.label: pachygyria with 5 - 10 mm cortical thickness
HP_0020192.definition: Pachygyria with a mildly thickened cerebral cortex measuring 5-10 mm. Note that cortical thickness cannot be measured reliably on scans done between 3 and 24 months of age.

HP_0020193.label: prolonged reptilase time
HP_0020193.definition: An abnormally increased duration of the reptilase time. Reptilase time is a functional plasma clotting assay, which is based on the enzymatic activity of batroxobin. By specifically cleaving fibrinogen A from fibrinogen, batroxobin leads to the formation of a stable fibrin clot. The time, starting from the addition of batroxobin to the plasma sample, until clot formation is the reptilase time and is given in seconds.

HP_0020194.label: iga heavy chain paraproteinemia
HP_0020194.definition: An abnormal IgA heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

HP_0020195.label: igg heavy chain paraproteinemia
HP_0020195.definition: An abnormal IgG heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

HP_0020196.label: igm heavy chain paraproteinemia
HP_0020196.definition: An abnormal IgM heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

HP_0020197.label: increased circulating arachidonic acid concentration
HP_0020197.definition: An increased circulation of arachidonic acid in the blood circulation.
HP_0020197.synonyms: increased circulating arachidonate level | increased circulating arachidonic acid level

HP_0020198.label: abnormal circulating 18 - hydroxycorticosterone level
HP_0020198.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

HP_0020199.label: decreased circulating 18 - hydroxycortisone level
HP_0020199.definition: A subnormal concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

HP_0020200.label: increased circulating 18 - hydroxycortisone level
HP_0020200.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of 18-Hydroxycorticosterone level in the blood circulation.

HP_0020201.label: abnormal sarcomere morphology
HP_0020201.definition: Any structural anomaly of the sarcomere, which is unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

HP_0020202.label: abnormal z disc morphology
HP_0020202.definition: Any structural anomaly of the Z disc, which is the platelike region of a muscle sarcomere to which the plus ends of actin filaments are attached.

HP_0020203.label: z - band streaming
HP_0020203.definition: Streaming or smearing of the Z band, which is then no longer confined to a narrow zone which bisects the I band. The Z disc may extend across the I band or the entire sarcomere in a zigzag manner. Focal thickening, smudging, and blurring of the Z band takes place concurrently. Myofibrillar disorganization is a frequent but not invariable accompanying change.

HP_0020204.label: tubulointerstitial bacterial infiltration
HP_0020204.definition: Tubulointerstitial infiltration of bacteria identified on routine and/or special (Brown-Hopps) stains.

HP_0020205.label: tubulointerstitial fungal infiltration
HP_0020205.definition: Tubulointerstitial infiltration of yeast or hyphal-microrganisms identified on routine and/or special (PAS, silver) stains.

HP_0020206.label: simple ear
HP_0020206.definition: The pinna has fewer folds and grooves than usual.
HP_0020206.UMLS synonyms: Simple ear | simple repair of external ear | Excision external ear; partial, simple repair | Simple laceration of auricle of ear | Simple drainage of hematoma of external ear | Simple drainage of abscess of external ear | simple repair of left external ear | simple repair of right external ear | Drainage external ear, abscess or hematoma; simple | Contaminated simple laceration of auricle of ear | Partial removal of external ear with simple repair | Simple and small local skin flap of ear | Simple drainage of abscess or blood accumulation of external ear | Simple repair of superficial wound of ear, 2.6-5.0 cm | Simple repair of superficial wound of ear, 20.1-30.0 cm | Simple repair of superficial wound of ear, 7.6-12.5 cm | Simple repair of superficial wound of ear, 5.1-7.5 cm | Simple repair of superficial wound of ear, 12.6-20.0 cm | Simple repair of superficial wound of ear, more than 30.0 cm | Simple repair of superficial wound of ear, 2.5 cm or less | Simple laceration of left pinna | Simple laceration of right pinna | Large simple ears | Small, simple ears | Protruding, simple ears

HP_0020207.label: reflex seizure
HP_0020207.UMLS synonyms: Reflex seizure | Reflex anoxic seizure (finding) | Anoxic seizure (finding) | EPILEPSY, X-LINKED 1, WITH VARIABLE LEARNING DISABILITIES AND BEHAVIOR DISORDERS | Monitor for neurological and/or neuromuscular manifestations of metabolic alkalosis (e.g., seizures, confusion, stupor, coma, tetany, hyperactive reflexes) | Monitor for neuromuscular manifestations of hypomagnesemia (e.g., weakness, muscle twitching, foot or leg cramps, paresthesias, hyperactive deep tendon reflexes, Chvostek's sign, Trousseau's sign, dysphagia, nystagmus, seizures, and tetany) | Observe for clinical manifestations of hypocalcemia (e.g., tetany [classic sign]; tingling in tips of fingers, feet, or mouth; spasms of muscles in face or extremities; Trousseau's sign; Chvostek's sign; altered deep tendon reflexes; seizures [late sign]) | Ictal auditory features commonly include simple unformed sounds (buzzing, ringing, clicking, humming), but may also include complex auditory features (voices, music), distorted auditory features (volume changes, muffling), cognitive auditory features (receptive aphasia), reflex auditory features (seizures precipitated by sounds)

HP_0020208.label: eating - induced seizure
HP_0020208.definition: A seizure precipitated by aspects of anticipating food, eating itself, or the post-prandial period.

HP_0020209.label: hot water - induced seizure
HP_0020209.definition: A seizure precipitated by pouring cupfuls of very hot water (40 to 50 degrees Celsius) in rapid succession over the head. Bathing in this manner is the most common trigger.

HP_0020210.label: praxis - induced seizure
HP_0020210.definition: A seizure precipitated by complex, cognition-guided tasks often involving visuomotor coordination and decision-making.

HP_0020211.label: proprioceptive - induced seizure
HP_0020211.definition: A seizure precipitated by movement or a change in posture.

HP_0020213.label: somatosensory - induced seizure
HP_0020213.definition: A somatosensory reflex seizure is a seizure precipitated by somatic stimulation of a specific part of the body in the absence of startle or surprise.

HP_0020214.label: startle - induced seizure
HP_0020214.definition: Startle-induced seizures are triggered by multiple and non-specific stimuli (auditory, somatosensory, and rarely visual) and are characterized by their sudden unexpected nature. Sudden noise rather than pure sound is the most effective acoustic stimulus.

HP_0020215.label: thinking - induced seizure
HP_0020215.definition: Seizures induced by thinking and decision-making. comment:

HP_0020216.label: visually - induced seizure
HP_0020216.definition: Seizures evoked by visual stimuli. This includes clinical seizures induced by strobe lighting, television and other screens, flickering environmental lighting and self-induction by causing a strobe effect.

HP_0020217.label: focal aware motor seizure
HP_0020217.definition: A type of focal motor seizure in which awareness is retained throughout the seizure.
HP_0020217.UMLS synonyms: Focal onset aware motor onset epileptic seizure | Jacksonian Seizure | Focal onset aware nonmotor onset epileptic seizure | Focal onset impaired awareness motor onset epileptic seizure | Focal onset impaired awareness nonmotor onset epileptic seizure

HP_0020218.label: focal aware atonic seizure
HP_0020218.definition: A type of focal atonic seizure during which awareness is fully retained throughout.
HP_0020218.UMLS synonyms: Focal onset aware atonic epileptic seizure | Focal onset impaired awareness atonic epileptic seizure

HP_0020219.label: motor seizure
HP_0020219.definition: A motor seizure is a type of seizure that is characterized at onset by involvement of the skeletal musculature. The motor event could consist of an increase (positive) or decrease (negative) in muscle contraction to produce a movement.
HP_0020219.UMLS synonyms: Motor epileptic seizure | Convulsive Seizures | Non-motor epileptic seizure | Generalized onset motor epileptic seizure | motor partial seizure with intractable seizure | Neonatal focal motor electro-clinical epileptic seizure | Frontal lobe supplementary motor cortex epileptic seizure | Frontal lobe primary motor cortex epileptic seizure | Seizure, versive, partial, motor | Seizure, somatic, partial, motor | Seizure, postural, partial, motor | Seizure, dysphasic, partial, motor | Focal onset aware motor onset epileptic seizure | Neonatal focal non-motor electro-clinical epileptic seizure | motor partial seizure, non-intractable | Seizure, somatic, inhibitory, partial, motor | Epilepsy, Partial, Motor | Focal onset impaired awareness motor onset epileptic seizure | Absence Epilepsy

HP_0020220.label: focal atonic seizure
HP_0020220.definition: A focal seizure characterized at onset by sudden loss or diminution of muscle tone without apparent preceding myoclonic or tonic activity, typically lasting more than 500 ms but less than 2 seconds. It may involve the head, trunk, jaw or limb musculature.
HP_0020220.synonyms: localised atonic seizure | localised hypotonic seizure | localized atonic seizure | localized hypotonic seizure | partial atonic seizure | partial hypotonic seizure | segmental atonic seizure | segmental hypotonic seizure
HP_0020220.UMLS synonyms: Focal onset atonic epileptic seizure | Focal onset aware atonic epileptic seizure | Focal onset impaired awareness atonic epileptic seizure

HP_0020221.label: clonic seizure
HP_0020221.definition: A clonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by sustained rhythmic jerking, that is regularly repetitive.
HP_0020221.UMLS synonyms: Clonic Seizures | Clonic seizure, refractory | Generalized onset clonic epileptic seizure | Neonatal focal clonic epileptic seizure | Tonic-clonic seizure, refractory | Clonic seizure, grand mal | Tonic-Clonic Seizures | Generalized onset tonic-clonic epileptic seizure | Focal onset aware clonic epileptic seizure | Focal Clonic Seizures | Tonic-clonic seizure, non-refractory | SEIZURE DISORDER GENERALIZED TONIC CLONIC | Focal to bilateral tonic-clonic epileptic seizure | Focal onset impaired awareness clonic epileptic seizure | Generalized onset myoclonic-tonic-clonic epileptic seizure | Absence seizure with mild clonic components

HP_0020222.label: hypohomocysteinemia
HP_0020222.definition: A decreased concentration of homocysteine in the blood.
HP_0020222.UMLS synonyms: IMMUNODEFICIENCY, DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY, AND HYPOHOMOCYSTEINEMIA | Developmental delay, immunodeficiency, leukoencephalopathy, hypohomocysteinemia syndrome

HP_0020223.label: dermal sinus tract
HP_0020223.definition: A dermal sinus tract is an abnormality present at birth over the dorsal midline where an abnormal epithelialized connection from the skin tracks inwards towards the spine, most commonly seen in the lumbosacral region.
HP_0020223.UMLS synonyms: Occipital dermal sinus tract | Congenital spinal dermal sinus

HP_0020224.label: mammary duct ectasia
HP_0020224.definition: A non-proliferative inflammatory disorder of the large duct (milk duct) of the breast; as such, it affects nipple and areola complex. The condition is characterized by focal dilatation of the lactiferous duct system is due to endoluminal changes, as well as the loss of duct wall elastin, leading to abnormally dilated and tortuous lactiferous ducts with associated periductal inflammation and fibrosis. Mammary duct ectasia may present with nipple discharge or palpable mass.
HP_0020224.UMLS synonyms: Mammary duct ectasia | Focal Mammary Duct Ectasia | Mammary duct ectasia of left breast | Mammary duct ectasia of right breast | Mammary duct ectasia of unspecified breast | Duct Ectasia of the Mouse Mammary Gland

HP_0020225.label: breast abscess
HP_0020225.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the breast.
HP_0020225.UMLS synonyms: Abscess of breast | Nonpuerperal abscess of breast | Neonatal breast abscess | Subareolar breast abscess | puerperal breast abscess | Retromammary breast abscess | Intramammary breast abscess | Obstetric breast abscess | Postpartum abscess of breast | Drainage of breast abscess | Abscess of breast, antepartum | abscess; tuberculous, breast | tuberculosis; abscess, breast | Acute abscess of breast | Chronic abscess of breast | BREAST ABSCESS REMOVAL | BREAST ABSCESS MULTIPLE | BREAST ABSCESS RECURRENT | ultrasound of breast: abscess | ultrasound of breast: abscess of left breast | ultrasound of breast: abscess of right breast | Breast abscess during lactation | Recurrent subareolar breast abscess | abscess; breast, puerperal, postpartum | BREAST FOLD SKIN ABSCESS

HP_0020226.label: nipple tenderness
HP_0020226.definition: Pain or discomfort produced by touching the nipple.
HP_0020226.UMLS synonyms: Nipple tenderness | Monitors for nipple tenderness | Nipple non-tender | Uses techniques to prevent nipple tenderness | Determine if pain, lump, thickening, or tenderness; discharge, distortion, retraction, or scaling of nipple is present

HP_0020227.label: floating gallbladder
HP_0020227.definition: An abnormal configuration in which the gallbladder is pedunculated, hanging free of the liver, and attached only by the cystic mesentery,

HP_0020228.label: biospecimen phenotypic feature
HP_0020228.definition: A phenotypic abnormality obvserved in a biospecimen such as a biopsy or an extirpated tumor or tissue.

HP_0020229.label: abnormal lymph - node biospecimen
HP_0020229.definition: Any abnormal phenotypic feature observed in a biospecimen derived from a lymph node, generally obtained by lymph node biopsy (removal of lymph node tissue for microscopic examination).

HP_0020230.label: abnormal lymph - node tissue architecture
HP_0020230.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the architecture of the tissue of a lymph node.

HP_0020231.label: abnormal lymph - node cellular finding
HP_0020231.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality within cells located in a lymph node.

HP_0020233.label: abnormal lymph - node cellular antigen expression
HP_0020233.definition: Abnormal expression of an antigen (marker) that by cells located in a lymph node.

HP_0020234.label: altered lymph - node tissue architecture
HP_0020234.definition: An alteration that affects multiple components of the architecture of a lymph node.

HP_0020235.label: effaced lymph - node architecture
HP_0020235.definition: Effacement of architecture typically refers to a cellular infiltrate destroying the normal follicular architecture of a lymph node. This effacement may result in sheets of cells that do not form clear architecture (seen in many lymphomas) or may lead to replacement of the normal architecture by atypical architecture, for example effacement of normal lymph node architecture (including normal follicles and patent lymph node sinuses) by many abnormal follicles in follicular lymphoma.

HP_0020236.label: vaguely nodular lymph - node architecture
HP_0020236.definition: In contrast to normal lymph node architecture or that of follicular lymphoma, where follicles are typically distinct and readily identifiable on H&E stained biopsy sections, the cells within an atypical lymph node may show what appear to groups of cells forming vague nodules but not forming clear follicles.

HP_0020237.label: lymph - node capsular invasion by lymphocytes
HP_0020237.definition: Migration of substantial numbers of lymphocytes into the capsule of a lymph node.

HP_0020238.label: lymph - node extracapsular extension by lymph - node lymphocytes
HP_0020238.definition: Migration of lymphocytes into the soft tissues surrounding the lymph node.

HP_0020239.label: increased lymph - node epithelioid histiocyte count
HP_0020239.definition: Number of epithelioid histiocytes (histiocytes are tissue-resident macrophages) located within a lymph node above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0020240.label: scattered lymph node individual epithelioid histiocytes
HP_0020240.definition: Many individual (not clustered) epithelioid histiocytes throughout at least part of a lymph node.

HP_0020241.label: clustered lymph node epithelioid histiocytes
HP_0020241.definition: Formation of clusters (group of cells positioned near each other) of epithelioid histiocytes within a lymph node.

HP_0020242.label: abnormal lymph - node follicle architecture
HP_0020242.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the architecture of follicles of a lymph node.

HP_0020243.label: floral - pattern lymph node follicles
HP_0020243.definition: Atypical lymph node follicles that have mantle zone cells invaginating/infiltrating into the follicle centers, which is said to confer a flower-like appearance.
HP_0020243.synonyms: floral follicular lymph node architecture | floral growth pattern

HP_0020244.label: colonization of follicles by lymphoma cells
HP_0020244.definition: In contrast to follicular lymphoma, which typically is a lymphoma that forms follicles or potentially completely replaces normal follicles, some lymphomas (most commonly marginal zone lymphoma) can infiltrate normal follicles so both normal lymphocytes and the infiltrating lymphoma cells are present. This is called colonization of follicles by the lymphoma cells.

HP_0020245.label: crowded lymph - node follicles
HP_0020245.definition: Reduction in the average distance between adjacent lymph node follicles.

HP_0020246.label: lymph - node follicular lysis
HP_0020246.definition: An abnormal morphology of hyperplastic lymph node follicles characterized by distortion of the follicular architecture by tongues and clusters of dark blue mantle cells impinging on and invading the reactive germinal center (Mostly T cells and mantle-zone B cells).

HP_0020247.label: non - polarized lymph node germinal centers
HP_0020247.definition: A loss of the typical polarization of the architecture of a lymph node germinal center.

HP_0020248.label: irregularly shaped lymph node germinal centers
HP_0020248.definition: A deviation from the typically fairly round or oval form of a lymph node germinal center.

HP_0020249.label: abnormal lymph - node marginal or mantle zone morphology
HP_0020249.definition: An abnormality of the structure of the mantle or marginal zone of a lymph node.

HP_0020250.label: abnormal lymph node marginal zone morphology

HP_0020251.label: abnormal lymph node mantle zone morphology

HP_0020253.label: lymph node with expanded mantle zones
HP_0020253.definition: Enlargement of the typical outer ring of small lymphocytes (mantle zone) surrounding a germinal center of a lymph node.
HP_0020253.synonyms: germinal centers with expanded mantle zones | germinal centres with expanded mantle zones

HP_0020254.label: lymph node with poorly defined germinal center borders
HP_0020254.definition: Reduced demarcation of the border between germinal centers and mantle zones. This border is typically seen as a crisp line on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained lymph node sections.

HP_0020255.label: abnormal lymph - node germinal center morphology
HP_0020255.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of germinal centers of a lymph node.

HP_0020257.label: mantle zone pattern
HP_0020257.definition: This refers to an architectural pattern of infiltration where atypical lymphocytes surround germinal centers, often expanding the mantle zones but without effacing architecture.

HP_0020258.label: germinal centers with absent marginal zones

HP_0020261.label: poorly defined primary lymph - node follicles
HP_0020261.definition: Lack of the typical easily recognized delineation of primary follicles within lymph nodes.

HP_0020262.label: progressive transformation of germinal centers
HP_0020262.definition: This is a condition sometimes seen in a subset of germinal centers of reactive lymph nodes where germinal centers become enlarged and infiltrated by benign mantle zone cells and some T cells.

HP_0020263.label: absent germinal center tingible body macrophages
HP_0020263.definition: Lack of observable tingible body macrophages (TBMs) in germinal centers (GCs) of secondary lymphoid follicles. TBMs represent unique, large phagocytic cells that reside and are a subset of mononuclear phagocytes.

HP_0020264.label: lack of germinal center mitotic figures
HP_0020264.definition: Absence of extreme paucity of mitotic figures in a lymph node germinal center.

HP_0020265.label: non - polarized mantle zones
HP_0020265.definition: Lack of the typical polarization of the outer ring of small lymphocytes (mantle zone) surrounding a germinal center of a lymph node.

HP_0020266.label: hyalinized lymph - node vessels
HP_0020266.definition: Hyalinized means to become clear/translucent such as collagen becoming more pale staining (collagen is typically quite eosinophilic, meaning attracted to the pink/red dye eosin); however, with regard to vessels in the lymph node, hyalinization is often used to describe vessel walls that appear markedly thickened or surrounded by eosinophilic material such as collagen, not necessarily translucent appearing.

HP_0020267.label: lymph - node follicular sclerosis
HP_0020267.definition: Collagen deposition, typically with decreased cellularity, within lymph-node follicles.

HP_0020268.label: compressed lymph - node sinuses
HP_0020268.definition: Loss of the typical patency (openness) of lymph node sinuses.

HP_0020269.label: lymph - node proliferation centers
HP_0020269.definition: Proliferation centers are a finding specific to chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma where regions (typically relatively small, comparable to the size of a lymph node follicle) appear more pale on H&E stained sections (though they may become enlarged to merge together). These areas contain increased numbers of enlarged lymphoma cells with nucleoli (prolymphocytes and paraimmunoblasts) and show a higher proliferation rate (readily visualized with a Ki-67 immunohistochemical stain) than surrounding lymphoma cells. They can be mistaken as vague follicle formation and are therefore sometimes referred to as pseudofollicles.

HP_0020270.label: cytologic atypia in mantle cells
HP_0020270.definition: Lymphocytes in the mantle zones of lymph node secondary follicles show cellular atypia such as enlarged size, increased cytoplasm, atypical distribution of chromatin, or irregular nuclear contours.

HP_0020271.label: increased lymph - node eosinophils
HP_0020271.definition: Eosinophils count within a lymph node above normal limits.
HP_0020271.UMLS synonyms: Lymph node architecture severely altered: lack of follicles, depletion of lymphocytes, and increased proportion of interdigitating reticular cells and eosinophils

HP_0020272.label: increased lymph - node plasma cells
HP_0020272.definition: Number of plasma cells per lymph node above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0020273.label: high lymph node non - germinal center mitotic activity
HP_0020273.definition: Increased numbers of mitotic figures outside of germinal centers.

HP_0020274.label: lymph - node lymphocyte monocytoid morphology
HP_0020274.definition: Lymphocytes that show morphologic features resembling monocytes, such as increased cytoplasm and slightly enlarged nuclei that are more irregular than most lymph node lymphocytes.

HP_0020275.label: reduced lymph node lymphocyte morphological variability
HP_0020275.definition: Decreased morphological variability of lymph node lymphocytes as compared to the typically somewhat heterogeneous morphology of populations of benign lymph node lymphocytes.

HP_0020276.label: increased large lymphocytes in lymph node
HP_0020276.definition: An increased number of large lymphocytes within a lymph node compared to a normal non-reactive lymph node.

HP_0020277.label: hodgkin morphology cells
HP_0020277.definition: Hodgkin cells are typically large and often show very large nucleoli and sometimes binucleation or multinucleation. Reed-Sternberg cells are a type of Hodgkin cell that is binucleated with very large nucleoli that stains slightly red on H&E stained sections (often said to mimic owl eyes). Other Hodgkin cell morphologies include cells that are dying with dark basophilic (blue) nuclei that appear somewhat smudged (mummified cells) and cells with a large space around or adjacent to the nuclei and retracted cytoplasm after tissue fixation (lacunar cells). Hodgkin cells are characteristic of Hodgkin lymphoma, however several non-Hodgkin lymphomas and noN-neoplastic conditions are known to sometimes show a few similar morphology cells.
HP_0020277.UMLS synonyms: B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable, with features intermediate between diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and Hodgkin lymphoma

HP_0020278.label: abnormal lymph - node lymphoctye nuclear morphology

HP_0020279.label: irregular lymph - node lymphocyte nuclei
HP_0020279.definition: Lymph node lymphocyte nuclei that are more irregular than the typical round to slightly oval shapes of the majority of lymph node lymphocytes.

HP_0020280.label: lymph - node dutcher bodies
HP_0020280.definition: Dutcher bodies are collections of immunoglobulin protein that overlie or invaginate into the nucleus of plasma cells. These nuclear pseudoinclusions can occasionally be seen in reactive states and may be increased in specific neoplastic conditions.

HP_0020281.label: finely dispersed lymph node lymphocyte chromatin
HP_0020281.definition: Nuclei of lymphocytes with less dense, evenly distributed chromatin than the normal densely packed, often clumped chromatin of mature lymphocytes.

HP_0020282.label: abnormal lymph - node lymphocyte chromatin
HP_0020282.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the chromatin (complex of DNA and protein which comprises chromosomes) of lymphocytes that are located within a lymph node.

HP_0020283.label: clumping of lymph node lymphocyte chromatin
HP_0020283.definition: Nuclei of lymphocytes show multiple small densely packed areas of chromatin that appear as relatively evenly spaced clumps of basophilic (blue) staining within the nuclei on Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained sections.

HP_0020284.label: abnormal lymph - node lymphocyte cytoplasm morphology
HP_0020284.definition: Any phenotypic abnormality of the cytoplasm (material located within the cell membrane but excluding the nucleus) of lymphocytes that are located within a lymph node.

HP_0020285.label: decreased lymph node lymphocyte cytoplasm
HP_0020285.definition: The amount of cytoplasm in lymphocytes is even less than the relatively little cytoplasm found in the majority of lymphocytes within lymph nodes.

HP_0020286.label: increased lymph node lymphocyte cytoplasm
HP_0020286.definition: Increased amount of cytoplasm compared to the majority of lymphocytes in a benign lymph node.

HP_0020287.label: abnormal level of lymph - node cellular cd19 expression
HP_0020287.definition: Detection of an abnormal level of CD19 on the cell(s) of interest in a lymph node with the use of anti-CD19 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).

HP_0020288.label: abnormal lymph - node cellular b - cell marker expression
HP_0020288.definition: Abnormal expression of an antigen (marker) that is normally expressed by B lymphocytes.

HP_0020289.label: abnormal level of lymph - node cellular cd20 expression
HP_0020289.definition: Detection of abnormal levels of CD20 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD20 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).

HP_0020290.label: cd79a expression
HP_0020290.definition: Detection of the presence of CD79a on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-CD79a antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry) or fluorophore (for flow cytometry).

HP_0020291.label: increased lymph - node cellular cd20 expression
HP_0020291.definition: Increased levels of CD20 expression compared to normal B cells.

HP_0020292.label: decreased lymph - node cellular cd20 expression
HP_0020292.definition: Decreased levels of CD20 expression compared to normal B cells.

HP_0020293.label: decreased lymph - node cellular cd19 expression
HP_0020293.definition: Decreased levels of CD19 expression compared to normal B cells.

HP_0020294.label: increased lymph - node cellular cd19 expression
HP_0020294.definition: Increased levels of CD19 expression compared to normal B cells.

HP_0020295.label: pax5 expression
HP_0020295.definition: Detection of the presence of PAX5 on the cell(s) of interest with the use of anti-PAX5 antibodies conjugated to a chromogen (for immunohistochemistry).

HP_0020296.label: germinal center b - lymphocyte bcl2 expression
HP_0020296.definition: Positive staining for BCL2 apoptosis regulator protein in lymph-node germinal center B cells.

HP_0025004.label: hallux rigidus
HP_0025004.definition: Osteoarthritis of the metatarsophalangeal joint of the first toe.
HP_0025004.UMLS synonyms: Hallux Rigidus | congenital hallux rigidus | Acquired left hallux rigidus | Acquired right hallux rigidus | Hallux rigidus, unspecified foot | hallux rigidus of right foot | hallux rigidus of left foot | hallux rigidus of both feet | Procedures for hallux valgus or hallux rigidus | congenital hallux rigidus of right foot | congenital hallux rigidus of left foot | rigidus; hallux, late effect of rickets | Bilateral acquired hallux rigidus of bilateral feet | Correction of hallux valgus or rigidus by arthroplasty, bilateral | Correction of hallux valgus or rigidus by arthroplasty, unilateral | hallux rigidus correction with cheilectomy of first metatarsophalangeal joint | Hallux rigidus correction with cheilectomy, debridement and capsular release of the first metatarsophalangeal joint; with implant | hallux rigidus correction with cheilectomy of 1st MTP joint with implant | Hallux rigidus correction with cheilectomy, debridement and capsular release of the first metatarsophalangeal joint; without implant | Correction of hallux valgus or rigidus by arthroplasty with insertion of prosthesis, unilateral | Correction of hallux valgus or rigidus by arthroplasty with insertion of prosthesis, bilateral | Correction of hallux rigidus with cheilectomy, debridement and capsular release of first metatarsophalangeal joint

HP_0025005.label: thickening of glomerular capillary wall
HP_0025005.definition: Widening of the wall of capillary blood vessels in the glomerulus. This feature may be produced by deposits and other changes affecting either subepithelial and subendothelial regions or the glomerular basement membrane itself.

HP_0025006.label: abnormal glomerular capillary morphology
HP_0025006.definition: A structural anomaly of the capillary blood vessels in the renal glomerulus.
HP_0025006.synonyms: abnormalities of the glomerular capillary wall

HP_0025007.label: ectopic fovea
HP_0025007.definition: An abnormal anatomic position of the fovea, the small, central pit composed of closely packed cones that is located in the macula of the retina.

HP_0025008.label: tracheal tug on inspiration
HP_0025008.definition: Downward movement of the trachea during inspiration due to downward traction on the tracheobronchial tree.

HP_0025009.label: forward slanting upper incisors
HP_0025009.definition: The upper incisors deviate from the normal angle of being roughly parallel to the surface of the face and instead slant outwards.
HP_0025009.synonyms: forward directed upper incisors | proclination of the upper incisors | protruding upper incisors

HP_0025010.label: foveal atrophy
HP_0025010.definition: Partial or complete loss of foveal tissue that was once present.
HP_0025010.UMLS synonyms: OPTIC ATROPHY 13 WITH RETINAL AND FOVEAL ABNORMALITIES

HP_0025011.label: pyriform aperture stenosis
HP_0025011.definition: Narrowing of the anterior nasal aperture (piriform or pyriform aperture), which is a pear-shaped opening in the skull that forms the bony inlet of the nose.
HP_0025011.UMLS synonyms: Congenital stenosis of nasal pyriform aperture | Congenital nasal pyriform aperture stenosis | Correction of stenosis of nasal pyriform aperture | Holoprosencephaly with nasal pyriformis aperture

HP_0025012.label: status cribrosum
HP_0025012.definition: Diffusely widened perivascular spaces in the basal ganglia, affecting especially the corpus striatum. Status cribrosum is usually symmetrical, with the perivascular spaces showing CSF signal and without diffusion restriction. The word cribriform means sievelike, with multiple perforations.
HP_0025012.UMLS synonyms: Dilated perivascular spaces with a typical status cribrosum

HP_0025013.label: decerebrate rigidity
HP_0025013.definition: A type of rigidity that is manifested by an exaggerated extensor posture of all extremities.
HP_0025013.UMLS synonyms: decerebrate rigidity bilateral | Decerebrate State | decerebrate rigidity of left side only | decerebrate rigidity of right side only | Glasgow: best motor response: decerebrate rigidity (2) | Glasgow: best motor response: flexion (decorticate or decerebrate rigidity) (3)

HP_0025014.label: subcutaneous spheroids
HP_0025014.definition: Small, hard cyst-like nodules, freely moveable in the subcutis over the bony prominences of the legs and arms, which have an outer calcified layer with a translucent core on x-ray.

HP_0025015.label: abnormal vascular morphology
HP_0025015.UMLS synonyms: Arteriosclerosis | Vascular ring | Nevus sanguineous | Vascular anomaly | Vascular graft (body structure) | Vascular polyp | Vascular wall degeneration | Congenital vascular proliferation | Elastic vascular sclerosis | Atypical vascular lesion | Anomalous vascular connection | Vascular surgical margin | Basophilic vascular deposition | Post-surgical vascular structure | Congenital vascular malformation - mass | Congenital vascular malformation, corrected | Vascular catheter insertion site | Low-flow congenital vascular malformation | Congenital vascular anomaly, macular type | High-flow congenital vascular malformation

HP_0025016.label: abnormal capillary morphology
HP_0025016.definition: A structural anomaly of the tiny blood vessels that connect arterioles with venules and whose walls act as semipermeable membranes that mediate the diffusion of fluids and gases between the blood circulation and body tissues.
HP_0025016.UMLS synonyms: Strawberry nevus of skin | Capillary lymphangioma | Capillary telangiectasia

HP_0025017.label: capillary fragility
HP_0025017.definition: Reduced resistance to rupture of capillary blood vessels. Capillary fragility may manifest as a bleeding diathesis with spontaneous ecchymoses (bruises).
HP_0025017.UMLS synonyms: Capillary Fragility | Capillary fragility test | Increased capillary fragility | Decreased capillary fragility | Capillary fragility abnormality | Capillary fragility normal | Capillary fragility abnormal | purpura; capillary fragility | Capillary fragility | Patient | Coagulation | Capillary fragility detected by tourniquet test | Capillary fragility not detected by tourniquet test | Hereditary vascular fragility | Capillary fragility:PrThr:Pt:^Patient:Ord | Capillary fragillity - finding | Screen for increased intracranial pressure, capillary fragility, bleeding tendencies, severe acute cardiac difficulties with hypertension, or other conditions in which tensing muscles might produce greater physiological injury and modify the technique, as appropriate

HP_0025018.label: abnormal capillary physiology
HP_0025018.definition: A functional anomaly of the tiny blood vessels that connect arterioles with venules and whose walls act as semipermeable membranes that mediate the diffusion of fluids and gases between the blood circulation and body tissues.

HP_0025019.label: arterial rupture
HP_0025019.definition: Sudden breakage of an artery leading to leakage of blood from the circulation.
HP_0025019.UMLS synonyms: Rupture of artery | artery; rupture, meningeal | Bone Fragility with Contractures, Arterial Rupture, and Deafness | Connective tissue disorder due to lysyl hydroxylase-3 deficiency | Check for signs and symptoms of severely compromised hemodynamic status (e.g., arterial trauma or rupture) | Coronary artery rupture | Rupture iliac artery | Pulmonary artery rupture | Carotid artery rupture | Rupture popliteal artery | Rupture axillary artery | Rupture subclavian artery | Vertebral artery rupture | Rupture femoral artery | Rupture radial artery | Rupture brachial artery | Rupture ulna artery | Hypogastric artery rupture | Omental artery rupture | Ruptured popliteal artery aneurysm | Rupture anterior tibial artery | Rupture posterior tibial artery | Ruptured aneurysm of artery | Rupture of transplanted artery | Anterior spinal artery rupture

HP_0025020.label: elevated prostate - specific antigen level
HP_0025020.definition: An increased concentration of prostate specific antigen (PSA) in the circulation.

HP_0025021.label: abnormal erythrocyte sedimentation rate
HP_0025021.definition: A deviation from normal range of the erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. An elevation may indicate inflammation or may be caused by any condition that elevates fibrinogen. A decreased ESR may be seen in polycythemia or in certain blood diseases in which red blood cells have an irregular or smaller shape that causes slower settling.
HP_0025021.synonyms: abnormal esr | abnormal westergren sedimentation rate
HP_0025021.UMLS synonyms: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate outside reference range | Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and abnormality of plasma viscosity

HP_0025022.label: decreased erythrocyte sedimentation rate
HP_0025022.definition: A reduced erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). The ESR is a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. A decreased ESR may be seen in polycythemia or in certain blood diseases in which red blood cells have an irregular or smaller shape that causes slower settling.
HP_0025022.UMLS synonyms: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate below reference range

HP_0025023.label: rectal atresia
HP_0025023.definition: A developmental defect resulting in complete obliteration of the lumen of the rectum. That is, there is an abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the rectum.
HP_0025023.UMLS synonyms: Congenital atresia of rectum | Rectal and large intestine atresia/stenosis | Non-syndromic anorectal malformation with rectal atresia | Reanastomosis of rectum to anal canal for correction of congenital atresia of rectum

HP_0025024.label: megarectum
HP_0025024.definition: An abnormal dilation of the rectum. There is a large filled rectum as a result of underlying innervation or muscular abnormalities, which remains after disimpaction of the rectum.

HP_0025025.label: rectovestibular fistula
HP_0025025.definition: A congenital malformation characterized by an abnormal connection (fistula) between the rectum and the vulval vestibule, at the lower aspect of the vaginal opening.

HP_0025026.label: h - type rectovestibular fistula
HP_0025026.definition: Rectovestibular fistula with a normal anus is known as H-type fistula or double termination of the alimentary tract.

HP_0025027.label: osteoma cutis
HP_0025027.definition: The term osteoma refers to the anomalous presence of ossification (bone formation) in the interior of the dermis or epidermis. The dermal or subcutaneous bone formation presents as stony hard nodules. The osteomata appear as irregular, hardened small nodules that are well circumscribed and generally of the same color as the skin.
HP_0025027.UMLS synonyms: Osteoma cutis | Progressive Heterotopic Heteroplasia | Dermal ossification (osteoma cutis)

HP_0025028.label: abnormal enteric nervous system morphology
HP_0025028.definition: A structural anomaly of nerves of the enteric nervous system.
HP_0025028.synonyms: abnormality of enteric nervous system morphology

HP_0025030.label: enteric neuronal degeneration
HP_0025030.definition: Deterioration of enteric neurons with impairment of enteric neuronal structure. Typical neuropathological findings include qualitative (e.g., neuronal swelling, intranuclear inclusions, axonal degeneration) and quantitative (e.g., reduction in the number of neurons) abnormalities of the enteric neurons.

HP_0025032.label: abnormality of digestive system physiology
HP_0025032.definition: A functional anomaly of the digestive system.

HP_0025033.label: abnormal digestive system morphology
HP_0025033.definition: A structural anomaly of the digestive system.

HP_0025034.label: abnormal morphology of erythroid progenitor cell
HP_0025034.definition: Abnormal form of the progenitor cells committed to the erythroid lineage.

HP_0025035.label: abnormal proerythroblast morphology
HP_0025035.definition: Anomalous form of the proerythroblast, i.e., the immature, nucleated erythrocyte occupying the stage of erythropoeisis that follows formation of erythroid progenitor cells. This cell is CD71-positive, has both a nucleus and a nucleolus, and lacks hematopoeitic lineage markers.

HP_0025037.label: hypothalamic gliosis
HP_0025037.definition: Focal proliferation of glial cells in the hypothalamus.

HP_0025038.label: intratesticular abscess
HP_0025038.definition: A collection of pus within a testicle. Ultrasonographic features include shaggy, irregular walls, intratesticular location, low-level internal echoes, and occasionally, hypervascular margins.

HP_0025039.label: basal ganglia edema
HP_0025039.definition: Swelling within the basal ganglia due to the accumulation of fluid.
HP_0025039.synonyms: basal ganglia oedema | edema of the basal ganglia | oedema of the basal ganglia

HP_0025040.label: thalamic edema
HP_0025040.definition: Swelling within the thalamus due to the accumulation of fluid.
HP_0025040.synonyms: edema of the thalamus | oedema of the thalamus | thalamic oedema

HP_0025041.label: thalamic calcification
HP_0025041.UMLS synonyms: Symmetrical thalamic calcification | computed tomography of brain: calcification of thalamus | computed tomography of brain: calcification of left thalamus | computed tomography of brain: calcification of right thalamus

HP_0025042.label: abnormality of mesenteric lymph nodes
HP_0025042.definition: A morphological anomaly of lymph nodes in the mesenteric root or throughout the mesentery.

HP_0025043.label: enlarged mesenteric lymph node
HP_0025043.definition: Increase in size of one or more mesenteric lymph nodes.
HP_0025043.UMLS synonyms: Mesenteric lymphadenopathy | open appendectomy: terminal ileum enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes | laparoscopic appendectomy assessment terminal ileum enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes

HP_0025044.label: lung abscess
HP_0025044.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in lung parenchyma, which leads to a cavity, and after formation of bronchopulmonary fistula, can manifest as an air-fluid level inside the cavity.
HP_0025044.UMLS synonyms: Lung Abscess | Amebic lung abscess | Single lung abscess | gangrenous lung abscess | post lung abscess | necrotic lung abscess | tuberculosis; abscess, lung | Abscess of lung with pneumonia | LUNG LEFT ABSCESS | LUNG ABSCESS CRYPTOCOCCAL | LUNG ABSCESS OPEN | LUNG LLL ABSCESS | LUNG RUL ABSCESS | Tuberculous abscess of lung | Drainage of lung abscess | Abscess of lung without pneumonia | LUNG LLL ABSCESS RESECTION | LUNG RML ABSCESS RECURRENT | Abscess of lung and mediastinum | abscess; lung, amebic, with brain abscess (etiology) | abscess; liver, amebic, with lung abscess (etiology) | Specimen from abscess of lung | lung abscess, cytochrome B-positive | lung abscess due to immunodeficiency | abscess; tuberculous, lung, primary (progressive)

HP_0025045.label: abnormal brain lactate level by mrs
HP_0025045.definition: A deviation from normal of the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP_0025045.synonyms: abnormal lactate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025046.label: reduced brain lactate level by mrs
HP_0025046.definition: A decrease in the level of lactate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP_0025046.synonyms: reduced brain lactate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025047.label: abnormal brain choline level by mrs
HP_0025047.definition: A deviation from normal in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP_0025047.synonyms: abnormal brain choline level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025048.label: reduced brain choline level by mrs
HP_0025048.definition: An decrease in the level of choline-containing compounds in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP_0025048.synonyms: reduced brain choline level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025049.label: abnormal brain creatine level by mrs
HP_0025049.synonyms: abnormal brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025050.label: elevated brain creatine level by mrs
HP_0025050.definition: An increase in the level of creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP_0025050.synonyms: elevated brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025051.label: reduced brain creatine level by mrs
HP_0025051.definition: A decrease in the level of creatine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP_0025051.synonyms: low brain creatine phosphate | reduced brain creatine level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025052.label: abnormal brain n - acetyl aspartate level by mrs
HP_0025052.definition: A deviation from normal in the level of N-acetyl aspartate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP_0025052.synonyms: abnormal brain n - acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025053.label: elevated brain n - acetyl aspartate level by mrs
HP_0025053.definition: An increase in the level of N-acetyl aspartate in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).
HP_0025053.synonyms: elevated brain n - acetyl aspartate level by magnetic resonance spectroscopy

HP_0025057.label: abnormal olfactory lobe morphology
HP_0025057.definition: A structural anomaly of the olfactory lobe, the structure within the brain that receives neural input from the nasal cavity and thereby processes the sense of smell.

HP_0025058.label: hypothalamic atrophy
HP_0025058.definition: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of hypothalamus tissue that was once present.

HP_0025059.label: splenic abscess
HP_0025059.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the parenchyma of the spleen.
HP_0025059.UMLS synonyms: Splenic abscess | Drainage of splenic abscess | splenic abscess due to Pseudomonas | splenic abscess due to Enterobacteriaceae | splenic abscess due to Serratia | splenic abscess due to Bacteroides | splenic abscess due to Brucella | spleen; abscess, amebic

HP_0025060.label: multifocal splenic abscess
HP_0025060.definition: Multiple abscess lesions in the spleen.

HP_0025061.label: unifocal splenic abscess
HP_0025061.synonyms: solitary splenic abscess | unilocular splenic abscess

HP_0025062.label: geophagia
HP_0025062.definition: The practice of eating earth or soil-like substrates such as clay or chalk.

HP_0025063.label: scaphoid abdomen
HP_0025063.definition: The anterior abdominal wall is sunken and presents a concave rather than a convex contour.

HP_0025064.label: thalamic hemorrhage
HP_0025064.UMLS synonyms: Thalamic hemorrhage | intracerebral hemorrhage thalamic | CNS THALAMIC CVA HEMORRHAGIC

HP_0025065.label: abnormal mean corpuscular volume
HP_0025065.definition: A deviation from normal of the mean corpuscular volume, or mean cell volume (MCV) of red blood cells, usually taken to be 80 to 100 femtoliters.

HP_0025066.label: decreased mean corpuscular volume
HP_0025066.definition: A reduction from normal of the mean corpuscular volume, or mean cell volume (MCV) of red blood cells (usually defined as an MCV below 80 femtoliters).
HP_0025066.synonyms: decreased mcv | microcytosis | reduced erythrocyte volume

HP_0025068.label: incomitant strabismus
HP_0025068.definition: Strabismus in which the angle of deviation differs depending upon the direction of gaze or according to which eye is fixing, associated with: (i) defective movement of the eye, (ii) asymmetrical accommodative effort.

HP_0025069.label: concomitant strabismus
HP_0025069.definition: Strabismus in which the angle of deviation of the squiting eye remains the same in relation to the other eye, in all directions of gaze, and whichever eye is fixing.
HP_0025069.UMLS synonyms: Strabismus, Comitant | Esotropia | Exotropia | Vertical-non concomitant-horizontal strabismus syndrome | Strabismus, Noncomitant

HP_0025070.label: abnormal u wave
HP_0025070.definition: An anomaly of the U wave of the electrocardiogram (EKG). The U wave is a small (0.5 mm) deflection immediately following the T wave, usually in the same direction as the T wave. It is best seen in leads V2 and V3.
HP_0025070.UMLS synonyms: EKG: U wave abnormal | Electrocardiogram U-wave abnormality

HP_0025071.label: u wave inversion
HP_0025071.definition: Direction of the U wave opposite to the T wave (i.e., below baseline) in leads with upright T waves.
HP_0025071.UMLS synonyms: Electrocardiogram U wave inversion | Monitor cardiac manifestations of hypokalemia (e.g., hypotension, T wave flattening, T wave inversion, presence of U wave, ectopy, tachycardia, and weak pulse)

HP_0025072.label: prominent u wave
HP_0025072.definition: Increased amplitude of the U wave, defined as an amplitude greater than 1-2mm or 25 percent of the height of the T wave.
HP_0025072.UMLS synonyms: Electrocardiogram U-wave prominent | interim stress electrocardiogram prominent U waves | Prominent U-waves in anterior leads on electrocardiogram

HP_0025073.label: exercise - induced u wave inversion
HP_0025073.definition: U wave inversion that is induced by exercise stress testing.

HP_0025074.label: abnormal qrs complex
HP_0025074.definition: An anomaly of the complex formed by the Q, R, and S waves, which occur in rapid succession on the electrocardiogram.
HP_0025074.UMLS synonyms: EKG: QRS complex abnormal | QRS Complex Abnormality by ECG Finding

HP_0025075.label: increased qrs voltage
HP_0025075.definition: Elevation of the voltage (height) of the QRS complex. There are several criteria in use, but the most common is the Sokolov-Lyon criterion (S wave depth in V1 + tallest R wave height in V5-V6 greater than 35 mm).

HP_0025076.label: abnormal qrs voltage
HP_0025076.definition: Abnormal amplitude of the QRS complex of the electrocardiogram (EKG).

HP_0025077.label: decreased qrs voltage
HP_0025077.definition: Reduced amplitude (height) of the QRS complex of the electrocardiogram (EKG), defined as amplitudes of all the QRS complexes in the limb leads are less than 5 mm or amplitudes of all the QRS complexes in the precordial leads less than 10 mm.

HP_0025078.label: electrical alternans
HP_0025078.definition: The QRS complexes of the electrocardiogram alternate in height.
HP_0025078.UMLS synonyms: Electrical alternation of heart | electrocardiogram: electrical alternans microvolt T-wave alternans | interim stress electrocardiogram electrical alternans | stress test electrocardiogram: electrical alternans at rest | stress test electrocardiogram: electrical alternans at peak response

HP_0025079.label: pancreatic abscess
HP_0025079.definition: A circumscribed area of pus or necrotic debris in the parenchyma of the pancreas.
HP_0025079.UMLS synonyms: Abscess of pancreas | Drainage of pancreatic abscess | Incision and drainage of pancreatic abscess | pancreatic abscess due to Bacteroides fragilis | pancreatic abscess due to anaerobic bacteria | pancreatic abscess due to Gram-negative anaerobes | drainage of pancreatic abscess with fluoroscopic guidance

HP_0025080.label: orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
HP_0025080.definition: A form of hyperkeratosis characterized by thickening of the cornified layer without retained nuclei.
HP_0025080.UMLS synonyms: Orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis | Orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis, marked | Severe orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis

HP_0025081.label: darier 's sign
HP_0025081.definition: A skin change elicited by briskly rubbing the skin lesion in urticaria pigmentosa (UP), whereby the area begins to itch and becomes raised and surrounded by erythema. Unlike other forms of dermatographism, Darier's sign refers to urtication that is limited to the UP involved areas and, as in this case, spares the skin unaffected by UP.

HP_0025082.label: abnormal cutaneous elastic fiber morphology
HP_0025082.definition: Any structural anomaly of the elastic fibers of the skin. Elastic fibers are the essential extracellular matrix macromolecules comprising an elastin core surrounded by a mantle of fibrillin-rich microfibrils.

HP_0025083.label: elevated dermal desmosine content
HP_0025083.definition: An increased amount of desmosine measure in the skin. Desmosine is a cross-linking amino acid formed from lysyl residues in elastin.

HP_0025084.label: folliculitis
HP_0025084.definition: Inflammatory cells within the wall and ostia of the hair follicle, creating a follicular-based pustule.
HP_0025084.UMLS synonyms: Folliculitis | Folliculitis decalvans | Pustular folliculitis | Superficial folliculitis | Scalp folliculitis | Bacterial folliculitis | Eosinophilic pustular folliculitis | Eosinophilic folliculitis | Malassezia folliculitis | Chronic folliculitis | Deep folliculitis | Agminate folliculitis | Nodular folliculitis | Actinic folliculitis | Tufted folliculitis | Folliculitis, CTCAE | Pityrosporum folliculitis | Acute folliculitis | Pityriasis Folliculitis | Nuchal folliculitis | Folliculitis pityrosporon | Folliculitis genital | Neutrophilic folliculitis | Cutaneous folliculitis | gonococcal; folliculitis

HP_0025085.label: bloody diarrhea
HP_0025085.definition: Passage of many stools containing blood.
HP_0025085.synonyms: blood in stool | bloody bowel movement | bloody diarrhea | bloody diarrhoea | bloody stool
HP_0025085.UMLS synonyms: Hemorrhagic diarrhea | DIARRHEA BLOODY ACUTE | DIARRHEA BLOODY CHRONIC | Instruct on signs and symptoms of infection (e.g., fever, chills or sweats, persistent cough, sore throat, difficulty breathing, any new pain, vomiting, diarrhea, bloody urine, skin rash, redness or swelling at IV site)

HP_0025086.label: bloody mucoid diarrhea
HP_0025086.definition: Passage of many stools containing blood and mucus.

HP_0025087.label: delayed recoil upon stretching of skin
HP_0025087.definition: Area of skin requiring an increased amount of time to return to its original shape after being stretched.

HP_0025088.label: onychomadesis
HP_0025088.definition: Complete shedding (separation) of the nail from the proximal matrix. Onychomadesis is the proximal separation of the nail plate from the nail matrix due to a temporary cessation of nail growth.
HP_0025088.UMLS synonyms: Nail Loss | Onychomadesis due to and following hand foot and mouth disease

HP_0025089.label: feculent vomiting
HP_0025089.definition: Vomiting of material that is of fecal origin.
HP_0025089.synonyms: faecal vomiting | fecal vomiting | stercoraceous vomiting | vomiting faecal matter | vomiting fecal matter
HP_0025089.UMLS synonyms: Vomiting fecal matter | Vomit odor feculent

HP_0025090.label: abnormal large intestinal mucosa morphology
HP_0025090.definition: A structural anomaly of the mucous lining of the large intestine.

HP_0025092.label: epidermal acanthosis
HP_0025092.definition: Diffuse hypertrophy or thickening of the stratum spinosum of the epidermis (prickle cell layer of the skin).
HP_0025092.synonyms: acanthosis | acanthotic epidermis | epidermal hyperplasia | thickening of upper layer of skin

HP_0025093.label: peripapillary exudate
HP_0025093.definition: A retinal exudate in the area surrounding the optic nerve head.

HP_0025095.definition: A sudden violent, spasmodic, audible expiration of breath through the nose and mouth.

HP_0025103.definition: A type of skin nodule that has a small depression that resembles a navel (i.e., is umbilicated).
HP_0025103.UMLS synonyms: umbilical nodule | Nodule of umbilical structure

HP_0025104.label: capillary malformation
HP_0025104.definition: A capillary malformation is a flat, sharply defined vascular stain of the skin. It may cover a large surface area or it may be scattered and appear as little islands of color. In a capillary maformation, the predominant vessels are small, slow-flow vessels (i.e., arterioles and postcapillary venules).

HP_0025105.label: nevus anemicus
HP_0025105.definition: A congenital skin lesion characterized by irregular hypopigmented macules that coalesce to form plaques and occur particularly on the chest. It is generally present at birth or develops in the first days of life. It is more common in females. Diagnosis is confirmed by applying gentle friction to the lesion and the surrounding skin and checking that the erythema produced in the healthy skin does not appear in the hypopigmented lesion. This pale macule becomes more conspicuous when the lesion and its surroundings are rubbed. The margin of the naevus is ill-defined and consists of an archipelago of small anaemic spots.

HP_0025106.label: nevus roseus
HP_0025106.definition: A variant of port-wine stain characterized by a pale red or even pink tone, in contrast to the darker hue of the port-wine stain. By analogy with the term port-wine stain, this variant rose-wine stain, or nevus roseus. Nevus roseus, however, cannot be definitely diagnosed until adulthood as port-wine stains are sometimes pink in children. While the natural history of port-wine stains includes hypertrophy, darkening, and nodularity, nevus roseus remains unchanged for life.

HP_0025107.label: cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita
HP_0025107.definition: A congenital vascular malformation that presents as localized or generalized erythematous-telangiectatic lesions with a reticular pattern; the lesions are almost always present at birth or develop in the first days of life. Cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita (CMTC) appears as marble-like pattern (mottling) on the surface of the skin. In contrast to cutis marmorata, the marbling is more severe and always visible.
HP_0025107.UMLS synonyms: Cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita | Megalencephaly cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita | Megalencephaly Cutis Marmorata Telangiectatica Congenita (test kit)

HP_0025108.label: angioma serpentinum
HP_0025108.definition: Angioma serpiginosum consists of punctate, tightly packed telangiectatic lesions. Characteristic histopathological features are dilated and tortuous capillaries involving the uppermost part of the dermis.

HP_0025109.label: reduced red cell pyruvate kinase level
HP_0025109.definition: Decrease in the level of pyruvate kinase (PK) within erythrocytes. PK catalyzes the reaction: ATP + pyruvate = ADP + phosphoenolpyruvate.

HP_0025110.label: placoid macular lesion
HP_0025110.definition: Yellow/white, sharply delineated lesion, typically of inflammatory nature, involving the macula.

HP_0025112.label: auditory sensitivity
HP_0025112.UMLS synonyms: Auditory sensitivity | AUDITORY NEUROPATHY, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE, 1, TEMPERATURE-SENSITIVE

HP_0025113.label: misophonia
HP_0025113.definition: An adverse response (dislike) to sound no matter what volume the sound is, characterized by a strong negative reaction to soft sounds that can sometimes be further triggered by seeing the source of the offending sound.

HP_0025114.label: hypergranulosis
HP_0025114.definition: Hypergranulosis is an increased thickness of the stratum granulosum.
HP_0025114.UMLS synonyms: Focal hypergranulosis | Hypergranulosis, mild | Papillomatosis Hypergranulosis | Hypergranulosis in epidermis | Alternating hypogranulosis and hypergranulosis | Acanthosis with hypergranulosis and hyperkeratosis in affected skin

HP_0025115.label: civatte bodies
HP_0025115.definition: Eosinophilic hyaline ovoid bodies which are often found in the subepidermal papillary regions or sometimes in the epidermis. Civatte bodies (CBs) are seen as rounded, homogenous, eosinophilic masses on routine H and E staining lying in the deeper parts of epidermis/epithelium and more frequently in dermis/connective tissue. They are known as CBs (in epithelium/epidermis), colloid bodies, or hyaline bodies (in connective tissue). They are 10-25 micrometers in diameter and situated mostly within or above the inflammatory cell infiltrate. In lichen planus, the number of necrotic keratinocytes may be so large that they are seen lying in clusters in the uppermost dermis. These bodies show a positive periodic acid Schiff reaction and are diastase resistant
HP_0025115.synonyms: colloid bodies | colloid bodies of civatte | cytoid bodies | hyaline bodies

HP_0025116.label: fetal distress
HP_0025116.definition: An intrauterine state characterized by suboptimal values in the fetal heart rate, oxygenation of fetal blood, or other parameters indicative of compromise of the fetus. Signs of fetal distress include repetitive variable decelerations, fetal tachycardia or bradycardia, late decelerations, or low biophysical profile.

HP_0025117.label: rete ridge flattening
HP_0025117.definition: Rete pegs (or ridges) are the epithelial extensions that project into the underlying connective tissue in both skin and mucous membranes. Rete ridge flattening refers to the loss of these projections so that the skin epithelium acquires a relatively flat appearance.
HP_0025117.synonyms: flattened rete pegs | flattened rete ridges

HP_0025118.label: lip discoloration
HP_0025118.definition: Lightening or darkening of the lips from their usual coloring.

HP_0025119.label: violet lip discoloration
HP_0025119.definition: An alteration of the color of the lip to take on a violet color. This term does not include cyanosis.

HP_0025122.label: sawtooth acanthosis
HP_0025122.definition: A type of epidermal acanthosis characterized by a jagged (sawtooth) appearance of the rete ridges of the epidermis.

HP_0025123.label: white streaks / specks on enamel .
HP_0025123.definition: Areas of white discoloration visible on the surface of the teeth (enamel) in the form of streaks or specks.

HP_0025124.label: fragile teeth
HP_0025124.definition: A tendency of teeth to fracture as manifested by a history of repeated fracture of the dental enamel without adequate trauma.
HP_0025124.synonyms: enamel with tendency to chip | spontaneous tooth fracture

HP_0025125.label: white lesion of the oral mucosa
HP_0025125.definition: White lesions of the oral mucosa are generally caused by a condition that increases the thickness of the epithelium. This increases the distance to the vascular bed and thereby tends to change the usual reddish color of the oral mucosa to white. Common causes include hyperkeratosis (thickening of the keratin layer), acanthosis (thickening of the spinous cell layer), increased edema in the epithelium (leukoedema), and reduced vascularity of the underlying lamina propria. Additionally, fibrin caps or surface ulcerations and collapsed bullae can appear white.

HP_0025126.label: oral hairy leukoplakia
HP_0025126.definition: A corrugated white lesion of the oral mucosa that usually occurs on the lateral or ventral surfaces of the tongue and may have a shaggy or frayed appearance.
HP_0025126.UMLS synonyms: Oral hairy leukoplakia recurrent | Leukoplakia, Hairy | Oral hairy leukoplakia associated with immunodeficiency | HIV-induced oral hairy leukoplakia of tongue | Oral hairy leukoplakia associated with HIV disease | Leukoplakia of tongue associated with HIV disease

HP_0025127.label: actinic keratosis
HP_0025127.definition: A scaly, crusty lesion caused by damage from the ultraviolet radiation of the sun, with typical location on sun-exposed areas of the skin. Actinic keratosis lesions are often elevated, rough, and wartlike, and may be red, or occasionally tan, pink, or flesh-toned in color.

HP_0025128.label: reduced intraabdominal adipose tissue
HP_0025128.definition: An abnormally reduced amount of adipose tissue in the abdominal cavity.

HP_0025129.label: abnormal small intestinal mucosa morphology
HP_0025129.definition: A structural anomaly of the mucous lining of the small intestine.

HP_0025130.label: decreased small intestinal mucosa lactase level
HP_0025130.definition: Lactase is produced in the small intestine in humans, Lactase is a member of the beta-galactosidase family of enzymes, and hydrolyzes D-lactose to form D-galactose and D-glucose, which can be absorbed by the small intestine. There are many ways of assessing lactase activity. In one test, an endoscopic biopsy from the postbulbar duodenum is incubated with lactose on a test plate, and a color reaction develops within 20 min as a result of hydrolyzed lactose (a positive result) in patients with normolactasia, whereas no reaction (a negative result) develops in patients with severe hypolactasia. Other, less direct, tests include the hydrogen breath test, and blood tests following lactose challenges.
HP_0025130.UMLS synonyms: Decreased small intestinal mucosa lactase level

HP_0025131.label: finger swelling
HP_0025131.definition: Enlargement of the soft tissues of one or more fingers.

HP_0025141.label: gingival calcification
HP_0025141.definition: Ectopic deposition of calcium salts found in the gingiva.

HP_0025146.label: foveal degeneration
HP_0025146.definition: Deterioration of the tissue of the fovea, i.e.,the region of sharpest vision within the macula of the retina.

HP_0025147.label: beaten bronze macular sheen
HP_0025147.definition: A shiny appearance of the macula, which is often called a beaten bronze appearance.
HP_0025147.synonyms: beaten metal macular appearance | beaten - bronze macular appearance | beaten - bronze macular sheen

HP_0025148.label: dark choroid
HP_0025148.definition: A fluorescein angiographic finding of absence of the normal background fluorescence (a dark choroid).

HP_0025149.label: atrophic muscularis propria
HP_0025149.definition: Partial or complete wasting (loss) of muscularois propria tissue that was once present. The atrophy may involve a marked vacuolar degeneration of myocytes, loss of muscle fibers and some cases a highly characteristic honeycomb fibrosis.
HP_0025149.synonyms: autonomic visceral myopathy | degenerative enteric myopathy

HP_0025150.label: hypoganglionosis
HP_0025150.UMLS synonyms: Acquired hypoganglionosis of large intestine | Congenital hypoganglionosis of large intestine | Hypoganglionosis proximal to aganglionic segment | Hypoganglionosis proximal to aganglionic segment of colon

HP_0025151.label: ganglioneuromatosis
HP_0025151.definition: Hyperplastic submucosal and myenteric plexus containing an increased number of ganglion cells, glial cells and nerve fibers.
HP_0025151.UMLS synonyms: Ganglioneuromatosis | Ganglioneuromatosis of the Alimentary Tract | benign ganglioneuromatosis of small intestine | benign ganglioneuromatosis of large intestine | large intestine biopsy benign ganglioneuromatosis | biopsy small intestine benign neoplasm ganglioneuromatosis

HP_0025152.label: poor visual behavior for age
HP_0025152.definition: Lack of visual responsiveness or decrease in visual capabilities suggesting a lack of visual responsiveness or decrease in visual capabilities in an infant or young child in which visual behavior fails to meet normal developmental milestones.
HP_0025152.synonyms: abnormal visual behavior for age | abnormal visual behaviour for age | poor visual behaviour for age

HP_0025153.label: transient
HP_0025153.definition: Short-lived and not permanent. This term applies to a phenotypic abnormality that is temporary and of short duration.
