HP_0025154.label: portosystemic collateral veins
HP_0025154.definition: Presence of biliary veins that serve as a collateral channel to the systemic circulation
HP_0025154.synonyms: collateral biliary circulation | collateral biliary veins

HP_0025155.label: abnormality of hepatobiliary system physiology
HP_0025155.definition: A functional anomaly of the hepatobiliary system

HP_0025156.label: dependency on intravenous nutrition
HP_0025156.definition: Inability to be weaned from intravenous (parenteral) nutrition, as judged by the hydration status (urine output, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, urine sodium concentration), ability to maintain weight, stool output, and serum electrolyte status.

HP_0025157.label: increased urinary sedoheptulose
HP_0025157.definition: An increased concentration of sedoheptulose in the urine. Sedoheptulose is a monosaccharide with seven carbon atoms and a ketone functional group.

HP_0025158.label: hyperautofluorescent retinal lesion
HP_0025158.definition: Increased amount of autofluorescence in the retina as ascertained by fundus autofluorescence imaging.

HP_0025159.label: hypoautofluorescent retinal lesion
HP_0025159.definition: Decreased amount of autofluorescence in the retina as ascertained by fundus autofluorescence imaging.

HP_0025160.label: abnormal temper tantrums
HP_0025160.definition: Temper tantrums are brief episodes of extreme, unpleasant, and sometimes aggressive behaviors in response to frustration or anger, which are a normal part of development in toddlers. Temper tantrums that occur more frequently in a given time and/or are more severe in symptomatology and/or longer in duration and/or inappropriate for the given age compared to a temper tantrum that naturally occurs as a part of the developmental process are classified as abnormal temper tantrums.

HP_0025161.label: frequent temper tantrums
HP_0025161.definition: Temper tantrums that occur more frequently compared to the temper tantrums that are a part of the normal developmental process.

HP_0025162.label: severe temper tantrums
HP_0025162.definition: Temper tantrums, which occur with more severe symptomatology compared to a temper tantrum that occurs as a part of normal developmental process.

HP_0025163.label: abnormal optic chiasm morphology
HP_0025163.definition: A structural abnormality of the optic chiasm.The optic chiasm, located below the hypothalamus, is a partial crossing of the optic nerves.

HP_0025164.label: increased number of elastic fibers in the dermis
HP_0025164.definition: An elevated number of elastic fibers, that is of bundles of proteins and glycoproteins in the extracellular matrix in the reticular dermis. Elastic fibers can stretch and recoil back to their original length. This feature can be appreciated on histology with hematoxylin and eosin or other staining methods.
HP_0025164.synonyms: increased number of elastic fibres in the dermis

HP_0025165.label: clumping of elastic fibers in the dermis
HP_0025165.definition: Formation of clumps or aggregates that make up small protuberances from elastic fibers within the dermis (especially the reticular dermis).
HP_0025165.synonyms: clumping of elastic fibres in the dermis

HP_0025166.label: thickened elastic fibers in the dermis
HP_0025166.definition: An increase of the diameter of elastic fibers in the dermis.
HP_0025166.synonyms: thickened elastic fibres in the dermis

HP_0025167.label: fragmented elastic fibers in the dermis
HP_0025167.definition: Elastic fibers in the dermis exhibit an increased number of breaks associated with disorganization of the structure of the elastic fibers.
HP_0025167.synonyms: fragmented elastic fibres in the dermis

HP_0025168.label: left ventricular diastolic dysfunction
HP_0025168.definition: Abnormal function of the left ventricule during left ventricular relaxation and filling.

HP_0025169.label: left ventricular systolic dysfunction
HP_0025169.definition: Abnormality of left ventricular contraction, often defined operationally as an ejection fraction of less than 40 percent.

HP_0025170.label: neuronal / glioneuronal neoplasm of the central nervous system
HP_0025170.definition: A central nervous system neoplasm with neuronal and, less consistently, glial differentiation.
HP_0025170.synonyms: glioneuronal tumor | glioneuronal tumour | neuronal and mixed neuronal - glial tumor | neuronal and mixed neuronal - glial tumour | neuronal / glioneuronal neoplasm of the cns

HP_0025171.label: rosette - forming glioneuronal tumor
HP_0025171.definition: A tumor of the central nervous system that has components of both neurocytic and glial areas, whereby usually the glial component of the tumor predominates. Rossette-forming glioneuronal tumors (RGNT) have biphasic cytoarchitecture with two elements; neurocytic rosettes resembling Homer-Wright rosettes, and astrocytic component resembling a pilocytic astrocytoma. RGNTs are low-grade tumors that lack histopathological signs of malignancy.
HP_0025171.synonyms: rosette - forming glioneuronal neoplasm | rosette - forming glioneuronal tumor of the fourth ventricle | rosette - forming glioneuronal tumour | rosette - forming glioneuronal tumour of the fourth ventricle

HP_0025172.label: smooth septal thickening on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025172.definition: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with a smooth appearance of the interlobular septa.

HP_0025173.label: nodular septal thickening on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025173.definition: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with a nodular or beaded appearance of the interlobular septa.

HP_0025174.label: irregular septal thickening on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025174.definition: Thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a high-resolution computed tomography scan with an irregular appearance of the interlobular septa. THis feature is often associated with distortion of lung architecture.

HP_0025175.label: honeycomb lung
HP_0025175.definition: Honeycombing represents destroyed and fibrotic lung tissue containing numerous cystic airspaces with thick fibrous walls, representing the late stage of various lung diseases, with complete loss of acinar architecture. The cysts range in size from a few millimeters to several centimeters in diameter, have variable wall thickness, and are lined by metaplastic bronchiolar epithelium. On chest radiographs, honeycombing appears as closely approximated ring shadows, typically 3-10 mm in diameter with walls 1-3 mm in thickness, that resemble a honeycomb; the finding implies end-stage lung disease. On CT scans, the appearance is of clustered cystic air spaces, typically of comparable diameters on the order of 3-10 mm but occasionally as large as 2.5 cm. Honeycombing is usually subpleural and is characterized by well-defined walls. It is a CT feature of established pulmonary fibrosis. Because honeycombing is often considered specific for pulmonary fibrosis and is an important criterion in the diagnosis of usual interstitial pneumonia, the term should be used with care, as it may directly impact patient care.
HP_0025175.UMLS synonyms: Honeycomb lung | Congenital honeycomb lung | HONEYCOMB LUNG END STAGE | Honeycomb lung Pneumonia, usually interstitial | x-ray of chest: interstitial infiltrate with honeycomb pattern

HP_0025176.label: intralobular interstitial thickening
HP_0025176.definition: A fine reticular pattern on high-resolution computed tomography, with the visible lines separated by a few millimeters. Regions of the lung with intralobular interstitial thickening characteristically show a fine lacelike or netlike appearance.

HP_0025177.label: peribronchovascular interstitial thickening
HP_0025177.definition: Thickening of the peribronchovascular interstitium, a connective tissue sheath that surrounds the central bronchi and pulmonary arteries. The peribronchovascular interstitium extends from the level of the pulmonary hila into the peripheral lung. This feature may be ascertained on high-resolution computer tomography.

HP_0025178.label: subpleural interstitial thickening
HP_0025178.definition: Increase in thickness of the subpleural interstitium.

HP_0025179.label: ground - glass opacification
HP_0025179.definition: On chest radiographs, ground-glass opacity appears as an area of hazy increased lung opacity, usually extensive, within which margins of pulmonary vessels may be indistinct. On CT scans, it appears as hazy increased opacity of lung, with preservation of bronchial and vascular margins. It is caused by partial filling of airspaces, interstitial thickening (due to fluid, cells, and/or fibrosis), partial collapse of alveoli, increased capillary blood volume, or a combination of these, the common factor being the partial displacement of air. Ground-glass opacity is less opaque than consolidation, in which bronchovascular margins are obscured.
HP_0025179.synonyms: ground glass opacities | ground - glass opacification on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025179.UMLS synonyms: Ground glass opacity | Radiography shows hazy, ground-glass interstitial opacifications | Radiograph shows granular, hazy, ground-glass interstitial opacifications | Granular, hazy, ground-glass interstitial opacifications seen on radiograph | CT scan shows patchy, ground-glass opacifications with superimposed interlobular septal and intralobular thickening leading to 'crazy paving' pattern

HP_0025180.label: centrilobular ground - glass opacification on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025180.definition: A hazy area of increased attenuation in centrilobular areas of the lung with preserved bronchial and vascular markings seen on a computer tomography scan. Centrilobular refers to a location that is central within secondary pulmonary lobules.
HP_0025180.synonyms: centrilobular groundglass opacification | centrilobular groundglass opacity

HP_0025181.label: abdominal aseptic abscess
HP_0025181.definition: An abscess-like lesion located within the abdomen. The lesions are localized in the spleen, liver, abdominal lymph nodes. The lesions represent visceral sterile collections of mature neutrophils that do not respond to antibiotics but regress quickly when treated with corticosteroids, but relapses occur frequently.

HP_0025182.label: localized area of pendulous skin
HP_0025182.definition: A confined region of lax skin that hangs below the level of the surrounding skin. Histopatholigically, there is a loss of elastic fibers in the dermis of the affected region.

HP_0025186.label: marcus gunn jaw winking synkinesis
HP_0025186.definition: Unilateral ptosis with associated upper eyelid contraction and contraction of either the external or the internal pterygoid muscle. It is thought to occur because of congenital miswiring of a branch of the fifth cranial nerve into the branch of the third cranial nerve supplying the levator muscle. In Marcus Gunn jaw winking synkinesis, elevation and even retraction of the affected eyelid is triggered by chewing, suction, lateral mandible movement, smiling, sternocleidomastoid contraction, protruding tongue, Valsalva manoeuvre and even by breathing.
HP_0025186.synonyms: marcus gunn jaw - winking syndrome | pterygoid - levator synkinesis | trigemino - oculomotor synkinesis

HP_0025188.label: retinal vasculitis
HP_0025188.definition: Inflammation of retinal blood vessels as manifested by perivascular sheathing or cuffing, vascular leakage and/or occlusion.

HP_0025190.label: bilateral tonic - clonic seizure with generalized onset
HP_0025190.definition: A bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with generalized onset is a type of bilateral tonic-clonic seizure characterised by generalized onset; these seizures rapidly engage networks in both hemispheres at the start of the seizure.

HP_0025192.label: subtentorial periventricular white matter hyperdensity
HP_0025192.definition: Areas of brighter than expected signal on magnetic resonance imaging emanating from the cerebral white matter that surrounds the fourth cerebral ventricle (which is located beneath the tentorium of the cerebellum).

HP_0025193.label: posterolateral diaphragmatic hernia
HP_0025193.definition: A posterolateral defect in the diaphragm, commonly referred to as a Bochdalek hernia, which is often accompanied by herniation of the stomach, intestines, liver, and/or spleen into the chest cavity.
HP_0025193.UMLS synonyms: Congenital hernia of foramen of Bochdalek

HP_0025194.label: morgagni diaphragmatic hernia
HP_0025194.definition: An anterior retrosternal or parasternal hernia that can result in the herniation of liver or intestines into the chest cavity.
HP_0025194.UMLS synonyms: Congenital hernia of foramen of Morgagni

HP_0025195.label: central diaphragmatic hernia
HP_0025195.definition: A congenital diaphragm defect involving the central tendinous (e.g., amuscular) portion of the diaphragm, whereby the entire rim of diaphragmatic musculature is present.

HP_0025196.label: increased total iron binding capacity
HP_0025196.definition: An elevation in the total-iron binding capacity, which measures how much serum iron is bound if an excess of radioactive iron is added. A high TIBC corresponds to a high transferrin concentration. The latent (or free) iron binding capacity is the difference between the TIBC and the measured serum iron, corresponding to the transferrin not bound to iron, i.e., free iron binding capacity.

HP_0025197.label: inclusion body fibromatosis
HP_0025197.definition: A benign tumor made up of mostly myofibroblasts that appears almost exclusively on the digits of the hands and feet, rarely involving the thumb or big toe. The lesion displays a proliferation of bland intradermal spindle cells arranged in whorls, fascicles, or a storiform pattern in a collagenous background of varying degrees. Also usually present are perpendicular tumor cell fascicles that extend to the epidermis. The small intracytoplasmic inclusions are said to appear similar to red blood cells. The inclusion bodies have been shown to be made up of densely packed vimentin and actin filaments. The tumor often causes a dome-shaped elevation of the overlying structures, forming a protuberant or polypoid nodule. The overlying epidermis can display a host of changes, including acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, rete ridge flattening, entrapment of adnexal structures, and, rarely, ulceration.
HP_0025197.synonyms: digital fibrous tumor of reye | digital fibrous tumour of reye | infantile digital fibroma | infantile digital fibromatosis

HP_0025198.label: inflammatory cap polyp
HP_0025198.definition: A non-malignant sessile or pedunculated polyp in the colon and rectum that displays a cap of inflammatory granulation tissue with fibrinopurulent exudate that covers the polyp.

HP_0025200.label: muscle fiber actin filament accumulation
HP_0025200.definition: Accumulation in muscle cells of filaments composed of actin.

HP_0025201.label: abnormal circulating apolipoprotein concentration
HP_0025201.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration in blood of an apolipoprotein, i.e., of a protein that binds lipids to form lipoprotein and is thereby responsible for the transport of lipids in the blood and lymph circulation.

HP_0025202.label: elevated circulating apolipoprotein a - iv concentration
HP_0025202.definition: An increased concentration in blood of apolipoprotein A-IV, a major component of HDL and chylomicrons that has a role in VLDL secretion and catabolism and is required for efficient activation of lipoprotein lipase by ApoC-II.

HP_0025203.label: caput medusae
HP_0025203.definition: Distended and engorged umbilical veins which are seen radiating from the umbilicus across the abdomen to join systemic veins.

HP_0025247.label: dermoid cyst
HP_0025247.definition: A congenital subcutaneous cyst that arises from entrapment of skin along the lines of embryonic fusion. HP_0025250.definition: A comedo in which the top of the pore is not stretched open and thus does not expose the clogged portion (which would appear black), hence the name whitehead.

HP_0025310.label: oval pupil

HP_0025321.definition: An anomalous build up of copper (Cu) in the liver.

HP_0025327.definition: Reduced dimension of the solid part of the kidney (parenchyma, the renal cortex and medulla) as measured from the collecting system (renal calyces and pelvis) to the border of the kidney. HP_0025329.label: anti - glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody positivity
HP_0025329.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against glutamic acid decarboxylase.

HP_0025330.label: downgaze palsy
HP_0025330.definition: A limitation of the ability to direct one's gaze below the horizontal meridian.

HP_0025331.label: upgaze palsy
HP_0025331.definition: A limitation of the ability to direct one's gaze above the horizontal meridian.

HP_0025332.label: abnormality of foot cortical bone
HP_0025332.definition: An anomaly of the outer shell (cortex) of a foot bone.
HP_0025332.synonyms: abnormality of the cortex of foot bones

HP_0025333.label: cortical thinning of foot bones
HP_0025333.definition: A reduction in the thickness of the outer shell (cortex) of foot bones.

HP_0025334.label: triggered by emotion
HP_0025334.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by a strong spontaneously arising mental state, reaction or feeling (emotion).
HP_0025334.UMLS synonyms: Emotional sweating affecting palms and soles | Cataplexy often triggered by strong emotions | Expresses emotions triggered by stressful situations | Onset may be triggered by emotional stress, fever, exercise, exposure to heat

HP_0025335.label: delayed ability to stand
HP_0025335.definition: A failure to achieve the ability to stand up at an appropriate developmental stage. Most children begin to walk alone at 11 to 15 months of age. On average, children can stand while holding on at the age of 9 to 10 months, can pull up to stand and walk with one hand being held at 12 months, and can stand alone and walk well at 18 months.

HP_0025336.label: delayed ability to sit
HP_0025336.definition: A failure to achieve the ability to sit at an appropriate developmental stage. Most children sit with support at 6 months of age and sit steadily without support at 9 months of age.

HP_0025337.label: red eye
HP_0025337.definition: A reddish appearance over the white part (sclera) of the eye ranging from a few enlarged blood vessels appearing as wiggly lines over the sclera to a bright red color completely covering to sclera.

HP_0025338.label: circumlimbal hyperemia
HP_0025338.definition: A ring of redness at the limbus of the eye, the border between the cornea and the sclera.

HP_0025339.label: superficial episcleral hyperemia
HP_0025339.definition: Prominence of blood vessels of the superficial episcleral tissues.

HP_0025340.label: deep episcleral hyperemia
HP_0025340.definition: Prominence of blood vessels of the deep episcleral tissues.

HP_0025341.label: corneal keratic precipitates
HP_0025341.definition: An inflammatory cellular deposit deposited on the corneal endothelium and visible as spots on the cornea.

HP_0025342.label: central retinal artery occlusion
HP_0025342.definition: Blockage of the main artery in the retina. The typical presentation is one of profound monocular visual loss.

HP_0025343.label: lupus anticoagulant
HP_0025343.definition: Presence of lupus anticoagulant (LA) autoantibodies. LA represent a heterogeneous group of autoantibodies, IgG, IgM, or a mixture of both classes, that interfere with standard phospholipid-based coagulant tests (this is only an in vitro phenomenon, LA do not cause reduction of coagulation in vivo). The antibodies are directed against plasma proteins which also bind to phospholipid surfaces.

HP_0025344.label: interlobular bile duct destruction
HP_0025344.definition: Damage to and obliteration of intrahepatic bile ducts (bile ducts that transport bile between the Canals of Hering and the interlobar bile ducts).

HP_0025345.label: abnormality of circulating beta - 2 - microglobulin level
HP_0025345.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood.
HP_0025345.synonyms: abnormality of circulating b2m level | abnormality of circulating beta2 microglobulin level | abnormality of circulating beta2 - m level | abnormality of circulating beta2m level

HP_0025346.label: increased circulating beta - 2 - microglobulin level
HP_0025346.definition: Elevated concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood.

HP_0025347.label: decreased circulating beta - 2 - microglobulin level
HP_0025347.definition: Reduced concentration of beta-2-microglobulin in the blood.

HP_0025348.label: abnormal corneal limbus morphology
HP_0025348.definition: An anomaly of the margin of the cornea overlapped by the sclera.

HP_0025349.label: limbal edema
HP_0025349.definition: Swelling of the margin of the cornea overlapped by the sclera.

HP_0025350.label: giant conjunctival papillae
HP_0025350.definition: Conjunctival papillae with a diameter greater than 1 millimeter. They characteristically have flattened tops which sometimes demonstrate staining with fluorescein.

HP_0025351.label: recurrent interdigital mycosis
HP_0025351.definition: A history of repeated fungal infections located between the fingers or toes, usually manifested by scaling, maceration, and itching. The toes are more commonly affected than the fingers.

HP_0025352.label: typically de novo
HP_0025352.definition: Description of conditions that are exclusively or predominantly observed to display de novo variants. In some cases, this may be due to the limited reproductive fitness of affected individuals.
HP_0025352.synonyms: autosomal dominant germline de novo mutation

HP_0025353.label: anti - multiple nuclear dots antibody positivity
HP_0025353.definition: A type of antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity revealed by indirect immunofluorescence (IFL). The multiple nuclear dots (MND) pattern is immunomorphologically characterized by the staining of 3-20 dots of variable size distributed all over the cell nucleus, but sparing the nucleoli, and, in contrast to the anticentromere pattern, MND reactivity does not stain the chromosomes in mitotic cells.

HP_0025354.label: abnormal cellular phenotype
HP_0025354.definition: An anomaly of cellular morphology or physiology.

HP_0025355.label: retinal arterial macroaneurysms
HP_0025355.definition: Acquired focal dilatations of branches of the retinal artery, usually second-order retinal arterioles, that range in size from 100 to 200 micrometers in diameter. Macroaneurysms are generally located at the termporal retina and may be hemorrhagic or exudative.
HP_0025355.UMLS synonyms: Retinal Arterial Macroaneurysm | Retinal arterial macroaneurysms, multiple, developing at sites of beading | Ruptured Retinal Arterial Macroaneurysm | RETINAL ARTERIAL MACROANEURYSM WITH SUPRAVALVULAR PULMONIC STENOSIS | RETINAL ARTERIAL MACROANEURYSM WITH SUPRAVASCULAR PULMONIC STENOSIS

HP_0025357.label: erratic myoclonus
HP_0025357.definition: A type of myoclonus in which the myoclonias shift from body region to another in a random and asynchronous fashion. Erratic myoclonus can affect the face or limbs, are brief, single or repetitive, very frequent and nearly continuous.

HP_0025358.label: uveal ectropion
HP_0025358.definition: Presence of iris pigment epithelium on the anterior surface of the iris.

HP_0025359.label: polygonal renal calices
HP_0025359.definition: An abnormal polygonal shape of the calices of the kidney (which normally have a rounded or cup-shaped appearance).

HP_0025360.label: polycalycosis
HP_0025360.definition: Increased number of calices of the kidney.

HP_0025361.label: abnormal medullary pyramid morphology
HP_0025361.definition: A structural anomaly of the pyramid of the adult kidney, cone-shaped structures with a broad base adjacent to the renal cortex and the narrow apex that is termed papilla.

HP_0025362.label: renal medullary pyramid hypoplasia
HP_0025362.definition: Undergrowth of the pyramid of the adult kidney, cone-shaped structures with a broad base adjacent to the renal cortex and the narrow apex that is termed papilla.

HP_0025363.label: glomerular endocapillary hypercellularity
HP_0025363.definition: Hypercellularity due to increased number of cells within glomerular capillary lumina, causing narrowing of the lumina.

HP_0025364.label: glomerular extracapillary hypercellularity
HP_0025364.definition: Hypercellularity (increased number of cells) in the renal glomerulus but external to the glomerular capillaries, i.e., in the Bowman space or more than one layer of parietal or visceral epithelial cells.

HP_0025367.label: trichoepithelioma
HP_0025367.definition: A benign hair follicle tumor whose tumor cells form rudimentary hair follicles but not actual hair shafts. A trichoepithelioma is usually less than one centimeter, firm, round, and shihy with yellow, pink, brown, or bluish color. They may occur multiply, usually on the face, and may gradually increase in number with age.

HP_0025368.label: abnormal growth plate morphology
HP_0025368.definition: A structural anomaly of the growth plates (epiphyseal plates), areas of cartilage located near the ends of long bones that are located between the metaphysis (widened part of the shaft of the bone) and the epiphysis (end of the bone) and in which growth occurs in the developing bone. After conclusion of bone growth, the growth plates ossify (harden into solid bone).

HP_0025369.label: thick growth plates
HP_0025369.definition: Increased thickness (dimension along the axis of the bone) of the growth plate.
HP_0025369.UMLS synonyms: Thick growth plates with dense islets of calcified cartilage

HP_0025370.label: abnormal ossification of the sacrum
HP_0025370.definition: Abnormal bone tissue formation (ossification) affecting the sacrum.

HP_0025371.label: delayed ossification of the sacrum
HP_0025371.definition: Formation of the sacrum bone tissue occurs later than age-adjusted norms.

HP_0025372.label: loud snoring
HP_0025372.definition: Snoring at a particularly loud or abnormally high volume.
HP_0025372.synonyms: has loud snoring | have loud snoring | heavy snoring | snores loudly
HP_0025372.UMLS synonyms: Loud snoring | Have Loud Snoring question

HP_0025373.label: interictal eeg abnormality
HP_0025373.definition: Interictal refers to a period of time between epileptic seizures. Electroencephalographic (EEG) patterns are important in the differential diagnosis of epilepsy, and the EEG is almost always abnormal during a seizure. Some persons with seizures may show EEG abnormalities between seizures, while others do not. In some cases, multiple interictal EEGs must be recorded before an abnormality is observed. In most cases the electrographic pattern of seizure onset is completely different from the activity recorded during interictal discharge.
HP_0025373.UMLS synonyms: Abnormal interictal EEG | Interictal abnormalities seen on EEG | Interictal EEG may be normal or abnormal

HP_0025374.label: duplicated odontoid process
HP_0025374.definition: The presence of two distinct odontoid processes. The odontoid process, also known as the dens of the axis, is a protuberance of the C2 vertebral body around which the first vertebra rotates.

HP_0025375.label: orthotopic os odontoideum
HP_0025375.definition: Os odontoideum is classified into two anatomic types (orthotopic and dystopic). Os odontoideum is defined as an ossicle that consists of smooth and separate caudal portions of the odontoid process.With dystopic os odontoideum, the ossicle is located near the basion or is fused with the clivus.

HP_0025376.label: hyperglutaminuria
HP_0025376.definition: An increased concentration of glutamine in the urine.

HP_0025377.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exertion or physical exercise.

HP_0025383.label: dorsocervical fat pad

HP_0025386.label: bitemporal hollowing
HP_0025386.definition: Depression of profile in both temporal regions.

HP_0025389.definition: High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) can distinguish findings that characterize characterise interstitial lung diseases in a way not possible with other modalities.

HP_0025390.label: reticular pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025390.definition: On pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography, reticular pattern is characterised by innumerable interlacing shadows suggesting a mesh.

HP_0025391.label: crazy paving pattern
HP_0025391.definition: The so-called crazy paving pattern appears as thickened interlobular septa and intralobular lines superimposed on a background of ground-glass opacity, resembling irregularly shaped paving stones. The crazy-paving pattern is often sharply demarcated from more normal lung and may have a geographic outline. It was originally reported in patients with alveolar proteinosis and is also encountered in other diffuse lung diseases that affect both the interstitial and airspace compartments, such as lipoid pneumonia.
HP_0025391.synonyms: crazy paving pattern on pulmonary hrct | crazy - paving pattern
HP_0025391.UMLS synonyms: Crazy paving pattern | Crazy-paving pattern in chest CT | CT scan shows patchy, ground-glass opacifications with superimposed interlobular septal and intralobular thickening leading to 'crazy paving' pattern

HP_0025392.label: nodular pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025392.definition: A nodular pattern is characterised on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography by the presence of numerous rounded opacities that range from 2 mm to 1 cm in diameter, with micronodules defined as smaller than 3 mm in diameter.

HP_0025393.label: reticulonodular pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025393.definition: Co-occurrence of reticular and micronodular patterns on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.

HP_0025394.label: cystic pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025394.definition: On pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography, the cystic pattern is composed by well-defined, round and circumscribed air-containing parenchymal spaces with a well-defined wall and interface with normal lung. The wall of the cysts may be uniform or varied in thickness, but usually is thin (less than 2 mm) and occurs without associated emphysema.

HP_0025395.label: combined cystic and ground - glass pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025395.definition: Co-occurrence of the cystic pattern and the ground-glass pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography,

HP_0025396.label: decreased attenuation pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025396.definition: Areas of low density corresponding to parenchymal destruction and reduced perfusion, and attenuation of the pulmonary vasculature, as visualized on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.
HP_0025396.synonyms: black lung pattern on pulmonary hrct

HP_0025397.label: mosaic attenuation pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025397.definition: A patchwork of intermingled areas of increased and decreased attenuation visualized on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography.

HP_0025398.label: nodular - perilymphatic pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025398.definition: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that has a perilymphatic distribution.

HP_0025399.label: nodular - centrilobular with tree - in - bud pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025399.definition: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that displays a tree-in-bud pattern, representing centrilobular branching structures that resemble a budding tree.

HP_0025400.label: nodular - random pattern on pulmonary hrct
HP_0025400.definition: A nodular pattern on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography that has an apparently random pattern.

HP_0025401.label: staring gaze
HP_0025401.definition: An abnormality in which the eyes are held permanently wide open.

HP_0025402.label: square - wave jerks
HP_0025402.definition: Square wave jerks are saccadic eye movements which, when recorded with open eyes are considered to be a pathological sign, caused by fixation instability, and pointing to a central neurological lesion.

HP_0025418.label: renal cortical necrosis
HP_0025418.definition: Patchy or diffuse ischemic destruction of all the elements of renal cortex resulting from significantly diminished renal arterial perfusion. Coagulative necrosis may be present, involving all tubular segments and glomeruli. Nuclei may be pale and pyknotic, or may no longer be apparent. Thrombi may be present in vessels at the edge of the infarct.

HP_0025419.label: pulmonary pneumatocele
HP_0025419.definition: A pneumatocele is a thin walled, gas-filled space in the lung. It is most frequently caused by acute pneumonia, trauma, or aspiration of hydrocarbon fluid and is usually transient. The mechanism is believed to be a combination of parenchymal necrosis and check-valve airway obstruction. A pneumatocele appears as an approximately round, thin-walled airspace in the lung.

HP_0025420.label: diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
HP_0025420.definition: A type of of pulmonary hemorrhage that originates from the pulmonary microcirculation, including the alveolar capillaries, arterioles, and venules. It presents with hemoptysis, anemia, diffuse lung infiltration, and acute respiratory failure. The diagnosis is confirmed by the observation of the accumulation of red blood cells, fibrin, or hemosiderin-laden macrophage in the alveolar space on pathologic biopsy. Hemosiderin, a product of hemoglobin degradation, appears at least 48-72 hours after bleeding and is helpful in distinguishing diffuse alveolar hemorrhage from surgical trauma. Mild interstitial thickening, organizing pneumonia, or diffuse alveolar damage can also be seen.

HP_0025421.label: pneumomediastinum

HP_0025451.label: testicular adrenal rest tumor
HP_0025451.definition: Testicular adrenal rest tumor (TART) is a abenign tumor of the testis. TART generally occurs multiply and bilaterally within the rete testis. Histologically, TART resemble adrenocortical tissue, which led to the name. The tumous are not encapsulated and consist of sheets or confluent cords of large polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm.

HP_0025452.label: pyoderma gangrenosum
HP_0025452.definition: A deep skin ulcer with a well defined border, which is usually violet or blue. The ulcer edge is often undermined (worn and damaged) and the surrounding skin is erythematous and indurated. The ulcer often starts as a small papule or collection of papules, which break down to form small ulcers with a so called cat's paw appearance. These coalesce and the central area then undergoes necrosis to form a single ulcer.

HP_0025453.label: delayed adrenarche
HP_0025453.definition: Occurence of adrenarche at a later than normal age. Adrenarche normally occurs between six and eight years of age with increased adrenal androgen secretion; its exact biologic role is not well understood. It is accompanied by changes in pilosebaceous units, a transient growth spurt and the appearance of axillary and pubic hair in some children, but no sexual development.

HP_0025464.definition: An accumulation of free radical groups in the body inadequately neutralized by antioxidants, which creates a potentially unstable and damaging cellular environment linked to tissue damage.

HP_0025465.label: abnormal circulating beta globulin level
HP_0025465.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of beta globulin. The beta globulins are a group of globular (globe-shaped) proteins in blood.

HP_0025466.label: beta 2 - microglobulinuria
HP_0025466.definition: Increased level of beta 2-microglobulins in the urine.

HP_0025470.label: telogen effluvium

HP_0025471.label: congenital panfollicular nevus
HP_0025471.definition: A hamartomatous proliferation containing malformed hair follicles in various stages of development. Panfolliculomas are well-circumscribed lesions demonstrating all stages of follicular differentiation.

HP_0025472.label: recurrent plantar mycosis
HP_0025472.definition: A history of repeated fungal infections located on the sole of the foot, usually manifested by scaling, maceration, and itching.

HP_0025473.label: hyperpigmented papule
HP_0025473.definition: A papule (circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid, varying in size from a pinhead to less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point) that exhibits increased pigmentation (is darker) compared to the surrounding skin.
HP_0025473.UMLS synonyms: Mulitple papules (1-2 mm skin colored and hyperpigmented)

HP_0025474.label: erythematous plaque
HP_0025474.definition: A plaque (a solid, raised, plateau-like (flat-topped) lesion greater than 1 cm in diameter) with a red or reddish color often associated with inflammation or irritation.
HP_0025474.UMLS synonyms: Erythematous plaque | Erythematous pinta plaque | erythematous skin plaque | Papulosquamous erythematous plaques | Fixed erythematous keratotic plaques | Erythematous annular scaly plaques | Annular erythematous edematous plaques | Erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on extremities | Erythematous indurated plaques on the shins | Erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on periorificial areas | Confluent erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on torso | Plaques, erythematous, covered with fine powdery scales | Erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on dorsal surface of extremities | Erythematous patches/plaques (primarily on the trunk, also face and limbs)

HP_0025475.label: erythematous macule
HP_0025475.definition: A macule (flat, distinct, discolored area of skin less than 1 cm wide that does not involve any change in the thickness or texture of the skin) with a red or reddish color often associated with inflammation or irritation.

HP_0025476.label: testicular lipomatosis
HP_0025476.definition: Multiple foci of adipocytes within the testicular interstitium, usually presenting as multiple bilateral ill-defined hyperechoic intratesticular lesions of different sizes but generally with maximum diameter of 4 mm.

HP_0025477.label: periarticular calcification
HP_0025477.definition: Calcified deposits in soft tissue structures outside a joint.
HP_0025477.UMLS synonyms: Periarticular calcification | Hands, vascular and periarticular calcification of | Fingers, periarticular joint capsule calcification of | Periarticular calcifications present | Periarticular joint capsule calcifications | Vascular and periarticular calcifications (shoulders, elbows, hips, and knees)

HP_0025478.label: atrial standstill
HP_0025478.definition: Atrial standstill or silent atrium is a rare condition presenting with the absence of electrical and mechanical activity in the atria. It presents with the absence of P waves, bradycardia, and wide QRS complex in the electrocardiogram.
HP_0025478.UMLS synonyms: Atrial standstill | ATRIAL STANDSTILL 2 | ATRIAL STANDSTILL 1 | CARDIOMYOPATHY, FAMILIAL, WITH CONDUCTION DISTURBANCE | ATRIAL STANDSTILL 1, DIGENIC

HP_0025479.label: self - neglect
HP_0025479.definition: Neglecting one's own needs and well-being.
HP_0025479.UMLS synonyms: Self-Neglect | At increased risk for self neglect | Moderate risk of self neglect | History of deliberate self neglect | High risk of self neglect | At low risk for self-neglect | Insufficient intake of food and water with self neglect | insufficient intake of food and water due to self neglect

HP_0025480.label: lipomyelomeningocele
HP_0025480.definition: A type of spinal dysraphism presenting as a subcutaneous fatty mass, that is, a spinal defect associated with lipomatous tissue, and covered by skin. The most usual location for lipomyelomeningocele is at the gluteal cleft.
HP_0025480.UMLS synonyms: Lipomyelomeningocele | Familial lipomyelomeningocele | Perineal hemangioma, external genitalia malformation, lipomyelomeningocele, vesicorenal abnormality, imperforate anus syndrome

HP_0025481.label: cervical hemivertebrae
HP_0025481.definition: Absence of one half of the vertebral body in the cervical spine.
HP_0025481.UMLS synonyms: Cervical hemivertebra | Hemivertebrae in cervical and thoracic spine | Cervical hemivertebra- balanced | Cervical hemivertebra - unbalanced

HP_0025482.label: positive perchlorate discharge test
HP_0025482.definition: An abnormal result of the perchlorate discharge test. In this test, first radioactive iodine is administered, sufficient time is allowed to pass so that the radioactive iodine is captured by the thyroid,and then, perchlorate is administered orally. The perchlorate displaces non-organified iodide from the thyroid. The perchlorate discharge test is considered positive (abnormal) if there is an abnormally rapid loss of radioactive iodine from the thyroid.

HP_0025483.label: abnormal circulating thyroglobulin concentration
HP_0025483.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of thyroglobulin, a protein produced in the thyroid gland that acts as a precursor to thyrroid hormones.

HP_0025484.label: increased circulating thyroglobulin concentration
HP_0025484.definition: An abnormal elevation of the concentration of thyroglobulin, a protein produced in the thyroid gland that acts as a precursor to thyrroid hormones.

HP_0025485.label: vaginal adenosis
HP_0025485.definition: Vaginal adenosis is defined by the presence of metaplastic cervical or endometrial epithelium within the vaginal wall, thought to be derived from persistent Müllerian (synonymous with paramesonephric) epithelium islets in postembryonic life.

HP_0025486.label: fused labia majora
HP_0025486.definition: The outer labia are sealed together.

HP_0025487.label: abnormal bladder morphology
HP_0025487.definition: Any structural anomaly of the bladder.

HP_0025488.label: detrusor sphincter dyssynergia
HP_0025488.definition: A urodynamic anomaly characterized by bladder outlet obstruction from detrusor muscle contraction with concomitant involuntary urethral sphincter activation.
HP_0025488.UMLS synonyms: Detrusor and sphincter dyssynergia | Detrusor external sphincter dyssynergia

HP_0025489.label: bladder duplication
HP_0025489.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of two bladders.
HP_0025489.UMLS synonyms: Ureteroneocystostomy; anastomosis of duplicated ureter to bladder | Anastomosis of duplicated ureter to bladder | diagnostic cystoscopy of bladder showed ureteral orifice was duplicated | diagnostic cystoscopy of bladder showed left ureteral orifice was duplicated | diagnostic cystoscopy of bladder showed right ureteral orifice was duplicated | diagnostic cystoscopy of bladder showed both ureteral orifices were duplicated

HP_0025490.label: myocardial bridging
HP_0025490.definition: A congenital variant of a coronary artery in which a portion of an epicardial coronary artery (most frequently the middle segment of the left anterior descending artery) takes an intramuscular course.
HP_0025490.UMLS synonyms: Myocardial bridging | Coronary myocardial bridging | Myocardial bridge of coronary artery

HP_0025491.label: venous stenosis
HP_0025491.definition: Narrowing of a vein due to intimal hyperplasia and fibrosis.
HP_0025491.UMLS synonyms: Venous stenosis | Intrinsic venous stenosis | In-stent venous stenosis | Repair of pulmonary venous stenosis | Acquired stenosis of pulmonary venous structure | Pulmonary venous hypertension due to congenital stenosis of pulmonary vein | Stenosis of anastomosis between pulmonary venous confluence and left atrium after prior repair of anomalous pulmonary venous connection

HP_0025492.label: microcoria
HP_0025492.definition: A small pupil (typically diameter less than 2 mm) that dilates poorly or not at all in response to topically administered mydriatic drugs.
HP_0025492.UMLS synonyms: Microcoria, congenital | Nonreactive, fixed narrowing of the pupil ('microcoria') | Pierson syndrome

HP_0025493.label: palmoplantar erythema
HP_0025493.definition: Redness of the skin of the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.

HP_0025494.label: coated aorta
HP_0025494.definition: Regular circumferential periaortic fibrosis involving the whole aorta and leading to a coated aorta appearance on computed tomography scans
HP_0025494.UMLS synonyms: Drug coated abdominal aorta endovascular stent-graft | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta using Drug-Coated Balloon, Percutaneous Approach | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta using Drug-Coated Balloon, Open Approach | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta using Drug-Coated Balloon, Percutaneous Endoscopic Approach | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta with Intraluminal Device, using Drug-Coated Balloon, Open Approach | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta with Intraluminal Device, using Drug-Coated Balloon, Percutaneous Approach | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta with Intraluminal Device, using Drug-Coated Balloon, Percutaneous Endoscopic Approach | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta with Drug-eluting Intraluminal Device, using Drug-Coated Balloon, Percutaneous Approach | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta with Drug-eluting Intraluminal Device, using Drug-Coated Balloon, Open Approach | Dilation of Abdominal Aorta with Drug-eluting Intraluminal Device, using Drug-Coated Balloon, Percutaneous Endoscopic Approach

HP_0025495.label: descending aorta hypoplasia
HP_0025495.definition: Significant luminal narrowing of a long segment of the descending aorta.

HP_0025496.label: abnormal coronary artery physiology
HP_0025496.definition: Any anomaly of the function of a coronary artery.

HP_0025497.label: coronary artery spasm
HP_0025497.definition: A brief and sudden narrowing of a coronary artery.
HP_0025497.UMLS synonyms: Coronary Artery Vasospasm | Angina Pectoris, Variant | Cardiac arrhythmia due to coronary artery spasm | CORONARY ARTERY SPASM 1, SUSCEPTIBILITY TO | CORONARY ARTERY SPASM 2, SUSCEPTIBILITY TO | atherosclerosis of coronary artery with angina pectoris with documented spasm | Infusion of drug with evaluation of coronary artery spasm response | atherosclerosis of autologous artery coronary artery bypass graft with angina pectoris with documented spasm | atherosclerosis of coronary artery bypass graft with angina pectoris with documented spasm | atherosclerosis of other coronary artery bypass graft with angina pectoris with documented spasm | Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with angina pectoris with documented spasm | atherosclerosis of native coronary artery of transplanted heart with angina pectoris with documented spasm | atherosclerosis of autologous vein coronary artery bypass graft with angina pectoris with documented spasm | Atherosclerosis of coronary artery bypass graft(s), unspecified, with angina pectoris with documented spasm | Atherosclerosis of nonautologous biological coronary artery bypass graft(s) with angina pectoris with documented spasm | atherosclerosis of bypass graft of coronary artery of transplanted heart with angina pectoris with documented spasm | Spasm induced | Coronary arteries | Cardiac procedures | Spasm induced:Find:Pt:Coronary arteries:Ord

HP_0025498.label: aceruloplasminemia
HP_0025498.definition: Absence of ceruloplasmin in the blood.
HP_0025498.UMLS synonyms: Aceruloplasminemia (finding) | Deficiency of ferroxidase (disorder) | HEMOSIDEROSIS, SYSTEMIC, DUE TO ACERULOPLASMINEMIA | Aceruloplasminemia Gene Mutation Detection Reagents

HP_0025499.label: class i obesity
HP_0025499.definition: Obesity with a body mass index of 30 to 34.9 kg per square meter.

HP_0025500.label: class ii obesity
HP_0025500.definition: Obesity with a body mass index of 35 to 39.9 kg per square meter.

HP_0025501.label: class iii obesity
HP_0025501.definition: Obesity with a body mass index of 40 kg per square meter or higher.
HP_0025501.UMLS synonyms: Class III obesity | Body mass index 40+ - severely obese | Referral for obese class III care management

HP_0025502.label: overweight
HP_0025502.definition: Increased body weight with a body mass index of 25-29.9 kg per square meter.
HP_0025502.UMLS synonyms: Overweight | Childhood Overweight | Percentage overweight | Infant Overweight | Adolescent Overweight | feels overweight | Slightly overweight | Very overweight | Overweight persons | Overweight teenagers | Overweight children | Overweight and obesity | Overweight as adult | Overweight or obese | Overweight in infancy | Risk for overweight | Overweight or obesity | Overweight later in life | Is your child overweight | Body mass index 25-29 - overweight | Peripheral neuropathy due to overweight | Health risks related to overweight | Overweight, obesity and other hyperalimentation (E65-E68) | Neonatal disorder due to maternal overweight | Fetal disorder due to maternal overweight

HP_0025503.label: anomalous coronary artery arising from the opposite sinus
HP_0025503.definition: Origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left sinus of Valsalva or of the left main (LM) or left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsalva.

HP_0025505.label: anomalous origin of the circumflex artery from the right sinus of valsalva
HP_0025505.definition: The circumflex coronary artery originates from the right aortic sinus of Valsalva.

HP_0025506.label: coronary artery sandwich anomaly
HP_0025506.definition: Origin of the right coronary artery (RCA) from the left sinus of Valsalva or of the left main (LM) or left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsalva, with the additional feature that the artery passes between the two great arteries. This carries a risk of the artery being compressed by these two vessels,
HP_0025506.synonyms: anomalous coronary artery with aortic origin and course between the great arteries

HP_0025507.label: yellow papule
HP_0025507.UMLS synonyms: yellow skin papule | white to yellow papule of tongue with zone of erythema | white to yellow papule of larynx with zone of erythema | white to yellow papule of pharynx with zone of erythema | white to yellow papule of lip with zone of erythema | white to yellow papule of palate with zone of erythema | white to yellow papule of retromolar trigone with zone of erythema | white to yellow papule of oral vestibule with zone of erythema | white to yellow papule of buccal mucosa with zone of erythema | floor of mouth papule white to yellow with zone of erythema | Small, yellow papules (mouth, neck, axilla, elbows, groin, periumbilical region)

HP_0025508.label: gottron 's papules
HP_0025508.definition: Violaceous papules overlying the dorsal and lateral aspects of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints.

HP_0025509.label: piezogenic pedal papules
HP_0025509.definition: Flesh-colored or yellowish papules, 2 mm or larger, that are responses to internal mechanical pressure and weakness in the connective tissue in the dermis, appear commonly over the medial aspect of the heel, but in some cases on the wrists. They are thought to represent herniations of adipose tissue through the plantar fascia retinaculum.

HP_0025510.label: nevus spilus
HP_0025510.definition: A tan, regularly bordered patch with darker macules within the lesion.
HP_0025510.UMLS synonyms: Nevus spilus | NEVUS SPILUS, SOMATIC | Dysplastic Nevus | Nevoid lentigo

HP_0025511.label: nevus sebaceus
HP_0025511.definition: A solitary yellow-orange slightly raised plaque typically on scalp or face. The plaque typically thickens and becomes more verrucous or pebbly during childhood.
HP_0025511.UMLS synonyms: Nevus Sebaceus of Jadassohn | Nevus sebaceous | Didymosis aplasticosebacea

HP_0025512.label: skin - colored papule
HP_0025512.definition: A papule with the same color as the surrounding skin.
HP_0025512.UMLS synonyms: salmon colored skin papule | copper colored skin papule | salmon colored skin papule blanches with pressure | copper colored skin papule blanches with pressure | localized lightening of normal colored skin papule | skin papule with same color as surrounding skin | Mulitple papules (1-2 mm skin colored and hyperpigmented) | Multiple, flat, skin-colored warty papules (2-4mm in diameter on dorsum hands, feet, knees, and elbows) | Melanocytic skin tumors/papules, skin-colored to reddish-brown, dome-shaped or pedunculated, well circumscribed with an average size of 5 mm | Papules, firm, flat or dome-shaped, skin-colored some with a hair at or just outside the periphery and/or telangiectatic surface

HP_0025514.label: morning glory anomaly
HP_0025514.definition: An abnormality of the optic nerve in which the optic nerve is large and funneled and displays a conical excavation of the optic disc. The optic disc appears dysplastic.
HP_0025514.synonyms: morning glory disc anomaly | morning glory optic disc

HP_0025515.label: delayed thelarche
HP_0025515.definition: Later than normal development of the breasts.

HP_0025516.label: coronary - pulmonary artery fistula
HP_0025516.definition: A congenital malformation with abnormal connection between one of the coronary arteries and the pulmonary artery.
HP_0025516.UMLS synonyms: Congenital coronary artery fistula to pulmonary artery | Small coronary fistula to main pulmonary artery

HP_0025518.label: visual gaze preference
HP_0025518.definition: An abnormality of gaze that can be observed following an acute supranuclear cerebral lesion (e.g., stroke) that is characterized by an acute inability to direct gaze contralateral to the side of the lesion and is accompanied by a tendency for tonic deviation of the eyes toward the side of the lesion.

HP_0025519.label: multiple biliary hamartomas
HP_0025519.definition: Multiple biliary hamartomas are a rare clinicopathologic entity, consisting of small (less than 1.5cm), usually multiple and nodular cystic lesions in the liver.
HP_0025519.synonyms: biliary hamartoma | multiple bile duct hamartomas | von meyenburg complexes

HP_0025520.label: calcinosis cutis
HP_0025520.definition: Deposition of calcium in the skin.
HP_0025520.UMLS synonyms: Calcinosis Cutis | Metastatic Calcinosis Cutis | Dystrophic Calcinosis Cutis | Idiopathic Calcinosis Cutis | Iatrogenic Calcinosis Cutis | Calcinosis cutis metastatica | Calcinosis circumscripta | Calcinosis universalis | CRST syndrome | Scleroderma-associated calcinosis | CREST Syndrome

HP_0025521.label: increased body fat percentage
HP_0025521.definition: The percentage of fat as a part of total body weight above the norm, usually defined as 32% for females and 25% for males.

HP_0025522.label: elongated chordae tendinae of the mitral valve
HP_0025522.definition: Abnormal increased in length of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve.

HP_0025523.label: abnormal morphology of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve
HP_0025523.definition: A structural anomaly of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve, whose main function is to transmit the contraction and relaxation of the papillary muscles during the cardiac cycle, thus ensuring the closing of the leaflets of the mitral valve.

HP_0025524.label: palmoplantar scaling skin
HP_0025524.definition: Loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in large, scale-like flakes localized to the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot.

HP_0025525.label: scaling skin on fingertip
HP_0025525.definition: Loss of the outer layer of the epidermis in large, scale-like flakes localized to one or more fingertips.

HP_0025526.label: psoriasiform lesion
HP_0025526.definition: A skin lesions that resembles the lesions observed in psoriasis, viz., an erythematous plaque covered by fine silvery scales. Psoriasiform lesions can be observed in psoriasis as well as in other conditions including allergic contact dermatitis, seborrhoeic dermatitis, Atopic dermatitis, pityriasis rubra, and lichen simplex chronicus.
HP_0025526.synonyms: erythemato - squamous plaque | erythematosquamous plaque | psoriatic - like lesion

HP_0025527.label: serpiginous cutaneous lesion
HP_0025527.definition: A skin lesion with a snake- or serpent-like distribution.

HP_0025528.label: annular cutaneous lesion
HP_0025528.definition: A lesion of the skin with a ring-like distribution.

HP_0025529.label: hyperpigmented nodule
HP_0025529.definition: A nodule of the skin that exhibits an increased amount of pigmentation.

HP_0025530.label: xanthomas of the palmar creases
HP_0025530.definition: The presence of multiple xanthomas (xanthomata) in the skin distributed in the creases of the palm of the hand. Xanthomas are yellowish, firm, lipid-laden nodules in the skin.
HP_0025530.synonyms: xanthoma palmare striatum | xanthoma striatum palmare

HP_0025531.label: harlequin phenomenon
HP_0025531.definition: The Harlequin phenomenon consists of a sudden change in skin colour, resulting in two different body colours, one on each half of the body.

HP_0025532.label: positive pathergy test
HP_0025532.definition: With the pathergy test, a small, sterile needle is inserted into the skin of the forearm. The site of injectionis circuled and observed after one and two days. If a small red bump or pustule at the site of needle insertion occurs, the pathergy test is considered to have a positive (abnormal) result.

HP_0025533.label: peau d'orange
HP_0025533.UMLS synonyms: Peau d'orange surface of breast | Cellulite | Peau d'orange retinal changes | peau d'orange in left breast | peau d'orange in both breasts | peau d'orange in right breast | Peau d'orange retinal changes (yellow-mottled retinal hyperpigmentation) | peau d'orange in superior medial quadrant of left breast | peau d'orange in inferior lateral quadrant of right breast | peau d'orange in inferior medial quadrant of right breast | peau d'orange in inferior medial quadrant of left breast | peau d'orange in inferior lateral quadrant of left breast | peau d'orange in superior lateral quadrant of left breast | peau d'orange in superior lateral quadrant of right breast | peau d'orange in superior medial quadrant of right breast

HP_0025534.label: ocular melanocytosis
HP_0025534.definition: A congenital lesion of the sclera characterized by unilateral patchy but extensive slate-gray or bluish discoloration of the sclera . The conjunctiva are spared.
HP_0025534.UMLS synonyms: Congenital ocular melanocytosis | Ocular melanosis | Congenital ocular melanocytosis of left eye | Bilateral congenital ocular melanocytosis of eyes | Congenital ocular melanocytosis of right eye

HP_0025535.label: shawl sign
HP_0025535.definition: Erythematous, poikilodermatous macules distributed in a shawl pattern over the shoulders, arms and upper back.
HP_0025535.UMLS synonyms: Gottron's sign of back and shoulders (shawl sign)

HP_0025536.label: v - sign
HP_0025536.definition: Erythematous, poikilodermatous macules distributed in a V-shaped distribution over the anterior neck and chest.

HP_0025537.label: plantar edema
HP_0025537.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on sole of the foot.

HP_0025538.label: palmar edema
HP_0025538.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin on the palm of the hand.
HP_0025538.UMLS synonyms: tender palmar edema obliterating normal palmar concavity | tender palmar edema obliterating palmar concavity of left hand | tender palmar edema obliterating palmar concavity of right hand

HP_0025540.label: abnormal t cell subset distribution
HP_0025540.definition: Any abnormality in the proportion T cells subsets relative to the total number of T cells.

HP_0025541.label: obsolete decreased activity of complement receptor

HP_0025546.label: abnormal mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
HP_0025546.definition: A deviation from the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell). A reduced mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) may indicate a hypochromic anemia, but the MCH may be normal if both the total hemoglobin and the red blood cell count are reduced.

HP_0025547.label: decreased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
HP_0025547.definition: A reduction from the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell). A reduced mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) may indicate a hypochromic anemia, but the MCH may be normal if both the total hemoglobin and the red blood cell count are reduced.
HP_0025547.synonyms: decreased mch | decreased mchc | decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin | decreased mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration | decreased mean corpuscular hb concentration

HP_0025548.definition: An elevation over the normal range of the average amount of hemoglobin per red blood cell (27 to 31 picograms/cell).

HP_0025549.label: eccentric visual fixation
HP_0025549.definition: A uniocular condition in which there is fixation of an object by a point other than the fovea. This point adopts the principal visual direction. The degree of the eccentric fixation is defined by its distance from the fovea in degrees.

HP_0025550.label: elevated circulating ribitol concentration
HP_0025550.definition: An increase above the normal concentration of ribitol in the blood.
HP_0025550.synonyms: increased level of ribitol in serum

HP_0025551.label: optic nerve misrouting
HP_0025551.definition: Abnormal decussation of the visual pathways, typically identified using visual evoked potentials (VEP) (asymmetrical distribution of the VEP over the posterior scalp).
HP_0025551.synonyms: optic pathway misrouting | visual pathway misrouting
HP_0025551.UMLS synonyms: Optic nerve misrouting on visual evoked potential analysis | FOVEAL HYPOPLASIA 2 WITH OPTIC NERVE MISROUTING | FOVEAL HYPOPLASIA 2 WITH OPTIC NERVE MISROUTING AND ANTERIOR SEGMENT DYSGENESIS | FOVEAL HYPOPLASIA 2 AND OPTIC NERVE MISROUTING WITH OR WITHOUT ANTERIOR SEGMENT DYSGENESIS | FOVEAL HYPOPLASIA 2 | Misrouting of the optic nerves at the chiasm

HP_0025552.label: periorbital purpura
HP_0025552.definition: Multiple red/purple spots on the skin that surrounds the eyes that do not blanch (whiten) upon pressure. Purpura is caused by subcutaneous bleeding.

HP_0025553.label: periorbital ecchymosis with tarsal plate sparing
HP_0025553.definition: Subcutaneous bleeding with a diameter greater than 1 cm (ecchymosis). The bleeding does not extend into the tarsal plate (the comparatively thick, elongated plates of dense connective tissue within the eyelid) due to an anatomic structure called the orbital septum, which limits extravasation of blood beyond the tarsal plate.

HP_0025554.label: yellow nodule
HP_0025554.definition: A type of skin nodule (a lesions that is greater than either 10mm in both width and depth, and most frequently centered in the dermis or subcutaneous fat) with a yellowish coloration (that reflects a high lipid content of the lesion).

HP_0025555.label: periungual teleangiectasia
HP_0025555.definition: Telangiectasia (small dilated blood vessels) located near to the fingernails or toenails.

HP_0025558.label: lamellar cataract with riders
HP_0025558.definition: Lamellar cataracts with associated linear lens opacities radially extending towards the periphery of the lens.

HP_0025559.label: coronary cataract
HP_0025559.definition: A type of cataract characterised by club-shaped and dot opacities distributed radially in the deep cortex. These lens opacities surround the nucleus in an appearance that is though to resemble a crown.
HP_0025559.UMLS synonyms: Coronary cataract | coronary; coronary cataract | senile cataract; coronary | Coronary age-related cataract | coronary immature senile cataract | coronary incipient senile cataract

HP_0025560.label: anterior chamber cells
HP_0025560.definition: Tiny deposits corresponding to cells floating in the anterior chamber of the eye. This appearance is typically associated with intraocular inflammation leading to breakdown of the blood-aqueous barrier and resulting in an increase in the number of cells and in the aqueous humor. Grading (SUN Working Group) is performed by estimating the number of cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

HP_0025561.definition: Anterior chamber cells with 6-15 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

HP_0025562.definition: Anterior chamber cells with 1-5 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

HP_0025563.definition: Anterior chamber cells with less than one cell in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

HP_0025564.label: anterior chamber cells grade 2+
HP_0025564.definition: Anterior chamber cells with 16-25 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

HP_0025565.label: anterior chamber cells grade 3+
HP_0025565.definition: Anterior chamber cells with 26-50 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

HP_0025566.label: anterior chamber cells grade 4+
HP_0025566.definition: Anterior chamber cells with more than 50 cells in a 1 mm by 1 mm slit beam field, employing adequate light intensity and magnification on a slit lamp.

HP_0025567.label: central serous chorioretinopathy
HP_0025567.definition: An anomaly of the retina with serous detachment of the neurosensory retina secondary to one or more focal lesions of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and associated with blurred vision, usually in one eye only and perceived typically by the patient as a dark spot in the centre of the visual field with associated micropsia and metamorphopsia. Normal vision often recurs spontaneously within a few months.

HP_0025569.label: polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy
HP_0025569.definition: The presence of aneurysmal polypoidal lesions in the choroidal vasculature. The aneurysmal dilatations, also known as polyps, may be found at subfoveal, juxtafoveal, extrafoveal, peripapillary or even peripheral regions. These polypoidal dilatations may be visible as reddish-orange subretinal nodules during ophthalmoscopic examination. The polypoidal lesions are best detected on indocyanine green angiography (ICGA) and might be associated with a branching vascular network (BVN) of neovascularization.

HP_0025570.label: choroidal vascular hyperpermeability
HP_0025570.definition: Increased tendency of choiroidal blood vessels to allow fluids to leak characterized by multifocal choroidal hyperfluorescence on indocyanine green angiography (ICGA).

HP_0025571.label: christmas tree cataract
HP_0025571.definition: A type of cataract that shows a spectacular display of multiple colours that glitters with the change of incident light like an illuminated Christmas tree.

HP_0025572.label: punctal stenosis
HP_0025572.definition: Punctal stenosis is a condition in which the external opening of the lacrimal canaliculus is narrowed or occluded.

HP_0025573.label: mild myopia

HP_0025578.definition: Aortic valve prolapse can be diagnosed when either or both of the right or non-coronary aortic valve cusps (seen in the cross sectional echocardiographic long axis view) show backward bowing towards the left ventricle beyond a line joining the points of attachment of the aortic valve leaflets to the annulus.

HP_0025579.definition: Any structural abnormality of the left atrium.

HP_0025580.definition: Any structural abnormality of the right atrium.

HP_0025582.label: submacular hemorrhage
HP_0025582.definition: Bleeding between the neurosensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) arising from the choroidal or retinal circulation.

HP_0025583.label: tapetal - like fundal reflex
HP_0025583.definition: Golden, scintillating, particulate reflection noted on fundus examination (typically in the macula and sparing the fovea). The term tapetal is used to describe this 'metallic' sheen appearance as it is thought to be similar to the 'tapetal' reflex seen in the eyes of certain animals.

HP_0025584.label: hypotropia
HP_0025584.definition: A form of manifest strabismus (heterotropia) in which one eye is deviated downwards when both eyes are open.

HP_0025585.label: hyperphoria
HP_0025585.definition: Tendency for the visual axis of one eye to be higher than that of the other.

HP_0025586.label: hypertropia
HP_0025586.definition: A type of strabismus characterized by permanent upward deviation of the visual axis of one eye.

HP_0025587.label: hyperdeviation
HP_0025587.definition: A type of strabismus in which the visual axis of one eye is higher than that of the other.

HP_0025588.label: hypodeviation
HP_0025588.definition: A type of strabismus in which the visual axis of one eye is lower than that of the other.

HP_0025589.label: cyclodeviation
HP_0025589.definition: Cyclodeviation is defined as the rotation of an eyeball along the anteroposterior axis and cyclotropia as a misalignment of cyclodeviation between the two eyes.

HP_0025590.label: abnormal extraocular muscle physiology
HP_0025590.definition: A functional anomaly of the muscles of the eye.

HP_0025591.label: abnormal superior oblique muscle physiology
HP_0025591.definition: A functional anomaly of the superior oblique muscle, a fusiform muscle that originates in the upper, medial side of the orbit. The superior oblique muscle abducts, depresses and internally rotates the eye, and is the only extraocular muscle innervated by the fourth cranial nerve.

HP_0025592.label: superior oblique muscle weakness
HP_0025592.definition: Decreased strength of the superior oblique muscle.

HP_0025593.label: superior oblique muscle restriction
HP_0025593.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the superior oblique muscle.

HP_0025594.label: superior oblique muscle overaction
HP_0025594.definition: An ocular motility abnormality characterized by an overacting superior oblique muscle resulting to vertical incomitance of the eyes in lateral gaze. On examination, this is commonly seen as a downshoot of the adducting eye occuring when gaze is directed into the field of action of the inferior oblique muscle, producing a greater downward excursion of the adducted eye than of the abducted eye.

HP_0025595.label: superior oblique muscle underaction
HP_0025595.definition: Reduced ocular movement of the superior oblique muscle which improves on testing ductions, typically associated with neurogenic palsy.

HP_0025596.label: abnormal inferior oblique muscle physiology
HP_0025596.definition: A functional anomaly of the inferior oblique muscle, an extraocular muscle that has its origin on the maxillary bone just posterior to the inferior medial orbital rim and lateral to the nasolacrimal canal and that is innervated by the inferior branch of the oculomotor nerve.

HP_0025597.label: inferior oblique muscle restriction
HP_0025597.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the inferior oblique muscle.

HP_0025598.label: inferior oblique muscle weakness
HP_0025598.definition: Decreased strength of the inferior oblique muscle.

HP_0025599.label: inferior oblique muscle overaction
HP_0025599.definition: A common ocular motility disorder characterized by vertical incomitance of the eyes in lateral gaze. In primary inferior oblique muscle overaction, an upshoot of the adducting eye occurs when gaze is directed into the field of action of the inferior oblique muscle, producing a greater upward excursion of the adducted eye than of the abducted eye.

HP_0025600.label: abnormal inferior rectus muscle physiology
HP_0025600.definition: A functional anomaly of the inferior rectus muscle, which is innervated by the inferior division of oculomotor nerve and functions in the depression, adduction, and lateral rotation (extortion) of the eye.

HP_0025601.label: inferior rectus muscle weakness
HP_0025601.definition: Decreased strength of the inferior rectus muscle.

HP_0025602.label: inferior rectus muscle restriction
HP_0025602.definition: Mechanical limitation of the range of movement of the inferior rectus muscle.

HP_0025603.label: abnormal superior rectus muscle physiology
HP_0025603.definition: A functional anomaly of the superior rectus muscle, an extraocular muscle that is innervated by the superior division of the oculomotor nerve, and whose primary function is the elevation of the globe.

HP_0025604.label: orbital schwannoma
HP_0025604.definition: A schwannoma (benign, usually encapsulated slow growing tumor composed of Schwann cells) located in the orbit.

HP_0025605.label: lid lag on downgaze
HP_0025605.definition: Delayed descent of the upper eyelid on downgaze. Also described by some authors as von Graefe sign.
HP_0025605.synonyms: eyelid lag | lid lag | von graefe sign

HP_0025606.label: abnormal medial rectus muscle physiology
HP_0025606.definition: A functional anomaly of the medial rectus muscle, an extraocular muscle that is innervated by the inferior division of the oculomotor nerve and whose sole action is the adduction of the eyeball.

HP_0025607.label: upper eyelid entropion
HP_0025607.definition: An inward turning (inversion) of the margin of the upper eyelid.
HP_0025607.UMLS synonyms: Upper eyelid entropion | Entropion of left upper eyelid | Entropion of right upper eyelid | Spastic entropion of upper eyelid | Senile entropion of upper eyelid | Mechanical entropion of upper eyelid | Cicatricial entropion of upper eyelid | Cicatricial entropion of left upper eyelid | Cicatricial entropion of right upper eyelid | Mechanical entropion of left upper eyelid | Mechanical entropion of right upper eyelid | Correction of entropion of upper eyelid | Senile entropion of left upper eyelid | spastic entropion of left upper eyelid | Senile entropion of right upper eyelid | spastic entropion of right upper eyelid | Unspecified entropion of left upper eyelid | Unspecified entropion of right upper eyelid | trichiasis without entropion of left upper eyelid | trichiasis without entropion of right upper eyelid | Entropion of upper eyelid co-occurrent with ectropion of upper eyelid | repair of entropion of left upper eyelid | repair of entropion of right upper eyelid | entropion of both upper eyelids | Bilateral cicatricial entropion of upper eyelids

HP_0025608.label: cicatricial ectropion
HP_0025608.definition: An outward turning (eversion) or rotation of the eyelid margin (i.e., ectropion) caused by shortening or contraction of the anterior or middle lamellae related to scarring.

HP_0025609.label: anterior blepharitis
HP_0025609.definition: A type of blepharitis that affects the eyelid skin, base of the eyelashes, and the eyelash follicles.

HP_0025610.label: posterior blepharitis
HP_0025610.definition: A type of blepharitis that affects the meibomian glands and meibomian gland orifices. This abnormality can be associated with a spectrum of appearances ranging from meibomian seborrhoea (foaming meibomian gland secretions) and meibomianitis (inflamed meibomian glands), to chalazia.
HP_0025610.synonyms: meibomian gland disease | meibomian gland dysfunction

HP_0025611.label: epicanthus superciliaris
HP_0025611.definition: A type of epicanthus in which more extensive epicanthal folds with their origins in the eyebrow cover, pass in front of and lateral to the medial canthus (middle corner of the eye).

HP_0025612.label: corneal astigmatism
HP_0025612.definition: A type of refractive error related abnormal curvatures on the anterior or posterior surface of the cornea.

HP_0025613.label: focal emotional seizure
HP_0025613.definition: Seizures presenting with an emotion or the appearance of having an emotion as an early prominent feature, such as fear, spontaneous joy or euphoria, laughing (gelastic), or crying, (dacrystic). These emotional seizures may occur with or without objective clinical signs of a seizure evident to the observer.

HP_0025616.definition: An abscess not caused by infection with pyogenic bacteria. Operationally, a sterile abscess is inferred if investigations of an abscess fail to reveal evidence of pathogenic organisms.

HP_0025618.definition: An abnormally low number of plasma cells in the blood circulation. Plasma cells are the the effector cells dedicated to the production of a high amount of antibodies.

HP_0025619.label: elevated plasma cell count
HP_0025619.definition: An abnormally high number of plasma cells in the blood circulation. Plasma cells are the the effector cells dedicated to the production of a high amount of antibodies.

HP_0025620.label: abnormal proportion of cd4+ central memory cells
HP_0025620.definition: An abnormal proportion of central memory CD4+ T cells. These are memory cells that are located in the secondary lymphoid organs. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L+/CD45RA- phenotype.

HP_0025623.label: abnormal proportion of cd4+ effector memory cells
HP_0025623.definition: An abnormal proportion of effector memory CD4+ T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells have the phenotype CD3-positive, CD4-positive, CD62L-negative, CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
