HP_0025624.label: reduced proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cells
HP_0025624.definition: An abnormally decreased proportion of effector memory CD4+ T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells have the phenotype CD3-positive, CD4-positive, CD62L-negative, CCR7-negative, CD127-positive, CD45RA-negative, CD45RO-positive, and CD25-negative.
HP_0025624.synonyms: decreased proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cells | decreased proportion of cd4 - positive effector memory t cells | decreased proportion of effector memory cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cells

HP_0025625.label: elevated proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cells
HP_0025625.definition: An abnormally increased proportion of effector memory CD4+ T cells. These are memory cells that are short-lived cells that migrate to the site of an infection and attempt to eliminate the pathogen. These cells may have a CD3/CD4/CD62L-/CD45RA phenotype.
HP_0025625.synonyms: increased proportion of cd4+ effector memory t cells | increased proportion of cd4 - positive effector memory t cells | increased proportion of effector cd4 - positive , alpha - beta t cells

HP_0025626.label: increased circulating oleate level
HP_0025626.definition: An abnormally high concentration of oleic acid (oleate) in the blood circulation.

HP_0025627.label: increased circulating octadecanoate level
HP_0025627.definition: An abnormally high concentration of octadecanoate in the blood circulation. Octadecanoate is a fatty acid anion 18:0 that is the conjugate base of octadecanoic acid (stearic acid).

HP_0025628.label: increased circulating myristoleate level
HP_0025628.definition: An abnormally high concentration of myristoleate in the blood circulation.

HP_0025629.label: anti - myelin - associated glycoprotein antibody positivity
HP_0025629.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against myelin-associated glycoprotein (MAG).

HP_0025630.label: argininosuccinic aciduria
HP_0025630.definition: Increased amount of argininosuccinate in the urine.
HP_0025630.UMLS synonyms: Argininosuccinic Aciduria | Argininosuccinic Aciduria Gene Mutation Detection Reagents

HP_0025631.label: alpha - aminobutyric aciduria
HP_0025631.definition: Increased amount of alpha-aminobutyric acid in the urine.

HP_0025632.label: reduced reactive oxygen species production in neutrophils
HP_0025632.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of reactive oxygen produced by neutrophils in the respiratory burst.

HP_0025633.label: abnormal ureter morphology
HP_0025633.definition: A structural abnormality of the ureter. The ureter is the duct by which urine passes from the kidney to the bladder.

HP_0025634.label: abnormal ureter physiology
HP_0025634.definition: A functional abnormality of the ureter. The ureter is the duct by which urine passes from the kidney to the bladder.

HP_0025635.label: ureteral polyp
HP_0025635.definition: A growth protruding from the mucous membrane of the ureter. Ureteral polyps can be attached to the ureter by a broad base or a thin stalk.
HP_0025635.synonyms: polyp of the ureter | ureter polyp
HP_0025635.UMLS synonyms: Ureteric polyp | ureteral polyp on left | ureteral polyp on right | bilateral ureteral polyps | URETER, POLYP, BENIGN

HP_0025636.label: endometritis
HP_0025636.definition: Inflammation of the inner lining of the uterus (endometrium).
HP_0025636.synonyms: endometrial inflammation | inflammation of the inner lining of the uterus

HP_0025637.label: vasospasm
HP_0025637.definition: Narrowing of an artery due to constriction of the blood vessels.

HP_0025638.label: elevated urinary n - butyrylglycine
HP_0025638.definition: An increased level of N-butyrylglycine in the urine.

HP_0025639.label: increased urinary zinc level
HP_0025639.definition: An abnormally elevated amount of zinc in the urine, typically as assessed by a 24 hour urine collection.

HP_0025640.label: abnormal urinary mineral level
HP_0025640.definition: An abnormal concentration or amount of a mineral in the urine. Medically relevant minerals include calcium, phosphorus, potassium, sodium, chloride, magnesium, iron, zinc, iodine, chromium, copper, fluoride, molybdenum, manganese, and selenium.

HP_0025641.label: elevated circulating glycolate concentration
HP_0025641.definition: The concentration of glycolate in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0025643.label: tarlov cyst
HP_0025643.definition: A cerebrospinal fluid-filled nerve root cyst most often localized in the sacral spine.

HP_0025644.label: fixation - off epileptiform discharges
HP_0025644.definition: Fixation off sensitivity (FOS) is characterized by posterior or generalized epileptiform discharges that consistently occur with conditions that eliminate central vision, such as closed eyes, complete darkness, modified Ganzfeld stimulation (using a large white surface without visual cues), and Frenzel lenses. The FOS electroencephalogram (EEG) pattern usually consists of spikes/polyspikes and waves localized in occipital regions (bilateral or unilateral) or generalized discharges. It is usually inhibited by fixation of gaze, observing patterns, or intermittent photic stimulation (e.g., flashing light or patterns used as stimuli during the recording of the EEG).

HP_0025646.label: bilateral polymicrogyria
HP_0025646.definition: Polymicrogyria that affects all or some of both cerebral hemispheres.
HP_0025646.UMLS synonyms: Bilateral polymicrogyria | POLYMICROGYRIA, BILATERAL FRONTOPARIETAL | Bilateral generalized polymicrogyria | Bilateral frontal polymicrogyria | POLYMICROGYRIA, BILATERAL TEMPOROOCCIPITAL | Polymicrogyria, Bilateral Occipital | Cortical polymicrogyria, bilateral | Bilateral parasagittal parieto-occipital polymicrogyria | POLYMICROGYRIA, BILATERAL PERISYLVIAN, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE | Perisylvian syndrome | Bilateral Frontoparietal Polymicrogyria (BFPP) Gene Mutation Detection Reagents | Bilateral Occipital Polymicrogyria (BTOP) Gene Anomaly Detection Reagents | Baraitser Brett Piesowicz syndrome

HP_0025647.label: steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome
HP_0025647.definition: A type of nephrotic syndrome in which complete remission (albumin urine dipstick negative/trace or proteinuria <4mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio <200mg/g (<20 mg/mmol) for 3 consecutive days) is achieved within initial 4 weeks of corticosteroid therapy.

HP_0025648.label: steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome with infrequent relapses
HP_0025648.definition: A type of steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in which relapses occur at a frequency of one relapse (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria over 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) within 6 months of initial response, or one to three relapses in any 12-month period.

HP_0025649.label: steroid - sensitive nephrotic syndrome with frequent relapses
HP_0025649.definition: A type of steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in which relapses occur at a frequency of two or more relapses (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria over 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) within 6 months of initial response or four or more relapses in any 12-month period.

HP_0025650.label: steroid - dependent nephrotic syndrome
HP_0025650.definition: A type of nephrotic syndrome in which two consecutive relapses (albumin urine dipstick at least 3+ or proteinuria greater than 40 mg/m2/d or urinary protein to creatinine ratio at least 2000 mg/g for 3 consecutive days) occur during corticosteroid therapy, or within 14 days of ceasing therapy.

HP_0025652.label: abnormal placental adhesion into the uterine wall
HP_0025652.definition: Abnormal placental adhesion is characterized by an anomalous adherence of the placenta to the uterine wall. Based on the degree of adhesion, placental invasion can be classified into accreta, increta, or percreta.

HP_0025653.label: placenta percreta
HP_0025653.definition: Placenta percreta is a rare form of morbidly adherent placenta with penetration through the myometrium reaching serosa and even adjacent pelvic organs.
HP_0025653.synonyms: abnormal placental pentration beyond the uterine wall
HP_0025653.UMLS synonyms: Placenta Percreta | Placenta percreta, first trimester | transvaginal ultrasound: placenta percreta | placenta; percreta, without hemorrhage | Placenta percreta, unspecified trimester | Placenta percreta, second trimester | Placenta percreta, third trimester

HP_0025654.label: placenta accreta
HP_0025654.definition: Abnormally firm adherence of the placenta to the uterine wall.
HP_0025654.UMLS synonyms: Placenta Accreta | Cornual placenta accreta | Placenta accreta without hemorrhage | transvaginal ultrasound: placenta accreta | Placenta accreta, first trimester | Placenta accreta, unspecified trimester | Placenta accreta, third trimester | Placenta accreta, second trimester | Past pregnancy history of placenta accreta | c.delivery; placenta accreta (with hemorrhage) | c.delivery; placenta accreta, without hemorrhage | Morbidly adherent placenta (disorder) | c.delivery; placenta accreta, with hemorrhage, delayed or secondary (portions of placenta)

HP_0025655.label: placenta increta
HP_0025655.definition: Abnormal placental pentration into but not beyond the uterine wall.
HP_0025655.UMLS synonyms: Placenta Increta | transvaginal ultrasound: placenta increta | placenta; increta, without hemorrhage | Placenta increta, second trimester | Placenta increta, third trimester | Placenta increta, first trimester | Placenta increta, unspecified trimester

HP_0025656.label: prenatal double bubble sign
HP_0025656.definition: Sonographic detection of a double bubble sign in the upper abdomen is strongly indicative of duodenal obstruction. One bubble represents fetal stomach, and the other is attributed to a dilated proximal part of the duodenum; continuity between both bubbles is required for the sign.

HP_0025658.label: obsolete abnormal umbilical artery doppler pattern in pregnancy

HP_0025659.label: decreased circulating creatine kinase concentration
HP_0025659.definition: A reduction in the level of the enzyme creatine kinase (also known as creatine phosphokinase (CK; EC 2.7.3.2) in the blood.

HP_0025660.label: chiari type ii malformation
HP_0025660.definition: A type of Chiari malformation that consists of brainstem herniation and a towering cerebellum in addition to the herniated cerebellar tonsils and vermis due to an open distal spinal dysraphism/myelomeningocele.
HP_0025660.UMLS synonyms: Chiari malformation type II | type II Chiari malformation of thoracic region | type II Chiari malformation of cervical region | type II Chiari malformation of lumbar region | Arnold Chiari type 2 without hydrocephalus

HP_0025661.label: chiari type iii malformation
HP_0025661.definition: A type of Chiari malformation that involves herniation of the hindbrain (cerebellum with or without the brainstem) into a low occipital or high cervical meningoencephalocele.

HP_0025662.label: abnormal fetal skeletal morphology
HP_0025662.definition: An anomalous structural finding of the fetal skeleton. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other terms from the skeletal hierarchy can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

HP_0025663.label: reduced fetal femur / foot length ratio
HP_0025663.definition: This ratio relates the length of the fetal femur to that of the fetal foot. The ratio is approximately 1 throughout the age range of 14 to 40 weeks of gestation. A substantial reduction in the raio can help differentiate fetuses that have dysplastic limb reduction from those whose limbs are short because of constitutional factors or IUGR. It can reduce the problem of an unknown gestational age and help to distinguish between fetal skeletal dysplasia and intrauterine growth retardation caused by other factors.

HP_0025664.label: moderate to late preterm birth
HP_0025664.definition: Birth at 32 to 36 completed weeks of gestation.

HP_0025665.label: extremely preterm birth
HP_0025665.definition: Birth before 28 completed weeks of gestation (up to and including 27 weeks and 6 days of gestation).
HP_0025665.UMLS synonyms: GAIA Level 3 Neonatal Death in an Extremely Preterm Live Birth | GAIA Level 2 Neonatal Death in an Extremely Preterm Live Birth | GAIA Level 1 Neonatal Death in an Extremely Preterm Live Birth | Extreme Preterm Birth | Review history for risk factors commonly related to preterm labor (e.g., prior patient or family history of preterm birth or abortion; multifetal gestation; uterine cervical anomalies; early cervical change; uterine irritability; infection, including periodontal disease; short interpregnancy interval; technology-induced conception; history of vaginal bleeding in first and or second trimester; positive fetal fibronectin results; extremes of pre-pregnancy body weight)

HP_0025666.label: very preterm birth
HP_0025666.definition: Birth before 32 completed weeks of gestation (28 up to but not including 32 weeks).
HP_0025666.UMLS synonyms: INFANT PRETERM VERY LOW BIRTH WEIGHT

HP_0025667.label: fetal neck anomaly
HP_0025667.definition: A structural anomaly in the fetal neck region. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

HP_0025668.label: abnormal neck morphology
HP_0025668.definition: Any structural anomaly of the neck region.
HP_0025668.UMLS synonyms: Pancreatic neck surgical margin | Bladder neck surgical margin

HP_0025669.label: abnormal neck physiology
HP_0025669.definition: Any functional anomaly of the neck region.

HP_0025670.label: syntelencephaly
HP_0025670.definition: Syntelencephaly is a rare malformation that consists of an abnormal midline connection of the cerebral hemispheres in the posterior frontal and parietal regions, with interhemispheric separation of the basal forebrain, anterior frontal lobes, and occipital regions.

HP_0025671.label: fetal pericardial effusion
HP_0025671.definition: An abnormal accumulation of fluid in which the heart is partially or completely surrounded by fluid that is seen in all views and the thickness of the fluid as observed by prenatal ultrasound is above age-dependent norms.
HP_0025671.UMLS synonyms: Fetal pericardial effusion | FETAL HEART PERICARDIAL EFFUSION | Percutaneous aspiration of fetal pericardial effusion

HP_0025672.label: fetal skin edema
HP_0025672.definition: A separation of skin in one or more regions of the body or even along the entire length of body wall (to a degree greater than gestational-age related norms) related to pathologically increased fluid accumulation in the subcutaneous tissue.

HP_0025673.label: loculated ascites
HP_0025673.definition: A type of ascites (peritoneal fluid collection) that is divided into loculi (compartments) by septa (fibrous walls). Ascites fluid can become loculated when confined by adhesions, malignancy or infection.

HP_0025674.label: meconium pseudocyst
HP_0025674.definition: A meconium-containing cyst in the peritoneal space . Meconium pseudocysts form in the presence of meconium peritonitis, which is defined as a sterile peritonitis caused by escape of meconium from the intestinal tract into the general peritoneal cavity during the fetal or perinatal period. When the extruded meconium becomes walled off, it can form a rim-calcified mass representing the meconium pseudocyst.

HP_0025675.label: premature closure of the ductus arteriosus
HP_0025675.definition: A prenatal partial or complete closure of the ductus arteriosus (i.e., prior to delivery).
HP_0025675.synonyms: fetal arterial duct narrowing - closure | fetal ductus arteriosus narrowing - closure | fetal pad narrowing - closure | fetal pda narrowing - closure | foetal arterial duct narrowing - closure | foetal ductus arteriosus narrowing - closure | foetal pad narrowing - closure | foetal pda narrowing - closure | idiopathic constriction of the fetal ductus arteriosus | idiopathic constriction of the foetal ductus arteriosus

HP_0025676.label: fetal pleural effusion
HP_0025676.definition: Fetal pleural effusion is the accumulation of excess fluid in the layers of tissue (pleura) lining the lungs and wall of the chest. It may be primary, also termed hydrothorax, occurring as an isolated finding or it may be secondary, most commonly resulting from non-immune hydrops.
HP_0025676.UMLS synonyms: Fetal pleural effusion | Percutaneous aspiration of fetal pleural effusion

HP_0025677.label: fetal chylothorax
HP_0025677.definition: The presence of chyle (a type of lipid-rich lymph) in the pleural space (the space surrounding the lung) as observed in a fetus.

HP_0025678.label: fetal hydrothorax
HP_0025678.definition: Accumulation of lymphatic fluid in the pleural space. This finding is usually observed by prenatal sonography. Once neonatal feeding is established and the lymphatic fluid contains chyle, transformation to chylothorax may be observed.

HP_0025679.label: diskitis
HP_0025679.definition: Inflammation of an intervertebral disc or disk space.

HP_0025680.label: compound muscle action potential amplitude facilitation
HP_0025680.definition: Compound muscle action potential amplitude (CMAP) facilitation denotes an increase in tendon reflexes, strength, or CMAP amplitude after 10 seconds of maximal voluntary contraction.

HP_0025681.label: distal clavicular thinning
HP_0025681.definition: Abnormally reduced diameter (cross section) of the clavicles that is limited to the distal region.

HP_0025682.label: crouch gait
HP_0025682.definition: A gait disturbance that is characterized by excessive ankle dorsiflexion, knee and hip flexion during the stance phase.

HP_0025683.label: abnormal amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
HP_0025683.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Amyloid beta is a peptide of 36-43 amino acids that is processed from the Amyloid precursor protein. ABeta42, which is 42 amino acids in length, is the longer form.

HP_0025684.label: decreased amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
HP_0025684.definition: A reduction from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP_0025685.label: increased amyloid beta 42 peptide csf concentration
HP_0025685.definition: An elevation above the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP_0025686.label: abnormal amyloid beta 40 peptide csf concentration
HP_0025686.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of amyloid beta 42 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Amyloid beta is a peptide of 36-43 amino acids that is processed from the Amyloid precursor protein. ABeta40, which is 40 amino acids in length, is the shorter form.
HP_0025686.synonyms: abnormal abeta 40 level | abnormal beta amyloid 40 level

HP_0025687.label: increased amyloid beta 40 peptide csf concentration
HP_0025687.definition: An elevation above the normal concentration of amyloid beta 40 peptide in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP_0025688.label: abnormal amyloid beta peptide csf concentration
HP_0025688.definition: Any anomaly in the concentration of a cleaved APP amyloid beta protein fragment in the cerebrospinal fluid.

HP_0025689.label: extra - abdominal umbilical vein varix
HP_0025689.definition: Focal dilatation of the extra-abdominal portion of the umbilical vein. An extra-abdominal umbilical varix is difficult to diagnose prenatally as it can appear like a cyst on ultrasound prior to birth.

HP_0025690.label: fetal intra - abdominal umbilical vein varix
HP_0025690.definition: Fetal intra-abdominal umbilical vein varix (FIUVV) is defined by the focal dilatation of the fetal umbilical vein between its entry in the abdomen and its ending in the portal system. The dilatation can be defined using one of the following criteria: a portion of intra-abdominal umbilical vein that is at least 50% wider than the non-dilated portion; a dilatation of 9 mm or more, or a dilatation greater than 2 SD above the mean value for gestational age.
HP_0025690.synonyms: fetal umbilical vein dilatation | foetal umbilical vein dilatation

HP_0025691.label: impaired fasting glucose
HP_0025691.definition: Impaired fasting glucose (IFG) is indicated by a fasting plasma glucose above normal but below the diabetic range. Levels between 110 mg/dl (6.1 mmol/l) to 125 mg/dl (6.9 mmol/l) are diagnostic of IFG.

HP_0025692.label: atelencephaly
HP_0025692.definition: A defect of development of the brain characterized by absence of the telencephalon (embryonic structure from which the mature cerebrum develops).

HP_0025693.label: pituitary macroadenoma
HP_0025693.definition: A pituitary gland adenoma that is larger than 10mm.
HP_0025693.UMLS synonyms: Pituitary macroadenoma | Functioning Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor/Macroadenoma | Non-Functioning Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor/Macroadenoma | Pituitary macroadenoma with extrasellar extension | MRI of pituitary fossa: macroadenoma | MRI of pituitary fossa: macroadenoma with suprasellar extension | MRI of pituitary fossa: macroadenoma with lateral extension | MRI of pituitary fossa: macroadenoma with lateral extension bilateral | Macroprolactinoma | MRI of pituitary fossa: macroadenoma with lateral extension to left | MRI of pituitary fossa: macroadenoma with lateral extension to right | MRI of pituitary fossa: macroadenoma with suprasellar extension compressing optic chiasm

HP_0025694.label: pituitary microadenoma
HP_0025694.definition: A pituitary adenoma that is less than 10 mm in diameter.
HP_0025694.UMLS synonyms: Pituitary microadenoma | PITUITARY MICROADENOMA RESECTION | Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor/Microadenoma | Functioning Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor/Microadenoma | Non-Functioning Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumor/Microadenoma | MRI of pituitary fossa: microadenoma | Microprolactinoma

HP_0025695.label: mucus plug
HP_0025695.definition: Mucus that is abnormally thick in consistency (ie, inspissated) and plugs the airway is known as a mucus plug. Mucus plugs consist of mucins and cells and can partially or completely obstruct one or more airways and cause serious consequences, including atelectasis and recurrent infection.
HP_0025695.UMLS synonyms: Cervical Mucus Plug | Bronchial mucus plug | mucus; plug, tracheobronchial | Mucus cast | Passing of Mucus Plug | plug; mucus, tracheobronchial, newborn | plug; mucus, aspiration, newborn | Mucus plug in os cervix | Mucus plug in respiratory tract | Sialendoscopic removal of mucus plug of salivary duct | Multiple tracheobronchial mucus plugs

HP_0025696.label: airway casts
HP_0025696.definition: A replicate of airways from accumulated and condensed mucous and cellular material. These semisolid occlusions take the shape of the airway within they are formed, leading to obstruction of the tracheobronchial tree with consecutive respiratory insufficiency. Based on their principal composition, one can differentiate fibrin casts and mucin casts. Plastic bronchitis is the name of the condition characterized by the formation of airway casts.

HP_0025697.label: fibrin casts
HP_0025697.definition: A type of airway casts that consist of plasma components and inflammatory cells.
HP_0025697.synonyms: cellular airway casts | diphtheroid membranes | pseudomembranes | type i airway casts

HP_0025698.label: mucin casts
HP_0025698.definition: A type of airway casts that consist of impacted mucus.
HP_0025698.synonyms: acellular airway casts | type ii airway casts

HP_0025699.label: perisylvian fdg hypermetabolism
HP_0025699.definition: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography and computed tomography (FDG-PET/CT) evaluates the glucose metabolism of the brain. FDG uptake is interpreted to represent glycolysis. This term therefore represents an abnormally increased FDG uptake (increased glucose metabolism) in the region of the brain that surrounds the Sylvian fissure.

HP_0025700.label: anhydramnios
HP_0025700.definition: A complete or near-complete lack of amniotic fluid surrounding a fetus. This finding can be observed sonographically in the third trimesters if the deepest pocket of amniotic fluid is less than or equal to 2 cm.

HP_0025701.label: distended jugular lymphatic sacs
HP_0025701.definition: The jugular lymphatic sacs (JLS) are a physiological and temporary part of fetal lymphatic development. They are formed from small buds of lymphatic endothelial cells arising from the internal jugular veins. By 14 weeks gestation they have developed into lymphatic nodes which drain into the systemic circulation. Visibility of JLS on ultrasound past 14 weeks of gestation implies distension and this may be associated with raised nuchal translucency.

HP_0025702.label: type 1 schizencephaly
HP_0025702.definition: A type of Schizencephaly in which there is a trans-mantle column of abnormal grey matter but no evidence of a CSF-containing cleft on MR imaging.

HP_0025703.label: type 2 schizencephaly
HP_0025703.definition: A type of Schizencephaly in which CSF-containing cleft is present with abutting lining lips of abnormal grey matter that are opposed to each other.

HP_0025704.label: type 3 schizencephaly
HP_0025704.definition: A type of Schizencephaly in which CSF-containing cleft present with non-abutting lining lips of abnormal grey matter.

HP_0025705.label: abnormal fetal nasal bone visualization
HP_0025705.definition: Abnormal appearance or non-visualization (apparent absence) of the nasal bone of a fetus in first trimester sonographic screening. Assessment of the fetal nasal bone is generally performed at 11-14 weeks gestational age.

HP_0025706.label: absent fetal nasal bone
HP_0025706.definition: The nasal bone is considered absent when it is not visualized on a midsagittal view of the profile. In the second trimester, a true midsagittal view of the fetal profile is obtained and magnified to fill the majority of the image space. The nasal bone appears as an echogenic linear structure below the skin edge. The optimal angle of insonation is 45 degrees to the longitudinal axis of the fetal nasal bone. If the angle of insonation is 0 or 180 degrees, the nasal bone may appear artificially absent. The presence or absence of the nasal bone may be determined at the time of the 11- to 14-week ultrasound examination and used as part of the risk assessment for aneuploidy.
HP_0025706.synonyms: absence of fetal nasal bone | absence of foetal nasal bone | unossified nasal bone
HP_0025706.UMLS synonyms: Lack of ossification of nasal bone

HP_0025707.label: hypoplastic nasal bone
HP_0025707.definition: Length of the nasal bone below a predetermined cut-off as seen on antenatal ultrasound using standard imaging techniques.

HP_0025708.label: early young adult onset
HP_0025708.definition: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 16 to under 19 years.

HP_0025709.label: intermediate young adult onset
HP_0025709.definition: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 19 to under 25 years.

HP_0025710.label: late young adult onset
HP_0025710.definition: Onset of disease at an age of greater than or equal to 25 to under 40 years.

HP_0025711.label: convergence - retraction nystagmus
HP_0025711.definition: Convergence-retraction nystagmus is an irregular, jerky nystagmus in which both eyeballs rhythmically converge and retract into the orbit, particularly on attempting an upward gaze.

HP_0025712.label: spontaneous chorioamniotic separation
HP_0025712.definition: Persistence separation of the chorionic and amnionic membranes after the 16th week of gestation (not as a result of a procedure such as amniocentesis).

HP_0025713.label: neurite dystrophy
HP_0025713.definition: Dystrophic neurites are abnormal neuronal processes characterized microscopically by aberrant sprouting, dystrophic expansion, and accumulation of various cellular organelles and cytoskeletal/signaling proteins.

HP_0025714.label: cerebral cortical microinfarct
HP_0025714.definition: An infarct located on the outer layer of the cerebrum that can only be observed microscopically. Cerebral microinfarcts are typically defined as sharply delimited microscopic regions of cellular death or tissue necrosis, sometimes with cavitation (that is, a central fluid-filled cavity). The term microscopic denotes that these lesions are not visible by gross inspection of the brain but seen by light microscopy. The term infarct is most commonly used for ischemia-related tissue loss, and indeed the pathologic appearance of microinfarcts is consistent with that of known ischemic infarctions.

HP_0025715.label: abnormal umbilical artery doppler waveform during pregnancy
HP_0025715.definition: Abnormal waveforms the Doppler sonographic examination of bloodflow in the umbilical artery. vUmbilical arterial Doppler assessment is used in surveillance of fetal health in the third trimester.

HP_0025716.label: fetal anemia
HP_0025716.definition: Low hemoglobin/hematocrit in a fetus as evidenced by percutaneous umbilical cord sampling and Doppler ultrasonographic assessment of the peak velocity of systolic blood flow in the middle cerebral artery.
HP_0025716.UMLS synonyms: Fetal anemia | Anemia following fetal blood loss | Fetal twin anemia-polycythemia sequence | fetal anemia as antepartum condition | fetal anemia with baby delivered | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, unspecified trimester, not applicable or unspecified | Congenital anemia from fetal blood loss | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, first trimester | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, second trimester | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, third trimester | fetal; anemia, due to ABO (antibodies) (isoimmunization) (maternal/fetal incompatibility) | fetal; anemia, due to Rh (antibodies) (isoimmunization) (maternal/fetal incompatibility) | congenital anemia following fetal-twin blood donation | anemia; fetus or newborn, following fetal blood loss | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, second trimester, other fetus | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, unspecified trimester, fetus 3 | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, unspecified trimester, fetus 5 | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, first trimester, fetus 2 | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, first trimester, other fetus | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, second trimester, fetus 1 | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, third trimester, fetus 3 | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, unspecified trimester, other fetus | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, first trimester, fetus 4 | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, second trimester, fetus 2 | Fetal anemia and thrombocytopenia, second trimester, fetus 4

HP_0025717.label: skeletal muscle autophagosome accumulation
HP_0025717.definition: Abnormal accumulation of autophagosomes in skeletal muscle tissue.

HP_0025718.label: skeletal muscle hyperechogenicity
HP_0025718.definition: An increased echo intensity of muscle tissue on sonography, defined as an increased amount of returning echoes per square area of muscle tissue. On cross-section, normal muscle appears as a relatively anechoic structure with hyperechoic speckles within the tissue representing perimysial septa, giving it a starry night appearance. The boundaries of each muscle are delineated by the presence of hyperechoic fascia. In muscle disorders, one of the hallmark findings is replacement of healthy muscle with fat and fibrosis, manifested by an increase in echogenicity from higher sound transitions in the muscle. This increase in echogenicity is most distinct in conditions that lead to chronic pathology, such as long-standing muscle inflammation, dystrophy, or denervation.

HP_0025719.label: maternal vascular malperfusion
HP_0025719.definition: Gross findings of maternal vascular malperfusion include placental hypoplasia, placental infarction, and retroplacental hemorrhage. If information is available, it is preferable to annotate using the HPO terms that corresponding to the specific abnormalities.

HP_0025720.label: limited horizontal extraocular movement
HP_0025720.definition: Limited mobility of the eye to move from side to side (horizontally) within its socket.

HP_0025721.label: limited vertical extraocular movement
HP_0025721.definition: Limited mobility of the eye to move up and down (vertically) within its socket.

HP_0025722.label: cerebral infarct
HP_0025722.definition: A necrotic lesion in the cerebrum resulting from a sudden insufficiency of arterial or venous blood supply due to emboli, thrombi or mechanical factors.
HP_0025722.UMLS synonyms: Cerebral Infarction | Silent cerebral infarct | Cerebral septic infarct | Cerebral infarct pathology | Posterior cerebral circulation infarct | CEREBRAL CVA MICRO INFARCT | Infarction, Middle Cerebral Artery | Hemichorea due to cerebral infarction | Cerebral ischemic stroke due to global hypoperfusion with watershed infarct | Multi-infarct state | Cerebral infarction due to thrombosis of precerebral arteries | late effects of cerebral infarction: monoplegia of lower limb affecting left nondominant side | late effects of cerebral infarction: monoplegia of lower limb affecting right nondominant side | late effects of cerebral infarction: monoplegia of upper limb affecting left nondominant side | late effects of cerebral infarction: monoplegia of upper limb affecting right nondominant side | Other cerebral infarction | Hemorrhagic cerebral infarction | Sequelae of cerebral infarction | Cerebral infarction foetal | Occipital cerebral infarction | Ischaemic cerebral infarction | Cerebral infarction due to thrombosis of cerebral arteries | Multiple cerebral infarction | Thrombotic cerebral infarction | Asymptomatic cerebral infarction

HP_0025723.label: abnormal fetal skin morphology
HP_0025723.definition: Any structural anomaly of the skin of the fetus or newborn. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.

HP_0025724.label: caseous vernix - like desquamation
HP_0025724.definition: Vernix caseosa is a physiological, viscous biofilm that is produced by desquamated fetal skin and sebaceous glands covering the fetus at the third trimester in-utero. The substance's gross morphology in post-partum is described by the etymology, as vernix means varnish, and caseosa means cheesy-like matter. This finding refers to an abnormally thick and greasy vernix caseosa-like scale present at birth.
HP_0025724.synonyms: greasy , thick vernix caseosa - like scale

HP_0025725.label: type 1 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HP_0025725.definition: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by multiple large cysts or a single dominant cyst.

HP_0025726.label: type 2 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HP_0025726.definition: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by multiple evenly spaced cysts (sponge-like appearance).

HP_0025727.label: type 3 congenital pulmonary airway malformation
HP_0025727.definition: A type of congenital pulmonary airway malformation that is characterized by a bulky firm mass with an adenomatoid appearance.

HP_0025728.label: periventricular pseudocyst
HP_0025728.definition: Pseudocysts that lack an epithelial lining, PVPCs are frequently observed in the caudothalamic groove or in the infero-lateral aspect of the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles, but may also be located elsewhere along the periventricular germinal matrix, as in the temporal or occipital horns.

HP_0025729.label: fetal vascular malperfusion
HP_0025729.definition: The term fetal vascular malperfusion (FVM) is used to describe placental pathology that is throught to result from an obstruction in fetal blood flow that could result from a number of conditions (eg, umbilical cord lesions, hypercoagulability, complications of fetal cardiac dysfunction, such as hypoxia, etc.).

HP_0025730.label: foramen ovale aneurysm
HP_0025730.definition: Foramen ovale aneurysm (FOA) or atrial septal aneurysm is abnormal redundancy of the atrial septum primum, with bulging of the septum by at least half the width of the atrial chamber, or by at least 10 mm beyond the level of the atrial septum. The abnormal protrusion of the interatrial septum results in decreased left atrial volume. On color Doppler there is reduced left ventricular inflow.
HP_0025730.synonyms: fetal atrial septal dilatation | foetal atrial septal dilatation | redundant septum primum flap

HP_0030000.label: emg : repetitive nerve stimulation abnormality
HP_0030000.definition: Abnormality observed upon electromyography when nerve studied is electrically stimulated six to ten times at 2 or 3 Hertz.

HP_0030001.label: lagophthalmos
HP_0030001.definition: A condition in which the eyelids do not close to cover the eye completely.
HP_0030001.synonyms: eyelids stay open | inability to close the eyelids
HP_0030001.UMLS synonyms: Lagophthalmos | Cicatricial Lagophthalmos | Paralytic Lagophthalmos | Mechanical lagophthalmos | Nocturnal Lagophthalmos | Lagophthalmos measurement | Iatrogenic Lagophthalmos | Blink Lagophthalmos | lagophthalmos; keratoconjunctivitis | Lower lid lagophthalmos | correction of lagophthalmos | Cicatricial lagophthalmos of left eyelid | Cicatricial lagophthalmos of right eyelid | lagophthalmos of both eyes | Left upper cicatricial lagophthalmos | Right upper cicatricial lagophthalmos | Lagophthalmos of left eyelid | Lagophthalmos of right eyelid | Cicatricial lagophthalmos of left lower eyelid | Cicatricial lagophthalmos of right lower eyelid | Lagophthalmos of left lower eyelid | Mechanical lagophthalmos of lower eyelid | Lagophthalmos of left upper eyelid | Bilateral lagophthalmos of lower eyelids | Paralytic lagophthalmos of left eyelid

HP_0030002.label: nocturnal lagophthalmos
HP_0030002.definition: The inability to close the eyelids during sleep.
HP_0030002.synonyms: eyelids stay open at night | inability to close the eyelids at night

HP_0030003.label: paralytic lagophthalmos
HP_0030003.definition: A type of lagophthalmos that occurs in association with facial nerve palsy.

HP_0030089.label: abnormal muscle fiber protein expression
HP_0030089.definition: An anomalous amount of protein present in or on the surface of muscle fibers. This feature may be appreciate upon immunohistochemical investigation of muscle biopsy tissue.

HP_0030090.label: abnormal muscle fiber merosin expression
HP_0030090.definition: An anomalous amount of merosin in muscle fibers. Merosin is a basement membrane-associated protein found in placenta, striated muscle, and peripheral nerve.

HP_0030091.label: absent muscle fiber merosin
HP_0030091.definition: Lack of merosin protein in the muscle biopsy.
HP_0030091.synonyms: absent merosin staining in muscle biopsy | absent muscle fiber laminin alpha 2 | absent muscle fibre laminin alpha 2 | absent muscle fibre merosin

HP_0030092.label: reduced muscle fiber merosin
HP_0030092.definition: A reduced amount of merosin in muscle fibers. This feature is usually assessed by immunohistochemical examination of muscle biopsy tissue.

HP_0030093.label: abnormal muscle fiber laminin beta 1
HP_0030093.definition: A deviation from normal of the amount of laminin beta 1 in muscle fiber tissue. Laminin 2 is a major component of the basal lamina of skeletal muscle cells. It is a heterotrimer composed of 3 chains: merosin (laminin alpha 2 chain), beta 1, and gamma 1.

HP_0030094.label: reduced muscle fiber laminin beta 1
HP_0030094.definition: A reduced amount of laminin beta 1 in muscle fiber tissue. Laminin 2 is a major component of the basal lamina of skeletal muscle cells. It is a heterotrimer composed of 3 chains: merosin (laminin alpha 2 chain), beta 1, and gamma 1.

HP_0030095.label: reduced muscle collagen vi
HP_0030095.definition: A decreased amount of collagen VI in muscle tissue. Collagen VI is a primarily associated with the extracellular matrix of skeletal muscle.

HP_0030096.label: abnormal muscle fiber dystrophin expression
HP_0030096.definition: A deviation from normal in the amount of dystrophin in muscle fiber tissue. Dystrophin is located at the muscle sarcolemma in a membrane-spanning protein complex that connects the cytoskeleton to the basal lamina.

HP_0030097.label: absent muscle dystrophin expression
HP_0030097.definition: Lack of dystrophin in muscle tissue. Immunohistochemistry reveals absent dystrophin protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030098.label: reduced muscle dystrophin expression
HP_0030098.definition: A decreased amount of dystrophin in muscle fiber tissue.

HP_0030099.label: reduced muscle fiber alpha dystroglycan
HP_0030099.definition: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced alpha dystroglycan protein in the muscle biopsy. Alpha-dystroglycan is a heavily glycosylated peripheral-membrane component of the dystrophin-associated glycoprotein complex (DAPC), which, in addition to laminin alpha2, binds perlecan and agrin in the extracellular matrix, whereas beta-dystroglycan, derived from the same gene, is a transmembrane protein that links to dystrophin intracellularly.

HP_0030100.label: abnormal muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
HP_0030100.definition: Deviation from normal in the amount of alpha sarcoglycan in muscle. The alpha, beta, gamma, and delta sarcoglycans are components of the dystrophin-complex. They are all N-glycosylated transmembrane proteins with a short intra-cellular domain, a single transmembrane region and a large extra-cellular domain containing a cluster of conserved cysteines.

HP_0030101.label: absent muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
HP_0030101.definition: Lack of alpha sarcoglycan in muscle. Immunohistochemistry reveals absent alpha sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030102.label: reduced muscle fiber alpha sarcoglycan
HP_0030102.definition: A decreased amount of alpha sarcoglycan in muscle. Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced alpha sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030103.label: abnormal muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
HP_0030103.definition: Deviation from normal in the amount of beta sarcoglycan in muscle. The alpha, beta, gamma, and delta sarcoglycans are components of the dystrophin-complex. They are all N-glycosylated transmembrane proteins with a short intra-cellular domain, a single transmembrane region and a large extra-cellular domain containing a cluster of conserved cysteines.

HP_0030104.label: abnormal muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
HP_0030104.definition: Deviation from normal in the amount of gamma sarcoglycan in muscle. The alpha, beta, gamma, and delta sarcoglycans are components of the dystrophin-complex. They are all N-glycosylated transmembrane proteins with a short intra-cellular domain, a single transmembrane region and a large extra-cellular domain containing a cluster of conserved cysteines.

HP_0030105.label: abnormal muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
HP_0030105.definition: Deviation from normal in the amount of delta sarcoglycan in muscle. The alpha, beta, gamma, and delta sarcoglycans are components of the dystrophin-complex. They are all N-glycosylated transmembrane proteins with a short intra-cellular domain, a single transmembrane region and a large extra-cellular domain containing a cluster of conserved cysteines.

HP_0030106.label: absent muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
HP_0030106.definition: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of beta sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030107.label: reduced muscle fiber beta sarcoglycan
HP_0030107.definition: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced beta sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030108.label: reduced muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
HP_0030108.definition: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced gamma sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030109.label: absent muscle fiber gamma sarcoglycan
HP_0030109.definition: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of gamma sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030110.label: absent muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
HP_0030110.definition: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of delta sarcoglycan protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030111.label: reduced muscle fiber delta sarcoglycan
HP_0030111.definition: Abnormally reduced amount of delta sarcoglycan in muscle.

HP_0030112.label: abnormal muscle fiber alpha dystroglycan
HP_0030112.definition: A deviation from normal of muscle alpha-dystroglcan expression. Alpha-dystroglycan is a heavily glycosylated peripheral-membrane component of the dystrophin-associated glycoprotein complex (DAPC), which, in addition to laminin alpha2, binds perlecan and agrin in the extracellular matrix, whereas beta-dystroglycan, derived from the same gene, is a transmembrane protein that links to dystrophin intracellularly.

HP_0030113.label: abnormal muscle fiber dysferlin
HP_0030113.definition: A deviation from normal in the expression of dysferlin in muscle tissue. Dysferlin is an ubiquitous 230-kDa transmembrane protein involved in calcium-mediated sarcolemma resealing.

HP_0030114.label: absent muscle fiber dysferlin
HP_0030114.definition: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of dysferlin protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030115.label: reduced muscle fiber dysferlin
HP_0030115.definition: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced dysferlin protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030116.label: abnormal muscle fiber emerin
HP_0030116.definition: A deviation from normal of the amount of the inner nuclear membrane protein emerin in muscle tissue.

HP_0030117.label: absent muscle fiber emerin
HP_0030117.definition: Immunohistochemistry shows complete lack of emerin protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030118.label: reduced muscle fiber emerin
HP_0030118.definition: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced emerin protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030119.label: abnormal muscle fiber calpain - 3
HP_0030119.definition: A deviation from normal in the amount of calpain-3 in muscle tissue. Calpains are intracellular nonlysosomal cysteine proteases modulated by calcium ions. A typical calpain is a heterodimer composed of two distinct subunits, one large (over 80 kDa) and the other small (30 kDa). While only one gene encoding the small subunit has been demonstrated, there are many genes for the large one. CAPN3 is similar to ubiquitous Calpain 1 and 2 (m-calpain and micro-calpain), but contains specific insertion sequences (NS, IS1 and IS2). Calpains cleave target proteins to modify their properties, rather than breaking down the substrates.

HP_0030120.label: absent muscle fiber calpain - 3
HP_0030120.definition: Western blot shows complete lack of calpain-3 protein in the muscle biopsy tissue.

HP_0030121.label: reduced muscle fiber calpain - 3
HP_0030121.definition: Western blot reveals reduced calpain-3 protein in the muscle biopsy tissue.

HP_0030122.label: reduced muscle fiber perlecan
HP_0030122.definition: Immunohistochemistry reveals reduced perlecan protein in the muscle biopsy. Perlecan is a basement membrane-specific heparan sulfate proteoglycan core protein (HSPG) also known as heparan sulfate proteoglycan 2 (HSPG2).

HP_0030123.label: abnormal muscle fiber lamin a / c
HP_0030123.definition: A deviation from the normal amount of lamin A/C in muscle tissue. The LMNA gene gives rise to at least three splicing isoforms including the two main isoforms, lamin A and lamin C. These are constitutive components of the fibrous nuclear lamina and have different roles, ranging from mechanical nuclear membrane maintenance to gene regulation.
HP_0030123.synonyms: abnormal muscle fibre lamin a / c

HP_0030124.label: reduced muscle fiber lamin a / c
HP_0030124.definition: A decreased amount of lamin A/C in muscle tissue. This feature can be shown by immunohistochemistry or Western blotting of muscle tissue.

HP_0030153.definition: Cholangiocarcinoma is a primary cancer originating in the biliary epithelium i.e., the cholangiocytes, of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic biliary ducts. It is extremely invasive, develops rapidly, often metastasizes, and has a very poor prognosis. They are slow growing tumors which spread longitudinally along the bile ducts with neural, perineural and subepithelial extension.

HP_0030158.definition: Cervical ectropion occurs when eversion of the endocervix exposes columnar epithelium to the vaginal milieu

HP_0030161.definition: A sensation of itching in the vagina.

HP_0030165.label: temporal artery tortuosity
HP_0030165.definition: The presence of an increased number of twists and turns of the temporal artery.

HP_0030167.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against mitochondria.

HP_0030168.definition: Increase in diameter of the veins located underneath the skin of the abdomen.

HP_0030170.label: cystic artery pseudoaneurysm
HP_0030170.definition: Presence of a pseudoaneurysm in the artery that supplies the gallbladder and cystic duct with blood. A pseudoaneurysm, also known as a false aneurysm, forms when blood leaks through a breach of the arterial wall but is contained by the adventitia or surrounding perivascular soft tissue.

HP_0030171.label: perirenal hematoma
HP_0030171.definition: A collection of clotted blood surrounding the kidney.

HP_0030172.label: peripheral amyelination
HP_0030172.definition: Congenital absence of the myelin sheath on a nerve.

HP_0030174.label: increased peripheral myelin thickness
HP_0030174.definition: Elevated thickness of the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves, in a regular and concentric fashion.

HP_0030175.label: myelin tomacula
HP_0030175.definition: The presence of multiple sausage-shaped swellings of the myelin sheath (The Latin tomaculum means sausage).
HP_0030175.UMLS synonyms: Tomacula (sausage-shaped swellings of the myelin sheath) on nerve biopsy | Tomaculae (paranodal myelin swellings)

HP_0030176.label: asymmetric peripheral demyelination
HP_0030176.definition: Loss of myelin from peripheral nerves in a pattern that differs between right and left.

HP_0030177.label: abnormality of peripheral nervous system electrophysiology
HP_0030177.definition: An abnormality of the function of the electrical signals with which peripheral nerve cells communicate with each other or with muscles.

HP_0030178.label: abnormality of central nervous system electrophysiology

HP_0030179.label: abnormal peripheral action potential amplitude
HP_0030179.definition: An anomaly in the magnitude of the action potential along a peripheral nerve, that is, of the rapid rise and fall of the electrical membrane potential of the nerve.

HP_0030180.label: oppenheim reflex
HP_0030180.definition: Dorsiflexion of the big toe, sometimes accompanied by fanning of the other toes, elicited by stroking along the medial side of the tibia (the normal response would be no movement of the big toe).

HP_0030181.label: gordon reflex
HP_0030181.definition: Dorsal extension of the big toe, sometimes accompanied by fanning of the other toes, elicited by compressing the calf muscles (a normal response is no movement of the big toe).

HP_0030182.label: tetraplegia / tetraparesis
HP_0030182.definition: Loss of strength in all four limbs. Tetraplegia refers to a complete loss of strength, whereas Tetraparesis refers to an incomplete loss of strength.
HP_0030182.UMLS synonyms: Paralytic syndrome of all four limbs as sequela of stroke

HP_0030183.label: impaired visually enhanced vestibulo - ocular reflex
HP_0030183.definition: The vestibulo-ocular reflex is responsible for the stabilization of the retinal image during movement. The visual vestibular ocular reflex (VVOR) or visual enhanced VOR, maintains ocular stability during head motion by generating compensatory eye movement opposite to head movement, and is a major component of visual vestibular interaction. This feature is an impairment of this reflex, manifested as the combined impairment of the three compensatory eye movement reflexes, namely the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), smooth pursuit (SP) and optokinetic reflex (OKR).
HP_0030183.synonyms: visually enhanced vestibulo - ocular reflex impairment | vvor impairment

HP_0030185.label: isometric tremor
HP_0030185.definition: An isometric tremor occurs with muscle contraction against a rigid stationary object (e.g., when making a fist).

HP_0030186.label: kinetic tremor
HP_0030186.definition: Tremor that occurs during any voluntary movement. It may include visually or non-visually guided movements. Tremor during target directed movement is called intention tremor.
HP_0030186.UMLS synonyms: Kinetic tremor | Intention tremor | Action Tremor | MDS-UPDRS - Kinetic Tremor of Left Hand | MDS-UPDRS - Kinetic Tremor of Right Hand | Low-amplitude high-frequency kinetic tremor of hands

HP_0030187.label: titubation
HP_0030187.definition: Nodding movement of the head or body.
HP_0030187.UMLS synonyms: Titubation | Cerebellar ataxic gait | Trunk titubation | Cryptus titubator | Head titubations | Staggering gait

HP_0030188.label: tremor by anatomical site
HP_0030188.definition: Tremor classified by the affected body part.

HP_0030190.label: oral motor hypotonia
HP_0030190.definition: Reduced muscle tone of oral musculature. In infants, this feature may be associated with difficulties in breast feeding, and may affect the latch, jaw motions, tongue placement, lip seal, suck/swallow/breathe pattern and overall feeding behavior.

HP_0030191.label: abnormal peripheral nervous system synaptic transmission
HP_0030191.definition: An anomaly in the communication from a neuron to a target across a synapse in the peripheral nervous system.

HP_0030192.label: fatigable weakness of bulbar muscles
HP_0030192.definition: A type of weakness of the bulbar muscles (muscles of the mouth and throat responsible for speech and swallowing) that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030193.label: fatigable weakness of chewing muscles
HP_0030193.definition: A type of weakness of the muscles involved in chewing that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030194.label: fatigable weakness of speech muscles
HP_0030194.definition: A type of weakness of the muscles involved in speech that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030195.label: fatigable weakness of swallowing muscles
HP_0030195.definition: A type of weakness of the muscles involved in swallowing that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030196.label: fatigable weakness of respiratory muscles
HP_0030196.definition: A type of weakness of the muscles involved in breathing (respiration) that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030197.label: fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles
HP_0030197.definition: A type of weakness of skeletal muscle that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030198.label: fatigable weakness of distal limb muscles
HP_0030198.definition: A type of weakness of a skeletal muscle of distal part of a limb that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030199.label: fatigable weakness of neck muscles
HP_0030199.definition: A type of weakness of a skeletal muscle in the neck that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030200.label: fatiguable weakness of proximal limb muscles
HP_0030200.definition: A type of weakness of a skeletal muscle of proximal part of a limb that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.

HP_0030201.label: response to drugs acting on neuromuscular transmission
HP_0030201.definition: Specific drugs interfere selectively with the different cellular mechanisms involved in neuromuscular transmission (synthesis, storage, release, action and inactivation of transmitter). The response of a patient to a specific drug can therefore be useful information for the differential diagnosis.

HP_0030202.label: favorable response of weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitors
HP_0030202.definition: Improvement of muscle strength in response to administration of an acetylcholine esterase inhibitor.
HP_0030202.synonyms: favourable response of weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitors

HP_0030203.label: unfavorable response of muscle weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitors
HP_0030203.definition: Lack of improvement of muscle strength in response to administration of an acetylcholine esterase inhibitor.
HP_0030203.synonyms: unfavourable response of muscle weakness to acetylcholine esterase inhibitors

HP_0030205.label: increased jitter at single fiber emg
HP_0030205.definition: The variation in the time interval between the two action potentials of the same motor unit is called jitter. This term therefore applies to increased variability in the interval between successive action potentials of the same motor unit, which is measured by electromyography (EMG).
HP_0030205.synonyms: increased jitter at single fibre electromyography | increased jitter at single fibre emg

HP_0030206.label: emg : incremental response of compound muscle action potential to repetitive nerve stimulation
HP_0030206.definition: A compound muscle action potential (CMAP) is a type of electromyography (EMG). CMAP refers to a group of almost simultaneous action potentials from several muscle fibers in the same area evoked by stimulation of the supplying motor nerve and are recorded as one multipeaked summated action potential. This abnormality refers to an abnormal increase in the amplitude during the course of the investigation.

HP_0030207.label: paradoxical respiration
HP_0030207.definition: Breathing movements in which the chest wall moves in on inspiration and out on expiration, in reverse of the normal movements. It may be seen in children with respiratory distress of any cause, which leads to indrawing of the intercostal spaces during inspiration. Patients with chronic airways obstruction also show indrawing of the lower ribs during inspiration, due to the distorted action of a depressed and flattened diaphragm. Crush injuries of the chest, with fractured ribs and sternum, can lead to a severe degree of paradoxical breathing.
HP_0030207.UMLS synonyms: Paradoxical respiration | Paradoxical movement of vocal cord on respiration

HP_0030208.label: anti - acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity
HP_0030208.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against ganglioside-monosialic acid (GM1), which is a type of glycosphingolipid with one sialic acid. GM1 is located on the outer layer of the plasma membrane, and plays a vital role in neurogenesis, nerve development, differentiation and repair after injury.
HP_0030208.synonyms: acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity | anti - achr antibody positivity

HP_0030209.label: calcium channel antibody positivity
HP_0030209.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against voltage-gated calcium channels.
HP_0030209.synonyms: ca channel antibody positivity | ca2+ channel antibody positivity

HP_0030210.label: anti - muscle - specific tyrosine kinase antibody
HP_0030210.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against muscle specific kinase (anti-MuSK Ab).
HP_0030210.synonyms: anti - muscle - specific tyrosine kinase antibody | anti - musk antibodies | muscle specific kinase antibody positivity
HP_0030210.UMLS synonyms: myasthenia gravis anti-skeletal muscle antibody | Muscle specific kinase antibody positivity

HP_0030211.label: slow pupillary light response
HP_0030211.definition: Reduced velocity and acceleration in the pupillary light response.

HP_0030212.label: collectionism
HP_0030212.definition: Excessive or pathological tendency to save and collect possessions.

HP_0030213.label: emotional blunting
HP_0030213.definition: Inability to feel positive or negative emotions, feelings of detachment, or reduced emotional responsiveness.

HP_0030214.label: hypersexuality
HP_0030214.definition: Pathological persistent sexual disinhibiting behavior, directed towards oneself or others.
HP_0030214.UMLS synonyms: Hypersexuality state | Compulsive Sexual Behavior Disorder | Hypersexualism | hypersexual; complex

HP_0030215.label: inappropriate crying
HP_0030215.definition: Uncontrolled episodes of crying occur without any apparent motivating stimuli.
HP_0030215.UMLS synonyms: Inappropriate crying or screaming (< 2 years of age) | Confused (>2 yrs); Cries but is consolable, inappropriate interactions (<=2 yrs) | non-infant: Inappropriate words; non-verbal infant: Cries to pain, screams to pain

HP_0030216.label: inertia
HP_0030216.definition: Reduction of goal-directed behaviors linked to the impairment in frontal executive functions (planning of an action for example).

HP_0030217.label: limb apraxia
HP_0030217.definition: Difficulty in performing the correct execution of limbs movements in absence of motor impairment.
HP_0030217.UMLS synonyms: Apraxia, Ideomotor | Unusual aura symptoms include alien limb phenomenon, diplopia, apraxia, dysarthria, impaired hearing, vertigo

HP_0030218.label: punding
HP_0030218.definition: Punding is a stereotypical motor behavior characterized by an intense fascination with repetitive, excessive and non-goal oriented handling, and examining of objects.

HP_0030219.label: semantic dementia
HP_0030219.definition: A progressive loss of the ability to remember the meaning of words, faces and objects.

HP_0030220.label: socially inappropriate behavior
HP_0030220.definition: Behavior that is not in line with social norms.
HP_0030220.synonyms: socially inappropriate behavior | socially inappropriate behaviour
HP_0030220.UMLS synonyms: Disruptive or socially inappropriate behavior | Does your child often do or say things that are tactless or socially inappropriate:Find:Pt:^Patient:Ord:CAST | Disruptive, infantile, or socially inappropriate behavior (excludes verbal actions) | Inappropriate social behavior | social interaction nonverbal behaviors inappropriate emotions | Alterability of socially inappropriate or disruptive behavioral symptoms | Frequency of socially inappropriate or disruptive behavioral symptoms | Frequency of socially inappropriate or disruptive behavioral symptoms:NRat:Pt:^Patient:Qn:MDS | Alterability of socially inappropriate or disruptive behavioral symptoms:Find:Pt:^Patient:Ord:MDS

HP_0030221.label: sweet craving
HP_0030221.definition: Excessive desire to eat sweet foods.

HP_0030222.label: visual agnosia
HP_0030222.definition: The condition is known as visual agnosia, which refers to the inability to recognize objects that are visually presented, even though the individual may have normal visual field, acuity, color vision, brightness discrimination, language, and memory.
HP_0030222.UMLS synonyms: Visual Agnosia | Primary visual agnosia | Visual agnosia absent | Visual agnosia present | Visual Agnosia for Objects | Alexia, Pure

HP_0030223.label: perseverative thought
HP_0030223.definition: Manifestations of perseverative thoughts are behaviors that do not meet the demands of the situation, are not the product of deliberation, and may unfold despite counter intention.

HP_0030224.label: abnormal muscle fiber desmin
HP_0030224.definition: A deviation from normal in the expression of desmin in muscle tissue. Desmin is an 53-kDa protein.

HP_0030225.label: accumulation of muscle fiber desmin
HP_0030225.definition: Immunohistochemistry shows accumulation of desmin protein in the muscle biopsy.
HP_0030225.synonyms: accumulation of muscle fibre desmin | muscle fiber desmin - reactive inclusion bodies | muscle fibre desmin - reactive inclusion bodies

HP_0030226.label: abnormal muscle fiber myotilin
HP_0030226.definition: A deviation from normal in the expression of myotilin in muscle tissue. Myotilin is a 57kDa cytoskeletal protein.

HP_0030227.label: accumulation of muscle fiber myotilin
HP_0030227.definition: Immunohistochemistry shows accumulation of myotilin protein in the muscle biopsy.

HP_0030228.label: abnormal muscle fiber valosin - containing protein
HP_0030228.definition: A deviation from normal in the expression of valosin-containing protein in muscle tissue. Valosin-containing protein is an ubiquitously expressed multifunctional 100-kD protein that is a member of the AAA+ (ATPase associated with various activities) protein family.
HP_0030228.synonyms: abnormal muscle fibre valosin - containing protein

HP_0030229.label: accumulation of muscle fiber valosin - containing protein
HP_0030229.definition: Immunohistochemistry shows accumulation of valosin-containing protein in the muscle biopsy.
HP_0030229.synonyms: accumulation of muscle fibre valosin - containing protein

HP_0030230.label: central core regions in muscle fibers
HP_0030230.definition: The presence of disorganized areas called cores in the center of muscle fibers. There is a typical appearance of the biopsy on light microscopy, where the muscle cells have cores that are devoid of mitochondria and specific enzymes. Cores are typically well demarcated and centrally located, but may occasionally be multiple and of eccentric.
HP_0030230.synonyms: central core regions in muscle fibres

HP_0030231.label: glycogen accumulation in muscle fiber lysosomes
HP_0030231.definition: An increased amount of glycogen in muscle tissue found specifically in lysosomes.
HP_0030231.synonyms: glycogen accumulation in muscle fibre lysosomes

HP_0030232.label: increased sarcoplasmic glycogen
HP_0030232.definition: Elevated glycogen content in the sarcoplasm (cytoplasm) of muscle fibers.

HP_0030233.label: bethlem sign
HP_0030233.definition: Limitation of wrist and finger extension on asking patient to form a prayer sign. This is a result of progressive wrist and finger flexion contractures.

HP_0030234.label: highly elevated creatine kinase
HP_0030234.definition: An increased CPK level between 4X and 50X above the upper normal level.
HP_0030234.synonyms: highly elevated cpk | highly elevated creatine phosphokinase | highly elevated serum ck | highly elevated serum cpk | highly elevated serum phosph - ck

HP_0030235.label: extremely elevated creatine kinase
HP_0030235.definition: An increased creatine kinase level more than 50X above the upper normal level.
HP_0030235.synonyms: extremely elevated cpk | extremely elevated creatine phosphokinase | extremely elevated phospho - ck serum level | extremely elevated serum ck level | extremely high cpk level

HP_0030236.label: abnormality of muscle size
HP_0030236.definition: Abnormalities of the overall muscle bulk based on clinical observation.

HP_0030237.label: hand muscle weakness
HP_0030237.definition: Reduced strength of the musculature of the hand.
