HP_0030239.label: hypoplasia of the upper arm musculature
HP_0030239.definition: Underdevelopment of the musculature of the upper arm, which may include the deltoid, the triceps, the biceps, and the brachioradialis.

HP_0030242.label: portal vein thrombosis
HP_0030242.definition: Thrombosis of the portal vein and/or its tributaries, which include the splenic vein and the superior and inferior mesenteric veins.
HP_0030242.UMLS synonyms: Portal Vein Thrombosis | Portal Vein Thrombosis, CTCAE | Grade 3 Portal Vein Thrombosis, CTCAE | Grade 5 Portal Vein Thrombosis, CTCAE | Grade 2 Portal Vein Thrombosis, CTCAE | Grade 4 Portal Vein Thrombosis, CTCAE | Portal Vein Thrombosis Gene Mutation Detection Reagents

HP_0030243.label: hepatic vein thrombosis
HP_0030243.definition: An obstruction in the veins of the liver caused by a blood clot (thrombosis).
HP_0030243.synonyms: blood clot in liver vein | hepatic venous thrombosis
HP_0030243.UMLS synonyms: Hepatic Vein Thrombosis | echocardiography: hepatic veins thrombosis

HP_0030244.label: maternal fever in pregnancy
HP_0030244.definition: The occurence of an elevated body temperature of the mother during pregnancy.

HP_0030245.label: intrapartum fever
HP_0030245.definition: The occurence of maternal fever during labor.
HP_0030245.synonyms: maternal fever during labor | maternal fever during labour

HP_0030246.label: maternal first trimester fever
HP_0030246.definition: The occurence of fever in a mother during the first trimester of pregnancy.

HP_0030247.label: splanchnic vein thrombosis
HP_0030247.definition: The term splanchnic vein thrombosis encompasses Budd-Chiari syndrome (hepatic vein thrombosis), extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO), and mesenteric vein thrombosis; the word splanchnic is used to refer to the visceral organs (of the abdominal cavity).

HP_0030248.label: mesenteric venous thrombosis
HP_0030248.definition: A clot that obstructs blood flow in a mesenteric vein (the superior and the inferior mesenteric vein drain blood from the small and large intestine).
HP_0030248.UMLS synonyms: Mesenteric Venous Thrombosis | Superior mesenteric vein thrombosis | Inferior mesenteric vein thrombosis

HP_0030249.label: enanthema
HP_0030249.definition: A sudden eruption (rash) of the surface of a mucous membrane of the mouth or pharynx.
HP_0030249.UMLS synonyms: Mucous membrane eruption | enanthema; viral | Drug enanthema | Pharyngeal enanthema | Mucous membrane eruption of oral mucous membrane

HP_0030250.label: pulmonary granulomatosis
HP_0030250.definition: The presence of multiple granulomata (small nodular inflammatory lesions containing grouped mononuclear phagocytes) in the lung.
HP_0030250.UMLS synonyms: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis of lung | Pulmonary Histiocytosis X | Pulmonary disease due to allergic granulomatosis angiitis

HP_0030251.label: absence of memory b cells
HP_0030251.definition: Complete lack of memory B cells, that is, of mature B cell type that is long-lived, readily activated upon re-encounter of its antigenic determinant, and has been selected for expression of higher affinity immunoglobulin.
HP_0030251.UMLS synonyms: Absence of class-switched memory B cells

HP_0030252.label: absent circulating b cells
HP_0030252.definition: Complete lack of mature B cells, that is, of B cells that have left the bone marrow.
HP_0030252.UMLS synonyms: Low or absent circulating B cells | Decreased or absent circulating B cells

HP_0030253.label: defective t cell proliferation
HP_0030253.definition: A reduced ability of a T cell population to expand by cell division following T cell activation.
HP_0030253.UMLS synonyms: Defective CD8+ T cell proliferation after stimulation | Defective T-cell proliferation in response to stimulation | Defects in T-cell activation and proliferation

HP_0030254.label: nail bed hemorrhage
HP_0030254.definition: Small areas of bleeding (hemorrhage) under the fingernail or toenail.

HP_0030255.label: large intestinal polyposis
HP_0030255.definition: The presence of multiple polyps in the large intestine.
HP_0030255.UMLS synonyms: Adenomatous Polyposis Coli | retention polyposis coli of large intestine | congenital polyposis coli of large intestine | benign polyposis coli of large intestine | large intestine biopsy benign polyposis coli | large intestine biopsy: congenital polyposis coli | large intestine biopsy: familial polyposis coli | large intestine biopsy: polyposis coli retention | benign familial polyposis coli of large intestine | adenocarcinoma in adenomatous polyposis coli of large intestine | biopsy of large intestine: adenocarcinoma in adenomatous polyposis coli | adenocarcinoma in situ in familial polyposis coli of large intestine | biopsy of large intestine showed adenocarcinoma in situ in familial polyposis coli

HP_0030256.label: small intestinal polyposis
HP_0030256.definition: The presence of multiple polyps in the small intestine.

HP_0030257.label: freckled genitalia
HP_0030257.definition: One or more brown punctate macules on the skin of the genitalia.

HP_0030258.label: hyperpigmented genitalia
HP_0030258.definition: Localized or generalized increased genital pigmentation.

HP_0030259.label: hypopigmented genitalia
HP_0030259.definition: Localized or generalized decreased genital pigmentation.

HP_0030260.label: microphallus
HP_0030260.definition: Length of penis more than 2 SD below the mean for age accompanied by hypospadias.
HP_0030260.UMLS synonyms: Microphallus <Microphallidae> | Small penis | Euryhaliotrema microphallus | Microphallus basodactylophallus | Microphallus ochotensis | Microphallus pseudopygmaeus | Microphallus triangulatus | Microphallus minutus | Microphallus piriformes | Microphallus pygmaeus | Microphallus turgidus | Microphallus szidati | Microphallus abortivus | Microphallus similis | Microphallus primas | Microphallus calidris | Microphallus fusiformis | Microphallus (46,XY) | Pallister-Hall syndrome

HP_0030261.label: absent penis
HP_0030261.synonyms: absent penis | aphallia | aplasia of the penis | penis aplasia
HP_0030261.UMLS synonyms: penis absent | Congenital absence of penis

HP_0030262.label: narrow penis
HP_0030262.definition: Penile width more than 2 standard deviations (SD) below the mean for age. Alternatively circumference of the flaccid penis more than 2 SD below the mean for age. Alternatively, apparently decreased penile width for age.

HP_0030263.label: torsion of the penis
HP_0030263.definition: Rotated position of the glans, with or without the penile shaft, of 30 degrees or more.

HP_0030264.label: webbed penis
HP_0030264.definition: Ventral skinfold extending from penis to scrotum.

HP_0030265.label: wide penis
HP_0030265.definition: Distance between left and right side of the flaccid penis at the attachment to the skin above the pubic symphysis more than 2 standard deviations above the mean for age.

HP_0030266.label: obsolete abnormality of the sacroiliac notch

HP_0030267.label: calcification of the interosseus membrane of the forearm
HP_0030267.definition: Deposition of calcium salts in the fibrous sheet that connects the radius and the ulna.

HP_0030268.label: hyperplastic callus formation
HP_0030268.definition: Increased growth of callus, the bony and cartilaginous material that forms a connecting bridge across a bone fracture during fracture healing.
HP_0030268.UMLS synonyms: Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase during hyperplastic callus formation | Increased urinary collagen type I N-telopeptide excretion (NTx) during hyperplastic callus formation

HP_0030269.label: increased circulating insulin - like growth factor 1 concentration
HP_0030269.definition: An elevated level of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) in the blood circulation.
HP_0030269.synonyms: elevated serum igf1 | increased serum igf1 | increased serum insulin - like growth factor 1

HP_0030270.label: elevated red cell adenosine deaminase activity
HP_0030270.definition: Increase in the level of adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzyme involved in purine metabolism, within erythrocytes. ADA is involved in the catabolism of adenosine.
HP_0030270.UMLS synonyms: Elevated adenosine deaminase (ADA) activity in red cell precursors

HP_0030271.label: reduced erythrocyte 2,3 - diphosphoglycerate concentration
HP_0030271.definition: This term refers to an inappropriate low 2,3-DPG concentration in erythrocytes. 2,3-diphosphoglycerate (2,3-DPG) controls the movement of oxygen from red blood cells to tissues. Anemia is usually accompanied by an increased level of 2,3-DPG in order to promote tissue oxygenation.

HP_0030272.label: abnormal erythrocyte enzyme level
HP_0030272.definition: An altered level of any enzyme to act as catalysts within erythrocytes. This term includes changes due to altered activity of an enzyme.

HP_0030273.label: reduced red cell adenosine deaminase level
HP_0030273.definition: Decrease in the level of adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzyme involved in purine metabolism, within erythrocytes. ADA is involved in the catabolism of adenosine.

HP_0030274.label: accessory scrotum
HP_0030274.definition: Additional scrotum, or part of a scrotum in an abnormal location.

HP_0030275.label: ectopic scrotum
HP_0030275.definition: Scrotum in a position other than the usual position inferior to the base of the penis.

HP_0030277.label: abnormal vertebral pedicle morphology
HP_0030277.definition: Abnormal morphology of a vertebral pedical.

HP_0030279.label: hypoplastic l5 vertebral pedicle
HP_0030279.definition: Underdeveloped pedicle of the fifth lumbar vertebra.

HP_0030280.label: rib gap
HP_0030280.definition: Radiolucent focal defect of a rib shaft.
HP_0030280.UMLS synonyms: Gap in ribs | Posterior rib gap defects | Cerebrocostomandibular Syndrome | Microcephaly, Severe, with Skeletal Anomalies including Posterior Rib-Gap Defects

HP_0030281.label: cervical c3 / c4 vertebral fusion
HP_0030281.definition: Fusion of cervical vertebrae at C3 and C4, caused by a failure in the normal segmentation or division of the cervical vertebrae during the early weeks of fetal development.

HP_0030282.label: posterior rib gap
HP_0030282.definition: Radiolucent focal defect of the posterior portion of a rib shaft. The 'gaps' may lead to flail chest.
HP_0030282.UMLS synonyms: Posterior rib gap defects | Microcephaly, Severe, with Skeletal Anomalies including Posterior Rib-Gap Defects

HP_0030283.label: partial absence of the septum pellucidum
HP_0030283.definition: Only part of the septum pellucidum (a thin, triangular, vertical membrane separating the lateral ventricles of the brain) is present. This feature can be appreciated on magnetic resonance tomography or computed tomography of the brain.

HP_0030284.label: triangular tongue
HP_0030284.definition: A form of macrogloassia (increased size of the tongue) characterized by a broad based root of the tongue but a small tongue tip, giving the appearance of a triangle.

HP_0030285.label: splayed superior cerebellar peduncle
HP_0030285.definition: Abnormal splayed configuration (spreading out) of the superior cerebellar peduncle.
HP_0030285.UMLS synonyms: Elevation and splaying of the superior cerebellar peduncles

HP_0030286.label: atrophic superior cerebellar peduncle
HP_0030286.definition: Atrophy of the superior cerebellar peduncle.

HP_0030289.label: flattened femoral epiphysis
HP_0030289.definition: An abnormal flattening of an epiphysis of femur.
HP_0030289.synonyms: flattended end part of thigh bone
HP_0030289.UMLS synonyms: Flattened capital femoral epiphyses | Mildly flattened proximal femoral epiphyses | Small flattened capital femoral epiphyses | Mildly flattened distal femoral epiphyses

HP_0030290.label: unossified sacrum
HP_0030290.definition: Lack of ossification of the sacrum.

HP_0030291.label: lower - limb metaphyseal irregularity
HP_0030291.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of one or more metaphyses of a bone of the leg.
HP_0030291.UMLS synonyms: Irregular metaphyses (upper and lower limbs) | Cupping and irregular widening of metaphyses of lower limb bones

HP_0030292.label: tibial metaphyseal irregularity
HP_0030292.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of a metaphysis of a tibia.

HP_0030293.label: fibular metaphyseal irregularity
HP_0030293.definition: Irregularity of the normally smooth surface of a metaphysis of a fibula.
HP_0030293.synonyms: irregularity of wide portion of calf bone

HP_0030299.label: distal femoral metaphyseal abnormality
HP_0030299.definition: An anomaly of the metaphysis of the distal femur (close to the knee).
HP_0030299.synonyms: abnormality of wide portion of outermost thighbone
HP_0030299.UMLS synonyms: Abnormal striations of distal femoral metaphyses | Abnormal shape of distal femoral metaphyses

HP_0030300.label: 10 pairs of ribs
HP_0030300.definition: Presence of only 10 (instead of the usual 12) pairs of ribs.

HP_0030301.label: abnormality of the anterior commissure
HP_0030301.definition: An anomaly of the anterior commissure, a bundle of nerve fibers that connect the two cerebral hemispheres across the midline. The anterior commissure plays a role in pain sensation and contains decussating fibers from the olfactory tracts.

HP_0030304.label: abnormal number of vertebrae
HP_0030304.definition: A deviation from the normal number of vertebrae in the spinal column.

HP_0030306.label: 11 thoracic vertebrae
HP_0030306.definition: The presence of 11 instead of the normal 12 thoracic vertebrae.

HP_0030307.label: flared lower limb metaphysis
HP_0030307.definition: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of one or more long bones of the leg.
HP_0030307.synonyms: flared metaphysis of lower limb bone

HP_0030308.label: flared distal tibial metaphysis
HP_0030308.definition: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of the distal tibia.
HP_0030308.synonyms: flared outermost metaphysis of shankbone | flared outermost metaphysis of shinbone

HP_0030309.label: flared distal fibular metaphysis
HP_0030309.definition: The presence of a splayed (i.e.,flared) metaphyseal segment of the distal fibula.
HP_0030309.synonyms: flared outermost wide portion of of calf bone

HP_0030310.label: upper extremity joint dislocation
HP_0030310.definition: Displacement or malalignment of one or more joints in the upper extremity (arm).

HP_0030311.label: lower extremity joint dislocation
HP_0030311.definition: Displacement or malalignment of one or more joints in the lower extremity (leg).

HP_0030312.label: obliteration of the calvarial diploe
HP_0030312.definition: Absence of the spongy bone structure (or tissue) of the internal part of the skull cap (i.e., of the calvarial diploe).

HP_0030313.label: abnormal periosteum morphology
HP_0030313.definition: An anomalous structure of the periosteum, i.e., of the membrane that covers the outer surface of bones.

HP_0030314.label: periostosis
HP_0030314.UMLS synonyms: periostosis; hyperplastic | periostosis; with osteomyelitis | Periostosis without osteomyelitis

HP_0030318.label: angular cheilitis
HP_0030318.definition: A type of inflammation of the lips involving one or both of the corners of the mouth.
HP_0030318.synonyms: angular cheilosis | angular stomatitis | commissural cheilitis | inflammation of corners of the mouth | inflammation of oral commisures | red and sore corners of the mouth
HP_0030318.UMLS synonyms: Angular cheilitis | Candida angular cheilitis | Staphylococcal angular cheilitis | Angular cheilitis due to bacterial infection | Cracked lips with angular cheilitis | Angular cheilitis due to nutritional deficiency | Angular cheilitis due to lack of adequate intermaxillary vertical dimension

HP_0030319.label: weakness of facial musculature
HP_0030319.definition: Reduced strength of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve (the seventh cranial nerve).
HP_0030319.synonyms: decreased facial muscle strength | decreased strength of facial muscles | face weakness | facial muscle weakness | facial weakness | myasthenia of facial muscles | reduced facial muscle strength | weakness of face | weakness of facial musculature

HP_0030320.label: increased intervertebral space
HP_0030320.definition: An increase in the vertical distance between adjacent vertebral bodies, observed as an increase in the intervertebral disc space.

HP_0030321.label: abnormal vertebral artery morphology
HP_0030321.definition: An anomaly of the vertebral artery, the major artery of the neck that originates from the subclavian artery and merges to form the single midline basilar artery in a complex called the vertebrobasilar system.

HP_0030322.label: vertebral artery hypoplasia
HP_0030322.UMLS synonyms: echocardiography: hypoplasia of left vertebral artery | echocardiography: hypoplasia of right vertebral artery

HP_0030323.label: unilateral vertebral artery hypoplasia
HP_0030323.definition: Underdevelopment of the vertebral artery on one side.

HP_0030324.label: bilateral vertebral artery hypoplasia
HP_0030324.definition: Underdevelopment of the vertebral artery on both sides.

HP_0030325.label: cervicomedullary schisis
HP_0030325.definition: Fissure within the spinal cord of the neck.

HP_0030326.label: abnormal macrophage count
HP_0030326.definition: An anomaly in the number of macrophages.

HP_0030327.label: abnormal osteoclast count
HP_0030327.definition: An anomaly in the number of osteoclasts in bone tissue, bone-resorbing cells that develop from macrophages. This finding can be observed by histological examination of bone tissue.

HP_0030328.label: decreased osteoclast count
HP_0030328.definition: Decreased number of osteoclasts in bone tissue.

HP_0030329.label: retinal thinning
HP_0030329.definition: Reduced anteroposterior thickness of the retina. This phenotype can be appreciated by retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT).
HP_0030329.UMLS synonyms: Central retinal thinning | Thinning of retinal vessels | optical coherence tomography: retinal thinning | Generalized retinal thinning seen on OCT | Temporal retinal nerve fiber layer thinning | Nasal retinal nerve fiber layer thinning | Outer retinal tissue thinning seen on OCT | Retinal thinning on ocular cohesion tomography (OCT) | Thinning of retinal nerve fiber layer (chronic phase) | Thinning of retinal nerve fiber layer seen on OCT | Thinning of outer retinal layer on optical coherence tomography | Thinning and blurring of all retinal layers seen on OCT | Thinning of peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer seen on OCT | Thinning of retinal nerve fiber layer seen on optical coherence tomography | Thinning of peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer seen on SD-OCT | Thinning of retinal nerve fiber layer seen on OCT (chronic phase) | Retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) thinning and photoreceptor loss correlate with thickness of sub-RPE deposits of lipid, esterified- and non-esterified cholesterol

HP_0030330.label: multinucleated giant chondrocytes in epiphyseal cartilage
HP_0030330.definition: The presence of cartilage cells (chondrocytes) that are substantially increased in size and contain more than one nucleus and are located within the resting zone of the epiphyseal cartilage.

HP_0030331.label: impaired stimulus - induced skin wrinkling
HP_0030331.definition: A reduced ability of the skin of the fingertips to wrinkle when exposed to stimuli such as soaking in water or application of EMLA cream (the fingertip remains smooth).

HP_0030333.label: abnormal alpha - beta t cell morphology
HP_0030333.definition: A structuraly anomaly of T cells that express an alpha-beta T cell receptor.

HP_0030334.label: abnormal cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive , alpha - beta regulatory t cell morphology
HP_0030334.definition: A structural anomaly of a CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta T cell. These cells are regulatory T cells.

HP_0030335.label: abnormal cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive , alpha - beta regulatory t cell count
HP_0030335.definition: A deviation from the normal count of CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cells.

HP_0030336.label: absence of cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive regulatory t cells
HP_0030336.definition: Lack of CD4+CD25+ T regulatory cells.
HP_0030336.synonyms: absence of cd4+cd25+ t regulatory cells | absence of cd4+cd25+ tregs

HP_0030337.label: elevated cd4 - positive , cd25 - positive regulatory t cell count
HP_0030337.definition: An increased number of CD4-positive, CD25-positive regulatory T cells.

HP_0030338.label: abnormal circulating gonadotropin concentration
HP_0030338.definition: An anomaly of the circulating level of a gonadotropin, that is, of a protein hormone secreted by gonadotrope cells of the anterior pituitary of vertebrates. The primary gonadotropins are luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).

HP_0030339.label: decreased circulating gonadotropin concentration
HP_0030339.definition: A reduction of the circulating level of a gonadotropin, that is, of a protein hormone secreted by gonadotrope cells of the anterior pituitary of vertebrates. The primary gonadotropins are luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).

HP_0030341.label: decreased circulating follicle stimulating hormone concentration
HP_0030341.definition: A reduction of the circulating level of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
HP_0030341.synonyms: decreased circulating follicle stimulating hormone level

HP_0030344.label: decreased circulating luteinizing hormone level
HP_0030344.definition: A reduction in the circulating level of luteinizing hormone (LH).

HP_0030345.label: abnormal circulating luteinizing hormone concentration
HP_0030345.definition: An anomaly of the circulating level of luteinizing hormone (LH).
HP_0030345.synonyms: abnormal circulating luteinizing hormone level | abnormal luteinizing hormone level | increased circulating lutropin
HP_0030345.UMLS synonyms: Luteinizing hormone level outside reference range

HP_0030346.label: abnormal circulating follicle - stimulating hormone concentration
HP_0030346.definition: An anomaly of the circulating level of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
HP_0030346.synonyms: abnormal circulating follicle - stimulating hormone level

HP_0030347.label: abnormal circulating androgen level
HP_0030347.definition: An anomaly in the blood concentration of an androgen, that is, of a steroid hormone that controls development and maintenance of masculine characteristics. The androgens include testosterone and Dehydroepiandrosterone.

HP_0030348.label: increased circulating androgen concentration
HP_0030348.definition: An elevation of the blood concentration of an androgen, that is, of a steroid hormone that controls development and maintenance of masculine characteristics. The androgens include testosterone and Dehydroepiandrosterone.

HP_0030349.label: decreased circulating androgen concentration
HP_0030349.definition: A reduction in the blood concentration of an androgen, that is, of a steroid hormone that controls development and maintenance of masculine characteristics. The androgens include testosterone and Dehydroepiandrosterone.

HP_0030350.label: erythematous papule
HP_0030350.definition: A circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid that is reddish (erythematous) in color.
HP_0030350.UMLS synonyms: erythematous papule of tongue | SKIN PAPULE OR PAPULAR RASH, ERYTHEMATOUS | erythematous papules of oropharynx | Rash (erythematous macules or papules)

HP_0030351.label: urticarial plaque
HP_0030351.definition: A well-circumscribed, intensely pruritic, raised wheal (edema of the superficial skin) typically 1 to 2 cm in diameter.
HP_0030351.UMLS synonyms: Pruritic urticarial papules plaques of pregnancy | Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy, familial

HP_0030352.label: abnormal serum insulin - like growth factor 1 level
HP_0030352.definition: An anomalous level of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) in the blood circulation.

HP_0030353.label: decreased serum insulin - like growth factor 1
HP_0030353.definition: A reduced level of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) in the blood circulation.
HP_0030353.UMLS synonyms: Decreased serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF1) | Decreased serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF1, 147440)

HP_0030354.label: abnormal circulating interferon concentration
HP_0030354.definition: Abnormal levels of interferon in the blood.

HP_0030355.label: abnormal circulating interferon - gamma concentration
HP_0030355.definition: Abnormal levels of interferon gamma measured in the blood circulation.

HP_0030356.label: increased circulating interferon - gamma concentration
HP_0030356.definition: An elevation in the concentration of interferon gamma measured in the blood circulation.

HP_0030357.label: small cell lung carcinoma
HP_0030357.definition: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a type of highly malignant lung cancer that is composed of small ovoid cells. In the past, SCLC was called oat cell carcinoma because the microscopic appearance of the cells was felt to resemble oats. SLCLC usually originates near the bronchi and in many cases may grow and metastasize quickly.
HP_0030357.synonyms: oat cell carcinoma of lung | oat cell lung cancer | small cell lung cancer

HP_0030359.definition: A type of non-small cell lung carcinoma that is derived from stratified squamous epithelial cells.

HP_0030360.label: large cell lung carcinoma
HP_0030360.definition: A type of non-small cell lung carcinoma that is derived from undifferentiated malignant neoplasms originating from transformed epithelial cells in the lung, and which is differentiate from small-cell lung carcinoma by the larger size of the anaplastic cells, a higher cytoplasmic-to-nuclear size ratio, and a lack of salt-and-pepper appearance of the chromatin.

HP_0030361.label: abnormal circulating eicosanoid concentration
HP_0030361.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of an icosanoid (also known as eicosanoids). These are signaling molecules derived from oxidation of 20-carbon fatty acids. Most are produced from arachidonic acid, a 20-carbon polyunsaturated fatty acid (5,8,11,14-eicosatetraenoic acid).

HP_0030362.label: reduced muscle carnitine level
HP_0030362.definition: A reduction in the level of carnitine in muscle tissue.

HP_0030363.label: primary caesarian section
HP_0030363.definition: Delivery by Caesarian section representing the first time the mother has delivered by Caesarian section.

HP_0030364.label: secondary caesarian section
HP_0030364.definition: Delivery by Caesarian section representing where the mother has already had a previous Cesarean delivery, and this is a repeat Cesarean birth.

HP_0030365.label: vaginal birth after caesarian
HP_0030365.definition: Vaginal birth after Caesarian (VBAC) refers to the situation where the mother has had a previous Cesarean delivery but has now delivered vaginally.

HP_0030366.label: delivery by odon device
HP_0030366.definition: The Odon device is an instrument for assisted vaginal deliveries that is applied on the head of the baby and used to apply traction to assist the birth process.

HP_0030367.label: finger hyperphalangy
HP_0030367.definition: Hyperphalangy is a digit morphology in which increased numbers of phalanges are arranged linearly within a digit. That is, there is an accessory phalanx that is arranged linearly with the other phalanges.
HP_0030367.UMLS synonyms: Finger hyperphalangy, toe anomalies, severe pectus excavatum syndrome | Hyperphalangy of index finger (accessory bone between 2nd-3rd proximal phalanges) | Catel Manzke syndrome

HP_0030368.label: hyperphalangy of the 2nd finger
HP_0030368.definition: An accessory phalanx of the index (second) finger that is arranged linearly with the other phalanges. Hyperphalangy of the index finger results from an accessory ossification center at the metacarpophalangeal joint, resulting in radial deviation of the index finger. Note that this term refers only to this type of hyperphalangy.

HP_0030369.label: induced vaginal delivery
HP_0030369.definition: Vaginal delivery following induction of labor, a procedure used to stimulate uterine contractions during pregnancy before labor begins on its own.
HP_0030369.UMLS synonyms: Induced abortion, by 1 or more vaginal suppositories (eg, prostaglandin) with or without cervical dilation (eg, laminaria), including hospital admission and visits, delivery of fetus and secundines | Induced abortion, by 1 or more vaginal suppositories (eg, prostaglandin) with or without cervical dilation (eg, laminaria), including hospital admission and visits, delivery of fetus and secundines; with hysterotomy (failed medical evacuation) | Induced abortion, by 1 or more vaginal suppositories (eg, prostaglandin) with or without cervical dilation (eg, laminaria), including hospital admission and visits, delivery of fetus and secundines; with dilation and curettage and/or evacuation

HP_0030370.label: abnormal proportion of naive b cells
HP_0030370.definition: A deviation in the normal proportion of naive B cells (CD19+/CD27-/IgD+/IgM+) relative to the total number of B cells. Naive B cells represent one of the subtypes of B cells in the peripheral blood, and are B cells that have not been exposed to antigen.

HP_0030371.label: increased proportion of naive b cells
HP_0030371.definition: An elevation above the normal proportion of naive B cells (CD19+/CD27-/IgD+/IgM+) relative to total number of B cells. Naive B cells represent one of the subtypes of B cells in the peripheral blood, and are B cells that have not been exposed to antigen.

HP_0030372.label: decreased proportion of naive b cells
HP_0030372.definition: A reduction below normal proportion of naive B cells (CD19+/CD27-/IgD+/IgM+) relative to total number of B cells. Naive B cells represent one of the subtypes of B cells in the peripheral blood, and are B cells that have not been exposed to antigen.

HP_0030373.label: abnormal proportion of memory b cells
HP_0030373.definition: A deviation of the normal proportion of memory B cells in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Memory B cells develop from naive B cells. Upon antigen rechallenge, memory B cells rapidly expand and differentiate into plasma cells under the cognate control of memory Th cells (Phase IV).

HP_0030374.label: decreased proportion of memory b cells
HP_0030374.definition: A reduction in the normal proportion of memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. Memory B cells develop from naive B cells. Upon antigen rechallenge, memory B cells rapidly expand and differentiate into plasma cells under the cognate control of memory Th cells (Phase IV).

HP_0030375.label: increased proportion of memory b cells
HP_0030375.definition: An elevation in the proportion of memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. Memory B cells develop from naive B cells. Upon antigen rechallenge, memory B cells rapidly expand and differentiate into plasma cells under the cognate control of memory Th cells (Phase IV).

HP_0030376.label: abnormal proportion of immature b cells
HP_0030376.definition: A deviation from normal proportion of immature B cells (CD19+/ CD21low) in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Immature B cells (IgM+) are still in final stages of development within the bone marrow. Naive B cells are those which have left the bone marrow, before they bind to the antigen for which they're specific (IgM+/IgD+).
HP_0030376.synonyms: abnormal proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cells

HP_0030377.label: increased proportion of immature b cells
HP_0030377.definition: An elevation in the proportion above normal of immature B cells (CD19+/ CD21low) in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Immature B cells (IgM+) are still in final stages of development within the bone marrow. Naive B cells are those which have left the bone marrow, before they bind to the antigen for which they're specific (IgM+/IgD+).
HP_0030377.synonyms: increased proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cells

HP_0030378.label: decreased proportion of immature b cells
HP_0030378.definition: A reduction in normal proportion of immature B cells (CD19+/ CD21low)in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Immature B cells (IgM+) are still in final stages of development within the bone marrow. Naive B cells are those which have left the bone marrow, before they bind to the antigen for which they're specific (IgM+/IgD+).
HP_0030378.synonyms: decreased proportion of cd19+ / cd21low b cells

HP_0030379.label: abnormal proportion of transitional b cells
HP_0030379.definition: A deviation in the normal proportion of transitional B cells (CD19+/CD38high/IgMhigh) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. B cells originate from precursors in the bone marrow, and the first cells which migrate to the peripheral blood have been classified as transitional B cells.

HP_0030380.label: decreased proportion of transitional b cells
HP_0030380.definition: A reduction in the normal proportion of transitional B cells (CD19+/CD38high/IgMhigh) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. B cells originate from precursors in the bone marrow, and the first cells which migrate to the peripheral blood have been classified as transitional B cells.

HP_0030381.label: increased proportion of transitional b cells
HP_0030381.definition: An elevation in the normal proportion of transitional B cells (CD19+/CD38high/IgMhigh) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. B cells originate from precursors in the bone marrow, and the first cells which migrate to the peripheral blood have been classified as transitional B cells.

HP_0030383.label: abnormal proportion of marginal zone b cells
HP_0030383.definition: A deviation of the normal proportion of marginal zone B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells.

HP_0030384.label: decreased proportion of marginal zone b cells
HP_0030384.definition: A reduction in the normal proportion of marginal zone B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells.

HP_0030385.label: increased proportion of marginal zone b cells
HP_0030385.definition: An elevation in the normal proportion of marginal zone B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells.

HP_0030386.label: abnormal proportion of class - switched memory b cells
HP_0030386.definition: A deviation of the normal proportion of class-switched memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM-/IgD-) in circulation relative to the total number of B cells. Marginal zone B cells undergo limited somatic hypermutation and produce high-affinity IgM and some IgG, whereas class-switched memory B cells synthetize IgG, IgM, and IgA.

HP_0030387.label: increased proportion of class - switched memory b cells
HP_0030387.definition: An increase in the normal proportion of class-switched memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) relative to the total number of B cells. Marginal zone B cells undergo limited somatic hypermutation and produce high-affinity IgM and some IgG, whereas class-switched memory B cells synthetize IgG, IgM, and IgA.

HP_0030388.label: decreased proportion of class - switched memory b cells
HP_0030388.definition: A reduction in the normal proportion of class-switched memory B cells (CD19+/CD27+/IgM+/IgD+) relative to the total number of B cells. Marginal zone B cells undergo limited somatic hypermutation and produce high-affinity IgM and some IgG, whereas class-switched memory B cells synthetize IgG, IgM, and IgA.

HP_0030389.label: abnormal circulating thromboxane concentration
HP_0030389.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration in the blood circulation of a thromboxane. Thromboxanes are derived from prostaglandin precursors in platelets, and stimulate aggregation of platelets and constriction of blood vessels.

HP_0030390.label: reduced circulating leukotriene c4 concentration
HP_0030390.definition: An abnormally decreased concentration of leukotriene C4 in the blood circulation.

HP_0030391.label: spoken word recognition deficit
HP_0030391.definition: Reduced ability of lexical discrimination, which refers to the process of distinguishing a stimulus word from other phonologically similar words. Lexical discrimination can be defined as the process of correctly identifying words in the mental lexicon to match the phonological input of a stimulus.

HP_0030392.label: choroid plexus carcinoma
HP_0030392.definition: Intraventricular papillary neoplasm derived from choroid plexus epithelium. Plexus tumors are most common in the lateral and fourth ventricles; while 80% of lateral ventricle tumors present in children, fourth ventricle tumors are evenly distributed in all age groups. Clinically, choroid plexus tumors tend to cause hydrocephalus and increased intracranial pressure. Histologically, choroid plexus papillomas correspond to WHO grade I, choroid plexus carcinomas to WHO grade III.

HP_0030393.label: endolymphatic sac tumor
HP_0030393.definition: A low-grade papillary epithelial neoplasm (adenocarcinoma) with a slow growth pattern. The endolymphatic duct emerges from the posterior wall of the saccule (of the inner ear) and ends in a blind pouch, the endolymphatic sac. Endolymphatic sac tumors (ELSTs) are known under different names in the literature (Heffner tumor, aggressive papillary middle ear tumor, and low-grade adenocarcinoma of endolymphatic sac origin).

HP_0030393.UMLS synonyms: Endolymphatic sac tumor | Endolymphatic sac tumors (ELSTs)

HP_0030394.label: fallopian tube carcinoma
HP_0030394.definition: Carcinoma that originates in the Fallopian tube. It may be located in the wall or within the lumen as a growth attached to the wall by a stalk.

HP_0030396.label: abnormal platelet granule secretion
HP_0030396.definition: Platelets are replete with secretory granules, which are critical to normal platelet function. Among the three types of platelet secretory granules - alpha-granules, dense granules, and lysosomes - the alpha-granule is the most abundant. Granule contents must be released from their intracellular repository in order to achieve their physiologic function, and this term refers to a functional defect in granule secretion.

HP_0030397.label: abnormal platelet dense granule secretion
HP_0030397.definition: Abnormal release of dense granules from platelets.

HP_0030398.label: abnormal platelet atp dense granule secretion
HP_0030398.definition: Abnormal secretion of the platelet dense-granule content adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

HP_0030399.label: abnormal platelet alpha granule secretion
HP_0030399.definition: Abnormal release of alpha granule contents from platelets.

HP_0030400.label: abnormal platelet lysosome secretion
HP_0030400.definition: Abnormal release of lysosome contents from platelets.

HP_0030401.label: abnormal platelet dense granule atp / adp ratio
HP_0030401.definition: Deviation from normal of the ratio of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to adenosine diphosphate (ADP) within platelets.

HP_0030402.label: abnormal platelet aggregation
HP_0030402.definition: An abnormality in the rate and degree to which platelets aggregate after the addition of an agonist that stimulates platelet clumping. Platelet aggregation is measured using aggregometer to measure the optical density of platelet-rich plasma, whereby platelet aggregation causes the plasma to become more transparent.

HP_0030403.label: spontaneous platelet aggregation
HP_0030403.definition: Clumping together of platelets in the blood in a platelet aggregation test without addition of agents normally used to induce aggregation.

HP_0030404.label: glucagonoma
HP_0030404.definition: An endocrine tumor of the pancreas that secretes excessive amounts of glucagon.

HP_0030405.label: pancreatic endocrine tumor
HP_0030405.definition: A neuroendocrine tumor originating in a hormone-producing cell (islet cell) of the pancreas.

HP_0030406.label: primary peritoneal carcinoma
HP_0030406.definition: A type of cancer that originates in the peritoneum. It is to be distinguished from metastatic cancer of the peritoneum. Peritoneal cancer can occur anywhere in the abdominal space, and affects the surface of organs contained inside the peritoneum.

HP_0030407.label: pineocytoma
HP_0030407.definition: A type of pineal parenchymal cell neoplasm that is a mature well-differentiated tumor (WHO grade I).
HP_0030407.UMLS synonyms: Pineocytoma | Adult Pineocytoma | Mouse Pineocytoma | Mixed Pineocytoma-Pineoblastoma

HP_0030408.label: pineoblastoma
HP_0030408.definition: Pineoblastoma is a rare primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) arising in the pineal gland. Pineoblastomas are classified as a WHO grade IV tumor and comprise one-fourth to one-half of pineal parenchymal tumors. Pineoblastoma is a highly cellular tumor originating in the pineal gland and containing small, poorly differentiated cells.

HP_0030409.definition: A malignant tumor that arises from the transitional (urothelial) epithelial cells lining the urinary tract from the renal calyces to the ureteral orifice.

HP_0030410.definition: A carcinoma that arises in a sebaseous gland (an exocrine gland of the skin that secretes sebum, a waxy substance)

HP_0030411.label: jejunal adenocarcinoma
HP_0030411.definition: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the jejunum.

HP_0030412.label: ileal adenocarcinoma
HP_0030412.definition: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the ileum.

HP_0030413.label: squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue
HP_0030413.definition: A carcinoma derived from a squamous epithelial cell of the tongue.

HP_0030414.label: verrucous cell carcinoma of the tongue
HP_0030414.definition: A low-grade variant of squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue with a warty (verrucous) appearance.

HP_0030415.label: sarcomatoid carcinoma of the tongue
HP_0030415.definition: Sarcomatoid (spindle cell) carcinomas of the tongue is a variant of squamous carcinoma of tongue that is monoclonal, having evolved from a conventional squamous carcinoma with dedifferentiation associated with sarcomatoid transformation.

HP_0030416.label: vulvar neoplasm
HP_0030416.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the female external genital tract (vulva).

HP_0030425.definition: A cyst of the ovary that exhibits deposition of calcium salts.

HP_0030429.definition: A benign but highly vascular nasopharyngeal neoplasm. The tumor originates from the sphenopalatine foramen and involves both the pterygopalatine fossa and the posterior nasal cavity.

Other structures such as retinal vessels and the crystalline lens may also influence autofluorescence through blocking and interference.

HP_0030661.definition: Yellow-white inflammatory aggregates in the vitreous that are found in the midvitreous and inferior periphery.

HP_0030662.label: vitreous inflammatory cells
HP_0030662.definition: The presence of inflammatory cells such as lymphocytes and macrophages in the vitreous.

HP_0030663.label: optically empty vitreous
HP_0030663.definition: Vestigial vitreous gel occupying the immediate retrolental space and minimal to no discernable gel in the central vitreous cavity, giving the appearance of an empty vitreous cavity.

HP_0030664.label: beevor 's sign
HP_0030664.definition: Weakness of the inferior portion of the rectus abdominal muscle, which is ascertained clinically as follows. When a patient sits up or raises the head from a recumbent position, the umbilicus is displaced toward the head. This is the result of paralysis of the inferior portion of the rectus abdominal muscle, so that the upper fibres predominate pulling upwards the umbilicus.
HP_0030664.UMLS synonyms: Beevor's sign | Abdominal wall muscle weakness (positive Beevor sign)

HP_0030665.label: rubral tremor
HP_0030665.definition: Rubral tremor is characterized by a slow coarse tremor at rest that is exacerbated by postural adjustments and by guided voluntary movements.

HP_0030666.label: retinal neovascularization
HP_0030666.definition: In wound repair, neovascularization (NV) involves the sprouting of new vessels from pre-existent vessels to repair or replace damaged vessels. In the retina, NV is a response to ischemia. The NV adheres to the inner surface of the retina and outer surface of the vitreous. NV are deficient in tight junctions and hence leak plasma into surrounding tissue including the vitreous. Plasma causes the vitreous gel to degenerate, contract, and eventually collapse which pulls on the retina. Since retinal NV is adherent to both retina and vitreous, as the vitreous contracts the NV may be sheared resulting in vitreous hemorrhage or the NV may remain intact and pull the retina with the vitreous resulting in retinal elevation referred to as traction retinal detachment.

HP_0030669.label: abnormal ocular adnexa morphology
HP_0030669.definition: A structural anomaly of the adjacent structures (i.e., adnexa) of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.

HP_0030670.label: hamartoma of the orbital region
HP_0030670.definition: A hamartoma (disordered proliferation of mature tissues) which can originate from any tissue of the orbital region.

HP_0030671.label: abnormal common tendinous ring morphology
HP_0030671.definition: Any anomaly of the ring of fibrous tissue that surrounds the optic nerve at its entrance at the apex of the orbit. The common tendinous ring, also known as the annulus of Zinn or annular tendon, is the origin for five of the seven extraocular muscles.

HP_0030713.label: vein of galen aneurysmal malformation
HP_0030713.definition: Vein of Galen aneurysmal malformation is a choroidal type of arteriovenous malformation that develops between 6 and 11 weeks of gestation. It results from 1 or more arteriovenous fistulas shunting blood toward the prosencephalic vein of Markowski, the embryonic precursor of the vein of Galen. HP_0030716.label: acrania
HP_0030716.definition: Partial or complete absence of the flat bones of the cranial vault. The condition is frequently, though not always, associated with anencephaly.

HP_0030717.label: meconium peritonitis
HP_0030717.definition: Peritonitis caused by intrauterine intestinal rupture and spillage of fetal meconium into the fetal peritoneal cavity. Intra-peritoneal meconium usually calcifies, sometimes within 24 hours. Ultrasound findings may include intraabdominal calcifications.

HP_0030726.label: spinal neurenteric cyst
HP_0030726.definition: A neurenteric cyst located in the spine.

HP_0030727.label: intracranial neurenteric cyst
HP_0030727.definition: A neurenteric cyst located within the skull.

HP_0030728.label: meromelia
HP_0030728.definition: Partial absence of a free limb (excluding girdle). It can refer to the proximal, middle or distal segment of the upper or lower limb. The deficiency may be transverse or longitudinal. Thus, meromelia is a lack of a part, but not all, of one or more limbs with the presence of a hand or foot.

HP_0030729.label: frontoethmoidal meningocele
HP_0030729.definition: A herniation of meninges through a congenital bone defect in the skull at the junction of the frontal and ethmoidal bones.

HP_0030730.label: parietal meningocele
HP_0030730.definition: A herniation of meninges through a congenital bone defect in the skull in the parietal region.

HP_0030731.label: carcinoma
HP_0030731.definition: A malignant tumor arising from epithelial cells. Carcinomas that arise from glandular epithelium are called adenocarcinomas, those that arise from squamous epithelium are called squamous cell carcinomas, and those that arise from transitional epithelium are called transitional cell carcinomas (NCI Thesaurus).

HP_0030732.label: dysplastic tricuspid valve
HP_0030732.definition: A congenital malformation of the tricuspid valve characterized by leaflet deformation.

HP_0030733.label: vesicoallantoic abdominal wall defect
HP_0030733.definition: An abdominal wall defected related to a developmental anomaly of the allantois, which is an embryonic structure that develops as a diverticulum off the yolk sac at about 16 days post fertilization. During further development, the allantois becomes incorporated into the body of the embryo, connecting the ventral aspect of the urogenital sinus (which will develop into the upper pole of the urinary bladder) to the external portion of the umbilicus. Upon further development, the lumen of the allantois becomes obliterated and forms a thick fibrous cord called the urachus, which connects the apex of the bladder to the umbilicus. In adults, the urachus is known as the median umbilical ligament. Failure of the allantoic cavity to obliterate can result of one of four conditions: 1) congenital patent urachus (a completely open connection between bladder and umbilicus); 2) vesicourachal diverticulum (a diverticulum off the bladder but not communicating with the umbilicus); umbilical cyst and sinus (not communicating with the bladder); and 4) alternating urachal sinus. An abdominal wall defect can be associated with a urachal cyst.

HP_0030735.label: ureterovesical junction obstruction
HP_0030735.definition: Blockage at the level of the bladder and the ureter caused by stenosis of the ureteral valves or failure of a narrow juxtavesical ureteral segment to dilate due to segmented fibrosis or localized absence of muscle.
HP_0030735.UMLS synonyms: Obstruction of vesicoureteric junction | congenital obstruction of ureterovesical junction on left | congenital obstruction of ureterovesical junction on right | Congenital obstruction of ureteral orifice | congenital obstruction of ureterovesical junction on both sides

HP_0030736.label: sacrococcygeal teratoma
HP_0030736.definition: A teratoma arising in the sacro-coccygeal region.
HP_0030736.UMLS synonyms: Sacrococcygeal teratoma | SACROCOCCYGEAL TERATOMA REMOVAL | Excision of sacrococcygeal teratoma | Altman type IV sacrococcygeal teratoma | Excision of sacrococcygeal teratoma, posterior approach | Excision of sacrococcygeal teratoma, posterior and abdominal approach | Repair of sacrococcygeal teratoma in the fetus, procedure performed in utero

HP_0030737.label: altman type i sacrococcygeal teratoma
HP_0030737.definition: A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma that is predominantly external and projects from the sacrococcygeal region and presents with distortion of the buttocks.

HP_0030738.label: altman type ii sacrococcygeal teratoma
HP_0030738.definition: A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma that is predominantly external but has a large intrapelvic component.

HP_0030739.label: altman type iii sacrococcygeal teratoma
HP_0030739.definition: A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma that is predominantly intrapelvic with a small external, buttock mass.

HP_0030740.label: anomalous muscle bundle of the right ventricle
HP_0030740.definition: An accessory (not normally present) muscle bundle in the right ventricle which obstructs the right ventricular outflow tract.

HP_0030741.label: mediastinal teratoma
HP_0030741.definition: A teratoma located within the mediastinum (the cavity between the pleural sacs that contains the heart and all of the thoracic viscera except the lungs).
HP_0030741.UMLS synonyms: Benign mediastinal teratoma | Mediastinal Immature Teratoma | Mediastinal Mature Teratoma | teratocarcinoma of mediastinum | teratoma of anterior mediastinum

HP_0030742.label: glial remnants posterior to lens
HP_0030742.definition: This anomaly, also known as Mittendorf dot, is a benign, nonprogressive recognizable lesion that does not cause visual impairment. However, it can resemble a pathological congenital or acquired cataract lesion which may enlarge and cause visual impairment. The dot appears as a black speck that ranges in size from the dot made by a sharp pencil point to the size of a poppy seed. It is usually well defined, although occasionally there may be irregular, fine lines radiating outward from the dot.

HP_0030743.label: glial remnants anterior to the optic disc
HP_0030743.definition: Persistence of a posterior remnant of the hyaloid artery located at the optic disc.

HP_0030744.label: hyaloid vascular remnant and retrolental mass
HP_0030744.definition: A type of persistence of the hyaloid vascular system associated with a retrolental mass that may lead to fetal cataract.

HP_0030745.label: dilatation of the ductus arteriosus
HP_0030745.definition: Ductus arteriosus aneurysm (DAA) is a saccular dilatation of the ductus arteriosus. DAA can be either congenital or acquired (e.g. as a complication of surgical closure of a patent ductus arteriosus). Although the majority of patients with congenital DAA are asymptomatic and have a benign course, severe complications, such as rupture or thromboembolism, can occur. DAA is likely to emerge in the third trimester from the aortic junction of the DA, extending towards its pulmonary end.
HP_0030745.synonyms: aneurysm of the ductus arteriosus | congenital ductus arteriosus aneurysm | ductus arteriosus aneurysm

HP_0030746.label: intraventricular hemorrhage
HP_0030746.definition: Bleeding into the ventricles of the brain.
HP_0030746.UMLS synonyms: Ventricular hemorrhage | Perinatal intraventricular hemorrhage | Intracerebral hemorrhage, intraventricular | Traumatic intraventricular hemorrhage | Cerebral Intraventricular Hemorrhage | intraventricular; subependymal hemorrhage | CNS INTRAVENTRICULAR HEMORRHAGE | Intraventricular hemorrhage of prematurity | Intraventricular hemorrhage of fetus | Nontraumatic Intracerebral Hemorrhage, Intraventricular | Intraventricular hemorrhage unspecified grade | Intraventricular hemorrhage due to birth injury | hemorrhage; newborn, subependymal, with intraventricular hemorrhage | Neonatal Intraventricular Hemorrhage, Adverse Event | computed tomography of brain: intraventricular hemorrhage | Grade 2 Intraventricular Hemorrhage of the Newborn | Neonatal non-traumatic intraventricular hemorrhage | Fetal non-traumatic intraventricular hemorrhage

HP_0030747.label: preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP_0030747.definition: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a premature infant.

HP_0030748.label: grade i preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP_0030748.definition: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a preterm infant and that is restricted to subependymal region/germline matrix which is seen in the caudothalamic groove.
HP_0030748.synonyms: germinal matrix haemorrhage | germinal matrix hemorrhage | grade i preterm intraventricular haemorrhage

HP_0030749.label: grade ii preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP_0030749.definition: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a preterm infant and that has extension into normal-sized ventricles and typically fills less than 50% of the volume of the ventricle.

HP_0030750.label: grade iii preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP_0030750.definition: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a preterm infant and that has extension into dilated ventricles.

HP_0030751.label: grade iv preterm intraventricular hemorrhage
HP_0030751.definition: Intraventricular hemorrhage that occurs in a preterm infant and that shows parenchymal extension.

HP_0030752.label: dacryocystocele
HP_0030752.definition: A nasolacrimal duct obstruction presenting as a grey-blue cystic swelling just below the medial canthus. Believed to be a result of concomitant upper obstruction of the Rosenmuller valve and lower obstruction of the Hasner valve.
HP_0030752.UMLS synonyms: Lacrimal mucocele | Congenital cyst of nasolacrimal duct | Dacryocystocoele acquired

HP_0030753.label: intrauterine fetal demise of one twin after midgestation
HP_0030753.definition: Loss of one twin occurring after midgestation (17 weeks gestation).
HP_0030753.synonyms: intrauterine foetal demise of one twin after midgestation | single - twin demise

HP_0030754.label: allantoic cyst
HP_0030754.definition: A swelling formed at the base of umbilicus associated with a patent urachus which results from an allantoic remnant. The urachus is a fibrous remnant of the allantois which communicates from the apex of the urinary bladder to the umbilicus. Failed obliteration of the urachus can lead to various abnormalities: urachal cyst, urachal diverticulum, sinus or patent urachus - the most common type. Allantoic cysts in infants with patent urachus can be formed due to the drainage of urine into the umbilical cord, or in uncommon situations, after leakage of hypo-osmotic urine into the Wharton's jelly.
HP_0030754.UMLS synonyms: Allantoic cyst | Urachal Cyst | Benign non-infected urachal cyst

HP_0030755.label: craniofacial teratoma
HP_0030755.definition: A teratoma located in the craniofacial region.

HP_0030756.label: erythrodontia
HP_0030756.definition: Reddish, brown opalescent discoloration of teeth in normal light.

HP_0030757.label: tooth abscess
HP_0030757.definition: A pocket of pus located within a region of a tooth.

HP_0030758.definition: A tooth abscess that occurs at the tip of the root (apex) of a tooth.

HP_0030759.label: adipocyte hypertrophy
HP_0030759.definition: An increase in mean adipocyte cell size. This feature can be measured by determining the average cell diameter of adipocytes microscopically using abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue obtained by biopsy.

HP_0030760.label: renal fibrosis
HP_0030760.definition: Renal fibrosis is the consequence of an excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix that occurs in virtually every type of chronic kidney disease.

HP_0030762.definition: Partial or complete dissolution of the mesangial matrix, identified by reduced staining on a periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) or silver stain.

HP_0030764.label: ochronosis
HP_0030764.definition: Brown or blue-gray discoloration of the skin that can present on the axillary and inguinal areas, face, palms or soles. In addition, blue-black discoloration can be apparent on skin overlying cartilage in which the pigment is deposited, such as the ears. This is a characteristic manifestation of alkaptonuria, which is an autosomal recessively inherited deficiency of homogentisic acid oxidase that results in accumulation of homogentisic acid in collagenous structures. The sclerae are also typically involved.

HP_0030766.label: ear pain
HP_0030766.definition: Pain in the ear can be a consequence of otologic disease (primary or otogenic otalgia), or can arise from pathologic processes and structures other than the ear (secondary or referred otalgia).

HP_0030767.label: epignathus
HP_0030767.definition: Epignathus is a teratoma originating from the upper jaw, usually connected with the sphenoid bone or hard palate.

HP_0030769.label: exencephaly
HP_0030769.definition: A malformation of the neural tube with a large amount of protruding brain tissue and absence of calvarium.

HP_0030770.label: craniorachischisis
HP_0030770.definition: A neural tube defect in which both the brain and spinal cord remain open to varying degrees.
HP_0030770.UMLS synonyms: Craniorachischisis | obstetric ultrasound of fetus: craniorachischisis

HP_0030771.label: mallet finger
HP_0030771.definition: Mallet finger refers to a condition in which the end joint of a finger bends but will not straighten by itself. In this situation, the joint can be pushed straight but will not hold that position on its own.

HP_0030773.label: internuclear ophthalmoplegia
HP_0030773.definition: An abnormality of conjugate lateral gaze in which the affected eye shows impairment of adduction. The pathognomonic clinical sign of internuclear ophthalmoplegia is an impaired adduction while testing horizontal saccades on the side of the lesion in the ipsilateral medial longitudinal fascicule.

HP_0030774.label: mitochondrial swelling
HP_0030774.definition: The mitochondrial matrix refers to the substance occupying the space enclosed by the inner membrane of a mitochondrion, which contains enzymes, DNA, granules, and inclusions of protein crystals, glycogen, and lipid. Mitochondrial swelling refers to an increase in size of the mitochondrial matrix. This phenomenon is thought to be related to a permeabilized inner membrane that originates a large swelling in the mitochondrial matrix. Mitochondrial swelling may distend the outer membrane until it ruptures.
HP_0030774.UMLS synonyms: Mitochondrial Swelling | Swollen mitochondrial sheath seen on transmission electron microscopy

HP_0030775.label: modic type vertebral endplate changes
HP_0030775.definition: An abnormal magnetic resonance tomography signal from a vertebral endplate according to a widely used classification published by Dr. Michael Modic.

HP_0030776.label: modic type i vertebral endplate changes
HP_0030776.definition: An abnormal magnetic resonance tomography signal from a vertebral endplate with a low signal on T1-weighted sequences and high signal on T2-weighted sequences. Modic type I changes are thought to represent bone marrow edema and inflammation.

HP_0030777.label: modic type ii vertebral endplate changes
HP_0030777.definition: An abnormal magnetic resonance tomography signal from a vertebral endplate with a high signal on T1-weighted sequences and high- or isointense signal on T2 sequences. Modic type II signals are thought to indicate fatty replacement in the bone marrow.

HP_0030778.label: modic type iii vertebral endplate changes
HP_0030778.definition: An abnormal magnetic resonance tomography signal from a vertebral endplate with a low signal on T1 and T2-weighted sequences. Modic type III signals are thought to correspond to subchondral sclerosis seen on plain radiographs.

HP_0030779.label: ethmocephaly
HP_0030779.definition: Ethmocephaly is the rarest form of holoprosencephaly, which occurs due to an incomplete cleavage of the forebrain. Clinically, the disease presents with a proboscis, hypotelorism, microphthalmos and malformed ears.

HP_0030780.label: abnormality of the protein c anticoagulant pathway
HP_0030780.definition: An anomaly of the protein C anticoagulant pathway, which serves as a major system for controlling thrombosis, limiting inflammatory responses, and potentially decreasing endothelial cell apoptosis in response to inflammatory cytokines and ischemia. A natural anticoagulant system denoted the protein C pathway exerts its anticoagulant effect by regulating the activity of FVIIIa and FVa. The vitamin K-dependent protein C is the key component of the pathway. Activated protein C (APC) cleaves and inhibits coagulation cofactors FVIIIa and FVa, which result in downregulation of the activity of the coagulation system. The endothelial protein C receptor stimulates the T-TM-mediated activation of protein C on the endothelial cell surface. The two cofactors, protein S and the intact form of FV, enhance the anticoagulant activity of APC.

HP_0030781.label: increased circulating free fatty acid level
HP_0030781.definition: A higher than normal levels of the fatty acids which can occur in plasma as a result of lipolysis in adipose tissue or when plasma triacyglycerols are taken into tissues.

HP_0030782.label: abnormal circulating interleukin concentration
HP_0030782.definition: An abnormal amount of any of the interleukins, a class of cytokines, in the circulation.
HP_0030782.synonyms: abnormal serum il level | abnormal serum interleukin level

HP_0030783.label: increased circulating interleukin 6 concentration
HP_0030783.definition: An increased concentration of interleukin-6 in the blood circulation.
HP_0030783.synonyms: increased serum il - 6 | increased serum interleukin - 6

HP_0030784.label: anomic aphasia
HP_0030784.definition: An inability to name people and objects that are correctly perceived. The individual is able to describe the object in question, but cannot provide the name.
HP_0030784.synonyms: amnesic aphasia | amnestic aphasia | anomia | nominal aphasia | word - finding difficulty
HP_0030784.UMLS synonyms: Anomia | anomic dysphasia or aphasia | Computer assisted anomia treatment

HP_0030785.label: mediastinal cystic lymphangioma
HP_0030785.definition: A lymphangioma (congenital malformation consisting of focal proliferations of well-differentiated lymphatic tissue in multi cystic or sponge like structures) located within the mediastinum, i.e., the central compartment of the thoracic cavity that is surrounded by loose connective tissue. Mediastinal lymphangioma is a slow growing mass with benign features, and accounts for 1% of all mediastinal tumors.
HP_0030785.synonyms: intrathoracic cystic hygroma | thoracic cystic lymphangioma

HP_0030787.label: cerumen abnormality
HP_0030787.definition: Any anomaly of the cerumen (ear wax), the yellowish waxy substance secreted in the ear canal.

HP_0030788.label: impacted cerumen
HP_0030788.definition: Blockage of the external auditory canal by a buildup of earwax.

HP_0030790.label: abnormal cerumen color
HP_0030790.definition: An anomolous earwax color. Earwax (cerumen) is usually light to dark brown or orange in color.
HP_0030790.synonyms: abnormal cerumen colour | abnormal cerumen pigmentation

HP_0030791.label: abnormal jaw morphology
HP_0030791.definition: A structural anomaly of the jaw, the bony structure of the mouth that consists of the mandible and the maxilla.

HP_0030792.label: jaw neoplasm
HP_0030792.definition: A tumor originating in the jaw (mandible or maxilla).

HP_0030793.definition: Abnormal enlargement in the upper jaw (maxilla) or in the lower jaw (mandible).
HP_0030793.UMLS synonyms: Swelling of jaw angle | Swelling of lower jaw region | Symmetric, hard, painless, swelling of the jaw region

HP_0030794.label: abnormal circulating c - peptide concentration
HP_0030794.definition: An anomolous circulating concentration of the connecting (C) peptide, which links the insulin A and B chains in proinsulin, providing thereby a means to promote their efficient folding and assembly in the endoplasmic reticulum during insulin biosynthesis. After cleavage of proinsulin, C-peptide is stored with insulin in the soluble phase of the secretory granules and is subsequently released in equimolar amounts with insulin, providing a useful independent indicator of insulin secretion.
HP_0030794.synonyms: abnormal c peptide level | abnormal c - peptide level

HP_0030795.label: reduced c - peptide level
HP_0030795.definition: A decreased concentration of C-peptide in the circulation. Since C-peptide is secreted in equimolar amounts to insulin, this feature correlates with reduced insulin secretion.

HP_0030796.label: increased c - peptide level
HP_0030796.definition: An elevated concentration of C-peptide in the circulation. Since C-peptide is secreted in equimolar amounts to insulin, this feature correlates with increased insulin secretion.

HP_0030797.label: reduced volume of central subdivision of bed nucleus of stria terminalis
HP_0030797.definition: A diminished volume of the central part of the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis.

HP_0030798.label: abnormality of the bed nucleus of stria terminalis
HP_0030798.definition: The stria terminalis is a slender, compact fiber bundle that connects the amygdala (amygdaloid body) with the hypothalamus and other basal forebrain regions. The bed nucleus of the stria terminalis is a limbic forebrain structure that receives heavy projections from, among other areas, the basolateral amygdala, and projects in turn to hypothalamic and brainstem target areas that mediate many of the autonomic and behavioral responses to aversive or threatening stimuli. This term refers to an anomaly of the bed nucleus.

HP_0030799.label: scaphocephaly
HP_0030799.definition: Scaphocephaly is a subtype of dolichocephaly where the anterior and posterior aspects of the cranial vault are pointed (boat-shaped). Scaphocephaly is caused by a precocious fusion of sagittal suture without other associated synostosis.

HP_0030800.label: abnormal visual accommodation
HP_0030800.definition: An anomaly in the process of visual accommodation, which is the process of adjustment of the eye to enable sharp vision of objects at different distances. Accommodation is mediated by contraction of the ciliary muscles, which alter the convexity of the lens and, consequently, its refractive power.

HP_0030801.label: reduced visual accommodation
HP_0030801.definition: A decreased ability of the eye to adjust and thereby enable sharp vision of objects at different distances.

HP_0030802.label: lower eyelid retraction
HP_0030802.definition: Inferior malposition of the lower eyelid margin without eyelid eversion.

HP_0030804.label: trachyonychia

HP_0030805.label: absent lunula
HP_0030805.definition: Lack of the lunula at the base of a nail. The lunula is the crescent-shaped whitish area of the bed of a fingernail or toenail.

HP_0030806.label: fast - growing nails
HP_0030806.definition: Nails whose growth is quicker than normal.

HP_0030807.label: abnormal nail growth
HP_0030807.definition: Nail whose growth pattern or speed deviates from normal.

HP_0030808.label: ragged cuticle
HP_0030808.definition: The cuticle (properly known as the eponychium, or the medial nail fold or the proximal nail fold), is the thickened layer of skin surrounding fingernails and toenails. Its function is to protect the area between the nail and epidermis from exposure to bacteria. This term refers to the presence of and irregular edge or outline of the cuticle.

HP_0030810.label: abnormal tongue physiology
HP_0030810.definition: Any functional anomaly of the tongue.

HP_0030824.label: mizuo phenomenon
HP_0030824.definition: Change in the color of the fundus from red in the dark-adapted state to golden immediately or shortly after the onset of the light. The color of the fundus reflex in the light adapted state has also been described as golden-yellow, gray-white, and yellow-white. This reflex can appear either homogeneous or in streaks in the fundus. The retinal vessels appear to be protruding in contrast to the radiant background. Dark adaptation leads to disappearance of the unusual fundus coloration [Digital Journal of Ophthalmology 2008; Volume 14, Number 14].
HP_0030824.UMLS synonyms: Mizuo-Nakamura phenomenon (fundus color changes from red in the dark-adapted state to golden after light exposure)

HP_0030843.label: cardiac amyloidosis
HP_0030843.definition: Extracellular deposition in cardiac tissue of a proteinaceous material that, when stained with Congo red, demonstrates apple-green birefringence under polarized light and that has a distinct color when stained with sulfated Alcian blue. Viewed with electron microscopy, the amyloid deposits are seen to be composed of a beta-sheet fibrillar material. These nonbranching fibrils have a diameter of 7.5 to 10 nm and are the result of protein misfolding.

HP_0030844.label: undetectable pattern electroretinogram
HP_0030844.definition: Absent response to a pattern electroretinogram (PERG).

HP_0030845.label: heliotrope rash of eyelid
HP_0030845.definition: Heliotrope rash is a violaceous discoloration of the eyelids associated with periorbital edema.

HP_0030847.label: abnormal jugular venous pressure
HP_0030847.definition: An anomaly of the jugular venous pressure. The internal jugular veins, being continuous with the superior vena cava, provide a visible measure of the degree to which the systemic venous reservoir is filled. The vertical height above the right atrium to which they are distended and above which they are in a collapsed state provides an imperfect reflection of the right atrial pressure.

HP_0030849.label: hepatojugular reflux
HP_0030849.definition: The examiner applies firm but persistent pressure over the liver for 10 seconds while observing the mean jugular venous pressure. Normally there is either no rise or only a transient (i.e., 2 to 3 sec) rise in mean jugular venous pressure. A sustained increase in the mean venous pressure until abdominal compression is released is abnormal and indicates impaired right heart function. This abnormal response is called hepatojugular reflux.
HP_0030849.UMLS synonyms: Hepatojugular reflux | jugular vein hepatojugular reflux

HP_0030883.label: femoroacetabular impingement
HP_0030883.definition: Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) results from one or more bony abnormalities that lead to abnormal contact between the acetabulum and the femoral head or neck. The femoral abnormality is proposed to cause compression and shear stresses in the region between the labrum and cartilage, anterosuperiorly. These stresses cause a separation between the labrum and cartilage as the labrum is pushed outwards and the cartilage is pushed centrally. This eventually leads to articular degeneration and eventually global hip osteoarthritis.

HP_0030903.label: grasp reflex
