HP_0030970.label: abnormal vena cava physiology
HP_0030970.definition: An abnormality of the function of the veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body into the heart, i.e., the superior vena cava and the inferior vena cava.

HP_0030972.label: abnormal systemic blood pressure
HP_0030972.definition: A chronic deviation from normal pressure in the systemic arterial system.

HP_0030973.label: postexertional symptom exacerbation
HP_0030973.definition: Post-exertional symptom exacerbation (PESE), also referred to as post-exertional malaise (PEM), is defined as the worsening of symptoms that can follow minimal cognitive, physical, emotional, or social activity, or activity that could previously be tolerated. Symptoms typically worsen 12 to 72 hours after activity and can last for days or even weeks, sometimes leading to a relapse.

HP_0030974.label: cryptozoospermia
HP_0030974.definition: A type of oligozoospermia in which spermatozoa can be detected in an ejaculate only after centrifugation and inspection of the pellet.

HP_0030975.label: pontine tegmental cap
HP_0030975.definition: An abnormal curved or vaulted (capped) structure covering the middle third of the dorsal pontine tegmentum and projecting into the fourth ventricle.

HP_0030976.label: abnormal factor viii activity
HP_0030976.definition: A deviation from the normal activity of coagulation factor VIII. Factor VIII (fVIII) is a cofactor in the intrinsic clotting cascade that is activated to fVIIIa in the presence of minute quantities of thrombin. fVIIIa acts as a receptor, for factors IXa and X.

HP_0030977.label: increased factor viii activity
HP_0030977.definition: Increased activity of the coagulation factor VIII. Factor VIII (fVIII) is a cofactor in the intrinsic clotting cascade that is activated to fVIIIa in the presence of minute quantities of thrombin. fVIIIa acts as a receptor, for factors IXa and X.

HP_0030978.label: decreased csf / serum albumin ratio
HP_0030978.definition: A reduction below normal limits of the ratio of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) albumin concentration to serum albumin concentration.

HP_0030979.label: dilatation of large choroidal vessels
HP_0030979.definition: Enlargement of the large blood vessels in the choroid.

HP_0030980.label: reduced brain glutamine level by mrs
HP_0030980.definition: An decrease in the level of glutamine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

HP_0030981.label: abnormal csf / serum albumin ratio
HP_0030981.definition: A deviation from the normal range of the ratio of the albumin concentration in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to the concentration in serum (which may be defined as 3.2-9.0). This is an index of blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, adjusted for the serum albumin concentration, and an increased ratio is taken as a sign of a loss of integrity of the BBB with leakage of albumin into the CSF.

HP_0030983.label: ovarian thecoma
HP_0030983.definition: A sex cord-stromal tumor of the ovary. Thecomas range from small tumors to large solid or solid-cystic masses of up to 15 cm. They are unilateral in over 90 percent of cases and are rarely malignant. Thecomas are stromal tumors made up of cells that resemble theca cells, lutein cells and fibroblasts. They are traditionally classified within the sex cord-stromal tumor category of ovarian tumor types.
HP_0030983.UMLS synonyms: Ovarian Thecoma | Malignant Ovarian Thecoma | Typical Ovarian Thecoma | Mouse Malignant Ovarian Thecoma | Benign Ovarian Luteinized Thecoma | Malignant Ovarian Luteinized Thecoma | Benign Ovarian Partly Luteinized Thecoma | Ovarian Tumor of the Thecoma/Fibroma Group | Thecoma, luteinized | Benign thecoma | Ovarian Luteinized Thecoma Associated with Sclerosing Peritonitis

HP_0030984.label: abnormal serum bile acid concentration
HP_0030984.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of serum bile acid concentration.

HP_0030985.label: decreased serum bile acid concentration
HP_0030985.definition: A reduction in the concentration of bile acid in the blood.

HP_0030986.label: biliary epithelial hyperplasia
HP_0030986.definition: Hyperplasia of lining epithelia of the septal and large bile ducts manifesting as micropapillary projections or as a stratification of the epithelium with or without dilatation of the duct lumen.

HP_0030987.label: suppurative cholangitis
HP_0030987.definition: Cholangitis characterized by the presence of numerous polymorphonuclear cells around and within the wall as well as within the lumen of the ducts. This may involve ducts of any size and is occasionally associated with abscess formation (cholangitic abscess).
HP_0030987.UMLS synonyms: Suppurative cholangitis | Acute obstructive suppurative cholangitis | Primary Biliary Cholangitis

HP_0030988.label: granulomatous cholangitis
HP_0030988.definition: Cholangitis characterized by the accumulation of granulomas. Granulomas are aggregates of modified macrophages (epithelioid cells) and other inflammatory cells that accumulate after chronic exposure to antigens. The underlying trigger may be exposure to noxious agents that cannot be biochemically degraded or to immune dysfunction. The ultimate result is a release of a variety cytokines that stimulate mononuclear cells that fuse to form multinucleated giant cells with a surrounding rim of lymphocytes and fibroblasts.

HP_0030989.label: lymphoid cholangitis
HP_0030989.definition: Cholangitis characterized by a close association between duct branches, usually interlobular bile ducts, and lymphocytic aggregates, which may show a follicular arrangement.

HP_0030990.label: pleomorphic cholangitis
HP_0030990.definition: Cholangitis associated with mixed inflammatory infiltrates and the presence of fibrosis or sclerosis of the biliary tree.

HP_0030991.label: sclerosing cholangitis
HP_0030991.definition: Cholangitis associated with evident ductal fibrosis that develops as a consequence of long-standing bile duct inflammatory, obstruction, or ischemic injury; it can be obliterative or nonobliterative.
HP_0030991.UMLS synonyms: Cholangitis, Sclerosing | Primary sclerosing cholangitis | Secondary sclerosing cholangitis | SCLEROSING CHOLANGITIS, NEONATAL | HIV-related sclerosing cholangitis | Isolated neonatal sclerosing cholangitis | IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis | ICHTHYOSIS, LEUKOCYTE VACUOLES, ALOPECIA, AND SCLEROSING CHOLANGITIS | Pancreatitis, Sclerosing Cholangitis, and Sicca Complex | Cirrhosis of liver with primary sclerosing cholangitis | Primary biliary cholangitis and/or primary sclerosing cholangitis and autoimmune hepatitis overlap syndrome

HP_0030992.label: abnormal pancreatic duct morphology
HP_0030992.definition: Any structural anomaly of the pancreatic duct, which is the tubular structure that collects exocrine pancreatic secretions and transports them to the duodenum.

HP_0030993.label: duplication of pancreatic duct
HP_0030993.definition: A congenital anomaly characterized by the presence of two separate pancreatic ducts.

HP_0030994.label: pancreas divisum
HP_0030994.definition: A congenital anomaly of the pancreas that results from failed fusion of the dorsal and ventral ducts during embyological development. Three variants have been described: type 1 or classical divisum in which there is total failure of fusion; type 2 in which dorsal drainage is dominant in the absence of the duct of Wirsung; and type 3 or incomplete divisum where a small communicating branch is present.
HP_0030994.UMLS synonyms: Pancreas Divisum | Complete Pancreas Divisum | Incomplete Pancreas Divisum | Reverse Pancreas Divisum | ERCP: pancreas divisum | magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography: pancreas divisum | Extent of pancreas divisum

HP_0030995.label: peritoneal effusion
HP_0030995.definition: An increase in the amount of fluid present in the peritoneal cavity (between the layers of the peritoneum that lines the abdomen).
HP_0030995.UMLS synonyms: Peritoneal Effusion | Chronic peritoneal effusion (disorder) | Bloody peritoneal effusion | peritoneal cavity; effusion | Peritoneal Primary Effusion Lymphoma | Hemoperitoneum | Chylous Ascites | Malignant ascites | Hemorrhagic ascites | Carcinomatous ascites | Transudative ascites | Fibrinous ascites | Modified transudative ascites

HP_0030996.label: megaduodenum
HP_0030996.definition: Dilation and elongation of the duodenum with hypertrophy of all layers of the duodenum.
HP_0030996.UMLS synonyms: Megaduodenum | Acquired megaduodenum | Congenital megaduodenum | Megaduodenum and-or Megacystis | Visceral Myopathy, Familial | MUNGAN SYNDROME

HP_0030997.label: atretic vas deferens
HP_0030997.definition: Abnormal closure or blockage of the vas deferens.
HP_0030997.synonyms: atresia of the vas deferens | vas deferens atresia

HP_0030998.label: cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhoea
HP_0030998.definition: Drainage of cerebrospinal fluid through the nose. This can occur when there is a fistula between the dura and the skull base and discharge of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the nose.
HP_0030998.UMLS synonyms: Cerebrospinal Fluid Rhinorrhea | Leakage of cerebrospinal fluid from nose following surgical procedure | Cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea due to hydrocephalus | Intracranial hypotension due to cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea | Cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea due to pituitary tumor | Cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea due to empty sella syndrome

HP_0030999.label: abnormal vestibular saccule morphology
HP_0030999.definition: Any structural anomaly of the saccule of the vestibule. The saccule is the otolith organ that senses motions in the sagittal plane (i.e., up-down movement).

HP_0031000.label: vestibular saccular degeneration
HP_0031000.definition: Deterioration or loss of the tissues of the saccule of the vestibule.

HP_0031001.label: minifascicle formation
HP_0031001.definition: A nerve fascicle or fasciculus is a small bundle of axons, enclosed by the perineurium. A minifascule refers to a group of thinly myelinated and unmyelinated axons surrounded by a delicate perineurium, and with a smaller diameter than a normal nerve fascicle.

HP_0031002.label: neuritis
HP_0031002.UMLS synonyms: Neuritis | Optic Neuritis | Retrobulbar Neuritis | Brachial Plexus Neuritis | Ulnar Neuritis | Lumbosacral neuritis | Cranial neuritis | Acoustic neuritis | Thoracic neuritis | Neuritis, Sensory | Sciatic Neuritis | Tuberculous neuritis | Gouty neuritis | Cochlear Neuritis | Spinal neuritis | NEURITIS BULBAR | lumbar neuritis | Fungal neuritis | Bacterial neuritis | Autoimmune neuritis | Femoral Neuritis | Facial Neuritis | Lophocalama neuritis | Suppurative neuritis | Nonsuppurative neuritis

HP_0031003.label: polyneuritis
HP_0031003.UMLS synonyms: Polyneuritis | Acute Infective Polyneuritis | Inflammatory polyneuropathy, unspecified | Polyneuritis cranialis | polyneuritis; erythredema | polyneuritis; febrile | Diphtheritic polyneuritis | POLYNEURITIS, DIABETIC | polyneuritis; nutritional (manifestation) | polyneuritis; diabetes (manifestation) | polyneuritis; diphtheritic (manifestation) | polyneuritis; endemic (manifestation) | POST-VACCINE POLYNEURITIS | Cauda Equina Syndrome | Alcoholic Neuropathy | Beriberi | Acute (post-)infective polyneuritis | Acrodynia | Multiple cranial nerve palsy | polyneuritis; lack of vitamin (manifestation) | Infantile poisoning caused by mercury | psychosis; polyneuritic | nutritional; polyneuritic (manifestation) | endemic; polyneuritic (manifestation) | diphtheritic; polyneuritic (manifestation)

HP_0031004.label: hemiareflexia
HP_0031004.definition: Areflexia that is limited to one side of the body.

HP_0031006.label: acroparesthesia
HP_0031006.definition: A type of paresthesia (tingling, pins-and-needles, burning or numbness or stiffness) that occurs in the hands and feet and particularly in the fingers and toes.
HP_0031006.UMLS synonyms: Acroparesthesia | Vasomotor acroparesthesia | Simple acroparesthesia | Acroparesthesia Syndrome | Schultze's type acroparesthesia; simple | Vasomotor acroparesthesia [Nothnagel's type] | Acroparesthesia disease, Schulze's type | Acroparesthesias, episodic

HP_0031007.label: orofacial action - specific dystonia induced by speech

HP_0031008.label: lingual dystonia
HP_0031008.definition: Involuntary protrusions, movements, spams and contortions of the tongue.

HP_0031009.label: ainhum
HP_0031009.definition: Development of a fibrotic constriction ring involving the base of one or more toes, conditioning eversion and absorption of distal structures, possibly progressing to spontaneous amputation.
HP_0031009.UMLS synonyms: Ainhum | Ainhum of fifth toe | Pseudoainhum | Ainhum (spontaneous amputation) of toe (primarily 5th)

HP_0031010.label: hyperphalangy of the 3rd finger
HP_0031010.definition: An accessory phalanx of the third (middle) finger that is arranged linearly with the other phalanges. Hyperphalangy results from an accessory ossification center at the metacarpophalangeal joint.

HP_0031011.label: fatty streak
HP_0031011.definition: Yellow-colored streaks, patches, or spots on the intimal surface of arteries. Fatty streaks stain red with Sudan III or Sudan IV.

HP_0031012.label: thin - cap fibroatheroma
HP_0031012.definition: Thin-cap fibroatheroma is characterized by a relatively large necrotic core with an overlying thin fibrous cap measuring less than 65 micrometers and typically containing numerous macrophages, and is considered to be the precursor lesion of plaque rupture which is the most common cause of coronary thrombosis.

HP_0031013.label: ankylosis
HP_0031013.definition: A reduction of joint mobility resulting from changes involving the articular surfaces.
HP_0031013.UMLS synonyms: Ankylosis | Tooth Ankylosis | Temporomandibular ankylosis | Osseous ankylosis | Knee joint ankylosis | Fibrous ankylosis | Thoracolumbar ankylosis | Cervicothoracic ankylosis | sacral ankylosis | Glossopalatine ankylosis | Atlantoaxial ankylosis | Ossicular ankylosis | Ankylosis of spine | wrist; ankylosis | ankylosis; shoulder | ankylosis; cricoarytenoid | Ankylosis of the elbow joint | Cervical spine ankylosis | Mandibular ankylosis | ankylosis; finger | ankylosis; postoperative | Ankylosis of hip | VERTEBRA ANKYLOSIS

HP_0031014.label: arteria lusoria
HP_0031014.definition: Usually, three large arteries arise from the arch of the aorta: the brachiocephalic trunk (divided into the right common carotid artery and the right subclavian artery), the left common carotid artery, and the left subclavian artery. However, when aberrant right subclavian artery variant is present, the brachiocephalic trunk is absent and four large arteries arise from the arch of the aorta: the right common carotid artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery, and the final one with the most distal left sided origin, the right subclavian artery, also called the arteria lusoria.
HP_0031014.synonyms: aberrant right subclavian artery | lusorian artery
HP_0031014.UMLS synonyms: aberrant right subclavian artery | Aberrant retroesophageal subclavian artery causing dysphagia lusoria

HP_0031015.label: intrahepatic portal vein sclerosis
HP_0031015.definition: Sclerosis of the intrahepatic portal veins of the liver and generally accompanied by non-cirrhotic portal hypertension, features of which may include splenomegaly and varices.
HP_0031015.synonyms: idiopathic non - cirrhotic portal hypertension | incomplete septal cirrhosis | non cirrhotic portal fibrosis | obliterative portal venopathy

HP_0031016.label: alternating radiolucent and radiodense metaphyseal lines
HP_0031016.definition: Areas of radio-opaque sclerotic bands alternating with those of normal lucency give rise to stripes akin to a zebra.

HP_0031017.label: swiss cheese atrial septal defect
HP_0031017.definition: Multiple defects in the atrial septum.

HP_0031018.label: eccrine syringofibroadenoma
HP_0031018.definition: Eccrine syringofibroadenoma (ESFA) is a benign adnexal tumor arising most often on the extremities of elderly individuals characterized by anastomosing cords of cuboidal epithelial cells surrounded by a fibrovascular stroma containing plasma cells and ductal structures. ESFA stains positively with epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA).
HP_0031018.synonyms: acrosyringeal adenomatosis | eccrine syringofibroadenomatous hyperplasia | syringofibroadenoma

HP_0031019.label: pyknotic bone marrow neutrophils
HP_0031019.definition: Nuclear lobes of neutrophils in the bone marrow are thickened and condensed, and individual lobes are connected by unusually long chromatin filaments.

HP_0031020.label: bone marrow hypercellularity
HP_0031020.definition: A larger than normal amount or percentage of hematopoietic cells relative to marrow fat.
HP_0031020.UMLS synonyms: Bone marrow myeloid hyperplasia (finding) | Hypercellularity seen on bone marrow biopsy | Hypercellular bone marrow | Hypercellular bone marrow with erythroid hyperplasia

HP_0031021.label: squamous papilloma
HP_0031021.definition: A benign epithelial neoplasm characterized by a papillary growth pattern and a proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells without morphologic evidence of malignancy [NCI thesaurus].
HP_0031021.UMLS synonyms: Papilloma, Squamous Cell | Lung Squamous Papilloma | Bladder Squamous Papilloma | Vulvar Squamous Papilloma | Vaginal Squamous Papilloma | Nasopharyngeal Squamous Papilloma | Inverted Squamous Cell Papilloma | Squamous Papilloma of the Larynx | Squamous cell papilloma of esophagus | Squamous cell papilloma of eyelid | Squamous cell papilloma of oral cavity | Tonsil squamous cell papilloma | Childhood Laryngeal Squamous Papilloma | Rat Squamous Cell Papilloma | squamous cell papilloma of anal canal | Squamous Papilloma of the Urinary Tract | Squamous cell papilloma of skin | Skin tag | Squamous Cell Papilloma of the Rat Bronchus | Squamous Cell Papilloma of the Rat Larynx | Squamous Cell Papilloma of the Rat Tongue | Squamous Cell Papilloma of the Rat Trachea

HP_0031022.label: oropharyngeal squamous papilloma
HP_0031022.definition: A benign exophytic neoplasm that arises from the oropharynx. It is characterized by the presence of a connective tissue core covered by stratified squamous epithelium [NCI thesaurus].
HP_0031022.UMLS synonyms: HPV positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma

HP_0031023.label: multiple mucosal neuromas
HP_0031023.definition: Multiple painful, dome-shaped, translucent pink to skin-colored papules on oral mucosa. Histologically, the lesions may demonstrate dermal proliferation of well-demarcated nerve bundles associated with abundant mucin and surrounded by a distinct perineural sheath.

HP_0031024.label: cylindroma
HP_0031024.definition: A benign skin adnexal tumor of eccrine differentiation.
HP_0031024.UMLS synonyms: Cylindroma of skin | Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma | Eccrine dermal cylindroma | Sporadic Cylindroma | Malignant cylindroma of skin | Cylindroma of breast | Familial multiple cylindroma | Ancell-Spiegler cylindromas | Metastatic adenoid cystic carcinoma | Adenoid cystic carcinoma of trachea | Malignant neoplasm arising from pre-existing cylindroma | Primary adenoid cystic carcinoma of trachea | Cylindroma Type of Basaloid Follicular Neoplasm of the Mouse Skin | Cylindromas may show malignant transformation | Cylindromas, multiple (face, trunk and extremities) | Cylindromas usually occur on the scalp may coalesce into large 'turban tumors' | Cylindromas, multiple (usually occur on the scalp, but may also occur on the face, trunk, and extremities)

HP_0031025.label: gastric leiomyosarcoma
HP_0031025.definition: A malignant neoplasm of the stomach that grows submucosally in the gastric wall. Necrosis and hemorrhage may be visible radiologically. Histologically, spindle cells with abnormal mitotic activity may be visible.
HP_0031025.UMLS synonyms: Leiomyosarcoma of stomach | Leiomyosarcoma of gastric corpus structure | Carney Triad

HP_0031026.label: snail - like ilia
HP_0031026.definition: The ilia is round and hypoplastic with a very flat acetabular roof and a very unusual medial projection of bone that is said to resemble the head of a snail. Figure 4 of PMID:3799723 illustrates this feature.
HP_0031026.synonyms: schneckenbecken dysplasia | snail - like pelvis | snail - shaped ilia

HP_0031027.label: internal notch of the femoral head
HP_0031027.definition: A small V-shaped indentation on the internal aspect of the femoral head. This feature is well illustrated in Figure 5 of PMID:11694546.

HP_0031028.label: lactescent serum
HP_0031028.definition: Serum sample with a grossly white (milk-like, i.e., lactescent) appearance. This feature is indicative of an extremely elevated serum triglyceride level.

HP_0031029.label: elevated carcinoembryonic antigen level
HP_0031029.definition: An increased blood concentration of the carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA). CEA is a member of the immunoglobulin supergene family. The human CEA gene family is clustered on chromosome 19q and comprises 29 genes. CEA is highly expressed in embryonic tissue and in some cancers, and is a widely used tumor marker.

HP_0031030.label: elevated carcinoma antigen 125 level
HP_0031030.definition: An increased blood concentration of carcinoma antigen 125 (CA-125). CA-125, also known as mucin 16, can exhibit increased blood levels in certain types of cancer.

HP_0031031.label: abnormal retinol - binding protein level
HP_0031031.definition: A deviation from normal blood concentration of retinol-binding protein (RBP). The most commonly used indicator of vitamin A status is the serum retinol concentration (retinol is one of the several compounds known as vitamin A). The serum RBP concentration is used as a surrogate measure for serum retinol.

HP_0031032.label: decreased retinol - binding protein level
HP_0031032.definition: A reduced blood concentration of retinol-binding protein. This finding predicts vitamin A deficiency with high sensitivity and specificity.

HP_0031033.label: impaired urinary acidification
HP_0031033.definition: The kidney contributes towards acid-base homeostasis by excreting H+ ions and retaining bicarbonate. This process is known as acidification of the urine. The pH of urine ranges normally from 4.5 to 8. The inability to reduce the pH of the urine in a situation where it would be otherwise expected is known as an acidification defect.

HP_0031034.label: abnormal insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit level
HP_0031034.definition: A deviation from the normal blood concentration of the insulin like growth factor binding protein acid labile subunit (IGFALS; Entrez Gene ID 3483). The acid-labile subunit (IGFALS) acts in the insulin-like growth (IGF) system by binding circulating IGF1 in a ternary complex with binding protein (IGFBP)-3 to prevent IGF1 from crossing the endothelial barrier.

HP_0031035.label: chronic infection
HP_0031035.definition: Presence of a protracted or persistent infection by a pathogen potentially related to an underlying abnormality of the immune system that is not able to clear the infection.
HP_0031035.UMLS synonyms: Chronic Infection | Chronic staphylococcal infection | Chronic EBV infection | Chronic bronchopulmonary infection | Have Chronic Infection | adenoid; infection, chronic | Kidney infection chronic NOS | Chronic infection with HIV | Chronic urinary tract infection | Chronic active EBV infection | Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection | Chronic Haemophilus influenzae infection | Chronic bacterial anorectal infection | HBeAg-negative chronic infection | chronic hepatitis D infection | chronic upper respiratory infection | chronic hepatitis G infection | respiratory tract; infection, chronic | maxilla; infection, sinus (chronic) | FOOT INFECTION OSTEOMYELITIS CHRONIC | Chronic Epstein-Barr virus infection syndrome | Chronic sinusitis

HP_0031036.label: reduced growth - hormone binding protein level
HP_0031036.definition: A decreased blood concentration of growth hormone binding protein.

HP_0031037.label: reduced insulin - like factor 3 level
HP_0031037.definition: Blood concentration of insulin-like factor 3 (ILF3) is below normal limits.

HP_0031038.label: spermatogenesis maturation arrest
HP_0031038.definition: Maturation arrest (MA) is defined as germ cells that fail to complete maturation. Uniform MA is characterized by spermatogenic arrest at the same stage of spermatogenesis throughout the seminiferous tubules. MA is subcategorized into early MA, in which only spermatogonia or spermatocytes are found, and late MA, in which spermatids are detected without spermatozoa.
HP_0031038.UMLS synonyms: History of maturation arrest of spermatogenesis | Spermatogenesis maturation arrest (at zygotene or pachytene state)

HP_0031039.label: spermatocyte maturation arrest
HP_0031039.definition: A type of spermatogenesis maturation arrest in which the block of developmental occurs in the spermatocyte stage. Testicular histology shows seminiferous tubules with Sertoli cells, spermatogonial cells and spermatocytes but no further differentiated cells like round spermatids.
HP_0031039.synonyms: spermatocyte arrest | spermatocyte meiotic arrest | spermatocytic arrest
HP_0031039.UMLS synonyms: Maturation arrest at primary spermatocyte (pachytene stage)

HP_0031040.label: round spermatid arrest
HP_0031040.definition: A failure of spermatogenesis to progress beyond the round spermatid stage. The round spermatid is the first haploid cells produced during spermatogenesis and normally further develop into mature spermatozoa. This abnormality can be visualized with testicular biopsy and is characterized seminiferous tubules with increased numbers of round spermatids with few or no mature spermatozoa.
HP_0031040.synonyms: late spermatogenesis maturation arrest | maturation arrest of spermatogenesis at spermatid stage
HP_0031040.UMLS synonyms: Maturation arrest at round spermatid stage

HP_0031041.label: obstruction of the superior vena cava
HP_0031041.definition: Blockage of blood flow through the superior vena cava (SVC). Because the venous drainage from the upper extremities, upper thorax and head is obstructed, SVC obstruction presents with symptoms related to engorgement of these areas. Both the degree of SVC compromise and the extent of collateral veins determine the varied clinical presentation, which can be as mild as slight facial and upper extremity edema or as dire as intracranial swelling, seizures, hemodynamic instability and tracheal obstruction.
HP_0031041.synonyms: superior vena cava obstruction | superior vena cava syndrome
HP_0031041.UMLS synonyms: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome | Occlusion of superior vena cava

HP_0031042.label: strawberry tongue
HP_0031042.definition: Inflamed tongue with hyperplastic (enlarged) fungiform papillae that is said to resemble a strawberry or raspberry.
HP_0031042.UMLS synonyms: Strawberry tongue | strawberry color of tongue | Injected, dry, fissured lips or strawberry tongue

HP_0031043.label: type a4 brachydactyly
HP_0031043.definition: A type of brachydactyly characterized by brachymesophalangy affecting mainly the 2nd and 5th digits.

HP_0031044.label: type a5 brachydactyly
HP_0031044.definition: A type of brachydactyly characterized by absent middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5.
HP_0031044.UMLS synonyms: Brachydactyly type A5 | Brachydactyly type A5 nail dysplasia

HP_0031045.label: acral blistering
HP_0031045.definition: Bullae (defined as fluid-filled blisters more than 5 mm in diameter with thin walls) of the skin with an acral distribution (affecting peripheral regions such as hands and feet).
HP_0031045.UMLS synonyms: Neonatal acral blistering | Blistering primarily at acral sites | Basan syndrome

HP_0031046.label: absent soft palate
HP_0031046.definition: A developmental defect characterized by lack of a soft palate.

HP_0031047.label: paraproteinemia
HP_0031047.definition: An abnormal immunoglobulin or part of an Ig (light chain) in the circulation. Paraproteins are typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.
HP_0031047.UMLS synonyms: Paraproteinemias | Monoclonal Paraproteinemia | Benign paraproteinemia | Neuropathy, paraproteinemia | Paraproteinemia-associated scleredema | Monoclonal Gammapathies | Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma with paraproteinemia | Hereditary hypertrophic neuropathy with paraproteinemia | Subcorneal pustular dermatosis with paraproteinemia | paraproteinemia; secondary to malignant disease | secondary; paraproteinemia (secondary to malignant disease) | Paraproteinemia secondary to malignant or inflammatory disease | Monoclonal Paraproteinemia Present in Lower than Myeloma Levels | CANOMAD syndrome | Other paraproteinemias

HP_0031048.label: light - chain paraproteinemia
HP_0031048.definition: An abnormal immunoglobulin light chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

HP_0031049.label: heavy - chain paraproteinemia
HP_0031049.definition: An abnormal immunoglobulin heavy chain in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

HP_0031050.label: whole - immunoglobulin paraproteinemia
HP_0031050.definition: An abnormal immunoglobulin (heavy and light chain) in the circulation and typically produced by a clonal population of B-cell derived plasma cells.

HP_0031051.label: tarsal sclerosis
HP_0031051.definition: An elevation in bone density in one or more tarsal bones of the foot. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.

HP_0031052.label: elevated vascular endothelial growth factor level
HP_0031052.definition: Increased blood concentration of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).

HP_0031053.label: coarctation in the transverse aortic arch
HP_0031053.definition: Narrowing or constriction of the aorta localized to the region of the transverse aortic arch.

HP_0031054.label: long segment coarctation of the aorta
HP_0031054.definition: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a long segment of the arch of the aorta.

HP_0031055.label: abnormal branching pattern of left aortic arch
HP_0031055.definition: A deviance from the norm of the origin or course of the right brachiocephalic artery, the left common carotid artery, the left subclavian artery or the proximal vertebral arteries, whereby the aortic arch descends on the left as normal (as opposed to right aortic arch).

HP_0031056.label: fusiform cerebral aneurysm
HP_0031056.definition: A localized circumferential (i.e., bulges on all sides) dilatation or ballooning of a cerebral artery.

HP_0031057.label: skin fissure
HP_0031057.definition: A clearly-defined and roughly linear cleavage in the skin that usually extends to the dermis.
HP_0031057.UMLS synonyms: Fissure in skin | skin fissure number (# ___) (physical finding) | No fissure in skin | skin fissure on glabella | skin fissure total number | skin fissure on ear | skin fissure on forehead | skin fissure on chin | skin fissure on forearm | skin fissure of chest | skin fissure on breast | skin fissure on abdomen | skin fissure of perineum | skin fissure of scrotum | skin fissure of vulva | skin fissure of foot | skin fissure on temple | skin fissure on nose | skin fissure on eyelid | skin fissure on canthus | skin fissure on cheek | skin fissure on lip | skin fissure on elbow | skin fissure of wrist | skin fissure on hand

HP_0031058.label: impairment of activities of daily living
HP_0031058.definition: Difficulty in performing one or more activities normally performed every day, such as eating, bathing, dressing, grooming, work, homemaking, and leisure.
HP_0031058.UMLS synonyms: Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study-Activities of Daily Living Inventory Mild Cognitive Impairment Questionnaire | Activities of daily living impaired | Assessment of and care planning for a patient with cognitive impairment, requiring an independent historian, in the office or other outpatient, home or domiciliary or rest home, with all of the following required elements: Cognition-focused evaluation including a pertinent history and examination, Medical decision making of moderate or high complexity, Functional assessment (eg, basic and instrumental activities of daily living), including decision-making capacity, Use of standardized instruments for staging of dementia (eg, functional assessment staging test [FAST], clinical dementia rating [CDR]), Medication reconciliation and review for high-risk medications, Evaluation for neuropsychiatric and behavioral symptoms, including depression, including use of standardized screening instrument(s), Evaluation of safety (eg, home), including motor vehicle operation, Identification of caregiver(s), caregiver knowledge, caregiver needs, social supports, and the willingness of caregiver to take on caregiving tasks, Development, updating or revision, or review of an Advance Care Plan, Creation of a written care plan, including initial plans to address any neuropsychiatric symptoms, neuro-cognitive symptoms, functional limitations, and referral to community resources as needed (eg, rehabilitation services, adult day programs, support groups) shared with the patient and/or caregiver with initial education and support. Typically, 60 minutes of total time is spent on the date of the encounter.

HP_0031059.label: impaired ability to bathe oneself
HP_0031059.definition: This term applies to an individual who requires help to bathe more than one part of the body, get in or out of the tub or shower, or who requires total bathing.

HP_0031060.label: impaired ability to dress oneself
HP_0031060.definition: This applies to an individual who needs help with dressing or needs to be completely dressed.

HP_0031061.label: impaired toileting ability
HP_0031061.definition: This term applies to an individual who requires help transferring to the toilet, cleaning self or who uses bedpan or commode.
HP_0031061.UMLS synonyms: Impaired ability to manipulate clothing for toileting | Impaired ability to flush toilet | Impaired ability to reach toilet | Impaired ability to sit on toilet | Impaired ability to complete toilet hygiene | Impaired ability to rise from toilet | Impaired ability to transfer on or off a toilet

HP_0031062.label: impaired transferring ability
HP_0031062.definition: Applies to an individual who needs help in moving from bed to chair or requires a complete transfer.
HP_0031062.UMLS synonyms: Impaired transferring ability | Impaired ability to transfer location | Difficulty transferring location | Impaired ability to transfer between uneven levels | Impaired ability to transfer between chair and floor | Impaired ability to transfer between bed and chair | Impaired ability to transfer between car and chair | Impaired ability to transfer between chair and standing position | Impaired ability to transfer between floor and standing position | Impaired ability to transfer between bed and standing position | Impaired ability to transfer in or out of shower | Impaired ability to transfer on or off a toilet | Impaired ability to transfer on or off a commode | Impaired ability to transfer in or out of bath tub

HP_0031063.label: impaired feeding ability
HP_0031063.definition: Applies to an individual who needs partial or total help with feeding or requires parenteral feeding.
HP_0031063.UMLS synonyms: Self-feeding deficit | Impaired ability to self-feed a complete meal | Impaired ability to self-feed in an acceptable manner

HP_0031064.label: impaired continence
HP_0031064.definition: Partial or total incontinence of bowel or bladder.

HP_0031065.label: abnormal ovarian morphology
HP_0031065.UMLS synonyms: Cystic ovarian follicle | Ovarian follicular stigma | Uterine tumor resembling ovarian sex cord tumor

HP_0031067.label: empty ovarian follicle
HP_0031067.definition: A failure to collect oocytes after an apparently normal controlled ovarian hyperstimulation cycle for in vitro fertilization.

HP_0031069.label: abnormal femoral torsion
HP_0031069.definition: Femoral torsion, also known as femoral rotation or femoral version, refers to the twist between the proximal and distal parts of the femur on the transverse plane. Femoral anteversion averages between 30-40 degress at birth, and between 8-14 degrees in adults. This term applies if the amount of femoral torsion deviates from this range.

HP_0031071.label: abnormal endocrine morphology
HP_0031071.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of an organ ofthe endocrine system.
HP_0031071.UMLS synonyms: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia | Benign tumor of endocrine gland | Endocrine tumor morphology | Malignant endocrine tumor morphology | Functioning endocrine tumor | Mixed Ductal-Endocrine Carcinoma | Mixed acinar-endocrine carcinoma | Mixed acinar-endocrine-ductal carcinoma | Endocrine mucin-producing sweat gland carcinoma

HP_0031072.label: abnormal endocrine physiology
HP_0031072.definition: Any anomaly of the function of the endocrine system.

HP_0031073.label: abnormal response to endocrine stimulation test
HP_0031073.definition: An anomalous response to a test that is designed to probe the function of the endocrine system.

HP_0031074.label: abnormal response to acth stimulation test
HP_0031074.definition: An anomolous response to stimulation by adminstration of the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH). ACTH stimulation normally stimulates the adrenal glands to release cortisol and adrenaline.
HP_0031074.synonyms: abnormal response to adrenocorticotropic - hormone stimulation test | abnormal response to corticotropin stimulation test

HP_0031075.label: abnormal response to insulin tolerance test
HP_0031075.definition: An anomalous response to the insulin tolerance test (ITT), in which insulin is administered intravenously and blood glucose and potentially other compounds are measured at intervals. Insulin administration is intended to induce extreme hypoglycemia (bloodgluoce below 40 mg/dl), which in turn induces release of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and growth hormone (GH). ACTH induces the adrenal gland to release cortisol, which together with GH opposes the action of insulin on the blood glucose level.

HP_0031076.label: impaired cortisol response to insulin stimulation test
HP_0031076.definition: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the insulin tolerance test (ITT).

HP_0031077.label: abnormal response to corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test
HP_0031077.definition: An anomalous response to the corticotropin releasing hormone (CRH) stimulation test. Normally,CRH is released by the hypothalamus to induce adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) release by the anterior pituitary. In the stimulation test, CRH is administered intravenously and ACTH and cortisol are measured at intervals.
HP_0031077.synonyms: abnormal response to crh stimulation test

HP_0031078.label: impaired cortisol response to corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test
HP_0031078.definition: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test.

HP_0031079.label: impaired growth - hormone response to insulin stimulation test
HP_0031079.definition: Failure of growth hormone levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the insulin tolerance test (ITT).

HP_0031080.label: abnormal response to glucagon stimulation test
HP_0031080.definition: An anomalous response to the glucagon stimulation test, which like the insulin tolerance test (ITT) stimulates the release of both adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and growth hormone (GH).

HP_0031081.label: impaired cortisol response to glucagon stimulation test
HP_0031081.definition: Failure of cortisol levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the glucagon stimulation test.

HP_0031082.label: impaired growth - hormone response to glucagon stimulation test
HP_0031082.definition: Failure of growth hormone levels to respond adequately (by increasing) to the glucagon stimulation test.

HP_0031083.label: abnormal response to human chorionic gonadotrophin stimulation test
HP_0031083.definition: An anomalous response to intravenous stimulation by human chorionic gonadotrophin. Stimulation with hCG stimulates testicular Leydig cells to secrete androgens via the Leydig hormone receptors.
HP_0031083.synonyms: abnormal response to hcg stimulation test

HP_0031084.label: excessive insulin response to glucagon test
HP_0031084.definition: An abnormally high increase in insulin levels following a glucagon stimulation test.

HP_0031085.label: decreased prealbumin level
HP_0031085.definition: A reduced concentration of prealbumin in the blood. Prealbumin, also known as transthyretin, has a half-life in plasma of about 2 days, much shorter than that of albumin. Prealbumin is therefore more sensitive to changes in protein-energy status than albumin, and its concentration closely reflects recent dietary intake rather than overall nutritional status.

HP_0031086.label: ectopic ovary
HP_0031086.definition: Undescended or ectopic ovaries are characterized by the attachment of the upper pole of the ovary to an area above the level of the common iliac vessels.
HP_0031086.UMLS synonyms: Ectopic ovary | Ectopic pregnancy of left ovary | Ectopic pregnancy of right ovary | Removal of ectopic fetus from ovary without oophorectomy | left oophorectomy for ectopic pregnancy | right oophorectomy for ectopic pregnancy | Level IV surgical pathology with gross and microscopic examination

HP_0031087.label: absent pubertal growth spurt
HP_0031087.definition: The abrupt and transient increase in the annual growth rate normally observed in adolescent individuals does not occur.
HP_0031087.UMLS synonyms: Delayed or absent pubertal growth spurt | Weak or absent pubertal growth spurt

HP_0031088.label: vaginal dryness
HP_0031088.UMLS synonyms: Vaginal dryness | Vaginal Dryness, CTCAE_3 | Vaginal Dryness, CTCAE_5 | Have Vaginal Dryness | Vaginal dryness on intercourse | Bothered by Vaginal Dryness | Had Vaginal Dryness or Pain | Grade 1 Vaginal Dryness, CTCAE | Grade 3 Vaginal Dryness, CTCAE | Grade 2 Vaginal Dryness, CTCAE | PRO-CTCAE V1.0 - Vaginal Dryness Severity | Worst Severity Past Seven Days Vaginal Dryness | Have Vaginal Dryness or Other Problem During Intercourse | I have vaginal dryness in the past 7D | FACIT-Searchable Item Library Adult Version - I Have Vaginal Dryness | I have vaginal dryness in the past 7D:Find:7D:^Patient:Ord:FACIT

HP_0031089.label: palatal edema
HP_0031089.definition: Swelling related to fluid accumulation within the palate.
HP_0031089.synonyms: palatal oedema | palate edema | palate oedema

HP_0031090.label: finger dactylitis
HP_0031090.definition: Fingers appear swollen and plump owing to inflammation of the complete finger.
HP_0031090.UMLS synonyms: Dactylitis of finger | dactylitis of left little finger | dactylitis of left ring finger | dactylitis of left middle finger | dactylitis of left index finger | dactylitis of right ring finger | dactylitis of right little finger | dactylitis of right index finger | dactylitis of right middle finger | dactylitis of index finger of left hand | dactylitis of little finger of left hand | dactylitis of ring finger of left hand | dactylitis of middle finger of left hand | dactylitis of middle finger of right hand | dactylitis of index finger of right hand | dactylitis of ring finger of right hand | dactylitis of little finger of right hand | Extra-articular swelling of hands or fingers (i.e., sausage finger or dactylitis) | dactylitis of left fingers | dactylitis of right fingers

HP_0031091.label: toe dactylitis
HP_0031091.definition: Toes appear swollen and plump owing to inflammation of the complete toe.
HP_0031091.UMLS synonyms: Sausage toe | dactylitis of left third toe | dactylitis of left little toe | dactylitis of left great toe | dactylitis of left fourth toe | dactylitis of left second toe | dactylitis of right little toe | dactylitis of right great toe | dactylitis of right second toe | dactylitis of right third toe | dactylitis of right fourth toe | dactylitis of fifth toe of left foot | dactylitis of third toe of left foot | dactylitis of second toe of left foot | dactylitis of fourth toe of left foot | dactylitis of third toe of right foot | dactylitis of second toe of right foot | dactylitis of fourth toe of right foot | dactylitis of little toe of right foot | dactylitis of left toes | dactylitis of right toes

HP_0031092.label: spindle - shaped finger
HP_0031092.definition: Swelling of the hand at the knuckles, that gives the fingers a spindle shape (i.e., a round stick with tapered end and a broader base).

HP_0031093.label: abnormal breast morphology
HP_0031093.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of the breast.
HP_0031093.UMLS synonyms: Accessory breast | Breast cavity | Secretory breast carcinoma | Cylindroma of breast | Lobular development of breast | Cyclic alteration of breast | Menstrual involution of breast | Acinar development of breast | Post-surgical breast structure | Papillary carcinoma of the breast | Secretory cyclic alteration of breast | Inappropriate lobular activity of breast | Proliferative cyclic alteration of breast | Invasive micropapillary carcinoma of breast | Paget's disease and intraductal carcinoma of breast | Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma | Paget's disease and infiltrating duct carcinoma of breast

HP_0031094.label: abnormal breast physiology
HP_0031094.definition: Any anomaly of the function of the breast.

HP_0031095.label: abnormal humerus morphology
HP_0031095.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of the humerus.
HP_0031095.UMLS synonyms: Neer four-part fracture | Neer one-part fracture | Neer two-part fracture | Neer three-part fracture | Closed Neer three-part fracture | Closed Neer four-part fracture | Open Neer four-part fracture | Open Neer three-part fracture

HP_0031096.label: delayed vertebral ossification
HP_0031096.definition: A decrease in the amount of mineralized bone in one or more vertebrae compared with that expected for a given developmental age.
HP_0031096.UMLS synonyms: Mildly delayed vertebral ossification | Delayed vertebral body ossification, mild | Delayed ossification of cervical vertebral bodies | Vertebral body ossification delay

HP_0031097.label: abnormal thyroid - stimulating hormone level
HP_0031097.definition: Any deviation from the normal amount of the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), which is produced by the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates the function of the thyroid gland.
HP_0031097.synonyms: abnormal circulating thyrotropin concentration | abnormal thyrotropin level | abnormal tsh level
HP_0031097.UMLS synonyms: Serum thyroid stimulating hormone level outside reference range

HP_0031098.label: decreased thyroid - stimulating hormone level
HP_0031098.definition: Reduced amount of the thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), which is produced by the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates the function of the thyroid gland.
HP_0031098.synonyms: decreased plasma tsh | decreased thyrotropin level
HP_0031098.UMLS synonyms: Thyroid stimulating hormone level below reference range

HP_0031099.label: abnormal circulating inhibin level
HP_0031099.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of inhibins, which are heterodimeric protein hormones secreted by granulosa cells of the ovary in females and Sertoli cells of the testis in males. Inhibins suppress the secretion of pituitary follicle-stimulating hormone.

HP_0031100.label: decreased inhibin b level
HP_0031100.definition: A reduced concentration of inhibin B in the blood.

HP_0031101.label: abnormal circulating antimullerian hormone concentration
HP_0031101.definition: Any deviation from the normal range of the antimullerian hormone, a peptide produced by the granulosa cells of follicles. Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH), also known as Mullerian inhibiting substance, is produced by the granulosa cells of small antral follicles of the ovary. AMH has an inhibiting role in the ovary, contributing to follicular arrest. AMH levels in women are low until the age of 8, rise rapidly until puberty and decline steadily from the age of 25 until menopause, when AMH production ceases.

HP_0031102.label: increased circulating antimullerian hormone concentration
HP_0031102.definition: An elevation above the normal range of the antimullerian hormone in the circulation.
HP_0031102.synonyms: increased antimullerian hormone level | increased plasma amh

HP_0031103.label: decreased cirrculating antimullerian hormone circulation
HP_0031103.definition: A reduction below the normal range of the antimullerian hormone in the circulation.
HP_0031103.synonyms: anti - mullerian hormone low | decreased antimullerian hormone level | decreased plasma amh

HP_0031104.label: insulin receptor antibody positivity
HP_0031104.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against the insulin receptor.

HP_0031105.label: abnormal uterus morphology
HP_0031105.definition: Any anomaly of the structure of the uterus

HP_0031106.label: t - shaped uterus
HP_0031106.definition: An abnormality of the uterus characterized by a normal uterine outline but with an abnormal T-shaped uterine cavity with narrowing cavity due to thickened lateral walls with a correlation 2/3 uterine corpus and 1/3 cervix. The abnormlaity is said to resemble the letter T in hysterosalpingographic imaging.
HP_0031106.UMLS synonyms: transvaginal ultrasound: T-shaped uterus | Cesarean section through inverted T shaped incision of uterus | Elective lower segment cesarean section through inverted T shaped incision of uterus

HP_0031107.label: decreased fibular diameter
HP_0031107.definition: Reduced width of the cross sectional diameter of the fibula.

HP_0031108.label: triceps weakness
HP_0031108.definition: A lack of strength in the triceps muscle, which normally is responsible for extending (straightening) the elbow and mediating certain shoulder movements.
HP_0031108.UMLS synonyms: weakness of left triceps | weakness of right triceps | weakness of triceps of both arms

HP_0031109.label: agalactia
HP_0031109.definition: Failure of secretion of milk following childbirth associated with an inability to breastfeed an infant.
HP_0031109.UMLS synonyms: Failure of lactation | Failure of lactation in non-human animal | agalactia; elective | Therapeutic agalactia | Secondary agalactia | Primary agalactia | agalactia with baby delivered | Mastitis-metritis-agalactia syndrome | Contagious agalactia of goat AND/OR sheep | Agalactia, with mention of attachment difficulty | Agalactia, without mention of attachment difficulty | agalactia as postpartum condition, delivered during current episode | Failure of lactation with antenatal complication | Failure of lactation with postnatal complication | Streptococcus agalactiae | Mycoplasma agalactiae | Streptococcus agalactiae antigen | Streptococcus agalactiae culture | Streptococcus agalactiae DNA | Streptococcus agalactiae rRNA | Mycoplasma agalactiae DNA | Streptococcus agalactiae Measurement | Streptococcus agalactiae septicaemia | sepsis; streptococcal, agalactiae | Mycoplasma agalactiae Ab

HP_0031110.label: twin - to - twin transfusion
HP_0031110.definition: As a result of sharing a single placenta, the blood supplies of monochorionic twin fetuses can become connected, so that they share blood circulation: although each fetus uses its own portion of the placenta, the connecting blood vessels within the placenta allow blood to pass from one twin to the other.Depending on the number, type and direction of the interconnecting blood vessels (anastomoses), blood can be transferred disproportionately from one twin (the donor) to the other (the recipient). This state of transfusion causes the donor twin to have decreased blood volume, retarding the donor's development and growth. The blood volume of the recipient twin is increased, which can strain the fetus's heart and eventually lead to heart failure.
HP_0031110.UMLS synonyms: twin to twin transfusion as antepartum condition | twin to twin transfusion with baby delivered | twin-to-twin; transfusion syndrome, affecting fetus | twin-to-twin; transfusion syndrome, mother (complicating pregnancy) | Renal tubular dysgenesis due to twin to twin transfusion | c.pregnancy; transfusion syndrome, placental, twin-to-twin, mother | Fetal disorder due to twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome | Fetus-to-fetus placental transfusion syndrome | Fetal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy due to twin to twin transfusion syndrome | Early neonatal disorder due to twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome | Polycythemia due to donor twin transfusion | Fetal pulmonary outflow tract obstruction due to twin to twin transfusion syndrome | Fetoscopic laser therapy for treatment of twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome | Fetoscopic laser photocoagulation of placental vessel for twin to twin transfusion syndrome | Rare disorder due to unbalanced inter-twin blood transfusion | Newborn affected by placental and cord abnormalities resulting in twin-to-twin or other transplacental transfusion | Fetus and newborn affected by placental transfusion syndromes

HP_0031111.label: cutaneous hamartoma
HP_0031111.definition: A hamartoma (tissue malformation consisting of an abnormal mixture of constitutive components) originating in the skin.
HP_0031111.UMLS synonyms: Hamartoma of skin | Cutaneous Neurocristic Hamartoma

HP_0031117.label: purely bicuspid aortic valve
HP_0031117.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by two equal-sized cusps, with no raphe and only two commissures. There is a lateral arrangement of the free edge of the cusps. Note that this differs from some other forms of BAV in which there are three commissures and two of the three cusps are joined by a raphe forming two functional leaflets. This type of BAV often is associated with aortic stenosis.

HP_0031118.label: single raphe bicuspid aortic valve
HP_0031118.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valvue (BAV) characterized by the presence of a single raphe that extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps, resulting in two leaflets of unequal size.

HP_0031119.label: bicuspid aortic valve with right - left cusp fusion
HP_0031119.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the right and left cusps (RL fusion pattern). This results in two leaflefts with an anterior-posterior leaflet orientation (also called the typical pattern). There is thus one completely developed noncoronary cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped left and right coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

HP_0031120.label: bicuspid aortic valve with right - noncoronary cusp fusion
HP_0031120.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the right and noncoronary cusps (RN fusion pattern). This results in two leaflets with right-left leaflet orientation (also called the atypical pattern). There is thus one completely developed left cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped right and noncoronary coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

HP_0031121.label: bicuspid aortic valve with left - noncoronary cusp fusion
HP_0031121.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) characterized by a single raphe between the left and noncoronary cusps (LN fusion pattern). There is thus one completely developed right cusp, two completely developed commissures, and one raphe between the underdeveloped left and noncoronary coronary cusps extending to the corresponding malformed commissure.

HP_0031122.label: two - raphe bicuspid aortic valve
HP_0031122.definition: A type of bicuspid aortic valvue (BAV) characterized by the presence of two raphes that each extend from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps. This type of BAV has developmental anlagen of three cusps, commissures, and sinuses, but two commissures are more or less malformed and obliterated, giving rise to a raphe, a fibrous ridge, which extends from the commissure to the free edge of the two underdeveloped, conjoint cusps. This type of BAV is typically associated with a high degree of aortic stenosis.

HP_0031123.label: recurrent gastroenteritis
HP_0031123.definition: Increased susceptibility to gastroenteritis, an infectious inflammationof the stomach and small intestines manifested by signs and symptoms such as diarheas and abdominal pain, as manifested by recurrent episodes of gastroenteritis.
HP_0031123.UMLS synonyms: CMV gastroenteritis recurrent | Recurrent infections at variable sites (sinusitis, otitis media, facial cellulitis, adenitis, blepharitis, conjunctivitis, gastroenteritis)

HP_0031124.label: decreased platelet thromboxane a2 receptor
HP_0031124.definition: Decreased cell membrane concentration of thromboxane A2 receptor that is stimulated by thromboxane A2 (TBXA2).

HP_0031125.label: decreased platelet alpha - 2a - adrenergic receptor
HP_0031125.definition: Decreased cell membrane concentration of alpha-2A adrenergic receptor that is stimulated by epinephrine.

HP_0031126.label: impaired clot retraction
HP_0031126.definition: Platelets contain contractile proteins (actin and myosin) that induce clot retraction. As the platelets contract, they pull on the surrounding fibrin strands, squeezing serum form the mass, compacting the clot and drawing the ruptured edges of the blood vessel more closely together. Clot retraction is directly proportional to the platelet count and inversely proportional to the fibrinogen concentration.
HP_0031126.UMLS synonyms: Blood coagulation disorder with impaired clot retraction time

HP_0031127.label: impaired convulxin - induced platelet aggregation
HP_0031127.definition: Abnormal response to convulxin as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of convulxin.

HP_0031128.label: impaired collagen - related peptide - induced platelet aggregation
HP_0031128.definition: Abnormal response to collagen-related peptide (CRP) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of CRP.

HP_0031129.label: impaired phorbol myristate acetate - induced platelet aggregation
HP_0031129.definition: Abnormal response to phorbol myristate acetate (PMA) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of PMA.

HP_0031130.label: impaired calcium ionophore - induced platelet aggregation
HP_0031130.definition: Abnormal response to calcium Ionophore (such as A23187) as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of the ionophore.
HP_0031130.synonyms: impaired ca ionophore - induced platelet aggregation | impaired ca2+ ionophore - induced platelet aggregation

HP_0031131.label: abnormal platelet phosphatidylserine exposure
HP_0031131.definition: An abnormality of phosphatidylserine (PS) on activated platelets. PS is normally located on the cytoplasmic face of the resting platelet membrane but appears on the plasma-oriented surface of discrete membrane vesicles that derive from activated platelets. Thrombin, the central molecule of coagulation, is produced from prothrombin by a complex (prothrombinase) between factor Xa and its protein cofactor (factor V(a)) that forms on platelet-derived membranes. This complex enhances the rate of activation of prothrombin to thrombin by roughly 150,000 fold relative to factor X(a) in solution. The negatively charged surface of PS-containing platelet-derived membranes is at least partly responsible for this rate enhancement.

HP_0031132.label: impaired annexin v binding to platelet phosphatidylserine
HP_0031132.definition: Reduced binding of annexin V to platelet membrane, which is mediated by exposed phosphatidylserine. This can be measured by flow cytometry.

HP_0031133.label: increased annexin v binding to platelet phosphatidylserine
HP_0031133.definition: Elevated binding of annexin V to platelet membrane, which is mediated by exposed phosphatidylserine. This can be measured by flow cytometry.

HP_0031134.label: cor triatrium sinister
HP_0031134.definition: A developmental anomaly of the heart characterized by the presence of three atria because the left atrium is divided by an abnormal septum.

HP_0031135.label: triggered by physical trauma
HP_0031135.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a trauma (injury to tissue).

HP_0031136.label: decreased acrosin in sperm head
HP_0031136.definition: A reduced amount of the enzyme acrosin in the sperm head acrosome. The acrosome is an organelle in the anterior half of the head of spermatozoa, and acrosin is a protease that contributes to the digestation of the zona pellucida in the fertilization process.

HP_0031137.label: storage in hepatocytes
HP_0031137.definition: Hepatocytes (liver parenchymal cells) exhibit a bloated appearance because of expansion of the cytoplasm by accumulated material.

HP_0031138.label: abnormal b - type natriuretic peptide concentration
HP_0031138.definition: A deviation from the normal circulating concentration of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP).
HP_0031138.synonyms: abnormal b - type natriuretic peptide level

HP_0031139.label: frog - leg posture
HP_0031139.definition: A type of rest posture in an infant that indicated a generalized reduction in muscle tone. The hips are flexed and the legs are abducted to an extent that causes the lateral thigh to rest upon the supporting surface. This posture is said to resemble the legs of a frog.

HP_0031140.label: abnormal liver sonography
HP_0031140.definition: An abnormal appearance of the liver or any of its components on sonography (ultrasound).

HP_0031141.label: increased hepatic echogenicity
HP_0031141.definition: Increased echogenicity of liver tissue on sonography, manifested as an increased amount of white on the screen of the sonography device.

HP_0031142.label: abnormal hepatic echogenicity
HP_0031142.definition: Any deviation from the normal degree of echogenicity of the liver on sonography. Echogenicity refers to the ability of a tissue to reflect or transmit ultrasound waves in the context of surrounding tissues. Whenever there is an interface of structures with different echogenicities, a visible difference in contrast will be apparent on the screen. Based on echogenicity, a structure can be characterized as hyperechoic (white on the screen), hypoechoic (gray on the screen) and anechoic (black on the screen).

HP_0031143.label: decreased hepatic echogenicity
HP_0031143.definition: Reduced echogenicity of liver tissue on sonography, manifested as an increased amount of black on the screen of the sonography device.

HP_0031144.label: coarsened hepatic echotexture
HP_0031144.definition: The appearance of the liver in sonographic images is normally uniform. This term applies when there is an irregular or non-uniform appearance of the liver parenchyma in liver sonography.

HP_0031145.label: starry sky appearance on hepatic sonography
HP_0031145.definition: An abnormal echotexture visible in liver ultrasound manifesting as a diffuse hyperechoic liver echotexture with multiple, small hypoechoic lesions. The appearance is said to resemble a starry sky (multiple white spots on a dark background).

HP_0031146.label: impaired oral bolus formation
HP_0031146.definition: An abnormality of swallowing characterized by reduced tongue coordination to form bolus after chewing. Food material spreads over the oral cavity instead of being concentrated into a bolus that is easily swallowed.

HP_0031150.label: vitreomacular adhesion
HP_0031150.definition: Perifoveal vitreous separation with remaining vitreomacular attachment and unperturbed foveal morphologic features. It is an OCT finding that is almost always the result of normal vitreous aging, which may lead to pathologic conditions.
HP_0031150.UMLS synonyms: Vitreomacular adhesion | Vitreomacular adhesion, bilateral | vitreomacular adhesion both eyes | Vitreomacular adhesion, unspecified eye | Vitreomacular adhesion of left eye | Vitreomacular adhesion of right eye | Vitreomacular adhesion of bilateral eyes

HP_0031151.label: vitreomacular traction
HP_0031151.definition: Vitreomacular traction is characterized by anomalous posterior vitreous detachment accompanied by anatomic distortion of the fovea, which may include pseudocysts, macular schisis, cystoid macular edema, and subretinal fluid. Vitreomacular traction can be subclassified by the diameter of vitreous attachment to the macular surface as measured by OCT, with attachment of 1500 micrometers or less defined as focal and attachment of more than 1500 micrometers as broad.

HP_0031152.label: full - thickness macular hole
HP_0031152.definition: Full-thickness macular hole (FTMH) is defined as a foveal lesion with interruption of all retinal layers from the internal limiting membrane to the retinal pigment epithelium. Full-thickness macular hole is primary if caused by vitreous traction or secondary if directly the result of pathologic characteristics other than vitreomacular traction. Full-thickness macular hole is subclassified by size of the hole as determined by OCT and the presence or absence of vitreomacular traction.
HP_0031152.UMLS synonyms: Full thickness macular hole stage III | Full thickness macular hole stage IV | Full thickness macular hole stage II | Full thickness macular hole of left eye | Full thickness macular hole of right eye | Full thickness hole of macula lutea | Bilateral full thickness hole of macula of eyes

HP_0031153.label: membranous vitreous appearance
HP_0031153.definition: Vitreous humor of the eye displaying consisting of a vestigial gel in the retrolental space bounded by a convoluted membrane.
HP_0031153.synonyms: membranous anomaly | membranous vitreous | membranous vitreous phenotype

HP_0031154.label: beaded vitreous appearance
HP_0031154.definition: Vitreous humor of the eye displaying beaded bundles of irregular diameters.

HP_0031155.label: increased arden ratio of electrooculogram
HP_0031155.definition: An abnormal increase in the Arden ratio, which is the ratio between the light peak and the dark trough of the smoothed (physiologic) EOG record.

HP_0031156.label: decreased platelet glycoprotein ib
HP_0031156.definition: Decreased platelet cell membrane concentration of glycoprotein Ib.
HP_0031156.UMLS synonyms: Platelets have decreased expression of glycoprotein Ib-alpha (CD42B)

HP_0031157.label: carotid cavernous fistula
HP_0031157.definition: An abnormal connection between a carotid artery and the cavernous sinus.
HP_0031157.UMLS synonyms: Carotid-Cavernous Sinus Fistula | Dural carotid cavernous fistula | Traumatic carotid cavernous fistula | Embolization of carotid cavernous fistula | Obliteration of carotid cavernous fistula | Acquired left carotid cavernous fistula | Acquired right carotid cavernous fistula | Traumatic left carotid cavernous fistula | Traumatic Carotid-Cavernous Sinus Fistula | Traumatic right carotid cavernous fistula | Intracranial electrothrombosis of carotid-cavernous fistula | Transcatheter embolization of carotid cavernous fistula | Injection procedure on carotid-cavernous fistula | Balloon catheterization of carotid-cavernous fistula | Intra-arterial embolization of carotid-cavernous fistula | Obliteration of carotid-cavernous fistula by dissection within cavernous sinus | Repair of carotid-cavernous fistula by balloon catheter | Repair of carotid-cavernous fistula by injection procedure | Repair of carotid-cavernous fistula by intracranial electrothrombosis | Obliteration of carotid aneurysm, arteriovenous malformation, or carotid-cavernous fistula by dissection within cavernous sinus | intracranial and cervical occlusion of carotid artery for carotid-cavernous fistula | Surgery of aneurysm, vascular malformation or carotid-cavernous fistula | Repair of carotid-cavernous fistula by intracranial and cervical occlusion of carotid artery | Surgery on carotid-cavernous fistula by intracranial and cervical occlusion of carotid artery | Surgery of aneurysm, vascular malformation or carotid-cavernous fistula; by intracranial electrothrombosis

HP_0031158.label: widened atrophic scar
HP_0031158.definition: An atrophic scar (fibrous connective tissue resulting from incomplete healing of a wound) that has stretched (gotten wider), a manifestation of tissue fragility.

HP_0031159.label: thinning of descemet membrane
HP_0031159.definition: A reduction in the thickness of Descemet's membrane.
HP_0031159.UMLS synonyms: Irregular thinning of Descemet membrane | Peters anomaly (central corneal opacification, anterior synechiae of anterior chamber, thinning of Descemet membrane)

HP_0031160.label: myelokathexis
HP_0031160.definition: Impaired egress of mature neutrophils from bone marrow causing neutropenia.
HP_0031160.UMLS synonyms: Myelokathexis | Myelokathexis (retention of neutrophils in the bone marrow) | WHIM syndrome | WHIM SYNDROME 1 | WHIM SYNDROME 2

HP_0031161.label: reduced brain glutamate level by mrs
HP_0031161.definition: An decrease in the level of glutamate (Glu) in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS).

HP_0031162.label: impaired oropharyngeal swallow response
HP_0031162.definition: Delay or absence of the swallow response, reflexes triggered by the contact the food bolus makes with the anterior faucial pillars.

HP_0031163.label: low femoral bone density
HP_0031163.definition: Reduced bone mineral density of the femur.

HP_0031164.label: growth arrest lines
HP_0031164.definition: Growth arrest lines are alternating transverse rings of sclerosis at the metaphysis of a long bone.

HP_0031165.label: multifocal seizures
HP_0031165.definition: Seizures that start from several different areas of the brain (i.e., with multiple ictal onset locations).
HP_0031165.UMLS synonyms: Seizures (clonic, multifocal) | Migrating focal or multifocal origin seizures | Seizure, focal or multifocal onset | Lethal neonatal spasticity, epileptic encephalopathy syndrome

HP_0031166.label: eyelid myokymia
HP_0031166.definition: Involuntary, fine, continuous, undulating contractions of the eyelid.

HP_0031167.label: triggered by ingestion of potassium - rich food
HP_0031167.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by eating or drinking foods rich in potassium.
HP_0031167.synonyms: potassium - rich food triggered symptoms | triggered by ingestion of k - rich food

HP_0031169.label: postterm pregnancy
HP_0031169.definition: A pregnancy that extends to 42 weeks of gestation or beyond.

HP_0031170.label: female fetal virilization
HP_0031170.definition: Fetal masculinization of female external genitalia.

HP_0031171.label: femoral spur
HP_0031171.definition: A bony projection (spur, osteophyte) originating from the femur, often in the medial femoral neck.

HP_0031172.label: sectoral retinitis pigmentosa
HP_0031172.definition: A variant of retinitis pigmentosa in which there is a regional distribution of the retinal degeneration.

HP_0031173.label: tibial spur
HP_0031173.definition: A bony projection (spur, osteophyte) originating from the tibia.

HP_0031174.label: double - layered patella
HP_0031174.definition: An anomaly of the patella characterized by two layers visible on lateral knee X-ray such that one layer is in front of the other in the sagittal orientation (See Figure 2A and 3B of PMID:12966518). This finding persists into adulthood.

HP_0031175.label: absent cervical vertebra
HP_0031175.definition: A developmental defect characterized by agenesis of one or more vertebral bodies of the cervical spine.

HP_0031176.label: absent thoracic vertebra
HP_0031176.definition: A developmental defect characterized by agenesis of one or more vertebral bodies of the thoracic spine.

HP_0031177.label: finger flexor weakness
HP_0031177.definition: Reduced ability to flex (bend) the fingers. This can manifest as incomplete closure of the hand due to weakness in finger flexion.

HP_0031178.label: fixed head retroflexion
HP_0031178.definition: Head is bent in the posterior direction in a permanent fashion.

HP_0031179.label: nuchal rigidity
HP_0031179.definition: Resistance of the extensor muscles of the neck to being bent forwards (i.e., impaired neck flexion) as a result of muscle spasm of the extensor muscles of the neck. Nuchal rigidity is not a fixed rigidity. Nuchal rigidity has been used as a bedside test for meningism, although its sensitivity for this purpose has been debated.
HP_0031179.UMLS synonyms: Nuchal Rigidity | Nuchal rigidity due to meningitis | Check patient for nuchal rigidity | Nuchal rigidity due to subarachnoid hemorrhage

HP_0031180.label: erythema migrans
HP_0031180.definition: An expanding erythematous (red) skin lesion, usually round or oval, by definition at least 5 cm in size (in largest diameter).
HP_0031180.UMLS synonyms: Erythema Chronicum Migrans | Glossitis, Benign Migratory | Suspected erythema migrans | Erythema necrolyticum migrans | Erythema Chronicum Migrans Diagnostic Reagents | Necrolytic Migratory Erythema | Panniculitis, Subacute Nodular Migratory | Cold Panniculitis | Pseudoglucagonoma Syndrome | Erythema chronicum migrans due to Borrelia burgdorferi | Chronic migratory panniculitis

HP_0031181.label: necrolytic migratory erythema
HP_0031181.definition: Acral or periorificial lesions that evolve in recurrent crops, with an annular and migratory distribution.

HP_0031185.label: increased circulating nt - probnp concentration
HP_0031185.definition: An elevated level of circulating N-terminal part of the prohormone of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP).

HP_0031186.label: abnormal circulating deoxycorticosterone level
HP_0031186.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of deoxycorticosterone in the blood. Deoxycorticosterone comprises 11-deoxycorticosterone and 21-deoxycorticosterone.

HP_0031187.label: abnormal circulating pregnenolone concentration
HP_0031187.definition: An abnormality of the concentration of pregnenolone in the blood.

HP_0031188.label: genital edema
HP_0031188.definition: A buildup of fluid that causes swelling in the soft tissues of the genital area.
HP_0031188.UMLS synonyms: Genital Edema | Genital Edema, CTCAE | Edema of male genital organs | Grade 3 Genital Edema, CTCAE | Grade 1 Genital Edema, CTCAE | Grade 2 Genital Edema, CTCAE | Oedema labial genital | Genital oedema female | Grade 5 Edema of the Trunk and Genital Area, CTCAE | Grade 3 Edema of the Trunk and Genital Area, CTCAE | Grade 4 Edema of the Trunk and Genital Area, CTCAE | Grade 1 Edema of the Trunk and Genital Area, CTCAE | Grade 2 Edema of the Trunk and Genital Area, CTCAE | Edema of the Trunk and Genital Area, CTCAE

HP_0031189.label: wrist drop
HP_0031189.definition: A condition in which the affected individual cannot extend the wrist, which hangs flaccidly.
HP_0031189.UMLS synonyms: Wrist-Drop | Left wrist drop | Right wrist drop | Bilateral wrist drop | WRIST DROP ACUTE | wrist drop on extension | Wrist or foot drop (acquired) | wrist drop of left wrist on extension | wrist drop of right wrist on extension | Wrist or foot drop (acquired), forearm | wrist drop of both wrists on extension | Wrist or foot drop (acquired), multiple sites | Wrist or foot drop (acquired), ankle and foot

HP_0031190.label: superficial dermal perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
HP_0031190.definition: Numerous lymphocytes surrounding blood vessels in the superfical part of the dermis.

HP_0031191.label: deep dermal perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
HP_0031191.definition: Numerous lymphocytes surrounding blood vessels in the deep part of the dermis.

HP_0031192.label: abnormal morphology of left ventricular trabeculae
HP_0031192.definition: Any structural anomaly of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the left ventricle of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

HP_0031193.label: abnormal morphology of right ventricular trabeculae
HP_0031193.definition: Any structural anomaly of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the right ventricle of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

HP_0031194.label: increased density of left ventricular trabeculae
HP_0031194.definition: An increased density (number and tightness) of the muscular columns which project from the inner surface of the left ventricles of the heart (cardiac trabeculae, trabeculae carneae).

HP_0031195.label: apical hypertrabeculation of the left ventricle
HP_0031195.definition: An increased number and density of the trabeculae in the apex (tip) of the left ventricle.

HP_0031196.label: thin myocardium compact layer
HP_0031196.definition: Reduced thickness of the outer, dense layer of the myocardium.

HP_0031197.label: cellular urinary casts
HP_0031197.definition: A type of urinary cast composed of cells incorporated in a protein matrix. The cells can be those found in the urinary sediment (erythrocytes, leuklocytes, renal tubular epithelial cells).

HP_0031198.label: renal tubular epithelial cell casts
HP_0031198.definition: A type of cellular urinary cast composed of renal tubular epithelial cells.

HP_0031199.label: acellular urinary casts
HP_0031199.definition: A type of urinary cast composed of a proteinaceous matrix without a substantial number of cells.

HP_0031200.label: hyaline casts
HP_0031200.definition: A type of acellular urinary cast that are composed only of Tamm-Horsfall glycoprotein, a fact which explains their low refractive index. Hyaline casts may display a spectrum of morphologies, which includes fluffy, compact, convoluted or wrinkled casts. Hyaline casts have a smooth texture and usually have parallel sides with clear margins and blunted ends.
HP_0031200.UMLS synonyms: Hyaline casts | urinalysis: hyaline casts | Hyaline-granular casts | Urine microscopy: hyaline casts (finding) | Hyaline casts|NCnc|Urine | Hyaline casts | Urine | Urinalysis | hyaline casts in automated urinalysis | Hyaline casts | Urine sediment | Urinalysis | Hyaline casts|Urine/Urine sed | Hyaline-granular casts|Urine/Urine sed | Hyaline-granular casts | Urine sediment | Urinalysis | hyaline casts in urine by automated count | Hyaline casts:NCnc:Pt:Urine:Qn | Hyaline casts:NCnc:Pt:Urine:Qn:Automated count | Hyaline casts:PrThr:Pt:Urine sed:Ord | Hyaline casts:Naric:Pt:Urine sed:Qn | hyaline casts in urine sediment by automated count | urinalysis by low power field microscopy showed hyaline casts in urine sediment | Hyaline casts:PrThr:Pt:Urine:Ord:Automated | Hyaline casts:Naric:Pt:Urine sed:Qn:Microscopy.light.LPF | Hyaline casts:Naric:Pt:Urine sed:Qn:Microscopy.light.HPF | Hyaline casts:PrThr:Pt:Urine sed:Ord:Microscopy.light | Hyaline casts:Naric:Pt:Urine sed:Qn:Automated count | Hyaline casts.broad:PrThr:Pt:Urine sed:Ord:Microscopy.light

HP_0031201.label: granular casts
HP_0031201.definition: A type of acelluar casts that have a surface composed of granules, which can vary in size. The granules can be rather heterogeneous, ranging from fine (finely granular cast) up to coarse (coarsely granular cast), dark, clear, and pigmented.

HP_0031202.label: waxy casts
HP_0031202.definition: A type of acellular urinary casts that display a melted wax (waxy) appearance, which gives them a high refractive index. They are frequently dark, with blunt extremities, indented and cracked edges and a large size, which is often several times that of other types of casts.
