HP_0031945.definition: An increased concentration of N,N-dimethylglycine in the circulation.

HP_0031946.label: elevated urinary n , n - dimethylglycine level
HP_0031946.definition: An increased concentration of N,N-dimethylglycine in the urine.

HP_0031947.label: tongue tremor
HP_0031947.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting the tongue.
HP_0031947.UMLS synonyms: Tremor of tongue | Tongue tremor on protrusion | Tremor, postural (arms, tongue, head, legs and trunk) | Tremor, action (arms, tongue, head, legs and trunk)

HP_0031948.label: snowball lesion of corpus callosum
HP_0031948.definition: Centrally located corpus callosum hyperintensities said to resemble snowballs upon magnetic resonance imaging (with T2 or Sagittal fluid attenuated inversion recovery [FLAIR] sequences). The central location in the callosum makes them pathognomonic for Susac syndrome.

HP_0031949.label: recurrent bacterial upper respiratory tract infections
HP_0031949.definition: An increased susceptibility to bacterial upper respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of recurrent bacterial upper respiratory tract infections (running ears - otitis, sinusitis, pharyngitis, tonsillitis).

HP_0031950.label: usual interstitial pneumonia
HP_0031950.definition: Temporal and spatial heterogeneity in lungs based on presence of fibrosis and honeycombing.
HP_0031950.UMLS synonyms: Usual Interstitial Pneumonia | Usual interstitial pneumonia on biopsy | Interstitial pneumonia (nonspecific) (usual) in diseases classified elsewhere | Interstitial pneumonia (nonspecific) (usual) due to collagen vascular disease | mRNA, gene expression analysis of 190 genes associated with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in transbronchial biopsy specimen, diagnostic algorithm reported as positive or negative for high probability of usual interstitial pneumonia | Honeycomb lung Pneumonia, usually interstitial | Pulmonary disease (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis [IPF]), mRNA, gene expression analysis of 190 genes, utilizing transbronchial biopsies, diagnostic algorithm reported as categorical result (eg, positive or negative for high probability of usual interstitial pneumonia [UIP])

HP_0031951.label: nocturnal seizures
HP_0031951.definition: Seizures that occur while the affected individual is sleeping.
HP_0031951.UMLS synonyms: nocturnal seizures | Nocturnal epilepsy | Nocturnal tonic seizures | Seizures, nocturnal, usually occur in clusters | Motor seizures, nocturnal, usually occur in clusters (up to 8 per night) during dozing or on awakening

HP_0031952.label: neurogenic claudication
HP_0031952.definition: Lumbar spinal stenoses may induce symptoms following an individually typical latency on standing or when walking due to swelling of the cauda equina, which leads to compression. This is referred to as neurogenic claudication. The symptoms of lumbar spinal stenosis can be explained by an increase in lumbar lordosis and spinal canal stenosis in an upright position compared to the sitting position or if spondylolisthesis is present by a shift of the vertebrae while standing and walking. Following an individually characteristic distance, walking becomes associated with deep muscular pain and with neurological deficits, such as sensory deficits and paresis in the lower limbs, which resolve within minutes when the affected person sits or lies down. Activities performed in a flexed posture, such as cycling often cause less problems than walking. For the same reason, walking uphill may be tolerated better than walking downhill. Clinical neurological examination at rest may be entirely normal but there is usually pain on hyperextension of the lumbar spine.
HP_0031952.UMLS synonyms: Neurogenic claudication | lumbar stenosis with neurogenic claudication | lumbar stenosis without neurogenic claudication | Spinal stenosis, lumbar region without neurogenic claudication | Spinal stenosis, lumbar region with neurogenic claudication

HP_0031953.label: cautious gait
HP_0031953.definition: Cautious gait refers to an excessive degree of age-related changes in walking and fear of falling. The walking difficulties seem out of proportion when considering the patient's actual sensory or motor deficits. The gait appears slow, with a wider base than normal, reduced arm swing bilaterally and a slightly stooped posture. This type of gait change often occurs after the first time a patient has fallen.

HP_0031954.label: dystonic gait
HP_0031954.definition: Dystonic gait disorders frequently appear bizarre, particularly because activity increases dystonic tonus and posture. The abnormal posture of the foot in dystonic gait typically involves inversion, plantar flexion and tonic extension of the big toe. In many patients complex types of walking, such as walking backwards and running are paradoxically less impaired than walking forward and may seem completely unaffected. Sensory tricks, for instance, if the affected individual rests a hand on his or her neck, may improve or even normalize dystonic gait in some patients.

HP_0031955.label: antalgic gait
HP_0031955.definition: To avoid pain weight is put on the affected leg for as short a time as possible, resulting in a limp. The patients appear to be walking as if there were a thorn in the sole of the foot. To reduce the load on the affected leg the patients lift and lower their foot in a fixed ankle position.
HP_0031955.UMLS synonyms: Antalgic gait | bilateral antalgic gait | antalgic gait on right | antalgic gait on left side

HP_0031956.label: elevated circulating aspartate aminotransferase concentration
HP_0031956.definition: An abnormally high concentration in the circulation of aspartate aminotransferase (AST).
HP_0031956.synonyms: aspartate aminotransferase increased | elevated serum aspartate aminotransferase | elevated serum ast | elevated serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase

HP_0031957.label: spastic hemiparetic gait
HP_0031957.definition: Spastic hemiparesis is characterized by a dominance of the tonus in the upper limb flexor muscles: the arm is held in an adducted posture and is bent and rotated inwards, the forearm is pronated and the hand and the fingers are flexed. The leg is slightly bent at the hip, the knee cannot be extended fully at the end of the stance phase and the foot is inverted and in a plantar flexed position. Gait is slow, with a wide base and asymmetrical with a shortened weight-bearing phase on the paretic side. During the swing phase, the paretic leg performs a lateral movement (circumduction) which is characteristic of this gait disorder, also termed Wernicke-Mann gait. Spastic gait problems typically worsen on attempts to walk faster.

HP_0031958.label: spastic paraparetic gait
HP_0031958.definition: A type of spastic gait in which the legs are usually slightly bent at the hip and in an adducted position. The knees are extended or slightly bent and the feet are in a plantar flexion position. This posture requires circumduction of the legs during walking. The gait may appear stiff (spastic gait disorder) or stiff as well as insecure (spastic ataxic gait disorder). In spastic paraparetic gait, each leg appears to be dragged forward. If the muscle tone in the adductors is marked, the resulting gait disorder is referred to as scissor gait.

HP_0031959.label: leg dystonia
HP_0031959.definition: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the legs.

HP_0031960.label: arm dystonia
HP_0031960.definition: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the arms.

HP_0031961.label: abnormal serum anion gap
HP_0031961.definition: Any deviation from the normal value of the serum anion gap, which is calculated from the electrolytes measured in the chemical laboratory, is defined as the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration.

HP_0031962.label: elevated serum anion gap
HP_0031962.definition: An abnormally high value of the serum anion gap (the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration).

HP_0031963.label: decreased serum anion gap
HP_0031963.definition: An abnormally low value of the serum anion gap (the sum of serum chloride and bicarbonate concentrations subtracted from the serum sodium concentration).

HP_0031964.label: elevated circulating alanine aminotransferase concentration
HP_0031964.definition: An abnormally high concentration in the circulation of alanine aminotransferase (ALT).
HP_0031964.synonyms: alanine aminotransferase increased | elevated serum alanine aminotransferase | elevated serum alt | elevated serum glutamic - pyruvic transaminase

HP_0031965.label: increased rbc distribution width
HP_0031965.definition: Red blood cell distribution width (RDW) is a simple parameter of the standard full blood count and a measure of heterogeneity in the size of circulating erythrocytes. It is provided by automated hematology analyzers and it reflects the range of the red cell size. It is calculated by dividing the standard deviation of erythrocyte volume by the mean corpuscular volume (MCV) and multiplied by 100 to convert to a percentage.
HP_0031965.synonyms: increased red blood cell distribution width

HP_0031967.label: cloudy urine
HP_0031967.definition: The appearance of the urine having visible material in suspension, i.e., appearing cloudy.
HP_0031967.UMLS synonyms: Cloudy urine | Slightly cloudy urine | cloudy urine from urethral catheter | dark but not cloudy urine

HP_0031969.label: reduced blood urea nitrogen
HP_0031969.definition: An abnormally low concentration of urea nitrogen in the blood.

HP_0031970.label: abnormal blood urea nitrogen concentration
HP_0031970.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of urea nitrogen in the blood.

HP_0031971.label: subaortic ventricular septal bulge
HP_0031971.definition: A localized hypertrophy of the subaortic segment of the ventricular septum has been frequently described in elderly persons, and variously termed subaortic ventricular septal bulge (VSB), sigmoid-shaped septum, localized or discrete upper septal hypertrophy.

HP_0031972.label: presyncope
HP_0031972.definition: Presyncope is a state of lightheadedness, muscular weakness, blurred vision, and feeling faint. Presyncope is most often cardiovascular in cause.
HP_0031972.UMLS synonyms: Presyncope | Presyncope, CTCAE | Orthostatic presyncope | Hypotensive presyncope | presyncope syndrome | PRESYNCOPE CARDIOGENIC | Presyncope or syncope | Grade 2 Presyncope, CTCAE | Presyncope Related to COVID-19

HP_0031973.label: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio
HP_0031973.definition: An abnormal increase in the ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc.

HP_0031974.label: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.6
HP_0031974.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 0.6 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

HP_0031975.label: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.7
HP_0031975.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 0.7 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

HP_0031976.label: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.8
HP_0031976.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 0.8 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

HP_0031977.label: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 0.9
HP_0031977.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 0.9 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

HP_0031978.label: increased vertical cup - to - disc ratio - 1.0
HP_0031978.definition: Ratio of the height of the cup of the optic nerve head to the height of the disc is 1.0 (The normal cup-to-disc ratio is 0.3).

HP_0031979.label: abnormal urine carbohydrate level
HP_0031979.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a carbohydrate in the urine.

HP_0031980.label: abnormal urine carboxylic acid level
HP_0031980.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a carboxylic acid in the urine.

HP_0031981.label: elevated urine glycolate
HP_0031981.definition: An increased concentration of glycolate in the urine.

HP_0031982.label: abnormal putamen morphology
HP_0031982.definition: Any structural anomaly of the putamen, a brain nucleus which together with the caudate nucleus and fundus striati makes up the striatum.

HP_0031983.label: abnormal pulmonary thoracic imaging finding
HP_0031983.definition: This term groups terms representing abnormal findings derived from chest X-ray investigation of the lung. In general, lung abnormalities can manifest as opacities (areas of increased density) or as regions with decreased density.

HP_0031984.label: esophageal food impaction
HP_0031984.definition: A piece of food that has gotten stuck in the esophagus and prevents further swallowing.

HP_0031985.label: esophageal exudate
HP_0031985.definition: An exudate is a mass of fluid and cells that has seeped out of blood vessels or an organ, usually related to inflammation. In the esophagus, exudates usually present as whitish plagues on the surface of the esophageal mucosa.
HP_0031985.UMLS synonyms: barium swallow: esophageal mucosal shaggy exudate

HP_0031986.label: polyminimyoclonus
HP_0031986.definition: Irregular, small-amplitude myoclonic movements of the hands and/or fingers on keeping outstretched posture (jerky postural tremor). Polyminimyoclonus is stimulus-sensitive and accentuated during voluntary movements. A cortical origin can be demonstrated by back-averaging techniques, and somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs) are sometimes giant.

HP_0031987.label: diminished ability to concentrate
HP_0031987.definition: Being unable to focus one's attention or mental effort on a particular object or activity.
HP_0031987.synonyms: concentration problems | lack of concentration | poor concentration

HP_0031989.label: perioral spasm
HP_0031989.definition: A sudden involuntary contraction of the musculature surrounding the mouth.

HP_0031990.label: chvostek sign
HP_0031990.definition: A contraction of ipsilateral facial muscles subsequent to percussion over the facial nerve.
HP_0031990.UMLS synonyms: Chvostek sign | Chvostek sign positive | Chvostek sign negative | Facial muscle twitching (Chvostek sign) | Tetany, hypocalcemic (Chvostek and Trousseau sign) | Monitor for Chvostek's and/or Trousseau's sign | Monitor for signs and symptoms of hypomagnesemia: respiratory muscle depression; mental apathy; Chvostek's sign (facial muscle spasm); Trousseau's sign (carpal spasm); confusion; facial tics; spasticity; and cardiac dysrhythmias | Observe for clinical manifestations of hypocalcemia (e.g., tetany [classic sign]; tingling in tips of fingers, feet, or mouth; spasms of muscles in face or extremities; Trousseau's sign; Chvostek's sign; altered deep tendon reflexes; seizures [late sign]) | Monitor for signs and symptoms of hypocalcemia: irritability; muscle tetany; Chvostek's sign (facial muscle spasm); Trousseau's sign (carpal spasm); peripheral numbness and tingling; muscle cramps; decreased cardiac output; prolonged ST segment and QT interval; bleeding; and fractures | Monitor for neuromuscular manifestations of hypomagnesemia (e.g., weakness, muscle twitching, foot or leg cramps, paresthesias, hyperactive deep tendon reflexes, Chvostek's sign, Trousseau's sign, dysphagia, nystagmus, seizures, and tetany)

HP_0031991.label: increased urinary excretion of galactosyl hydroxylysine
HP_0031991.definition: An increased concentration of beta-1-galactosyl-O-hydroxylysine (Gal-Hyl) in the urine. This is a biochemical marker of bone resorption.

HP_0031992.label: apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
HP_0031992.definition: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (AHCM) is diastolic dysfunction due to abnormal stiffness of the left ventricle during diastole, with resultant impaired ventricular filling. In AHCM thickened apical segments produce a crowded, spade-shaped, small apical cavity.
HP_0031992.UMLS synonyms: Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy | Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with aneurysm | Left Ventricular Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy | hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy with apical variant | MT-ATP8 gene

HP_0031993.label: hoffmann sign
HP_0031993.definition: A Hoffmann test is performed by flicking the fingernail of the long finger, from dorsal to volar, on each hand while the hand was supported by the examiner's hand. The test was done with the neck in the neutral position and then with the neck maximally forward flexed. Any flexion of the ipsilateral thumb and/or index finger was interpreted as a positive test.

HP_0031994.label: bronchial breath sound
HP_0031994.definition: Bronchial breath sounds contain much higher frequency components than normal breath sounds due to alteration of the low pass filtering function of the alveoli, as occurs in consolidation. It is loud, hollow, and high pitch. Expiratory phase is longer than inspiratory phase with the inspiratory-expiratory ratio (I:E) changing from normal 3:1 to 1:2. There is distinct pause between inspiration and expiration due to absent alveolar phase. It is associated with whispering pectoriloquy.
HP_0031994.UMLS synonyms: BREATH SOUND BRONCHIAL ROUGH | Bronchial breathing | bronchial breath sounds in both lungs | bronchial breath sounds on both sides laterally | bronchial breath sounds on both sides medially | bronchial breath sounds in left lung | bronchial breath sounds on left anteromedially | bronchial breath sounds in both apices | bronchial breath sounds on left posteromedially | bronchial breath sounds on left laterally | bronchial breath sounds on left medially | bronchial breath sounds in right lung | bronchial breath sounds at left apex | bronchial breath sounds at left base | bronchial breath sounds at both bases | bronchial breath sounds on right medially | bronchial breath sounds on right anteromedially | bronchial breath sounds on right posteromedially | bronchial breath sounds on right laterally | bronchial breath sounds at right base | bronchial breath sounds at right apex | bronchial breath sounds on both sides anteromedially | bronchial breath sounds on both sides posteromedially | bronchial breath sounds in left mid-lung field | bronchial breath sounds in both mid-lung fields

HP_0031995.label: squawks
HP_0031995.definition: Squawks are short inspiratory wheezes of less than 200 ms duration and are also known as squeaks. Acoustic analysis shows the fundamental frequency varying between 200 and 300 Hz. Squawks usually occur in late inspiration and are often preceded by late inspiratory crackles.

HP_0031996.label: inspiratory crackles
HP_0031996.definition: Crackles that are heard during the inspiratory phase.
HP_0031996.UMLS synonyms: Inspiratory crackles | inspiratory rales or crackles | inspiratory rales or crackles bilaterally | inspiratory rales or crackles on left | inspiratory rales or crackles on right | inspiratory rales or crackles bilaterally at apices | inspiratory rales or crackles bilaterally at bases | inspiratory rales or crackles on left at base | inspiratory rales or crackles on left at apex | inspiratory rales or crackles on right at apex | inspiratory rales or crackles on right at base | inspiratory rales or crackles bilaterally at midlung fields | anterior inspiratory rales bilaterally | posterior inspiratory rales bilaterally | inspiratory rales or crackles on left at midlung field | inspiratory rales or crackles on right at midlung field | inspiratory rales on left anteriorly | inspiratory rales on left posteriorly | inspiratory rales on right anteriorly | inspiratory rales on right posteriorly | coarse anterior inspiratory rales bilaterally | coarse posterior inspiratory rales bilaterally | fine anterior inspiratory rales bilaterally

HP_0031997.label: early inspiratory crackles
HP_0031997.definition: Crackles that appear at the beginning of inspiration and end before mid-inspiration.

HP_0031998.label: late inspiratory crackles
HP_0031998.definition: Crackles that appear any time after the beginning of inspiration and last till the end of inspiration.

HP_0031999.label: expiratory crackles
HP_0031999.UMLS synonyms: Expiratory crackles | expiratory rales or crackles | expiratory rales or crackles bilaterally | expiratory rales or crackles on left | expiratory rales or crackles on right | expiratory rales or crackles bilaterally at apices | expiratory rales or crackles bilaterally at bases | anterior expiratory rales bilaterally | posterior expiratory rales bilaterally | expiratory rales or crackles on left at base | expiratory rales or crackles on left at apex | expiratory rales or crackles on right at apex | expiratory rales or crackles on right at base | expiratory rales or crackles bilaterally at midlung fields | expiratory rales or crackles on left at midlung field | expiratory rales or crackles on right at midlung field | expiratory rales on left anteriorly | expiratory rales on left posteriorly | expiratory rales on right posteriorly | expiratory rales on right anteriorly | fine anterior expiratory rales bilaterally | fine posterior expiratory rales bilaterally | coarse anterior expiratory rales bilaterally | coarse posterior expiratory rales bilaterally | coarse expiratory rales on left anteriorly

HP_0032000.label: pleural rub
HP_0032000.definition: An abnormal breath sound that is nonmusical, short and explosive. It is grating, rubbing, creaky, or leathery in character and present in both phases of respiration. Typically the expiratory component mirrors the inspiratory component. It occurs due to inflamed pleural surface rubbing each other during breathing. Clinically, it is important to differentiate it from crackles
HP_0032000.UMLS synonyms: Pleural Rub | pleural friction rub inspiration | pleural friction rub bilaterally | pleural friction rub expiration | pleural friction rub on left | pleural friction rub on right | bilateral pleural friction rub on expiration | bilateral pleural friction rub on inspiration | pleural friction rub on inspiration on left | pleural friction rub on expiration on left | pleural friction rub on expiration on right | pleural friction rub on inspiration on right

HP_0032001.label: pink urine
HP_0032001.definition: An abnormal pink color of urine.

HP_0032002.label: orange urine
HP_0032002.definition: An abnormal orange color of urine.
HP_0032002.UMLS synonyms: Urine: orange | Orange-colored urine | bright orange urine | urine appearance orange

HP_0032003.label: green urine
HP_0032003.definition: An abnormal green color of urine.
HP_0032003.UMLS synonyms: Green-colored urine | Discoloration urine green | urine appearance green | blue-green urine

HP_0032004.label: pruritus vulvae
HP_0032004.definition: A sensation of itching in the vulvar region.

HP_0032005.label: hemidystonia
HP_0032005.definition: Hemidystonia refers to dystonia which involves the ipsilateral face, arm, and leg.

HP_0032006.label: lip tremor
HP_0032006.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement affecting the lip.
HP_0032006.UMLS synonyms: MDS-UPDRS - Rest Tremor Amplitude Lip or Jaw | ESRS-A - Tremor: Face/Jaw/Chin/Lips/Head | UPDRS - Motor Examination: Tremor at Rest, Face, Lips, Chin

HP_0032007.label: maceration
HP_0032007.definition: A softening and breaking down of skin resulting from prolonged exposure to moisture. Macerated skin becomes soft and wrinkly and takes on a whitish hue.
HP_0032007.synonyms: maceration of the skin | skin maceration
HP_0032007.UMLS synonyms: Maceration | Macerated skin (finding) | maceration; fetus | INTERDIGITAL MACERATION | maceration on vulva | maceration on labia | maceration on anus | maceration in perineum | maceration on scrotum | maceration in inguinal region | maceration in perianal region | Management of maceration | Infusion site maceration | Application site maceration | Injection site maceration | maceration on nipple | maceration on buttock | maceration on ankle | maceration on knee | maceration on feet | maceration on ear | maceration on eyebrows | maceration on face | maceration of finger | maceration on breast

HP_0032008.label: pulmonary fat embolism
HP_0032008.definition: The release of fat globules into the venous circulation, thereby blocking blood circulation to the lung.
HP_0032008.UMLS synonyms: Pulmonary fat embolism | Subacute pulmonary fat embolism | Obstetrical pulmonary fat embolism | fat embolism of pulmonary artery with acute cor pulmonale | fat embolism of pulmonary artery without acute cor pulmonale

HP_0032009.label: infantile constant exotropia
HP_0032009.definition: Constant exotropia occurring before 6 months of age.; often associated with a large angle of deviation and ocular/CNS abnormalities.

HP_0032010.label: basic constant exotropia
HP_0032010.definition: Constant exotropia for near and distance, presenting after 6 months of age.

HP_0032011.label: heterophoria
HP_0032011.definition: Heterophorias are latent deviations that are controlled by fusion. In certain circumstances (specific visual tasks, fatigue, illness, etc.), fusion can no longer be maintained and decompensation occurs.
HP_0032011.UMLS synonyms: Heterophoria | Ophthalmology Heterophoria | Heterophoria | Eyes | Heterophoria | Vertical heterophoria | Comitant heterophoria | Alternating heterophoria | Heterophoria method | Incomitant heterophoria | Heterophoria study | Heterophoria study:Find:Pt:^Patient:Doc | Heterophoria Assessment Rods | Deprecated Worth test for Heterophoria | vertical heterophoria of left eye | vertical heterophoria of right eye | Heterophoria:Prid:Pt:Eyes:Nom:Heterometer test | Heterophoria:Prid:Pt:Eyes:Nom:Maddox wing | Heterophoria:Prid:Pt:Eyes:Nom:Bagolini test | Heterophoria:Prid:Pt:Eyes:Nom:Schober test | Heterophoria:Prid:Pt:Eyes:Nom:Cover test | Heterophoria:Prid:Pt:Eyes:Nom:Maddox Stabchen test | Heterophoria:Prid:Pt:Eyes:Nom:Dark red glass test | Heterophoria:Prid:Pt:Eyes:Nom:Maddox double prism test

HP_0032012.label: heterotropia
HP_0032012.definition: Manifest deviation of the visual axes not controlled by fusion.
HP_0032012.UMLS synonyms: Heterotropia | Strabismus | Constant vertical heterotropia | Intermittent vertical heterotropia | Other and unspecified heterotropia | Intermittent tropia | Manifest vertical squint | Manifest paralytic strabismus | Strabismus, Comitant | Esotropias, Exotropias and Heterotropias

HP_0032013.label: hypermetric horizontal saccades
HP_0032013.definition: Overshoot of horizontal (sideways) saccadic eye movements.

HP_0032014.label: dysmetric vertical saccades
HP_0032014.definition: Inaccurate saccades (rapid movement of the eye between fixation points) in the vertical direction.

HP_0032015.label: dysmetric horizontal saccades
HP_0032015.definition: Inaccurate saccades (rapid movement of the eye between fixation points) in the horizontal direction.

HP_0032016.label: abnormal sputum
HP_0032016.definition: Abnormal appearance of material expectorated (coughed up) from the respiratory system and that is composed of mucus but may contain other substances such as pus, blood, microorganisms, and fibrin.
HP_0032016.UMLS synonyms: Abnormal sputum | Sputum abnormal - amount | Sputum abnormal - color | Sputum abnormal - odor | Sputum cytology abnormal | Expectoration of abnormal sputum | coughing up abnormal sputum | sputum; abnormal findings in specimen | sputum culture mixed flora nonspecific abnormal findings | Abnormality detected in sputum by cytology | Sputum microscopy: NAD

HP_0032017.label: sputum eosinophilia
HP_0032017.definition: An increased proportion of eosinophils in sputum in the differentiated cell count.

HP_0032018.label: multiple mononeuropathy
HP_0032018.definition: A type of peripheral neuropathy that happens when there is damage to two or more different nerve areas characterized by peripheral neuropathy of both the motor and sensory nerves of at least two different nerve trunks. Different nerves are affected either simultaneously or sequentially.
HP_0032018.UMLS synonyms: Mononeuritis Multiplex | Multiple mononeuropathy due to perinuclear antineutrophil cytoplasmic associated antibody associated vasculitis | Mononeuropathy Multiplex

HP_0032020.label: eosinophilic bladder infiltration
HP_0032020.definition: Transmural inflammation of the bladder predominantly with eosinophils, associated with fibrosis with or without muscle necrosis.

HP_0032021.label: eosinophilic liver infiltration
HP_0032021.definition: Cellular infiltration of the liver parenchyma with a preponderance of eosinophils.

HP_0032022.label: eosinophilic dermal infiltration
HP_0032022.definition: Presence of abnormally increased amounts of intraepidermal inflammatory cells with a predominance of eosinophils.

HP_0032023.label: eosinophilic gallbladder infiltration
HP_0032023.definition: Cellular infiltrate confirmed by a cellular infiltrate comprised of mainly eosinophils in the gallbladder wall on histological examination.

HP_0032024.label: ileal ulcer
HP_0032024.definition: An erosion of the mucous membrane in a portion of the ileum.
HP_0032024.UMLS synonyms: Ileal ulcer | Ileal Ulcer, CTCAE | Ileal ulcer perforation | Grade 3 Ileal Ulcer, CTCAE | Grade 2 Ileal Ulcer, CTCAE | Grade 5 Ileal Ulcer, CTCAE | Grade 1 Ileal Ulcer, CTCAE | Grade 4 Ileal Ulcer, CTCAE

HP_0032025.label: reduced circulating alpha - 1 - antitrypsin concentration
HP_0032025.definition: A reduced concentration or activity of circulating alpha-1 antitrypsin, which is a 52-kDa glycoprotein mainly synthesised and secreted by hepatocytes into the bloodstream. Alpha-1 antitrypsin is a serine-proteinase inhibitor that it is crucial in maintaining protease-antiprotease homeostasis in the lungs.

HP_0032026.label: anetoderma
HP_0032026.definition: Circumscribed area of flaccid skin due to the loss of elastic tissue in the dermis.
HP_0032026.UMLS synonyms: Atrophoderma maculatum | Anetoderma, Secondary | Anetoderma, Primary | Hereditary anetoderma | Administration site anetoderma | Schweninger-Buzzi anetoderma | Jadassohn-Pellizzari anetoderma | Anetoderma following varicella | Drug-induced anetoderma | Anetoderma secondary to syphilis | Lupus erythematosus-associated anetoderma | Exostosis, anetoderma, brachydactyly type E syndrome | Metaphyseal Dysplasia, Anetoderma, and Optic Atrophy

HP_0032027.label: retinal dots
HP_0032027.definition: Yellow, white or greyish lesions in the retina that are well-defined/distinct, individual and mostly uniform in size.
HP_0032027.UMLS synonyms: retinal white dots | Retinal white dots syndrome | White dots on the retinal pigment epithelium | Retinal dot hemorrhage

HP_0032028.label: macular dots
HP_0032028.definition: Yellow, white or greyish lesions in the macula that are well-defined/distinct, individual and mostly uniform in size.

HP_0032029.label: floppy eyelid
HP_0032029.definition: Excessive eyelid tissue laxity, typically affecting both upper eyelids and associated with spontanteous tarsal eversion during sleep. It is more common in the obese, it may be associated with obstructive sleep apnea and it may result in corneal exposure or chronic papillary conjunctivitis.
HP_0032029.UMLS synonyms: Floppy eyelid syndrome of left eye | Floppy eyelid syndrome of right eye | Bilateral floppy eyelid syndrome of eyes | Floppy lid syndrome | floppy left upper eyelid on laxity distraction test | floppy right upper eyelid on laxity distraction test

HP_0032030.label: lateral canthal tendon laxity
HP_0032030.definition: Laxity of the tendon stabilising the lateral aspect of the tarsal plate to the zygomatic bone. This can result in rounded appearence of the lateral canthus. Also, when the eyelid is pulled medially, more than 2 mm movement of the canthal angle may be observed.

HP_0032031.label: medial canthal tendon laxity
HP_0032031.definition: Laxity of the tendon stabilising the medial aspect of the tarsal plate to the anterior and posterior lacrimal crests. This may lead to more than 2mm movement of the punctum when the eyelid is pulled laterally.

HP_0032032.label: horizontal eyelid laxity
HP_0032032.definition: Abnormally lax eyelid associated with tissue relaxation, predominantly in the horizontal plane. It can be demonstrated by the horizontal eyelid distraction test (e.g. by pulling the eyelid medially and laterally). Medial and/or lateral canthal tendon laxity are often present.

HP_0032033.label: vertical eyelid laxity
HP_0032033.definition: Abnormally lax eyelid associated with tissue relaxation, predominantly in the vertical plane. It can be demonstrated by vertical lid pull. Loosening of vertical stabilising structures (e.g. lower lid retractors) or tarsal atrophy are often present.

HP_0032034.label: upper eyelid laxity
HP_0032034.definition: Abnormally lax upper eyelid associated with tissue relaxation.
HP_0032034.UMLS synonyms: bilateral upper eyelid laxity | laxity of left upper eyelid | laxity of right upper eyelid | floppy left upper eyelid on laxity distraction test | floppy right upper eyelid on laxity distraction test

HP_0032035.label: lower eyelid laxity
HP_0032035.definition: Abnormally lax lower eyelid associated with tissue relaxation.
HP_0032035.UMLS synonyms: bilateral lower eyelid laxity | laxity of left lower eyelid | laxity of right lower eyelid | laxity of lower eyelid with lateral rounding | laxity of right lower eyelid on distraction test | laxity of left lower eyelid on distraction test

HP_0032036.label: reduced contrast sensitivity
HP_0032036.definition: An abnormality in perception of contrast. Spatial contrast is a physical dimension referring to the light-dark transition of a border or an edge in an image that delineates the existence of a pattern or an object. Contrast sensitivity refers to a measure of how much contrast a person requires to see a target. Contrast-sensitivity measurements differ from acuity measurements; acuity is a measure of the spatial-resolving ability of the visual system under conditions of very high contrast, whereas contrast sensitivity is a measure of the threshold contrast for seeing a target.
HP_0032036.UMLS synonyms: Reduced protan, deutan, and tritan sensitivities seen on color contrast testing

HP_0032037.label: mildly reduced visual acuity
HP_0032037.definition: Mild reduction of the ability to see defined as visual acuity less than 6/12 (20/40 in US notation; 0.5 in decimal notation) but at least 6/18 (20/63 in US notation; 0.32 in decimal notation).
HP_0032037.synonyms: mild reduction in visual acuity | mild vision loss | mild visual loss

HP_0032039.label: abnormality of the ocular adnexa
HP_0032039.definition: An anomaly of the adjacent structures (i.e., adnexa) of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.

HP_0032040.label: abnormal ocular adnexa physiology
HP_0032040.definition: A functional anomaly of the adjacent structures (i.e., adnexa) of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.

HP_0032041.label: vocal cord polyp
HP_0032041.definition: A small growth on a vocal cord that may appear as pedunculated or sessile and have varying size, shape, and color.
HP_0032041.UMLS synonyms: Polyp of vocal cord | Excision of polyp of vocal cord | Polyp of vocal cord or larynx | Excision of bilateral vocal cord polyp | Excision of laryngeal polyp | polyp of true vocal cords

HP_0032044.label: decreased vigilance
HP_0032044.definition: A decrease in the ability to maintain sustained attention is characterized by reduced alertness.

HP_0032045.label: hypoplastic carotid canal
HP_0032045.definition: Underdevelopment of the carotid canal, which normally is a circular aperture in the temporal bone of the skull through which the internal carotid artery and the carotid plexus of nerves traverse.

HP_0032046.label: focal cortical dysplasia
HP_0032046.definition: A type of malformation of cortical development that primarily affects areas of neocortex. It can be identified on conventional magnetic resonance imaging as focal cortical thickening, abnormal gyration, and blurring between gray and white matter, often associated with clusters of heterotopic neurons.
HP_0032046.UMLS synonyms: Focal Cortical Dysplasia | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia | FOCAL CORTICAL DYSPLASIA OF TAYLOR | Cortical Dysplasia-Focal Epilepsy Syndrome | Focal cortical dysplasia type IIa | Focal cortical dysplasia type IIb | Focal cortical dysplasia type I | Focal cortical dysplasia type Ia | Focal cortical dysplasia type Ib | FOCAL CORTICAL DYSPLASIA, TYPE II, SOMATIC | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type IIb | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type IIa | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type II | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type Ia | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type Ib | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type Ic | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type I | Focal Cortical Dysplasia of Taylor, Type IIb | Focal Cortical Dysplasia of Taylor, Type IIa

HP_0032047.label: focal cortical dysplasia type i
HP_0032047.definition: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by abnormal cortical layering.
HP_0032047.UMLS synonyms: Focal cortical dysplasia type I | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type I

HP_0032048.label: focal cortical dysplasia type ia
HP_0032048.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal radial cortical lamination.
HP_0032048.UMLS synonyms: Focal cortical dysplasia type Ia | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type Ia

HP_0032049.label: focal cortical dysplasia type ib
HP_0032049.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal tangential cortical lamination.
HP_0032049.UMLS synonyms: Focal cortical dysplasia type Ib | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type Ib

HP_0032050.label: focal cortical dysplasia type ic
HP_0032050.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type I that is characterized by abnormal radial and tangential cortical lamination.
HP_0032050.UMLS synonyms: Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type Ic

HP_0032051.label: focal cortical dysplasia type ii
HP_0032051.definition: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by disrupted cortical lamination and specific cytological abnormalities.
HP_0032051.UMLS synonyms: FOCAL CORTICAL DYSPLASIA, TYPE II, SOMATIC | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type II | FOCAL CORTICAL DYSPLASIA OF TAYLOR | Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type II Gene Anomaly Detection Reagents

HP_0032052.label: focal cortical dysplasia type iia
HP_0032052.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type II that is characterized by dysmorphic neurons, which present with a significantly enlarged cell body and nucleus, malorientation, abnormally distributed intracellular Nissl substance and cytoplasmic accumulation of neurofilament proteins.
HP_0032052.UMLS synonyms: Focal cortical dysplasia type IIa | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type IIa | Focal Cortical Dysplasia of Taylor, Type IIa

HP_0032053.label: focal cortical dysplasia type iib
HP_0032053.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type II that is characterized by dysmorphic neurons (significantly enlarged with accumulation of neurofilament proteins) and balloon cells.
HP_0032053.UMLS synonyms: Focal cortical dysplasia type IIb | Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type IIb | Focal Cortical Dysplasia of Taylor, Type IIb

HP_0032054.label: focal cortical dysplasia type iii
HP_0032054.definition: A type of focal cortical dysplasia that is characterized by cortical lamination abnormalities associated with a principal lesion, usually adjacent to or affecting the same cortical area/lobe.

HP_0032055.label: focal cortical dysplasia type iiia
HP_0032055.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by alterations in architectural organisation (cortical dyslamination) or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons outside Layer 5) in patients with hippocampal sclerosis (also known as Ammon's horn sclerosis).

HP_0032056.label: focal cortical dysplasia type iiib
HP_0032056.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by altered architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia without six-layered structure) and/or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons) of the neocortex, which occur adjacent to glial or glioneuronal tumor.

HP_0032057.label: focal cortical dysplasia type iiic
HP_0032057.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by alterations in architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia) or cytoarchitectural composition of the neocortex (hypertrophic neurons), which occur adjacent to vascular malformations (cavernomas, arteriovenous malformations, leptomeningeal vascular malformations, telangiectasias, meningioangiomatosis).

HP_0032058.label: focal cortical dysplasia type iiid
HP_0032058.definition: A subtype of focal cortical dysplasia type III that is characterized by altered architectural (cortical dyslamination, hypoplasia without six-layered structure) or cytoarchitectural composition (hypertrophic neurons) of the neocortex, which occur adjacent to other lesions acquired during early life (not included into FCD Type IIIa-c). These lesions comprise a large spectrum including traumatic brain injury, glial scarring after prenatal or perinatal ischemic injury or bleeding, and inflammatory or infectious diseases, i.e. Rasmussen encephalitis, limbic encephalitis, bacterial or viral infections.

HP_0032059.label: mild malformation of cortical development
HP_0032059.definition: A malformation of cortical development characterized by mild abnormalities of the cortex: excessive heterotopic neurons in Layer 1 or microscopic neuronal clusters or excess of single neurons of normal morphology in deep white matter.

HP_0032060.label: epithelioid hemangioma
HP_0032060.definition: A benign neoplasm that includes blood vessel proliferation and a dense eosinophilic inflammatory infiltrate, manifesting as flesh/plum-colored pruritic nodules and papules, most commonly affecting the ear and the periauricular area.
HP_0032060.UMLS synonyms: Histiocytoid hemangioma | Epithelioid hemangioma of skin | Cellular epithelioid hemangioma | Atypical epithelioid hemangioma | Penile Epithelioid Hemangioma | Bone Epithelioid Hemangioma | Breast Epithelioid Hemangioma | childhood epithelioid hemangioma | Head and Neck Epithelioid Hemangioma | Epithelioid Hemangioma of the Mouse Blood Vessel | Epithelioid Hemangioma of the Mouse Blood Vessel, Malignant

HP_0032061.label: hypereosinophilia
HP_0032061.definition: A severely increased count of eosinophils in the blood defined as a blood eosinophil count of at least 1.5 billion cells per liter.
HP_0032061.UMLS synonyms: Hypereosinophilia | Hypereosinophilia, mild | Hypereosinophilia of Undetermined Significance | Eosinophilia, Tropical | Pre-mRNA 3'-End-Processing Factor FIP1 | Lymphocytic Variant Hypereosinophilic Syndrome [LHES] | Omenn Syndrome | myeloproliferative neoplasms with hypereosinophilia panel (MPN/HES) by FISH | Reticuloendotheliosis, familial, with eosinophilia | Hypereosinophilic syndrome

HP_0032062.label: mallory - weiss tear
HP_0032062.definition: Vomiting-induced mucosal laceration at the esophago-gastric junction.
HP_0032062.UMLS synonyms: Bleeding Mallory-Weiss tear | MALLORY WEISS TEAR STOMACH | Oozing bleeding Mallory-Weiss tear | Non bleeding Mallory-Weiss tear | Spurting bleeding Mallory-Weiss tear | Mallory-Weiss Syndrome | Stigmata of bleeding of Mallory-Weiss tear | Presence of stigmata of bleeding of Mallory-Weiss tear | Absence of stigmata of bleeding of Mallory-Weiss tear

HP_0032063.label: ankle joint effusion
HP_0032063.definition: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in or around the ankle joint.
HP_0032063.UMLS synonyms: Ankle joint effusion | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of left ankle | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of right ankle | Joint effusion of ankle AND/OR foot | Intermittent effusion of joint of ankle | Effusion of joint of left ankle | Effusion of joint of right ankle | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of left tibiotalar joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of left subtalar joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of left calcaneocuboid joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of left talonavicular joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of right tibiotalar joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of right subtalar joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of right calcaneocuboid joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of right talonavicular joint | Intermittent effusion of joint of left ankle | Intermittent effusion of joint of right ankle | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of left navicular-cuneiform joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of right navicular-cuneiform joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of left ankle with hemosiderin effect | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of right ankle with hemosiderin effect | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of middle facet of left subtalar joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of anterior facet of left subtalar joint | magnetic resonance imaging of ankle: joint effusion of posterior facet of left subtalar joint

HP_0032064.label: gastrointestinal eosinophilia
HP_0032064.definition: Eosinophilic infiltration of one or more gastrointestinal organs. Gastrointestinal eosinophilia is a broad term for abnormal eosinophil accumulation in the GI tract, involving many different disease identities. These diseases include primary eosinophil associated gastrointestinal diseases, gastrointestinal eosinophilia in HES and all gastrointestinal eosinophilic states associated with known causes. Each of these diseases has its unique features but there is no absolute boundary between them.
HP_0032064.synonyms: eosinophilic enteritis | eosinophilic gastroenteritis | eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease | eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorders | gi eosinophilia

HP_0032065.label: abnormal serum bicarbonate concentration
HP_0032065.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

HP_0032066.label: decreased serum bicarbonate concentration
HP_0032066.definition: An abnormal reduction of the concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

HP_0032067.label: elevated serum bicarbonate concentration
HP_0032067.definition: An abnormal increase in the concentration of bicarbonate, HCO3[-], in the circulation.

HP_0032068.label: increased urinary mucus
HP_0032068.definition: An increased amount of urinary mucus. A small amount of mucus is produced by mucous membrane epithelial cells of the urinary tract. An increased amount of mucus can be detected upon urinalysis or other assays and may indicate conditions such as urinary tract infection, urinary tract reconstruction involving the use of bowel segments, or contamination of the urine sample prior to urinalysis.

HP_0032069.label: anti - thyroglobulin antibody positivity
HP_0032069.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react to thyroglobulin.
HP_0032069.synonyms: anti - thyroid globulin antibody positivity | tgabs

HP_0032070.label: leptomeningeal enhancement
HP_0032070.definition: Contrast material enhancement of the pia mater or enhancement that extends into the subarachnoid spaces of the sulci and cisterns is leptomeningeal enhancement. Leptomeningeal enhancement is usually associated with meningitis, which may be bacterial, viral, or fungal. The primary mechanism of this enhancement is breakdown of the blood-brain barrier without angiogenesis.
HP_0032070.UMLS synonyms: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement seen on MRI

HP_0032071.label: eosinophilic pneumonia
HP_0032071.definition: The presence of eosinophils in lung tissue, generally as detected by tissue biopsy, with or without blood eosinophilia.
HP_0032071.synonyms: eosinophilic pulmonary infiltration | pulmonary eosinophilia | pulmonary eosinophilic infiltrate | pulmonary eosinophilic infiltration
HP_0032071.UMLS synonyms: Eosinophilic Pneumonia | Eosinophilic pneumonia acute | Tropical Eosinophilic Pneumonia | Eosinophilic pneumonia (SMQ) | Pulmonary eosinophilic infiltrate | pneumonia; bronchopneumonia, allergic (eosinophilic) | Cryptogenic pulmonary eosinophilia | Carrington syndrome | Idiopathic eosinophilic pneumonitis | Simple Pulmonary Eosinophilia | Idiopathic acute eosinophilic pneumonitis

HP_0032072.label: popliteal synovial cyst
HP_0032072.definition: A fluid-filled mass that is a distention of a preexisting bursa in the popliteal fossa, most commonly the gastrocnemio-semimembranosus bursa. This bursa is unique in that it communicates with the knee joint, unlike other periarticular bursae, via an opening in the joint capsule posterior to the medial femoral condyle.
HP_0032072.UMLS synonyms: Popliteal Cyst | Popliteal synovial cyst (Baker's cyst) | Rupture of synovial popliteal cyst | Excision of synovial cyst of popliteal fossa region of knee | Synovial popliteal cyst of bilateral knees | Synovial popliteal cyst of left knee | Synovial popliteal cyst of right knee | magnetic resonance imaging of knee: popliteal cyst with synovial debris | Rupture of synovial popliteal cyst of left knee | Rupture of synovial popliteal cyst of right knee | Family history of synovial cyst of popliteal space | Synovial cyst of popliteal space [Baker], left knee | Synovial cyst of popliteal space [Baker], right knee | Rupture of synovial cyst of knee | Synovial cyst of left knee | Synovial cyst of right knee

HP_0032073.label: aplasia of the fallopian tube
HP_0032073.definition: Aplasia, that is failure to develop, of the fallopian tube.

HP_0032075.label: splenopancreatic fusion
HP_0032075.definition: Fusion of the pancreatic tail and spleen.

HP_0032077.label: male urethral meatus stenosis
HP_0032077.definition: An abnormal narrowing of the urethral opening (meatus) of the penis.

HP_0032078.label: angel - shaped phalanx
HP_0032078.definition: A phalangeal malformation that is termed angel-shaped phalanx (ASP), because of its resemblance to the angels used for decoration of Christmas trees. The various components of an angel-shaped phalanx are: diaphyseal cuff (wings), surrounding a meta-diaphyseal core (body), which may appear empty or structured with a cone-shaped epiphysis (skirt) and pseudoepiphysis (head).
HP_0032078.UMLS synonyms: Angel-shaped proximal phalanges | Angel-shaped middle phalanges

HP_0032079.label: medial degeneration
HP_0032079.definition: Medial degeneration of the aorta is to be used as an overarching term for any aortic surgical specimens that demonstrate one or more of the specific histopathologies mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation, elastic fiber fragmentation and/or loss, elastic fiber thinning, elastic fiber disorganization, smooth muscle cell nuclei loss, laminar medial collapse, smooth muscle cell disorganization, medial fibrosis. Grading of medial degeneration is based on the average overall severity of specific histopathologies as described, considering the worst area(s) sampled from multiple slides and aorta sections.
HP_0032079.UMLS synonyms: Medial degeneration | degeneration; medial artery | magnetic resonance imaging of knee: intrasubstance degeneration of medial meniscus | magnetic resonance imaging of knee: type I intrasubstance degeneration of medial meniscus | MRI of knee: type II intrasubstance degeneration of medial meniscus | magnetic resonance imaging of knee: intrasubstance degeneration of body of medial meniscus | magnetic resonance imaging of knee: intrasubstance degeneration of anterior horn of medial meniscus | magnetic resonance imaging of knee: intrasubstance degeneration of posterior horn of medial meniscus

HP_0032081.label: intralamellar mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
HP_0032081.definition: A type of mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation in which the increase in mucoid extracellular matrix does not significantly alter the arrangement of the lamellar units.

HP_0032082.label: translamellar mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation
HP_0032082.definition: A type of mucoid extracellular matrix accumulation in which the increase in mucoid extracellular matrix alters the arrangement of the lamellar units to varying degrees.

HP_0032083.label: aortic elastic fiber fragmentation
HP_0032083.definition: Loss and/or fragmentation of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta creating increasingly extended translamellar spaces, with absence of elastic fibers, and increased gaps in elastic fiber lamellae as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.
HP_0032083.UMLS synonyms: Elastic fiber fragmentation observed in aneurysmal aortic wall

HP_0032084.label: aortic elastic fiber thinning
HP_0032084.definition: A thinning out of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta that creates widening of intralamellar spaces, as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.

HP_0032085.label: aortic elastic fiber disorganization
HP_0032085.definition: Nonparallel arrangement/disarray of elastic fibers of the media of the aorta as identified on a stain for elastic fibers.

HP_0032086.label: aortic smooth muscle cell nuclei loss
HP_0032086.definition: A region of the aortic media in which smooth muscle cell nuclei, involving multiple lamellae, are not clearly identifiable on an hematoxylin and eosin stain.

HP_0032087.label: aortic laminar medial collapse
HP_0032087.definition: Architecturally, a compaction of aortic medial elastic fibers that creates thinning of the lamellar unit secondary to a band-like smooth muscle cell loss identified using a stain for elastic fibers.

HP_0032088.label: aortic smooth muscle cell disorganization
HP_0032088.definition: Nonparallel arrangement/disarray of smooth muscle cells of the aortic media creating focal/multifocal disarray or sometimes nodular aggregates of smooth muscle cells.

HP_0032089.label: aortic medial fibrosis
HP_0032089.definition: An increase in collagen fibers creating areas of substitutive fibrosis or a widening of intralamellar spaces in the media of the aorta. This can be seen in conjunction with a loss to varying degrees of parallel arrangement of the elastic lamellae (or lamellar units).

HP_0032090.label: intralamellar aortic medial fibrosis
HP_0032090.definition: A type of aortic medial fibrosis in which the increase in collagen does not significantly alter the arrangement of the lamellar units.

HP_0032091.label: translamellar aortic medial fibrosis
HP_0032091.definition: A type of aortic medial fibrosis in which the increase in collagen is more scar-like, altering the arrangement of the lamellar units.

HP_0032092.label: left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
HP_0032092.definition: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction can occur at the valvular, subvalvular, or supravalvular level. In general, there is an obstruction to forward flow which increases afterload, and if untreated, can result in hypertrophy, dilatation, and eventual failure of the left ventricle.
HP_0032092.UMLS synonyms: Acquired left ventricular outflow tract obstruction | Postprocedural left ventricular outflow tract obstruction | Ventricular Outflow Obstruction, Left | Small left ventricular outflow tract without obstruction | cardiac catheterization left ventricular outflow tract obstruction | Removal of obstruction of left ventricular outflow tract | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to neoplasm | Progression of fetal left ventricular outflow tract obstruction | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to diaphragm | echocardiography: dynamic obstruction of left ventricular outflow tract | cardiac catheterization left ventricular outflow tract subaortic obstruction | Repair of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction by patch enlargement of the outflow tract | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to fibromuscular tunnel | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to atrioventricular valve | cardiac catheterization left ventricular outflow tract obstruction mean gradient | cardiac catheterization left ventricular outflow tract obstruction posterior velopharyngeal closure | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to subpulmonary fibromuscular shelf | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to anterolateral muscle band | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to malaligned outlet septum | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to prolapsed arterial valve | Obstruction of right ventricular outflow tract due to aortico-left ventricular tunnel | cardiac catheterization left ventricular outflow tract obstruction peak systolic gradient | Dynamic LVOT Obstruction | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to prolapse of Eustachian valve | Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to aneurysm of membranous septum

HP_0032094.label: increased circulating surfactant protein level
HP_0032094.definition: An increased concentration of a surfactant protein in the blood circulation. Pulmonary surfactant is a highly surface-active mixture of proteins and lipids that is synthesized and secreted onto the alveoli by type II epithelial cells. The protein part of surfactant constitutes of four types of surfactant proteins (SP), SP-A, SP-B, SP-C and SP-D. SP-A and SP-D are hydrophilic proteins that regulate surfactant metabolism and have immunologic functions. These two proteins are detectable in the bloodstream and an elevated level may reflect idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.

HP_0032096.label: abnormal manganese concentration
HP_0032096.definition: A deviation from the normal range of manganese in the blood circulation.

HP_0032097.label: hypermanganesemia
HP_0032097.definition: An elevation above the normal concentration of manganese in the blood.
HP_0032097.UMLS synonyms: Hypermanganesemia with dystonia | Hypermanganesemia with dystonia 2 | Hypermanganesemia with Dystonia Polycythemia and Cirrhosis

HP_0032098.label: hypomanganesemia
HP_0032098.definition: A reduction below the normal concentration of manganese in the blood.

HP_0032099.label: perioral radial furrowing
HP_0032099.definition: The presence of radial grooves in the skin surrounding the mouth (see Figure 4 of PMID:27833976).

HP_0032100.label: abnormal doll 's eye reflex
HP_0032100.definition: The doll's eye reflex (also known as oculocephalic reflex) is a test of brain function that is performed in comatose patients by elevating the head roughly 30 degrees and rapidly rotating the head from side to side with the eyes kept open. A normal response is for the eyes to move in the opposite direction. If the eyes do not move in the opposite direction this may indicate severe brain damage.

HP_0032101.label: unusual infection
HP_0032101.definition: A type of infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection. There are five general subtypes. (i) Opportunistic infection, meaning infection by a pathogen that is not normally able to cause infection in a healthy host (e.g., pneumonia by Pneumocystis jirovecii or CMV); (ii) Unusual location (focus) of an infection (e.g., an aspergillus brain abscess); (iii) a protracted course or lack of adequate response to treatment (e.g., chronic rhinosinusitis); (iv) Unusual severity or intensity of an infection; and (v) unusual recurrence of infections.
HP_0032101.UMLS synonyms: Unusual CNS infection | Consult specialist for unusual nail changes to determine if signs of disease or infection (e.g., dark streaks, redness and swelling, clubbing, thick and overgrown)

HP_0032102.label: wilson sign
HP_0032102.definition: Wilson sign is defined as the elicitation of pain by internally rotating the patient's tibia during knee extension between 90 degrees and 30 degrees of flexion and then relieving that pain by externally rotating the tibia.
HP_0032102.UMLS synonyms: Wilson's sign | Wilson's pronator sign | Wilson test

HP_0032104.label: saccadic oscillation
HP_0032104.definition: An involuntary abnormality of fixation in which there is an abnormal saccade away from fixation followed by an immediate corrective saccade.

HP_0032105.label: macrosaccadic oscillations
HP_0032105.definition: A type of saccadic oscillations with brief periods of fixation between saccades (intersaccadic interval approximately 200 msec). Macrosaccadic oscillations (up to 40 degrees) straddle the intended fixation position and show a crescendo-decrescendo pattern.

HP_0032106.label: conjunctival icterus
HP_0032106.definition: Conjunctival icterus is a condition where there is yellowing of the whites of the eyes. This is most commonly seen in patients who have liver disease.
HP_0032106.synonyms: scleral icterus | yellow conjunctiva | yellow sclera | yellowing of the whites of the eyes

HP_0032107.label: limbal stem cell deficiency
HP_0032107.definition: A condition characterized by a loss or deficiency of the stem cells in the limbus that are vital for re-population of the corneal epithelium and to the barrier function of the limbus.
HP_0032107.UMLS synonyms: Limbal Stem Cell Deficiency | Left limbal stem cell deficiency | Right limbal stem cell deficiency | Bilateral limbal stem cell deficiency | Corneal limbal stem cell deficiency (in homozygotes)

HP_0032108.label: mildly reduced contrast sensitivity
HP_0032108.definition: A mild reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 0.20-0.59 log unit contrast sensitivity loss.

HP_0032109.label: moderately reduced contrast sensitivity
HP_0032109.definition: A moderate reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 0.60-0.99 log unit contrast sensitivity loss.

HP_0032110.label: severely reduced contrast sensitivity
HP_0032110.definition: A severe reduction in the ability to perceive visual contrast characterized by 1.00 log unit or more contrast sensitivity loss.

HP_0032111.label: abnormal vistech contrast sensitivity test
HP_0032111.definition: An abnormality in perception of contrast as measured by the Vistech wall chart sine wave grating test.

HP_0032112.label: abnormal pelli robson contrast sensitivity chart test
HP_0032112.definition: An abnormality in perception of contrast as measured by the Pelli-Robson contrast sensitivity chart, which is a large wall-mounted chart, with letters of a fixed size (comprising spatial frequencies appropriate for estimating peak contrast sensitivity) that decrease in contrast.

HP_0032113.label: semidominant inheritance
HP_0032113.definition: A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on chromosomes in which a trait can manifest in a monoallelic (e.g. heterozygotes) and biallelic (e.g. homozygotes, compound heterozygotes) state, with similar or differing phenotype severity present dependent on the number of alleles affected.

HP_0032114.label: saccadic intrusion
HP_0032114.definition: An involuntary abnormality of fixation in which there is an abnormal saccade away from fixation followed by a delayed corrective saccade.
HP_0032114.UMLS synonyms: Autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia with saccadic intrusion syndrome | Roving eye movements with saccadic intrusions | SPINOCEREBELLAR ATAXIA, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE 4

HP_0032116.label: macrosquare - wave jerks
HP_0032116.definition: Horizontal 10-40 degree excursions from fixation and back again.

HP_0032118.label: retinitis
HP_0032118.definition: Inflammation of the retina of the eye.
HP_0032118.UMLS synonyms: Retinitis | Retinitis Pigmentosa | Solar Retinitis | Cytomegalovirus Retinitis | Focal retinitis | Granulomatous retinitis | Viral retinitis | Candida retinitis | Disseminated retinitis | Histoplasmosis with retinitis | Toxoplasma retinitis | Autoimmune retinitis | Cryptococcal retinitis | Syphilitic retinitis | Foveomacular Retinitis | Cheesy retinitis | Idiopathic retinitis | Retinitis sclopetaria | Necrotising retinitis | Noninfective retinitis | Fungal retinitis | Retinitis central | Peripheral retinitis | bacterial retinitis | retinitis; disciformis

HP_0032120.label: abnormal peripheral nervous system physiology
HP_0032120.definition: Any functional abnormality of the part of the nervous system that consists of the nerves and ganglia outside of the brain and spinal cord.

HP_0032121.label: froment sign
HP_0032121.definition: An abnormal result of a physical examination of the the hand that tests for palsy of the ulnar nerve. This nerve innervates the adductor pollicis and interossei muscles and thereby enables adduction of the thumb and extension of the interphalangeal joint. An abnormal result consists in reduced functionality and muscular weakness in the pinch grip between the thumb and index finger of the affected hand as the patient attempts to pinch a piece of paper that the examiner tries to pull away. The flexor pollicis longus muscle tries to compensate for the weakness by flexing the tip of the thumb at the interphalangeal joint.
HP_0032121.UMLS synonyms: Froment's sign | Froment's sign positive | Froment's sign negative | Froment's sign in left hand | Froment's sign in both hands | Froment's sign in right hand

HP_0032122.label: very low visual acuity
HP_0032122.definition: A reduction in visual acuity with best corrected visual acuity between 1.40 (20/500) and 1.89 logMAR (up to roughly 20/1590).

HP_0032123.label: ultra - low vision
HP_0032123.definition: Best corrected visual acuity worse than 1.90 logMAR (roughly 20/1590).

HP_0032124.label: abnormal proportion of unswitched memory b cells
HP_0032124.definition: A deviation of the normal proportion of unswitched memory B cells in circulation relative to the total number of B cells.
HP_0032124.synonyms: abnormal proportion of non - class - switched memory b cells

HP_0032125.label: increased proportion of unswitched memory b cells
HP_0032125.definition: An increase above the normal proportion of non-class-switched memory B cells relative to the total number of B cells.
HP_0032125.synonyms: elevated proportion of unswitched memory b cells | increased proportion of non - class - switched memory b cells

HP_0032126.label: decreased proportion of unswitched memory b cells
HP_0032126.definition: A reduction below the normal proportion of non-class-switched memory B cells relative to the total number of B cells.
HP_0032126.synonyms: decreased proportion of non - class - switched memory b cells | reduced proportion of unswitched memory b cells

HP_0032127.label: abnormal plasmablast proportion
HP_0032127.definition: A deviation from the normal proportion of plasmablasts in circulation relative to total number of B cells. Plasmablasts are antibody-secreting cells that originate after infection or vaccination.

HP_0032128.label: increased proportion of plasmablasts
HP_0032128.definition: An elevation above the normal proportion of plasmablasts in circulation relative to total number of B cells.

HP_0032129.label: decreased proportion of plasmablasts
HP_0032129.definition: A reduction below the normal proportion of plasmablasts in circulation relative to total number of B cells.

HP_0032130.label: mycobacterium abscessus abscessus infection
HP_0032130.definition: Mycobacterium abscessus complex comprises a group of rapidly growing, multidrug-resistant, nontuberculous mycobacteria that are responsible for a wide spectrum of skin and soft tissue diseases, central nervous system infections, bacteremia, and ocular and other infections.
HP_0032130.UMLS synonyms: Mycobacterium abscessus Infection | Mycobacteroides abscessus infection of skin | Disseminated Mycobacteroides abscessus infection | Infection caused by Mycobacteroides abscessus

HP_0032131.label: cervical dysplasia
HP_0032131.definition: Cervical dysplasia is the precursor to cervical cancer. It is caused by the persistent infection of the human papillomavirus (HPV) into the cervical tissue. Affected cells develop morphologic features with immature basaloid- type squamous cells and mitotic figures in the upper half of the cervical epithelium.

HP_0032140.label: decreased specific antibody response to vaccination
HP_0032140.definition: A reduced ability to synthesize postvaccination antibodies against toxoids and polysaccharides in vaccines, as measured by antibody titer determination following vaccination.

HP_0032141.label: precordial pain
HP_0032141.definition: A type of chest pain that arises in the or under the left breast and often described as throbbing, stabbing, or burning, and lasting hours or longer. The pain may arise with or after effort, and may spread to the left arm or left side of the neck.
HP_0032141.UMLS synonyms: Precordial pain | CHEST PAIN SITE PRECORDIAL | chest pain located left of center | chest pain located right of center

HP_0032142.label: fetor hepaticus
HP_0032142.definition: Fetor hepaticus is the characteristic breath of patients with severe parenchymal liver disease, which has been said to resemble the odor of a mixture of rotten eggs and garlic.

HP_0032143.label: burning mouth
HP_0032143.definition: An intense sensation of burning, scalding, or tingling feeling of the tongue or other regions of the oral mucosa.

HP_0032145.label: sural nerve atrophy
HP_0032145.definition: Wasting of the sural nerve, a sensory nerve in the calf region of the leg.

HP_0032146.definition: Presence of an abnormal type of hemoglobin characterized by the subsitution of a glutamic acid residue at position 7 following the initial methionine residue by a lysine (6GAG>6AAG). The presence of HbC can be determined by hemoglobin electrophoresis.

HP_0032147.definition: Recurrent episodes of redness, burning pain, and warmth of the extremities following exposure to heat or exercise with symptoms predominantly involving the feet.

HP_0032149.definition: A episode of severe pain that breaks through (i.e., temporarily exacerbates) a period of persistent pain.

HP_0032150.label: paroxysmal rectal pain
HP_0032150.definition: Excruciating burning pain in the rectal area that may be triggered by defecation.

HP_0032151.label: episodic eosinophilia
HP_0032151.definition: Recurrent episodes of marked eosinophilia that resolve spontaneously.

HP_0032152.label: keratosis pilaris
HP_0032152.definition: An anomaly of the hair follicles of the skin that typically presents as small, rough, brown folliculocentric papules distributed over characteristic areas of the skin, particularly the outer-upper arms and thighs.

HP_0032156.definition: Loss of sections of skin either spontaneously or after gentle handling.
HP_0032156.synonyms: detached skin | epidermal detachment | skin sloughing

HP_0032157.label: recurrent genital herpes
HP_0032157.definition: Recurrent episodes of genital herpes, typically characterized by stages of erythema, papules, short-lived vesicles, painful ulcers, and crusts on the skin of the genitals and surrounding area, and that typically resolve over a period of 2 to 3 weeks.

HP_0032158.label: unusual infection by anatomical site
HP_0032158.definition: An unusual infection classified by the affected body part.

HP_0032159.label: fungal meningitis
HP_0032159.definition: An infection of the meninges caused by a fungus. Generally, only individuals with deficiencies of the immune system contract fungal meningitis.
HP_0032159.UMLS synonyms: Meningitis, Fungal | Meningitis in other fungal diseases

HP_0032160.label: cryptococcal meningitis
HP_0032160.definition: A type of fungal meningitis caused by an encapsulated yeast that belongs to the genus Cryptococcus. Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are responsible for the majority of cases of human cryptococcosis.
HP_0032160.UMLS synonyms: Meningitis, Cryptococcal | Cryptococcal meningitis recurrent | meningitis; cryptococcosis (manifestation)

HP_0032161.label: coccidioidal meningitis
HP_0032161.definition: A type of fungal meningitis caused by dissemination of coccidioides to basilar meninges.

HP_0032162.label: unusual skin infection
HP_0032162.definition: A type of infection of the skin that can be regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection.

HP_0032163.label: molluscum contagiosum
HP_0032163.definition: Molluscum contagiosum is a cutaneous viral infection that is commonly observed in both healthy and immunocompromised children. The infection is caused by a member of the Poxviridae family, the molluscum contagiosum virus. Molluscum contagiosum presents as single or multiple small white or flesh-colored papules that typically have a central umbilication. The central umbilication may be difficult to observe in young children and, instead, may bear an appearance similar to an acneiform eruption. The lesions vary in size (from 1 mm to 1 cm in diameter) and are painless, although a subset of patients report pruritus in the area of infection. On average, 11-20 papules appear on the body during the course of infection and generally remains a self-limiting disease. However, in immunosuppressed patients, molluscum contagiosum can be a severe infection with hundreds of lesions developing on the body. Extensive eruption is indicative of an advanced immunodeficiency state.

HP_0032164.label: increased blood folate concentration
HP_0032164.definition: An elevated circulating concentration of folic acid, which is also known as vitamin B9.

HP_0032165.label: placental mesenchymal dysplasia
HP_0032165.definition: Placental mesenchymal dysplasia is a rare anomaly characterized by placentomegaly, dilatation of chorionic vessels and hydropic stem villi with cistern-like formation. It is often clinically mistaken for a partial hydatidiform mole but there is no trophoblastic proliferation. P57 immunohistochemical expression is discordant, showing a normal positive expression in the cytotrophoblastic cells, and loss of expression in the stromal cells.

HP_0032167.label: clostridium difficile enteritis
HP_0032167.definition: An infection of the small intestine (enteritis) by clostridium difficile.

HP_0032168.label: clostridium difficile colitis
HP_0032168.definition: An infection of the colon (colitis) by clostridium difficile.

HP_0032169.definition: A type of infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection because of unusual severity or intensity of the infection.

HP_0032170.label: severe varicella zoster infection
HP_0032170.definition: An unusually severe form of varicella zoster virus (VZV) infection. In the majority of the cases, especially in children, varicella is a very mild infection characterised by skin lesions, low grade fever and malaise. Severe infection is characterized by manifestions including VZV pneumonia, hepatitis, meningitis, and disseminated varicella.
HP_0032170.UMLS synonyms: Cordonnier Grade 3 Viral Complication, Severe Varicella Zoster Virus Infection

HP_0032171.label: bladder pain
HP_0032171.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to the urinary bladder. Bladder pain may be more pronounced with a full bladder and relieved upon urination, but this is not always the case.
