HP_0032172.label: air crescent sign
HP_0032172.definition: A crescent of air surrounding a soft-tissue mass in a pulmonary cavity and can be seen in both plain X-ray and CT scan.

HP_0032173.label: continuous diaphragm sign
HP_0032173.definition: This sign is seen in pneumomediastinum in which air accumulates between the lower border of the heart and the superior part of the diaphragm, which results in complete visualization of the diaphragm in chest X-ray, hence named continuous diaphragm sign.

HP_0032174.label: tree - in - bud pattern
HP_0032174.definition: The tree-in-bud pattern represents centrilobular branching structures that resemble a budding tree. The pattern reflects a spectrum of endo- and peribronchiolar disorders, including mucoid impaction, inflammation, and/or fibrosis (See Figure 70 of PMID:18195376).

HP_0032175.label: signet ring sign
HP_0032175.definition: This finding is composed of a ring-shaped opacity representing a dilated bronchus in cross section and a smaller adjacent opacity representing its pulmonary artery, with the combination resembling a signet (or pearl) ring. It is the basic sign of bronchiectasis in pulmonary computed tomography imaging.

HP_0032176.label: apical pulmonary opacity
HP_0032176.definition: An apical cap is a caplike lesion at the lung apex, usually caused by intrapulmonary and pleural fibrosis pulling down extrapleural fat or possibly by chronic ischemia resulting in hyaline plaque formation on the visceral pleura. The prevalence increases with age. It can also be seen in hematoma resulting from aortic rupture or in other fluid collection associated with infection or tumor, either outside the parietal pleura or loculated within the pleural space.

HP_0032177.label: parenchymal consolidation
HP_0032177.definition: Consolidation refers to an exudate or other product of disease that replaces alveolar air, rendering the lung solid (as in infective pneumonia).

HP_0032178.label: flaky paint dermatosis
HP_0032178.definition: A dermatosis characterized by generalized shiny, enamel-like, hyperpigmented scales in an irregular pattern. The scales may peel or desquamate, rather like old, sun-baked blistered paint, often with areas of underlying hypopigmentation. This has led to the terms peeling paint or flaky paint dermatosis (See the Figure in PMID:24285001).

HP_0032179.label: abnormal circulating globulin concentration
HP_0032179.definition: An abnormal concentration of globulins in the blood. Albumin makes up more than half of the total protein present in serum. The remaining blood proteins except albumin and fibrinogen (which is not in serum) are referred to as globulins. The globulin fraction includes hundreds of serum proteins including carrier proteins, enzymes, complement, and immunoglobulins. Most of these are synthesized in the liver, although the immunoglobulins are synthesized by plasma cells. Globulins are divided into four groups by electrophoresis. The four fractions are alpha1, alpha2, beta and gamma, depending on their migratory pattern between the anode and the cathode.

HP_0032180.label: abnormal circulating metabolite concentration
HP_0032180.definition: An abnormal level of an analyte measured in the blood.

HP_0032181.label: anomalous hepatic venous drainage into the left atrium
HP_0032181.definition: An abnormality of the hepatic veins, which normally drain de-oxygenated blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava, whereby the hepatic veins drain into the left atrium.

HP_0032182.label: abnormal proportion of memory t cells
HP_0032182.definition: An abnormal proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood. Memory T cells have previously encountered and responded to their cognate antigen and upon a repeated encounter with the antigen can mount a faster and stronger response.

HP_0032183.label: decreased proportion of memory t cells
HP_0032183.definition: An abnormally reduced proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood.

HP_0032184.label: increased proportion of memory t cells
HP_0032184.definition: An abnormally elevated proportion of memory T cells compared to the total number of T cells in the blood.

HP_0032185.label: disseminated molluscum contagiosum
HP_0032185.definition: The presense of molluscum contagiosum lesions across multiple areas of the body.

HP_0032186.label: anal neoplasm
HP_0032186.definition: A benign or malignant neoplasm that affects the anal canal or anal margin.

HP_0032187.definition: Anal intraepithelial neoplasia (AIN) is a premalignant lesion of the anal mucosa that is a precursor to anal cancer.

HP_0032188.label: cellular hypersensitivity to mitomycin c
HP_0032188.definition: An increased cellular sensitivity to the DNA cross-linking agent, mitomycin C (MMC). In the presence of increased sensitivity, MMC causes increased cell death, chromosome breakage, and accumulation in the G2 phase of the cell cycle.

HP_0032189.label: cellular hypersensitivity to diepoxybutane
HP_0032189.definition: An increased cellular sensitivity to the DNA cross-linking agent, diepoxybutane (DEB). In the presence of increased sensitivity, DEB causes cell death, chromosome breakage, and accumulation in the G2 phase of the cell cycle.

HP_0032190.label: abnormal meniscus morphology
HP_0032190.definition: Abnormal structure of the meniscus of the knee, two crescent shape fibrocartilaginous pads that disperse the weight of the body and reduce friction of the knee joint during movement.

HP_0032191.label: torn meniscus
HP_0032191.definition: A tear in the cartilaginous pad (meniscus) of the knee.

HP_0032192.definition: Hydatidiform mole (HM) is an aberrant human pregnancy with absence of, or abnormal embryonic development, hydropic degeneration of chorionic villi, and excessive proliferation of the trophoblast.

HP_0032193.definition: An abnormal decrease in the average size of low-density lipoprotein particle size in the blood circulation.

HP_0032195.label: abnormal s wave
HP_0032195.definition: Any anomaly of the S wave, which is the third component of the QRS wave complex. The S wave signifies the final depolarization of the ventricles at the base of the heart.

HP_0032196.label: prominent s wave in lead i
HP_0032196.definition: Increased amplitude (0.1 mV or more) and/or duration (40 ms or more) of the S wave as measured in lead I of the electrocardiogram.

HP_0032197.label: deep s wave in lead v5
HP_0032197.definition: Abnormal depth of the S wave in lead V5 of the electrocardiogram.

HP_0032198.label: decreased prothrombin time
HP_0032198.definition: Abnormally short time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.

HP_0032199.label: abnormal prothrombin time
HP_0032199.definition: Any deviation from the normal amount of time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio (INR), which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time (PT) to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.

HP_0032200.label: perivascular fibrosis
HP_0032200.definition: The presence of thick collagen bundles around blood vessels, often in an onion-skin type whorling pattern.

HP_0032201.label: rotator cuff tear
HP_0032201.definition: The term rotator cuff describes the tendons connecting the infraspinatus, supraspinatus, teres minor, and subscapularis muscles to the humeral head.Traumatic tears of the rotator cuff tend to occur at the tendon-bone junction of the supraspinatus and greater tuberosity of the humerus whereas degenerative tears tend to be seen posteriorly at the junction of the supraspinatus and infraspinatu A rotator cuff tear is when one or more of these tendons tears or detaches from the humerus.

HP_0032202.label: vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia
HP_0032202.definition: Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN) is widely accepted as the precursor lesion of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC). VSCC arises via either a human papilloma virus (HPV)-associated pathway, or more commonly, via a mechanism independent of HPV, often being linked to chronic inflammatory conditions such as lichen sclerosus (LS). Accordingly, two distinct subtypes of VIN are recognised: the HPV-associated high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion/usual VIN (HSIL/uVIN) and the non-HPV-associated differentiated VIN (dVIN). HSIL is clinically identified by its multifocal, warty appearance and on histology by conspicuous cytological and architectural atypia. Differentiated VIN, on the other hand, often produces ill-defined lesions, and on histology, notoriously mimics non-neoplastic epithelial disorders (NNED), particularly LS. As a result, dVIN is rarely identified in advance of a diagnosis of invasive malignancy, despite being the precursor lesion of the majority of VSCC.

HP_0032203.label: lymphoid nodular hyperplasia
HP_0032203.definition: Lymphoid nodular hyperplasia (LNH) of the terminal ileum and colon has been considered a mucosal response to nonspecific stimuli, most often infections, and consequently has been regarded as a pathophysiologic phenomenon during infancy and childhood. LNH can be ascertained by colonoscopy, whereby a lymphoid nodule is defined as an extruding follicle with a diameter of not more than 2 mm, and LNH is defined as a cluster of not more than 10 of such extruding lymphoid nodules (see Figure 1 of PMID:17368236).
HP_0032203.UMLS synonyms: Nodular lymphoid hyperplasia | Pulmonary nodular lymphoid hyperplasia | Nodular lymphoid hyperplasia of intestine | PULMONARY NODULAR LYMPHOID HYPERPLASIA, FAMILIAL

HP_0032204.label: chronic active epstein - barr virus infection
HP_0032204.definition: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is an uncommon outcome of EBV infection and may present as a waxing and waning or fulminant syndrome. Unlike acute infectious mononucleosis, wherein EBV establishes lifelong infection and survives by maintaining a delicate balance with the host as a latent infection, in chronic active EBV infection the host-virus balance is disturbed.

HP_0032209.definition: A deviation from the normal concentration of free triiodothyronine (T3) in the blood circulation. HP_0032215.label: disseminated cutaneous warts
HP_0032215.definition: Multiple skin warts located in multiple parts of the body, e.g., neck, trunks, and extremities.

HP_0032216.label: lymphocytic infiltration of the colorectal mucosa
HP_0032216.definition: Abnormally increased intraepithelial lymphocyte count. This finding may be appreciated as large numbers of surface intraepithelial lymphocytes as seen (for instance) with hematoxylin and eosin staining of a colonic biopsy sample taken during colonoscopy.

HP_0032217.label: indurated nodule
HP_0032217.definition: A skin nodule that is unusually hard (indurated).

HP_0032218.definition: A reduction in the proportion of CD4-positive T cells relative to the total number of T cells.

HP_0032220.label: interface hepatitis
HP_0032220.definition: Inflammation of the liver characterized by a mononuclear cell infiltrate whereby portal inflammatory cells extend through the limiting plate between the portal tract and liver parenchyma.

HP_0032221.label: periportal emperipolesis
HP_0032221.definition: The engulfing of lymphocytes by hepatocytes, which typically occurs in the interface hepatitis area.

HP_0032222.label: serrated intestinal polyps
HP_0032222.definition: The presence of multiple serrated polyps in the intestine. Unlike conventional adenomas, which are uniformly dysplastic, the vast majority of serrated lesions contain no dysplasia. The serrated class includes the hyperplastic polyps, which are not considered precancerous; sessile serrated polyps (also called sessile serrated adenomas); and traditional serrated adenomas. Sessile serrated polyps are larger on average and more often located in the proximal colon. Sessile serrated polyps have a more irregular surface, a pattern to the surface that has been called cloudlike, and indistinct edges compared with hyperplastic polyps. Sessile serrated polyps also have large open pits on the surface (type O pits) when viewed with magnification.

HP_0032223.label: blood group
HP_0032223.definition: Any of the various types of human blood whose antigen characteristics determine compatibility in transfusion. While the ABO and Rhesus systems are the most well known, there are in total about 300 different blood type antigens distributed across 34 different blood type systems.

HP_0032225.label: perifollicular fibroma
HP_0032225.definition: Perifollicular fibroma is a rare cutaneous hamartoma that shows differentiation in the connective tissue sheath of hair follicles. It can occur as a solitary papule or as multiple lesions. Histologically, the lesion consists of a concentric arrangement of cellular fibrous tissue around a normal hair follicle.

HP_0032226.label: abnormal sebaceous gland morphology
HP_0032226.definition: Any structural anomaly of the sebaceous glands.

HP_0032227.label: sebaceous hyperplasia
HP_0032227.definition: A common, benign skin condition involving hypertrophy of the sebaceous glands characterized by single or multiple lesions that manifest as yellow, soft, small papules with umbilication. The lesions are located commonly on the central face (specifically, the nose, cheeks and forehead) but may also occur elsewhere, including the chest, mouth, scrotum, foreskin, penile shaft, vulva, and areola.

HP_0032228.label: trichodiscoma
HP_0032228.definition: A small benign fibrovascular tumor of the dermal part of the hair disk. Trichodiscoma is rather simple in appearance and consists of a dome-shaped fibrous tumor with a prominent vascular component that fills the papillary dermis under an atrophic epidermis. As in a normal hair disk, a hair follicle may be present at one edge of the papular lesion.

HP_0032236.label: increased circulating immature neutrophil count
HP_0032236.definition: An abnormally increased number of immature neutrophils in the peripheral blood circulation.

HP_0032237.label: increased circulating myelocyte count
HP_0032237.definition: The number of myelocytes in the peripheral blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. Myelocytes are immature neutrophils with a size of 12-18 micrometers, a round or oval nucleus with no nucleoli, bluish-pink staining cytoplasm with primary and secondary granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 2:1.

HP_0032238.label: increased circulating metamyelocyte count
HP_0032238.definition: The number of metamyelocytes in the peripheral blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. Metamyelocytes are immature neutrophils with a size of 10-18 micrometers, an indented or kidney-shaped nucleus, pinkish-blue staining cytoplasm with secondary granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 1.5:1.

HP_0032239.label: increased circulating band cell count
HP_0032239.definition: The number of band cells in the peripheral blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. Band cells are immature neutrophils with a size of 10-18 micrometers, a horseshoe-shaped nucleus with no nucleoli, light-pink staining cytoplasm with many small secondary granules, and a nucleus:cytoplasm ratio of 1:2.
HP_0032239.synonyms: increased circulating band form neutrophils | left shift

HP_0032240.label: elevated circulating e selectin level
HP_0032240.definition: An increased concentration of E selectin in the blood circulation.

HP_0032241.label: cervical neoplasm
HP_0032241.definition: A tumor (abnormal growth of tissue) of the uterine cervix.

HP_0032249.label: coccidioidomycosis
HP_0032249.definition: Infection by a Coccidioides species fungus. These are dimorphic, soil-dwelling, fungi known to cause a broad spectrum of disease, ranging from a mild febrile illness to severe pulmonary manifestations or disseminated disease. HP_0032250.definition: An infection by Acinetobacter baumannii, a Gram-negative bacillus that is aerobic, pleomorphic and non-motile. HP_0032253.label: eosinophilic granuloma
HP_0032253.definition: A type of granuloma characterized morphologically by the predominance of Langerhans cells with characteristic grooved, folded, indented nuclei in the appropriate milieu that includes variable numbers of eosinophils and histiocytes including multinucleated forms, often appearing similar to osteoclasts or touton like giant cells, neutrophils and small lymphocytes. The concentration of the eosinophilic infiltrate varies from scattered mature cells to sheet-like masses of cells. Occasionally, areas of bone necrosis may interrupt the cellular infiltrate. The foamy cells may also be amassed in clumps, which are of no clinical significance because these clumps represent phagocytosis of lipid debris.

HP_0032255.definition: An infection that is caused by a fungus that would generally not be able to cause an infection in a host with a normal immune system. Such fungi take advantage of the opportunity, so to speak, that is provided by a weakened immune system.

HP_0032257.label: disseminated histoplasmosis
HP_0032257.definition: Histoplasmosis infection involving multiple sites of the body. Disseminated histoplasmosis can involve various organs, including reticuloendothelial organs, gastrointestinal tract, adrenal glands, central nervous system, endovascular structures, kidney, and skin. It typically presents with systemic symptoms like fever, generalized fatigue, night sweats, weight loss, and the symptoms related to the specific organ involved. Severe disseminated disease can manifest as septic shock, multi organ failure, and ARDS.

HP_0032259.label: chronic tinea infection
HP_0032259.definition: The term tinea means fungal infection, whereas dermatophyte refers to the fungal organisms that cause tinea. This term refers to a tinea infection that is chronic or recalcitrant to treatment and may be reflective of an immune defect.

HP_0032260.label: opportunistic bacterial infection
HP_0032260.definition: An infection that is caused by a bacterium that would generally not be able to cause an infection in a host with a normal immune system. Such bacteria take advantage of the opportunity, so to speak, that is provided by a weakened immune system.

HP_0032261.label: nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary infection
HP_0032261.definition: An infection of the lung caused by environmental mycobacteria. Such infections can occur in individuals with predisposing lung disease or immune disease.

HP_0032267.label: empty delta sign
HP_0032267.definition: This sign is created by a nonenhancing thrombus in the dural sinus surrounded by triangular enhancing dura as seen on cross-section. The sign, seen on contrast-enhanced CT scan images, suggests dural sinovenous thrombosis. It is best seen on wider window settings. It is a reliable sign of sinus thrombosis but is seen only in 25-30% of these cases.

HP_0032268.label: dural tail sign
HP_0032268.definition: This sign represents thickening and enhancement of the dura mater in continuity with a mass, which on MR images, gives the appearance of a tail arising from the mass. The dural tail is thought to represent reactive change; however, it may also be due to tumor invasion. Three criteria need to be met for a positive dural tail sign: the tail should be seen on two successive images through the tumor, it should taper away from the tumor, and it must enhance more than the tumor.

HP_0032269.label: lemon sign
HP_0032269.definition: The lemon sign refers to the shape of the fetal skull at ultrasonography (US) when the frontal bones lose their normal convex contour and appear flattened or inwardly scalloped. This gives the skull a shape that is said to resemble a lemon.. The sign is seen on transverse sonograms of the fetal cranium obtained at the level of the ventricles.

HP_0032270.label: optic nerve tram - track sign
HP_0032270.definition: A tram-track sign is composed of two enhancing areas of tumor separated from each other by the negative defect of the optic nerve. It is seen on contrast-enhanced CT scan and MRI images, in optic nerve sheath meningioma. The sign helps distinguish between optic nerve sheath meningioma and optic glioma. Optic glioma arises from glial cells within the optic nerve and there is no clear separation between the nerve and the tumor; hence the tram-track sign is not seen in optic gliomas. Calcification may be seen in optic nerve sheath meningiomas in 20-50% of cases and hence the tram-track sign may be seen on nonenhanced CT scan images as a linear calcification around the nerve, but this is less common.

HP_0032271.label: extrapulmonary tuberculosis
HP_0032271.definition: A type of tubercular infection located outside of the lung, which is the most common location of tuberculosis. There are two types of clinical manifestation of tuberculosis (TB) are pulmonary TB (PTB) and extrapulmonary TB (EPTB). The former is most common. EPTB refers to TB involving organs other than the lungs (e.g., pleura, lymph nodes, abdomen, genitourinary tract, skin, joints and bones, or meninges). A patient with both pulmonary and EPTB is classified as a case of PTB.

HP_0032282.definition: An inflammatory process in skin caused by an exogenous agent that directly or indirectly injure the skin. HP_0032301.label: genital warts

Their color is variable but tends to be skin colored or darker, and they may occasionally bleed. Warts may cause itching, redness, or discomfort. An outbreak of genital warts may also cause psychological distress.

HP_0032355.definition: A reduction in the maximum expiratory flow per minute, which can be used to measure how fast a subject can exhale as well as to judge the strength of the expiratory muscles and the condition of the large airways.

HP_0032356.label: decreased pre - bronchodilator forced vital capacity
HP_0032356.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can expel following maximal insipiration, with the test being performed before the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
HP_0032356.synonyms: decreased pre bronchodilator forced vital capacity | decreased prebronchodilator forced vital capacity

HP_0032357.label: decreased post - bronchodilator forced vital capacity
HP_0032357.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can expel following maximal insipiration, with the test being performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
HP_0032357.synonyms: decreased post bronchodilator forced vital capacity | decreased postbronchodilator forced vital capacity

HP_0032358.label: decreased post - bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second
HP_0032358.definition: An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can forcefully expel in one second, with the test being performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
HP_0032358.synonyms: decreased post bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second | decreased postbronchodilator forced expiratory volume in one second

HP_0032359.label: decreased forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
HP_0032359.definition: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled.

HP_0032360.label: decreased pre - bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
HP_0032360.definition: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled. Here, the test is performed before the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
HP_0032360.synonyms: decreased pre bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 % | decreased pre - bronchodilator fef25 - 75 % | decreased prebronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %

HP_0032361.label: decreased post - bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %
HP_0032361.definition: A reduction compared to the predicted value of the forced expiratory flow over the middle one-half of the FVC; the average flow from the point at which 25% of the FVC has been exhaled to the point at which 75% of the FVC has been exhaled. Here, the test is performed after the administration of a bronchodilating medication.
HP_0032361.synonyms: decreased post bronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 % | decreased post - bronchodilator fef25 - 75 % | decreased postbronchodilator forced expiratory flow 25 - 75 %

HP_0032362.label: increased circulating corticosterone level
HP_0032362.definition: An abnormally elevated concentration of corticosterone in the blood.

HP_0032363.label: decreased circulating corticosterone level
HP_0032363.definition: An abnormally reduced concentration of corticosterone in the blood.

HP_0032364.label: obsolete abnormal csf amino acid level

HP_0032365.label: exacerbated by aspirin exposure
HP_0032365.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by ingestion of aspirin.

HP_0032366.label: positive direct antiglobulin test
HP_0032366.definition: A positive result of the direct antiglobulin test (DAT), a method of demonstrating the presence of antibody or complement bound to red blood cell (RBC) membranes by the use of anti-human globulin to form a visible agglutination reaction.

HP_0032367.label: abnormal growth hormone level
HP_0032367.definition: Any deviation from the normal level of growth hormone (GH) in the blood circulation. GH or somatotropin is a peptide hormone that stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration. Its secretion from the pituitary is regulated by the neurosecretory nuclei of the hypothalamus, which can release Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH or somatocrinin) and Growth hormone-inhibiting hormone (GHIH or somatostatin) into the hypophyseal portal venous blood surrounding the pituitary. GH is secreted in a pulsatile manner, which is one of the reasons why an isolated measurement of its blood concentration is not meaningful.

HP_0032368.label: acidemia
HP_0032368.definition: An abnormally low blood pH (usually defined as less than 7.35).

HP_0032369.label: alkalemia
HP_0032369.definition: An abnormally high blood pH (usually defined as 7.41 or above).

HP_0032370.label: blood group a
HP_0032370.definition: ABO phenotype A, corresponding to the genotype AO or AA.

HP_0032371.label: isoleucinuria
HP_0032371.definition: An increased concentration of isoleucine in the urine.

HP_0032372.label: increased peripheral blast count
HP_0032372.definition: An increased count in the peripheral blood of cells that are precursors to mature circulating blood cells such as neutrophiles, monocytes, lymphocutes, and erythrocytes. Blasts are not usually found in significant numbers in the peripheral blood circulation, but can be observed in hematopoietic neoplasms such as leukemia, severe infections, and as a result of certain medications.
HP_0032372.synonyms: elevated blast count | elevated circulating blasts | increased peripheral myeloblast count

HP_0032373.label: duffy blood group
HP_0032373.definition: The Duffy blood group system is based on the presence of a glycoprotein termed Fy that is on the surface of erythrocytes and some other cells. There are two Duffy antigens named Fya and Fyb, and thus there are four Duffy phenotypes: a+b+, a+b-, a-b+,a-b-.

HP_0032374.label: duffy fya positivity
HP_0032374.definition: Presence of the Duffy Fya antigen.

HP_0032375.label: duffy fyb positivity
HP_0032375.definition: Presence of the Duffy Fyb antigen.

HP_0032376.label: anti - beta 2 glycoprotein i antibody positivity
HP_0032376.definition: Presence of antibodies against beta 2 glycoprotein I in the circulation. Beta-2 glycoprotein I (beta2GPI) is the principal target of autoantibodies in the antiphospholipid syndrome (APS).

HP_0032377.label: increased urinary orosomucoid
HP_0032377.definition: An increased concentration in the urine of alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP), also known as orosomucoid (ORM). AGP is a 41-43-kDa glycoprotein with a pI of 2.8-3.8. AGP is an acute-phase protein that has many activities including, but not limited to, acting as an acute-phase reactant and disease marker, modulating immunity, binding and carrying drugs, maintaining the barrier function of capillary, and mediating the sphingolipid metabolism.

HP_0032378.label: immediate - type hypersensitivity drug reaction
HP_0032378.definition: Hypersensitivity that is observed within 1 hr of exposures. A variety of adverse reactions can occur within minutes to hours of exposure to a drug. Some can be related to the pharmacological action of the drug (WHO Adverse Reaction Terminology type A for augmented) and usually have a low mortality. Others are not readily predictable based on the structure and pharmacological action of the drug and have a relatively high mortality risk (Type B for bizarre). The most serious form of immediate onset drug hypersensitivity reaction, anaphylaxis. Other reactions including itching, dizziness/light-headedness, nausea, chest discomfort but without any objective skin features, physical signs or physiological compromise. Skin only reactions include generalized erythema, urticaria or angioedema without any sentinel features (see below) of other organ involvement.

HP_0032379.label: polymorphous light eruption
HP_0032379.definition: The cardinal symptom is severely pruritic skin lesions. Macular, papular, papulovesicular, urticarial, multiforme- and plaque-like variants are differentiated morphologically, hence the name polymorphous. Usually one morphology dominates in a single individual (monomorphous). The skin lesions develop a few hours to several days after sun exposure. Initially, patchy erythema develops, accompanied by pruritus. Distinct lesions then develop. The upper chest, upper arms, backs of the hands, thighs, and the sides of the face are the primary localizations. The skin lesions resolve spontaneously within several days of ceasing sun exposure and do not leave behind any traces.
HP_0032379.UMLS synonyms: Polymorphous light eruption | Polymorphous light eruption, papulovesicular type | Polymorphous light eruption, eczematous type | Polymorphous light eruption, plaque type | Polymorphous light eruption, papular type | Polymorphous light eruption, diffuse erythematous type | Actinic prurigo

HP_0032381.label: hydroa vacciniforme
HP_0032381.definition: In response to the spring sun distinct inflamed reddened skin develops on the ears, nose, cheeks, fingers, backs of the hands, and the lower arms, on which blisters with serous or hemorrhagic content develop. These dry out with the formation of a blackish scab. After shedding of the scab, depressed, varioliform, often hypopigmented scars remain. In addition, hyper- and hypopigmentation are present together, resulting in a polymorphous skin presentation.
HP_0032381.synonyms: acute vesiculation and crusting and scarring following sun exposure
HP_0032381.UMLS synonyms: Hydroa Vacciniforme | Hydroa vacciniforme, familial | Hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoma | Systemic Hydroa Vacciniforme Lymphoproliferative Disorder | Classic Hydroa Vacciniforme Lymphoproliferative Disorder

HP_0032382.label: uniparental disomy
HP_0032382.definition: Inheritance of both homologues of a chromosome pair from the same parent.

HP_0032383.definition: A type of uniparental disomy in which the two different chromosomes (or chromosome segments) of the same parent are transmitted.

HP_0032384.label: uniparental isodisomy
HP_0032384.definition: A type of uniparental disomy in which the two identical chromosomes (or chromosome segments) of the same parent are transmitted.

HP_0032385.label: abnormal circulating transferrin concentration
HP_0032385.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation.

HP_0032386.definition: An abnormally increased concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation.

HP_0032387.label: reduced circulating transferrin concentration
HP_0032387.definition: An abnormally decreased concentration of transferrin in the blood circulation.

HP_0032388.label: periventricular nodular heterotopia
HP_0032388.definition: Nodules of heterotopia along the ventricular walls. There can be a single nodule or a large number of nodules, they can exist on either or both sides of the brain at any point along the higher ventricle margins, they can be small or large, single or multiple.

HP_0032389.label: periventricular laminar heterotopia
HP_0032389.definition: A large mass of heterotopia in a laminar configuration along the ventricular walls. Usually bilateral.

HP_0032390.label: periventricular ribbonlike heterotopia
HP_0032390.definition: Heterotopia that forms a continuous wavy line along the ventricular wall.

HP_0032391.label: subcortical heterotopia
HP_0032391.definition: A form of heterotopia were the mislocalized gray matter is located deep within the white matter.

HP_0032392.label: nodular subcortical heterotopia in peritrigonal regions
HP_0032392.definition: Solid nodular heterotopia situated in the region of the peritrigonal optic pathway posterior to the deep gray nuclei.

HP_0032393.label: diffuse ribbon - like subcortical heterotopia
HP_0032393.definition: Subcortical heterotopia consisting of a bilateral and symmetric single continuous, undulating ribbon-like layer of gray matter located in the frontal, parietal and occipital lobes. It has no visible connection to the overlying cortex.

HP_0032394.label: mesial parasagittal subcortical heterotopia
HP_0032394.definition: Subcortical heterotopia extending along the mesial aspect of the lateral ventricles, with direct connection to mesial polymicrogyria-like cortex at the anterior and posterior limits of the heterotopia.

HP_0032395.label: curvilinear subcortical heterotopia
HP_0032395.definition: Large subcortical heterotopia of variable morphology wiht streaks and swirls. These always connect to the overlying cortex in at least one, but usually in multiple, locations. Spaces with the signal intensity of CSF are usually seen within the heterotopia.

HP_0032396.label: transmantle columnar heterotopia
HP_0032396.definition: Linear heterotopia spanning from the cerebral mantle from the pia to the ependyma.

HP_0032397.label: citrullinuria
HP_0032397.definition: An increased concentration of citrulline in the urine.
HP_0032397.UMLS synonyms: Citrullinuria (finding) | Citrullinemia | Citrullinuria Gene Anomaly Detection Reagents

HP_0032398.label: dysgyria
HP_0032398.definition: An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation.

HP_0032399.label: dysgyria with normal cortical thickness
HP_0032399.definition: An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation but with a normal thickness of the cortex.

HP_0032400.label: dysgyria with thickened cortex
HP_0032400.definition: An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation and a thickened cortex intermediate between pachygyria and polymicrogyria.

HP_0032401.label: aspartic aciduria
HP_0032401.definition: A increased concentration of aspartic acid in the urine.

HP_0032403.label: asparaginuria
HP_0032403.definition: An increased concentration of asparagine in the urine.
HP_0032403.synonyms: increased level of asparagine in urine | increased urine asparagine level

HP_0032404.label: testicular mass
HP_0032404.definition: An abnormal bulge or lump in a testis. A testicular mass has a long differential diagnosis including testicular torsion, epididymitis, acute orchitis, strangulated hernia and testicular cancer.

HP_0032406.label: unilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria
HP_0032406.definition: A type of perisylvian polymicrogyria that largely affects one side of the brain.

HP_0032407.label: bilateral perisylvian polymicrogyria
HP_0032407.definition: A type of perisylvian polymicrogyria that affects both sides of the brain.
HP_0032407.UMLS synonyms: Perisylvian syndrome | POLYMICROGYRIA, BILATERAL PERISYLVIAN, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE

HP_0032408.definition: A breast lump is any discrete mass in a breast noticed by the patient, significant other, or physician.

HP_0032409.label: subcortical band heterotopia
HP_0032409.definition: A form of subcortical heterotopia with mislocalized gray matter within the white matter.It is defined as longitudinal bands of gray matter located deep to the cerebral cortex and separated from it by a thin layer of normal appearing white matter. It is part of the lissencephaly spectrum.

HP_0032410.label: bilateral generalized polymicrogyria
HP_0032410.definition: Symmetric generalized polymicrogyria with no obvious gradient or region of maximal severity; may have abnormal high signal in white matter.

HP_0032411.label: posterior predominant subcortical band heterotopia
HP_0032411.definition: Longitudinal bands of gray matter located deep to the cerebral cortex and separated from it by a thin layer of normal appearing white matter visible along the occipital cortex.
HP_0032411.synonyms: occipital subcortical band heterotopia | subcortical band heterotopia posterior predominant

HP_0032412.label: anterior predominant subcortical band heterotopia
HP_0032412.definition: Longitudinal bands of gray matter located deep to the cerebral cortex and separated from it by a thin layer of normal appearing white matter visible in the frontal and temporal lobes.

HP_0032413.label: diffuse subcortical band heterotopia
HP_0032413.definition: Longitudinal bands of gray matter located deep to the cerebral cortex and separated from it by a thin layer of normal appearing white matter visible along the whole brain.

HP_0032414.label: hydroxylysinuria
HP_0032414.definition: The presence of an elevated amount of 5-hydroxylysine in the urine. This compound is a hydroxylated derivative of the amino acid lysine that is present in certain collagens.
HP_0032414.UMLS synonyms: Hydroxylysinuria | Seizures and intellectual disability due to hydroxylysinuria

HP_0032415.label: parasagittal parieto - occipital polymicrogyria
HP_0032415.definition: Polymicrogyria in parasagittal and mesial aspects of parieto-occipital cortex.

HP_0032416.label: retinal microaneurysm
HP_0032416.definition: A localized dilation of microvasculature formed due to disruption of the internal elastic lamina of a retinal capillary blood vessel. The lesions present as small circular, red dots having distinct margins and are no larger than a blood vessel width at the disk margin. This expansion disturbs the normal flow pattern, changing shear force and pressure along the vessel. Shear force plays a key role in promoting the differentiation and proliferation of endothelial cells.

HP_0032417.definition: Circumferential fibrosis in the interstitium surrounding Bowman's capsule

HP_0032418.label: abnormal hdl subfraction concentration

HP_0032423.label: decreased hdl2b concentration
HP_0032423.definition: A reduction below the normal concentration of the HDL2b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL2b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 9.7-12 nm.

HP_0032424.label: increased hdl2b concentration
HP_0032424.definition: An elevation above the normal concentration of the HDL2b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL2b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 9.7-12 nm.

HP_0032425.label: abnormal hdl3a concentration
HP_0032425.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of the HDL3a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.2-8.79 nm.

HP_0032426.label: abnormal hdl3b concentration
HP_0032426.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of the HDL3b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.8-8.19 nm.

HP_0032427.label: abnormal hdl3c concentration
HP_0032427.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of the HDL3c subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3c particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.20-7.79 nm.

HP_0032428.label: increased hdl3a concentration
HP_0032428.definition: An elevation above the normal concentration of the HDL3a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.2-8.79 nm.

HP_0032429.label: decreased hdl3a concentration
HP_0032429.definition: A reduction below the normal concentration of the HDL3a subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3a particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 8.2-8.79 nm.

HP_0032430.label: increased hdl3b concentration
HP_0032430.definition: An elevation above the normal concentration of the HDL3b subfraction in the blood circulation. An HDL3b particle is defined as an HDL particle with a size of 7.8-8.19 nm.

HP_0032434.label: delayed umbilical cord separation

HP_0032435.definition: An infection of the umbilicus and/or surrounding tissues occurring in the neonatal period.

HP_0032436.label: abnormal circulating c - reactive protein concentration
HP_0032436.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of C-reactive protein in the blood circulation.

HP_0032437.label: reduced circulating c - reactive protein concecntration
HP_0032437.definition: An abnormal decrease of the C-reactive protein level in serum.

HP_0032438.label: platelet anisocytosis
HP_0032438.definition: Abnormally increased variability in the size of platelets.

HP_0032439.label: airborn particle hypersensitivity
HP_0032439.definition: An abnormally increased sensitivity to airborn particles. This can be diagnosed on the basis of the medical history, taking into account seasonality or a relationship to the concentration of airborn particles in the environment of the affected individual. Aerosol challenge is a gold standard of establishment of the symptom. There exist particle hypersensitivity (diesel exhaust, metals, inorganic material) vs. allergen (including pollen dander, etc) hypersensitivity. The responses are usually different and testing for allergen hypersensitivity is done in concert with serum IgE and or skin testing to the suspected allergen.

HP_0032443.label: past medical history
HP_0032443.definition: In a medical encounter, the physician generally will interview the patient about his or her current problem, and may perform additional testing. The past medical history (PMH) in contrast records information about the patient's medical, personal and family history that might be relevant to the presenting illness or to provide optimal clinical management. The PMH generally includes (if relevant) other major illnesses, hospitalizations, surgeries, injuries, allergies, gynecologic and obstetric history, family history, personal history including occupational history, alcohol and drug use, etc.
HP_0032443.UMLS synonyms: PMH - past medical history | past medical history unchanged | past medical history reviewed | Past medical history section | past medical history unobtainable | EMS past medical history | Medical History | no significant past medical history | Gathering of past medical history | Documentation of past medical history | RNAx assess past medical history | past medical history reported by patient | CMS - past medical - surgical history panel | past medical history reviewed with patient | past medical history reviewed by questionnaire | EMS past medical history:-:Pt:^Patient:Nar:NEMSIS | Past medical history+Level of function | CMS - past medical - surgical history panel:-:Pt:^Patient:Nar | Family Medical History | free text for past medical or surgical history | past medical history reviewed with no additions since (date) | Deprecated Medical social services treatment plan, Past medical history (narrative) | Past pregnancy history of medical termination of pregnancy | Medical history unknown

HP_0032444.label: status post organ transplantation
HP_0032444.definition: The affected individual has received an organ transplant previous to the current medical encounter.

HP_0032445.label: pulmonary cyst
HP_0032445.definition: A round circumscribed space within a lung that is surrounded by an epithelial or fibrous wall of variable thickness. A cyst usually has a thin and regular wall (less than 2 mm) and contains air, although some may contain fluid.
HP_0032445.UMLS synonyms: Lung cyst | Enucleation of pulmonary hydatid cyst | Echinococcosis, Pulmonary | Cyst of lung containing parasite ova | Acquired neonatal pulmonary cysts | Multiple lung cysts

HP_0032446.label: pulmonary bulla
HP_0032446.definition: Pulmonary bullae are rounded focal regions of emphysema with a thin wall which measure more than 1 cm in diameter. They are often subpleural in location and are typically larger in the apices. In some cases, bullae can be very large and result in compression of adjacent lung tissue. A giant bulla is arbitrarily defined as one that occupies at least one third of the volume of a hemithorax. When large, bullae can simulate pneumothorax. The most common cause is paraseptal emphysema but bullae may also be seen in association with centrilobular emphysema.
HP_0032446.UMLS synonyms: Bulla of lung | Pulmonary bullae rupture | Large pulmonary bullae | Pulmonary Bullae Causing Pneumothorax

HP_0032447.label: pulmonary bleb
HP_0032447.definition: A bleb is a small gas-containing space within the visceral pleura or in the subpleural lung, not larger than 1 cm in diameter. CT findings show a bleb as a thin-walled cystic air space contiguous with the pleura.

HP_0032448.label: achlorhydria
HP_0032448.definition: A condition in which production of hydrochloric acid in the stomach is absent.
HP_0032448.UMLS synonyms: Achlorhydria | achlorhydria; diarrhea | Achlorhydria in old age | secondary; achlorhydria (secondary to vagotomy) | Achlorhydric anemia | gastric fluid acid output: achlorhydria | Vipoma | Pancreatic Cholera

HP_0032449.label: abnormal dermoepidermal hemidesmosome morphology
HP_0032449.definition: An abnormal structure or appearance of hemidesmosomes, multiprotein complexes that facilitate the stable adhesion of basal epithelial cells to the underlying basement membrane.

HP_0032450.label: positive blood arsenic test
HP_0032450.definition: Detection of arsenic in the blood circulation.

HP_0032451.label: oral melanotic macule
HP_0032451.definition: Flat, distinct, discolored area of oral mucosal membrane less than 1 cm wide not associated with a change in the thickness or texture of the affected mucosal membrane. The lesions are small, solitary, well-circumscribed and often uniformly pigmented.
HP_0032451.UMLS synonyms: Melanotic macule of oral mucosa (reactive type)

HP_0032452.label: oral melanoacanthoma
HP_0032452.definition: Oral melanoacanthoma usually presents as an asymptomatic, ill-defined, rapidly enlarging, macular pigmentation. Although most lesions are heavily pigmented, the coloration may or may not be uniform. Any mucosal site may be affected, but buccal mucosal involvement is most common. Although typically solitary, rare patients may present with multifocal lesions.

HP_0032453.label: abnormal lip pigmentation
HP_0032453.definition: Abnormal coloring of the lip, whereby the lip discolored, blotchy, or darker or lighter than normal.

HP_0032454.label: labial melanotic macule
HP_0032454.definition: Flat, distinct, discolored area on the lip less than 1 cm wide not associated with a change in the thickness or texture.

HP_0032455.label: reduced granulocyte cd18 level
HP_0032455.definition: Reduced level of CD18 on the granulocyte surface. This feature can be assessed by flow cytometry.

HP_0032456.label: unlayered lissencephaly
HP_0032456.definition: A type of lissencephaly whereby upon neuropathological examination the cortical plate is severely disorganized with a festooned-like pattern and with neither lamination nor clear demarcation between white and grey matter.

HP_0032457.label: 2 - 3 - layered lissencephaly
HP_0032457.definition: Pachygyria-agyria spectrum whereby at neuropathological examination the cortical plate consists of a two-three layered organization made up of a molecular layer, a relatively thin wavy layer with a higher cellular density and a third layer with lower cellularity.

HP_0032458.label: narrowing of medullary canal
HP_0032458.definition: A reduction in diameter and volume of the central cavity of bone where red or yellow bone marrow is located.
HP_0032458.synonyms: medullary cavity obliteration | narrowing of bone marrow canal | narrowing of bone medullary canal | narrowing of the marrow cavity

HP_0032459.label: abnormal phosphoribosylpyrophosphate synthetase level
HP_0032459.definition: Any deviation from the normal level of the enzyme phosphoribosyl pyrophosphatesynthetase, which catalyzes the synthesis of PP-ribose-P from ATP and ribose-5-phosphate.

HP_0032460.label: decreased phosphoribosylpyrophosphate synthetase level
HP_0032460.definition: Abnormally reduced level of the enzyme phosphoribosyl pyrophosphatesynthetase, which catalyzes the synthesis of PP-ribose-P from ATP and ribose-5-phosphate.

HP_0032462.label: increased circulating palmitate level
HP_0032462.definition: An elevation beyond the normal concentration of palmitate (palmitic acid) in the blood circulation.

HP_0032463.label: reduced circulating fibronectin level
HP_0032463.definition: A reduction below the normal concentration of fibronectin the the blood circulation.

HP_0032464.label: ureteral hypoplasia
HP_0032464.synonyms: hypoplasia of the ureter | ureter hypoplasia

HP_0032465.label: bladder trabeculation
HP_0032465.definition: Muscular projections that protrude into the lumen of the bladder, criss-crossing the walls of the bladder on its inner surface.
HP_0032465.UMLS synonyms: Trabeculation of urinary bladder | diagnostic cystoscopy of bladder showed trabeculation

HP_0032466.label: aplasia of the olfactory bulb
HP_0032466.definition: Lack of formation (congenital absence) of the olfactory bulb.
HP_0032466.synonyms: aplastic olfactory bulb | olfactory bulb aplasia

HP_0032467.label: past obstetric history
HP_0032467.definition: Information about past pregnancies including gravidity (number of times a woman has been pregnant, regardless of the outcome), parity (total number of births), gestational age of births, and medical conditions related to past pregnancies.
HP_0032467.UMLS synonyms: Review health history, including prenatal and obstetrical history, developmental history, and past and present health status related to confirmed or suspected genetic risk factors | Review complete health history, including prenatal and obstetrical history, developmental history, and past and present health status related to confirmed or suspected genetic risk factors

HP_0032468.label: history of stillbirth
HP_0032468.definition: One or more previous pregnancies resulted in stillbirth, defined as death of a fetus in the later stages of pregnancy (definitions in the literature vary, with cut-offs ranging from 20 to 28 weeks gestation).
HP_0032468.UMLS synonyms: Past pregnancy history of stillbirth | Family history of stillbirth | Antenatal care: history of stillbirth | Supervision of pregnancy with history of stillbirth | visit for: prenatal exam with history of stillbirth | Supervision of pregnancy with history of stillbirth or neonatal death | Stillbirth of immature male (500-999 gms.) | Stillbirth of immature female (500-999 gms.) | Stillbirth of premature female (1000-2499 gms.) | Stillbirth of premature male (1000-2499 gms.) | Stillbirth of mature male (2500 gms. or more) | Stillbirth of mature female (2500 gms. or more) | Stillbirth of immature fetus, sex undetermined (500-999 gms.) | number of previous pregnancies with stillbirths (#___)

HP_0032469.label: anti - asialoglycoprotein receptor antibody positivity
HP_0032469.definition: Presence of autoantibodies against the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) in the blood circulation.

HP_0032470.label: monilethrix
HP_0032470.definition: The hair shaft has a beaded appearance due to the presence of elliptical nodes that have the diameter of normal hair and are medullated, regularly separated by internodes that are narrow, devoid of medulla and are the site of fracture.
HP_0032470.UMLS synonyms: Monilethrix | HYPOTRICHOSIS 6 | Menkes Kinky Hair Syndrome | KRT86 gene | KRT86 wt Allele | KRT86 protein, human

HP_0032471.label: focal polymicrogyria
HP_0032471.definition: Polymicrogyria affecting one or multiple small areas of the cerebral cortex.

HP_0032472.label: abnormal urine urobilinogen level
HP_0032472.definition: An abnormal concentration of urobilinogen in the urine.

HP_0032473.label: decreased urine urobilinogen
HP_0032473.definition: An abnormally reduced concentration of urobilinogen in the urine.

HP_0032476.label: abnormal circulating vitamin b6 concentration
HP_0032476.definition: An abnormal concentration of vitamin B6 in the blood circulation.

HP_0032477.label: elevated circulating vitamin b6 concentration
HP_0032477.definition: An abnormally increased concentration of vitamin B6 in the blood circulation.

HP_0032478.label: lateral spinal meningocele
HP_0032478.definition: Protrusion of the arachnoid and dura through spinal foramina.

HP_0032479.label: preimplantation lethality
HP_0032479.definition: It is estimated that about 40-70 percent of human embryos produced in vitro fertilization (IVF) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) are viable embryos, whereas others arrest at different early stages of development. The phenotype of preimplantation lethality is inferred if IVF and ICSI cycles fail because all of an individual's embryos are arrested at early stages of development.
HP_0032479.UMLS synonyms: OOCYTE/ZYGOTE/EMBRYO MATURATION ARREST 15 | OOCYTE/ZYGOTE/EMBRYO MATURATION ARREST 16

HP_0032480.label: beta - aminoisobutyric aciduria
HP_0032480.definition: An increased amount of beta-aminoisobutyric acid in the urine. Beta-aminoisobutyric acid is a non-protein amino acid originating from the catabolism of thymine and valine.

HP_0032481.label: abnormal pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
HP_0032481.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of circulating alpha polypeptide of glycoprotein hormones (NCBI Gene 1081).

HP_0032482.label: decreased pituitary glycoprotein hormone alpha subunit level
HP_0032482.definition: An reduced concentration of circulating alpha polypeptide of glycoprotein hormones (NCBI Gene 1081).
HP_0032482.synonyms: decreased pituitary glycoprotein alpha subunit level | decreased pituitary glycoprotein polypeptide alpha subunit level

HP_0032484.label: elevated fecal sodium
HP_0032484.definition: An elevated concentration of sodium in feces.

HP_0032485.label: abnormal fecal osmolality
HP_0032485.definition: Abnormal concentration of feces as assessed by the total number of solute particles per kilogram.

HP_0032486.label: elevated fecal osmolality
HP_0032486.definition: Abnormally high concentration of feces as assessed by the total number of solute particles per kilogram.

HP_0032487.label: reduced fecal osmolality
HP_0032487.definition: Abnormally low concentration of feces as assessed by the total number of solute particles per kilogram.

HP_0032488.label: abnormal fecal ph
HP_0032488.definition: Any deviation from the normal pH of feces. The pH reflects the acidity or alkalinity of a solution on a logarithmic scale on which 7 is neutral, whereby lower values are more acid and higher values more alkaline.

HP_0032489.label: elevated fecal ph
HP_0032489.definition: Abnormally high fecal pH, i.e., abnormal alkalinity of feces.
HP_0032489.synonyms: elevated faecal ph | stool ph high

HP_0032490.label: decreased fecal ph
HP_0032490.definition: Abnormally low fecal pH, i.e., abnormal acidity of feces.
HP_0032490.synonyms: decreased faecal ph | stool ph low

HP_0032491.label: increased circulating argininosuccinic acid
HP_0032491.definition: An increased level of the non-proteinogenic amino acid argininosuccinic acid in the blood circulation.

HP_0032492.label: anti - myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody positivity
HP_0032492.definition: Presence of antibodies in the serum that react against myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein.

HP_0032493.label: increased circulating trypsinogen
HP_0032493.definition: An abnormally high concentration of trypsinogen in the blood circulation.

HP_0032495.label: abnormal terminal : vellus ratio
HP_0032495.definition: A deviation from the normal proportion of terminal to vellus hairs.

HP_0032496.label: elevated terminal : vellus ratio
HP_0032496.definition: An increased proportion of terminal hairs compared to vellus hairs.

HP_0032497.label: reduced terminal : vellus ratio
HP_0032497.definition: A terminal:vellus ratio under 4:1 is characteristic of androgenetic alopecia.

HP_0032499.label: giant neutrophil granules
HP_0032499.definition: The presence of abnormally large granules in neutrophils. This finding can be appreciated on a peripheral blood smear. The finding is characteristic of Chediak Higashi syndrome. The giant granules are derived from azurophil granules, whereas peroxidase-negative granules are not involved in their formation.

HP_0032500.label: exacerbated by tobacco use
HP_0032500.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by smoking tobacco products.
HP_0032500.synonyms: aggravated by tobacco use | exacerbated by smoking | smoking or tobacco use exacerbates symptoms

HP_0032501.label: exacerbated by contraceptive medication exposure
HP_0032501.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by taking contraceptive medication.

HP_0032502.label: exacerbated by barbiturate exposure
HP_0032502.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by taking barbituates.

HP_0032503.label: ameliorated by ethanol ingestion
HP_0032503.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by drinking alcohol (ethanol).

HP_0032504.label: lhermitte 's sign
HP_0032504.definition: An electric shock-like sensation that occurs on flexion of the neck. This sensation radiates down the spine, often into the legs, arms, and sometimes to the trunk.
HP_0032504.UMLS synonyms: Barber's chair sign | Barber's chair sign positive

HP_0032505.label: hydrophobia
HP_0032505.definition: The word hydrophobia has been used to describe the avoidance of drinking in the presence of hydrophobic spasms that can be observed in human rabies (described as a blockage in the throat with worsening of dyspnea). However, rarely, the same word has been used to describe panic reactions observed in a patient when offered a glass of water. This term does not refer to the latter meaning.
HP_0032505.UMLS synonyms: Hydrophobia | Rabies (disorder) | Rabies - hydrophobia | Paralytic hydrophobia | Rabies vaccination

HP_0032506.label: alien limb phenomenon
HP_0032506.definition: Alien limb phenomenon refers to involuntary motor activity of a limb in conjunction with the feeling of estrangement from that limb.
HP_0032506.UMLS synonyms: Alien Limb Phenomenon | Unusual aura symptoms include alien limb phenomenon, diplopia, apraxia, dysarthria, impaired hearing, vertigo

HP_0032507.label: labiomental fasciculations
HP_0032507.definition: Fasciculations affecting the tongue muscle and the musculature of the chin.

HP_0032508.label: polyembolokoilamania
HP_0032508.definition: Habitual insertion of foreign bodies into bodily orifices.
HP_0032508.UMLS synonyms: Polyembolokoilamania (insertion of foreign bodies into body orifices)

HP_0032509.label: onychotillomania
HP_0032509.definition: Onychotillomania is characterized by the compulsive or irresistible urge in patients to pick at, pull off, or harmfully bite or chew their nails.

HP_0032510.label: tendon pain
HP_0032510.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) localized to a tendon.
HP_0032510.UMLS synonyms: Tenalgia | Achilles tendon pain | tendon graft; pain | Pain or swelling of tendon, insertion of tendon, or bursa | complications; prosthesis, orthopedic, muscle and tendon, pain | pain of right tibialis posterior tendon against resistance elicited by motion | pain of left posterior tibialis tendon elicited by motion | pain of right posterior tibialis tendon elicited by motion | pain of insertion of left Achilles tendon elicited by motion | pain of midsubstance of left Achilles tendon elicited by motion | pain of midsubstance of right Achilles tendon elicited by motion | pain of insertion of right Achilles tendon elicited by motion | pain of insertion of left tibialis posterior tendon elicited by motion | pain of musculotendinous junction of left Achilles tendon elicited by motion | pain of left peroneus longus tendon below malleolus elicited by motion | pain of left tibialis posterior tendon above malleolus elicited by motion | pain along course of left tibialis posterior tendon elicited by motion | pain of left peroneus brevis tendon at malleolus elicited by motion | pain of left peroneus longus tendon at malleolus elicited by motion | pain of left peroneus brevis tendon above malleolus elicited by motion | pain of left peroneus longus tendon above malleolus elicited by motion | pain at malleolus of left tibialis posterior tendon elicited by motion | pain of left tibialis posterior tendon below malleolus elicited by motion | pain of left tibialis posterior tendon against resistance elicited by motion | pain of left peroneus brevis tendon below malleolus elicited by motion

HP_0032511.label: superiorly positioned umbilicus
HP_0032511.definition: The position of the umbilicus (belly button) is abnormally high (superior).

HP_0032513.label: four - vessel umbilical cord
HP_0032513.definition: Four-vessel umbilical cord containing two arteries and two veins.

HP_0032514.label: supernumerary lacrimal punctum
HP_0032514.definition: A congenital developmental anomaly characterized by the presence of an additional lacrimal punctum in an eyelid.
HP_0032514.synonyms: accessory puncta | double lacrimal puncta | double punctum | lacrimal punctum , duplication | punctum reduplication | supernumerary punctum

HP_0032515.label: deep dermatophytosis
HP_0032515.definition: A type of invasive dermatophyte infection of the deep dermis characterized by extensive dermal infiltration by fungal elements.

HP_0032516.label: invasive dermatophyte infection
HP_0032516.definition: Infection that extends deeply into the dermis by dermatophytes, fungi that typically cause different types of superficial infection (tinea) or skin, hair, or nails.

HP_0032517.label: majocchi 's granuloma
HP_0032517.definition: Majocchi's granuloma (MG) is an inflammatory and granulomatous, dermatophytic infection characterized by a granulomatous inflammation around the hair follicle. Histopathologically, MG demonstrates a nodular perifollicular granulomatous infiltrate of lymphoid cells, macrophages, epithelioid cells, multinucleated giant cells, and neutrophils. Unlike superficial dermatophytoses, fungal hyphae and spores can be detected not only on the surface of the epidermis but also within or around the hair follicles.

HP_0032518.label: disseminated dermatophytosis
HP_0032518.definition: A type of invasive dermatophyte infection characterized by vascular involvement and dissemination to other organs.
HP_0032518.UMLS synonyms: Disseminated dermatophytosis | Disseminated dermatophytosis due to immunodeficiency | Deep seated dermatophytosis

HP_0032519.label: increased burr cell count
HP_0032519.definition: Burr cells, also known as echinocytes, have a speculated border over the entire cell surface. Burr cells are commonly found in both end-stage renal disease and liver disease. Small numbers of Burr cells are commonly found in healthy individuals.

HP_0032520.label: masseter muscular weakness
HP_0032520.definition: Reduced strength of the masseter muscle, whose primary function is to elevate the mandible and thereby raise the mandible towards the maxilla, closing the jaw.

HP_0032521.label: self hugging
HP_0032521.definition: Involuntary, tic-like movements consisted of crossing both arms across the chest and tensing the body or clasping the hands and squeezing the arms to the sides. The movements last a few seconds and may occur in series or flurries, generally accompanied by facial grimacing and occasional grunting.
HP_0032521.UMLS synonyms: Identify sexual behaviors that are unacceptable given particular setting and population (e.g., inappropriate remarks in public places, inappropriate statements to people they know; unwanted advances; touches, hugs, or kisses another more than appropriate; attempts to have sexual intercourse with others; exposes self or masturbates in public)

HP_0032522.label: ameliorated by immunosuppresion
HP_0032522.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with immunosuppresive medication.

HP_0032523.label: tendon thickening
HP_0032523.definition: An abnormal increase in the thickness (diameter) of a tendon.

HP_0032524.label: long thumb
HP_0032524.definition: Length of the thumb is greater than normal.

HP_0032525.label: exacerbated by acetylcholinesterase inhibitor exposure
HP_0032525.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor such as tensilon (edrophonium) or pyridostigmine (Mestinon).

HP_0032526.label: ameliorated by acetylcholinesterase inhibitor
HP_0032526.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor such as mestinon or tensilon.

HP_0032527.definition: The position of the umbilicus (belly button) is abnormally low (inferior).
HP_0032527.synonyms: low set umbilicus | low - set umbilicus

HP_0032528.label: elevated urinary 4 - hydroxybutyric acid
HP_0032528.definition: An increased amount of 4-hydroxybutyric acid in the urine.

HP_0032530.definition: Reduced level of succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH).

HP_0032531.label: elevated csf gamma - aminobutyric acid concentration
HP_0032531.synonyms: gamma - aminobutyric acid ( gaba ) high in csf

HP_0032532.definition: Abnormally increased level of 4-hydroxybutyric acid in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

HP_0032533.label: elevated circulating acetone concentration
HP_0032533.definition: An increased level of acetone in the blood circulation. Acetone is one of the predominant ketone bodies.

HP_0032534.label: exacerbated by methylxanthine ingestion
HP_0032534.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by ingestion of food containing a methylxanthine compound (for instance, coffee, caffeine, chocolate).

HP_0032535.definition: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in the neck.

HP_0032536.definition: An abnormally elevated number of lymph nodes in an anatomical region.

HP_0032537.definition: A delay in healing of a fracture past the expected duration.

HP_0032538.label: pretibial dimple
HP_0032538.definition: A groove or crease on the shins (pretibial, i.e., over the shin bone). Pretibial creases may be obvious at birth and may range from 3 cm to over 15 cm in length and lengthen as the limb grows. They appear as an elongated dimple because of the attachment of skin to underlying tissue (e.g., to the tibia). The dimple or crease grows in proportion to the growth of the leg.

HP_0032539.label: joint extensor surface localization
HP_0032539.definition: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in extensor surface of the joint. The extensor surface refers to the skin on the opposite side of a joint.

HP_0032540.label: joint flexor surface localization
HP_0032540.definition: Applies to an abnormality that is situated in flexor surface of the joint. The flexor surface refers to the skin that touches when a joint is bent (flexed).

HP_0032541.label: knuckle pad
HP_0032541.definition: Knuckle pads are benign fibrofatty subcutaneous pads located over the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints that can be mistaken for arthritis. Rarely they affect the dorsal aspect of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints. Clinically they are painless and often affect both hands in an asymmetrical pattern.
HP_0032541.synonyms: knuckle pads on dorsal aspect of finger joints
HP_0032541.UMLS synonyms: Knuckle pads | Knuckle pad of left hand | Bilateral knuckle pad of hands | Knuckle pad of right hand | Prominent knuckle pads | Knuckle pads, leuconychia and sensorineural deafness | Palmoplantar Keratoderma, Epidermolytic, with Knuckle Pads | Camptodactyly 1 | Knuckle pads on dorsal finger and toe joints | Knuckle Pads, Leukonychia, and Sensorineural Deafness Gene Anomaly Detection Reagents | Knuckle Pads, Deafness, and Leukonychia Syndrome Gene Anomaly Detection Reagents | PLACK syndrome

HP_0032542.label: exacerbated by pregnancy
HP_0032542.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by being pregnant.
HP_0032542.UMLS synonyms: Generalized enlargement of gingiva exacerbated by pregnancy

HP_0032543.label: lithoptysis
HP_0032543.definition: Expectoration (coughing up) of a broncholith. Broncholithiasis is defined as the presence of calculi in the tracheobronchial tree. It is a rare disease but can be characterized by clinical and radiological findings of a calcified lymph node eroding bronchial wall and opening into the bronchial lumen.

HP_0032544.label: predominant small joint localization
HP_0032544.definition: Applies to an abnormality that mainly affects the small joints, including fingers, toes, interphalangeal, metacarpophalangeal, metatarsophalangeal, wrists, ankles, vertebrae, and neck.

HP_0032545.label: abdominal rigidity
HP_0032545.definition: Involuntary tightening of the abdominal musculature that occurs in response to touching the abdomen to avoid pain. Rigidity can occur in the presence of abdominal inflammation and usually involves only the inflamed area.
HP_0032545.UMLS synonyms: Abdominal rigidity | Generalized abdominal rigidity | Abdominal rigidity absent | Abdominal rigidity of periumbilical region | abdominal rigidity in epigastric region | severe; abdominal pain, abdominal rigidity | Abdominal rigidity of left lower quadrant | Abdominal rigidity of left upper quadrant | Abdominal rigidity of right lower quadrant | Abdominal rigidity of right upper quadrant | Board-like abdominal rigidity | Abdominal rigidity of epigastrium | Severe abdominal pain (generalized) (with abdominal rigidity) | Abdominal rigidity, other specified site

HP_0032546.label: abdominal guarding
HP_0032546.definition: A voluntary contraction of the abdominal wall musculature to avoid pain.
HP_0032546.UMLS synonyms: Abdominal guarding (finding) | Abdominal voluntary guarding | Abdominal involuntary guarding | No abdominal guarding on palpation | checking for abdominal pain and guarding | Protective cup

HP_0032547.label: low intraocular pressure
HP_0032547.definition: An abnormal decrease of the pressure within the eye.

HP_0032549.label: persistent asymmetrical tonic neck reflex
HP_0032549.definition: Persistence beyond the normal age (roughly the first half of the first year of life) of the asymmetric tonic neck reflex (ATNR), which is an easily elicited primitive reflex in the immediate newborn period. The ATNR refers to the phenomenon whereby when the face of an infant is turned to one side, the ipsilateral arm and leg extend and the contralateral arm and leg flex. This posture has been compared to a typical posture of fencers.
HP_0032549.synonyms: persistent fencer 's reflex | tonic neck reflex asymmetrical and persistent

HP_0032550.label: howell - jolly bodies
HP_0032550.definition: Howell-Jolly bodies are small, intra-erythrocytic remnants of erythrocyte nuclei. These inclusions are solitary in each erythrocyte and strongly basophilic. These are often confused with overlying platelets, but can be distinguished by the presence of a halo around overlying platelets.
HP_0032550.UMLS synonyms: Howell-Jolly Bodies | Howell Jolly Bodies Test | Howell-Jolly bodies present | Howell-Jolly Body Measurement | Red blood cell Howell-Jolly bodies present | Howell-Jolly bodies seen in peripheral blood smear | Howell-Jolly bodies | Blood | Hematology and Cell counts | Howell-Jolly bodies:PrThr:Pt:Bld:Ord:Microscopy.light

HP_0032551.label: hemorrhoids
HP_0032551.definition: Enlarged, bulging blood vessels in and around the anus often associated with rectal bleeding, itching, and pain.
HP_0032551.UMLS synonyms: Hemorrhoids | Thrombosed hemorrhoids | Internal hemorrhoids | External hemorrhoids (disorder) | Prolapsed hemorrhoids | Strangulated hemorrhoids | Hemorrhoids in pregnancy | Ulcerated hemorrhoids | Hemorrhoids in puerperium | Hemorrhoids, CTCAE_3 | Hemorrhoids, CTCAE_5 | Destruction of hemorrhoids by sclerotherapy | Hemorrhoids necrosis | Hemorrhoids aggravated | Other hemorrhoids | Unspecified hemorrhoids | Thrombosed external hemorrhoids | Destruction of hemorrhoids by cryotherapy | hemorrhoids; complicating pregnancy | Thrombosed internal hemorrhoids | Hemorrhoids without complication | external hemorrhoids by exam | Bleeding internal hemorrhoids | Bleeding external hemorrhoids | Strangulated internal hemorrhoids

HP_0032552.label: abnormal pulse
HP_0032552.definition: An anomaly of the rhythmic throbbing of an artery that reflects the widening of the artery as blood flows through it and is caused by successive contractions of the heart.

HP_0032553.label: weak pulse
HP_0032553.definition: A diminution in the amplitude (strength) of the pulse such that the examiner has difficulty feeling the pulse.

HP_0032554.label: absent pulse
HP_0032554.definition: The pulsation of an artery where the pulse is taken (e.g. the radial artery at the wrist) cannot be detected on physical examination.
