HP_0034820.label: koeppe nodules
HP_0034820.definition: A type of iris nodule consisting of inflammatory cell precipitates which lie at the pupillary margin.
HP_0034820.UMLS synonyms: Iris-Koeppe nodule | Koeppe's nodule of left iris | Koeppe's nodule of right iris | Koeppe's nodule of both irises

HP_0034821.label: bussaca nodules
HP_0034821.definition: A type of iris nodule consisting of inflammatory cell precipitates which lie on the iris surface.

HP_0034823.label: decreased csf copper concentration
HP_0034823.definition: Concentration of copper in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) below the lower limit of normal.

HP_0034824.label: diffuse pulmonary lymphoid hyperplasia
HP_0034824.definition: Diffuse lymphoid hyperplasia (DLH) describes the pathological entity that lies between follicular bronchiolitis and lymphocytic interstitial pneumonia (LIP). It is pathologically characterized by a diffuse peribronchiolar proliferation of hyperplastic lymphoid follicles (BALT), extended along the lymphatics to involve the interlobular septa and pleura. Unlike LIP, DHL does not show uniform involvement of the alveolar septa.

HP_0034825.label: ameliorated by steroid medication
HP_0034825.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by treatment with a steroid medication such as prednisone.

HP_0034826.label: triggered by medication exposure
HP_0034826.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by administration of a medication.

HP_0034827.label: triggered by levothyroxin exposure
HP_0034827.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by administration of levothyroxin (thyroid hormone).

HP_0034828.label: reduced muscle laminin alpha - 2 chain staining
HP_0034828.definition: A decreased amount of laminin alpha-2 chain in muscle tissue. This feature can be shown by immunohistochemistry or Western blotting of muscle tissue.

HP_0034829.label: adrenal cortical sclerosis
HP_0034829.definition: Abnormal thickening of of the outer layer (cortex) of the adrenal gland due to fibrosis.

HP_0034830.label: reduced hepatic fructose - 1,6 - phosphate aldolase activity
HP_0034830.definition: Concentration or activity of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase in liver tissue below the lower limit of normal.

HP_0034831.label: pancreatic hamartoma
HP_0034831.definition: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the pancreas.

HP_0034832.label: liver angiomyolipoma
HP_0034832.definition: A benign liver neoplasm composed of fat, vascular, and smooth muscle elements.
HP_0034832.UMLS synonyms: Hepatic Angiomyolipoma | biopsy of liver angiomyolipoma

HP_0034833.label: cardiac lipoma
HP_0034833.definition: A lipoma that is located within a the heart.

HP_0034834.label: peripheral nerve polyglucosan inclusion bodies
HP_0034834.definition: Accumulation of a poorly branched and poorly spherical amylopectin-like glycogen (polyglucosan) in peripheral nerve fibers.

HP_0034835.label: cardiac polyglucosan accumulation
HP_0034835.definition: Accumulation of a poorly branched and poorly spherical amylopectin-like glycogen (polyglucosan) in myocardial tissue.

HP_0034836.label: cystic nephroma
HP_0034836.definition: A benign cystic neoplasm of the kidney.
HP_0034836.synonyms: bbenign multilocular cystic nephroma | multicystic nephroma | multilocular cystic renal tumor | multilocular cystic renal tumour | polycystic nephroblastoma
HP_0034836.UMLS synonyms: Benign cystic nephroma | Multilocular cystic nephroma | Childhood Cystic Nephroma | malignant cystic nephroma of ureter | malignant cystic nephroma of renal pelvis | Cystic Partially Differentiated Nephroblastoma

HP_0034837.label: absent dermal elastic fibers
HP_0034837.definition: Elastic fibers not demonstrable in skin biopsy.

HP_0034838.label: cleavage at junction of stratum corneum and stratum granulosum
HP_0034838.definition: Splitting of the skin (cell-cell adhesion of keratinocytes) localized to the interface between the stratum corneum and stratum granulosum layers of the epidermis.

HP_0034839.label: lymphoid hyperplasia
HP_0034839.definition: An abnormal bone marrow finding characterized by many poorly circumscribed and occasionally confluent lymphoid nodules. The nodules contain small and uniform lymphocytes with rounded nuclei, clumped chromatin, and without prominent nucleoli.

HP_0034840.label: absence of epidermal lamellar bodies
HP_0034840.definition: Lack of lamellar bodies (LBs) inthe epidermis. LBs are specialized organelles that contain pro-barrier lipids imparting a fully lamellar internal structure, but also other cargoes such as enzymes (lipid metabolizing and proteolytic), enzyme inhibitors, and antimicrobial peptides.

HP_0034841.label: gastrointestinal granulomatosis
HP_0034841.definition: The presence of multiple granulomas in the gastrointestinal tract (Pylorus, esophagus, jejunum, ileum, cecum, rectum, perirectal area, esophagus) as based on pathological examination. Granulomas are small 0.5 to 2 mm collections of modified macrophages called epithelioid cells usually surrounded by lymphocytes.

HP_0034842.label: enlarged sperm head vacuole
HP_0034842.definition: Increased size of sperm vacuoles, which are surface concavities typically located at the the tip or middle area of sperm heads. According to the WHO Laboratory Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human Semen, sperm head vacuoles are considered abnormal when exceeding 20% of the cross-sectional area of the head. Vacuoles are found in almost all samples with normal sperm morphology; this term applies if the proportion of sperm with abnormally large vacuoles is above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0034843.label: ureteral hamartoma
HP_0034843.definition: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the ureter.

HP_0034844.label: fetal methimazole exposure
HP_0034844.definition: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to methimazole.
HP_0034844.synonyms: maternal methimazole exposure | methimazole exposure during gestation

HP_0034845.label: fetal procarbazine exposure
HP_0034845.definition: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to procarbazine.
HP_0034845.synonyms: maternal procarbazine exposure | procarbazine exposure during gestation

HP_0034846.label: fetal fluorouracil exposure
HP_0034846.definition: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to fluorouracil.
HP_0034846.synonyms: fluorouracil exposure during gestation | maternal fluorouracil exposure

HP_0034847.label: fetal cytarabine exposure
HP_0034847.definition: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to cytarabine.
HP_0034847.synonyms: cytarabine exposure during gestation | maternal cytarabine exposure

HP_0034848.label: fetal tetracycline exposure
HP_0034848.definition: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to tetracycline.
HP_0034848.synonyms: maternal tetracycline exposure | tetracycline exposure during gestation

HP_0034958.definition: Insertion of the neck and midpiece into the head of a spermatozoon on an axis that diverges from the midline axis of the spermatozoon head. This term applies if the proportion of spermatozoa with this defect is above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0034959.label: bent sperm neck
HP_0034959.definition: Sharply angled insertion of the neck and midpiece into the head of a spermatozoon. This term applies if the proportion of spermatozoa with this feature is above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0034960.label: elevated urine 3,6 - epoxydicarboxylic acid level
HP_0034960.definition: The concentration of 3,6-epoxydicarboxylic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0034961.label: gallbladder biliary sludging
HP_0034961.definition: Presence of biliary sludge (a mixture of particulate solids that have precipitated from bile) in the gallbladder. Such sediment consists of cholesterol crystals, calcium bilirubinate pigment, and other calcium salts. Sludge is usually detected on transabdominal ultrasonography.

HP_0034962.label: exacerbated by amiodarone exposure
HP_0034962.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with amiodarone.

HP_0034963.label: ureteral mass
HP_0034963.definition: A swelling or enlargment localized to the ureter. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
HP_0034963.UMLS synonyms: computed tomography of abdomen: ureteral mass | ultrasound of kidney: mass of ureter | ultrasound of kidney: mass of left ureter | ultrasound of kidney: mass of right ureter

HP_0034964.label: wide cavum septum pellucidum
HP_0034964.definition: Width of the cavum septum pellucidum above the upper limit of normal, which is defined as a separation of greater than one cm of the leaves of the cavum septum pellucidum.

HP_0034965.label: hypoplastic trochlear nerve
HP_0034965.definition: Underdevelopment of the trochlear nerve, which is the fourth cranial nerve and one of the ocular motor nerves that controls eye movement.

HP_0034966.label: thymic cyst
HP_0034966.definition: A closed sac of tissue (cyst) located in the thymus. Thymic cysts are a rare, benign anomaly, are usually asymptomatic, and mostly occur in the anterior mediastinum .
HP_0034966.UMLS synonyms: Thymic Cyst | Multilocular Thymic Cyst | THYMIC CYST BENIGN | neoplasm of uncertain behavior of anterior thymic cyst

HP_0034967.label: uterine cyst
HP_0034967.definition: A closed sack of tissue (cyst) located in the uterus.

HP_0034968.label: urinary bladder mass
HP_0034968.definition: A swelling or enlargment localized to the urinary bladder. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.
HP_0034968.UMLS synonyms: Mass of urinary bladder | Mass of urinary bladder neck | Level V surgical pathology with gross and microscopic examination | Level IV surgical pathology with gross and microscopic examination

HP_0034969.label: endosteal scalloping
HP_0034969.definition: A series of indentations or erosions on a normally smooth margin of the inner layer of the cortex (i.e. the endosteum) of bones.

HP_0034970.label: urinary bladder hamartoma
HP_0034970.definition: A benign (noncancerous) tumorlike malformation made up of an abnormal mixture of cells and tissues that originates in the urinary bladder.

HP_0034971.label: peritoneal mass
HP_0034971.definition: A swelling or enlargment localized to the peritoneal cavity. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

HP_0034972.label: fallopian tube mass
HP_0034972.definition: A swelling or enlargment localized to the Fallopian tube. The word mass is usually used at an early stage of the diagnostic workup before the precise nature of the swelling has been determined.

HP_0034973.label: aplasia of the pyramids of the medulla oblongata
HP_0034973.definition: Congenital absence of the pyramids, that is, of the paired structures located at the medial aspect of the ventral medulla that flank the anterior median fissure.

HP_0034974.label: bathrocephaly
HP_0034974.definition: A deformity of the posterior skull with bulging of the midportion of the occipital bone that is often associated with a benign variant of the mendosal suture.

HP_0034975.label: occipital horn
HP_0034975.definition: Downward pointing exostoses of the occipital bone situated in the tendinous insertions of the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.

HP_0034976.label: absent pituitary stalk
HP_0034976.definition: A developmental defect characterized by failure to develop of the pituitary stalk. The pituitary stalk, also known as the infundibulum or infundibular stalk, is the connection between the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland.

HP_0034977.label: abnormal pituitary stalk morphology
HP_0034977.definition: A structural anomaly of the pituitary stalk, also known as the infundibulum or infundibular stalk, is the connection between the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland.

HP_0034978.label: interrupted pituitary stalk
HP_0034978.definition: A developmental defect characterized by a discontinuity of the pituitary stalk. The pituitary stalk, also known as the infundibulum or infundibular stalk, is the connection between the hypothalamus and the pituitary gland.

HP_0034979.label: facial synkinesis
HP_0034979.definition: Unintentional movement in one area of the face produced during intentional movement of another area of the face.

HP_0034980.label: synkinesis
HP_0034980.definition: Unintentional movement in one area of the body produced during intentional movement of another area of the body.

HP_0034982.label: perianal anethesia
HP_0034982.definition: Loss of sensation to the area of buttocks, perianal space and thighs.

HP_0034983.label: phenylephrine does not induce blanching of eye redness
HP_0034983.definition: Instillation of 2.5% phenylephrine drops into the eye does not induce blanching of eye redness. Failure to blanch suggests redness caused by scleral vessel engorgement (e.g., scleritis) or extravascular cause (e.g., hemorrhage), not episcleritis or conjunctivitis.

HP_0034984.label: fetal alcohol exposure
HP_0034984.definition: A history of exposure during pregnancy of the mother of a fetus or child to ethanol (alcohol).

HP_0034985.label: reduced cellular cobalamin uptake
HP_0034985.definition: Diminished ability of cells to transport cobalamine from the extracellular space to the cytoplasm.

HP_0034986.label: focal necrotic brainstem lesion
HP_0034986.definition: A localized area of cell death, often accompanied by infiltration of inflammatory cells, in the brainstem.

HP_0034987.label: focal necrotic optic nerve lesion
HP_0034987.definition: A localized area of cell death, often accompanied by infiltration of inflammatory cells, in the optic nerve.

HP_0034988.label: focal necrotic thalamus lesion
HP_0034988.definition: A localized area of cell death, often accompanied by infiltration of inflammatory cells, in the thalamus.

HP_0034989.label: interstitial dermal edema
HP_0034989.definition: Accumulation of fluid in the interstitial spaces of the skin. This finding can be appreciated my microscopic examination of a skin biopsy.

HP_0034990.label: shoulder abduction contracture
HP_0034990.UMLS synonyms: Abduction contracture-shoulder | shoulder motion bilateral contracture abduction | contracture of left shoulder on abduction | contracture of right shoulder on abduction

HP_0034991.label: shoulder external rotation contracture
HP_0034991.definition: A type of shoulder contracture characterized by decreased internal rotation of shoulder, that is, by a chronic reduction in active and passive ability to internally rotate the humerus at the shoulder joint (if the arm is flexed at the elbow, Internal rotation of the shoulder rotates the forearm towards the center of the body).
HP_0034991.synonyms: external rotation contracture of the shoulder joint
HP_0034991.UMLS synonyms: External rotation contracture-shoulder | shoulder motion bilateral contracture external rotation | contracture of left shoulder on external rotation | contracture of right shoulder on external rotation

HP_0034992.label: thumb adduction contracture
HP_0034992.definition: A type of thumb contracture characterized by a chronic reduction in active and passive ability of the metacarpal-phalangeal and/or interphalangeal joints of the thumb to bring from medial side to neutral position, where the neutral position for the thumb is when the distal and proximal segments of the thumb joint are in linear alignment.
HP_0034992.UMLS synonyms: contracture of left thumb on adduction | contracture of right thumb on adduction | contracture of metacarpophalangeal joint of right thumb on adduction | contracture of metacarpophalangeal joint of left thumb on adduction

HP_0034995.label: reduced hepatic fructose - 1,6 - bisphosphatase activity
HP_0034995.definition: Activity of fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (EC 3.1.3.11) in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

HP_0034996.label: reduced hepatic carbamoylphosphate synthetase activity
HP_0034996.definition: Activity of carbamoylphosphate synthetase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

HP_0034997.label: reduced intraepidermal small nerve fiber density
HP_0034997.definition: Reduced number of small nerve fibers in the skin.

HP_0034998.label: femoral artery duplication
HP_0034998.definition: A developmental defect characterized by the presence of a supernumerary femoral artery.

HP_0034999.label: intracellular accumulation of collagen vii
HP_0034999.definition: Collagen VII is the major molecular constituent of anchoring fibrils in the skin. Collagen VII is synthesized as three identical pro-alpha1(VII) polypeptide chains, which are hydroxylated and glycosylated in a coordinated manner and then fold into triple-helical procollagen VII in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Mature collagen VII undergoes a multistep fibril polymerization process to form the anchoring fibrils. Mutant pro-alpha1(VII) polypeptide chains or procollagen VII molecules do not pass the ER quality control and are retained in the ER or designated for ubiquitin-proteasome degradation resulting in reduced amounts of collagen VII in the skin.

HP_0035000.label: reduced reticular lamina anchoring fibril density
HP_0035000.definition: Diminished amount of the anchoring fibrils in the basement membrane zone that normally attach the epithelium to the basement membrane.

HP_0035001.label: reduced lamina lucida anchoring filament density
HP_0035001.definition: Diminished amount of the anchoring filaments that normally bridge the lamina lucida and insert into the lamina densa in the cutaneous basement membrane zone.

HP_0035002.label: reduced epidermal keratin 5 protein expression
HP_0035002.definition: Amount of keratin 5 in the epidermis below the lower limit of normal. The findiong is typically ascertained by immunofluorescent microscopy.

HP_0035003.label: reduced epidermal keratin 14 protein expression
HP_0035003.definition: Amount of keratin 14 in the epidermis below the lower limit of normal. The findiong is typically ascertained by immunofluorescent microscopy.

HP_0035004.label: reduced epidermal keratin protein expression
HP_0035004.definition: Amount of one or more keratins in the epidermis below the lower limit of normal. The findiong is typically ascertained by immunofluorescent microscopy.

HP_0035005.label: reduced hepatic alanine - glyoxylate aminotransferase activity
HP_0035005.definition: Activity of alanine-glyoxylate aminotransferase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.

HP_0035006.label: hepatic sinusoidal dilatation
HP_0035006.definition: Presence of an increased amount of blood in the hepatic capillaries.

HP_0035007.label: thin spermatozoon midpiece
HP_0035007.definition: The cross-sectional size (diameter) of the midpiece of the spermatozoon is below the lower limit of normal. This term applies if the proportion of spermatozoa with this defect is above the upper limit of normal.
HP_0035007.UMLS synonyms: thin midpiece spermatozoa/100 spermatozoa in semen | Spermatozoa.thin midpiece/100 spermatozoa | Spermatozoa.thin midpiece/100 spermatozoa:NFr:Pt:Semen:Qn | Spermatozoa.thin midpiece/100 spermatozoa | Semen | Fertility testing

HP_0035008.label: thick spermatozoon midpiece insertion
HP_0035008.definition: Increased width of the midpiece of the spermatozoon. The midpiece is the structure that is located between the head and the flagella (tail) of the spermatozoon. This term applies if the width of the midpiece increases progressively from the flagella to the head and if the proportion of individual spermatozoa with this anomaly is above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0035009.label: shoulder adduction contracture
HP_0035009.definition: A type of shoulder contracture characterized by a chronic reduction in the active and passive ability to abduct the shoulder. This results in the shoulders being closer to midline. The affected individual is not able to position the shoulders away from the body.
HP_0035009.UMLS synonyms: Adduction contracture-shoulder | shoulder motion bilateral contracture adduction | contracture of left shoulder on adduction | contracture of right shoulder on adduction

HP_0035010.definition: Exposure to a substance that results from the performance of an employee's duties.

HP_0035011.definition: A history of exposure to silver that has occurred in relation to performance of job duties.

HP_0035012.label: abnormal femoral artery morphology
HP_0035012.definition: Any structural abnormality of the femoral artey, a large blood vessel that provides oxygenated blood to lower extremity structures and in part to the lower anterior abdominal wall.

HP_0035014.label: extrahepatic bile duct fibrosis
HP_0035014.definition: Accumulation of fibrous connective tissue (collagen) in the extrahepatic bile ducts.

HP_0035015.definition: Concentration of short-chain acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. HP_0035016.definition: Concentration of C4 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C4 acylcarnitines have a four-carbon acyl chain.

HP_0035017.definition: Concentration of medium-chain acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. HP_0035018.label: elevated circulating long - chain acylcarnitine concentration
HP_0035018.definition: Concentration of long-chain acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. HP_0035019.definition: Concentration of C5 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C5 acylcarnitines have a five-carbon acyl chain.

HP_0035021.label: elevated circulating c16 acylcarnitine concentration
HP_0035021.definition: Concentration of C16 acylcarnitines in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. C16 acylcarnitines have a sixteen-carbon acyl chain.

HP_0035022.label: elevated circulating very long - chain acylcarnitine concentration
HP_0035022.definition: Concentration of very long-chain acylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. HP_0035023.label: elevated circulating acetylcarnitine concentration
HP_0035023.definition: Concentration of acetylcarnitine (C2 acylcarnitine) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Acetylcarnitine has a two-carbon acyl chain.

HP_0035024.label: elevated circulating methylmalonylcarnitine concentration
HP_0035024.definition: Concentration of methylmalonylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0035027.definition: Concentration of methylglutarylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0035028.label: elevated circulating 3 - hydroxyisovalerylcarnitine concentration
HP_0035028.definition: Concentration of 3-hydroxyisovalerylcarnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0035029.definition: Concentration of 3-hydroxyhexanoylcarnitine (C6-OH) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0035030.definition: Concentration of carnitine in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0035031.label: elevated circulating tiglylcarnitine concentration
HP_0035031.definition: Concentration of tiglylcarnitine (C5:1) in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

HP_0035032.definition: Concentration of acetylcarnitine (C2 acylcarnitine) in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. Acetylcarnitine has a two-carbon acyl chain.

HP_0035033.label: reduced circulating octadecenoylcarnitine concentration
HP_0035033.definition: Concentration of octadecenoylcarnitine (C18:1 acylcarnitine) in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.

HP_0040148.label: cortical myoclonus
HP_0040148.definition: Cortical myoclonus mainly affects the distal upper limbs and face, which reflects the largest cortical representations of these body areas. It is often focal, but may be multifocal, bilateral or generalized, as a consequence of intracortical and transcallosal spreading of abnormal activity. It typically occurs on voluntary action and may affect speech and gait. Cortical myoclonic jerks are stimulus sensitive, typically to touch, but sensitivity to visual stimuli is also described. Most patients with cortical myoclonus have both positive myoclonus and NM, occurring either independently or together as a complex of the two kinds of myoclonus. If cortical myoclonus is prolonged and lasts for hours, days or weeks, it is called epilepsia partials continua and is considered to be a rare form of focal epileptic status. Focal cortical myoclonus almost always points to an underlining lesion of the sensori-motor cortex, which produces hyperexcitability (e.g. vascular, inflammatory or neoplastic).

HP_0040223.label: pulmonary hemorrhage
HP_0040223.definition: Pulmonary hemorrhage is a bleeding within the lungs. Older children and adults may spit blood or bloody sputum. Neonates, infants and young children usually do not spit up blood. Anemia, pulmonary infiltrates, increasingling bloody return on BAL and the presence of hemosiderin-laden macrophages in broncho-alveolar lavage (BAL) fluid or lung biopsy can diagnose lung bleeding. Alveolar macrophages contain phagocytosed red blood cells and stain positive for hemosiderin, a product of hemoglobin degradation, after about 48-72 hours following pulmonary hemorraghe. Previous or recurrent bleeding can thus be distinguished from fresh events. A differentiation into local or diffuse is of importance. Also differentiate if pulmonary hemorrhage is due to a primary lung disorder or a manifestation of a systemic disease.

HP_0100001.definition: Malignant mesothelioma is a form of cancer that originates from the cells of the mesothelium, a thin tissue layer surrounding the body's internal organs. HP_0100016.label: abnormal mesentery morphology
HP_0100016.definition: Folds of membranous tissue (peritoneum, mesothelium) attached to the wall of the abdomen and enclosing viscera. Examples include the mesentery for the small intestine; the transverse mesocolon, which attaches the transverse portion of the colon to the back wall of the abdomen; and the mesosigmoid, which enfolds the sigmoid portion of the colon. Cells of the same embryologic origin also surround the other organs of the body such as the lungs (pleura) or the heart (pericardium).

HP_0100245.label: desmoid tumors
HP_0100245.definition: Benign, slow-growing tumors without any metastatic potential. Despite their benign nature, they can damage nearby structures causing organ dysfunction. HP_0100247.label: recurrent singultus
HP_0100247.definition: A contraction of the diaphragm that repeats several times per minute. In humans, the abrupt rush of air into the lungs causes the epiglottis to close, creating a hic sound. Also known as synchronous diaphragmatic flutter (SDF), or singultus, from the Latin singult, the act of catching one's breath while sobbing. The hiccup is an involuntary action involving a reflex arc.

HP_0100248.label: hemiballismus
HP_0100248.definition: Hemiballismus is a rare movement disorder that is caused primarily by damage to various areas in the basal ganglia. Hemiballismus is usually characterized by involuntary flinging motions of the extremities. The movements are often violent and have wide amplitudes of motion. They are continuous and random and can involve proximal and/or distal muscles on one side of the body, while some cases even include the facial muscles. The more a patient is active, the more the movements increase. With relaxation comes a decrease in movements.

HP_0100279.label: ulcerative colitis
HP_0100279.definition: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that includes characteristic ulcers, or open sores, in the colon. The main symptom of active disease is usually constant diarrhea mixed with blood, of gradual onset and intermittent periods of exacerbated symptoms contrasting with periods that are relatively symptom-free. In contrast to Crohn's disease this special form of colitis begins in the distal parts of the rectum, spreads continually upwards and affects only mucose and submucose tissue of the colon.

HP_0100280.label: crohn 's disease
HP_0100280.definition: A chronic granulomatous inflammatory disease of the intestines that may affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus, causing a wide variety of symptoms. It primarily causes abdominal pain, diarrhea which may be bloody, vomiting, or weight loss, but may also cause complications outside of the gastrointestinal tract such as skin rashes, arthritis, inflammation of the eye, tiredness, and lack of concentration. Crohn's disease is thought to be an autoimmune disease, in which the body's immune system attacks the gastrointestinal tract, causing inflammation.

HP_0410144.label: abnormal circulating biotinidase concentration
HP_0410144.definition: An abnormality in the biotinidase level, an enzyme that releases biotin from biocytin, the product of biotin-dependent carboxylases degradation.

HP_0410145.label: decreased circulating biotinidase concentration
HP_0410145.definition: Concentration of biotinidase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. Biotidinase is an enzyme that releases biotin from biocytin, the product of biotin-dependent carboxylases degradation.

HP_0410146.label: elevated circulating biotinidase concentration
HP_0410146.definition: Concentration of biotinidase in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal. Biotidinase is an enzyme that releases biotin from biocytin, the product of biotin-dependent carboxylases degradation.

HP_0410147.label: eosinophilic infiltration in the stomach mucosa
HP_0410147.definition: Infiltration of eosinophils in the stomach mucosa, that is diagnosed by an upper endoscopy and microscopy that shows more than 20 eosinophils per high-power field in association with peripheral eosinophilia and the absence of secondary cause of eosinophilia.

HP_0410148.label: idiopathic anaphylaxis
HP_0410148.definition: A rare form of anaphylaxis for which triggers cannot be identified despite a detailed history and careful diagnostic assessment.

HP_0410149.label: drug - induced anaphylaxis
HP_0410149.definition: A form of anaphylaxis that is triggered by intake of drugs or medications.

HP_0410151.label: eosinophilic infiltration of the esophagus
HP_0410151.definition: Infiltration of numerous eosinophils (usually greater than 15 per high power field) into the squamous epithelium of the esophagus, and layering of eosinophils on the surface layer of the esophagus.
HP_0410151.synonyms: eosinophilic esophagitis | eosinophilic infiltration of the oesophagus

HP_0410152.label: eosinophilic microabscess formation in the esophagus
HP_0410152.definition: The formation of small localized collection of eosinophiles (an eosinophilic microabscess) in the esophagus. Usually clusters of greater than or equal to 4 eosinophils are seen, that appear as exudates or white spots or white plaques.
HP_0410152.synonyms: eosinophilic micro - abscess formation in the esophagus | eosinophilic micro - abscess formation in the oesophagus | eosinophilic microabscess formation in the oesophagus

HP_0410153.label: increased level of methylsuccinic acid in urine

HP_0410154.label: increased level of myristic acid in serum

HP_0410166.label: defective interstrand cross - link repair
HP_0410166.definition: A defect in the of the process of interstrand cross-link repair: removal of a DNA interstrand crosslink (a covalent attachment of DNA bases on opposite strands of the DNA) and restoration of the DNA. DNA interstrand crosslinks occur when both strands of duplex DNA are covalently tethered together (e.g. by an exogenous or endogenous agent), thus preventing the strand unwinding necessary for essential DNA functions such as transcription and replication.

HP_0410167.definition: Any abnormality of the chest muscles.

HP_0410209.definition: A reduced concentration of folic acid, which is also known as vitamin B9 in the cerebrospinal fluid.

HP_0410210.label: abnormal cord blood measurement

HP_0410219.label: hypoplasia of mandible relative to maxilla

HP_0410220.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against dairy proteins, including casein, alpha-lactalbumin, beta-lactoglobulin or bovine serum albumin contained in cow, sheep or goat milk and milk products.

HP_0410222.label: increased anti - seafood ige antibody level

HP_0410223.label: increased anti - dust mite ige antibody level

HP_0410224.label: increased anti - bacteria ige antibody level
HP_0410224.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against bacteria.

HP_0410228.label: increased anti - plant based food allergen ige antibody level

HP_0410229.label: increased anti - gluten ige antibody level
HP_0410229.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye.

HP_0410230.label: increased anti - nut food product ige antibody level
HP_0410230.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against nut food products such as peanuts or tree nuts, such as hazelnuts, walnuts, cashews, and almonds.

HP_0410231.label: increased anti - egg ige antibody level
HP_0410231.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against eggs, including egg whites, egg yolks, and egg proteins such as ovoalbumin and ovomucoid.

HP_0410232.label: increased anti - fungi ige antibody level

HP_0410233.label: increased anti - meat allergen ige antibody level
HP_0410233.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against meat, such as mammalian meat, including beef or pork, or poultry, like duck or chicken.

HP_0410234.label: increased anti - parasite ige antibody level
HP_0410234.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against parasites, such as helminths (parasitic worms, such as Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, Ancylostoma duodenalis, Necator americanus, Strongyloides stercoralis) or parasites such as Toxoplasma gondii.

HP_0410235.label: increased anti - insect ige antibody level
HP_0410235.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against antigens from insects such as moths, mosquitos, or cockroaches.

HP_0410236.label: increased anti - venom ige antibody level
HP_0410236.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against venom from insects such as bees, wasps, hornets, yellowjackets.

HP_0410238.label: increased anti - plant product ige antibody level
HP_0410238.definition: Increased level of IgE antibody against antigens from plants and products derived from plants, such as wood or pollen.

HP_0410251.definition: An abnormality in the cleavage of L-selectin during the process of guiding neutrophils to the site of infection. Proteolytic cleavage of L-selectin results in rapid shedding from the cell surface, which has a role in neutrophil rolling and accumulation at the site of infection.

HP_0410252.label: chronic neutropenia
HP_0410252.definition: Neutropenia with an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) less than 1,500,000,000/L lasting for more than 3 months.

HP_0500050.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 1
HP_0500050.definition: The retinal vessels stop and then a linear flat white line is present that usually runs the circumference of the vascular retina.

HP_0500051.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 2
HP_0500051.definition: The accumulating neovascularization thickens and manifests as a linear bump. The neovascularization remains along the surface of the retina and does not extend off the retina into the cortical vitreous.

HP_0500052.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 3
HP_0500052.definition: The neovascularization accumulates at the edge of the vascularized retina and extends into the vitreous (also called extra retinal fibrosis proliferation). In cases of Zone 2 and Zone 3, this may be sausage shaped. In more posterior Zone 1 disease, the stage 3 can appear as a direct extension of the normal retinal vessels but extending tangentially over the avascular retina.

HP_0500053.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 4
HP_0500053.definition: Scar tissue that forms a continuous sheet coming up from the edge of the vascularized retina. This scar tissue can grow toward the vitreous base/posterior lens capsule resulting in traction, distortion, and even detachment.

HP_0500054.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 4a
HP_0500054.definition: A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that does not extend into the macula.

HP_0500055.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 4b
HP_0500055.definition: A detachment that involves the peripheral retina that involves the macula itself. The detachment usually starts in the temporal periphery although can also involve the nasal retina as well.

HP_0500056.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 5
HP_0500056.definition: Funnel detachment from the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.
HP_0500056.UMLS synonyms: Retinopathy of prematurity stage 5 - total retinal detachment | Right retinopathy of prematurity stage 5 | Left retinopathy of prematurity stage 5 | Bilateral retinopathy of prematurity stage 5 | Retinopathy of prematurity, stage 5, unspecified eye

HP_0500057.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 5a
HP_0500057.definition: An open funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

HP_0500058.label: retinopathy of prematurity stage 5b
HP_0500058.definition: A closed funnel detachment of the retina with generally traction in all four quadrants.

HP_0500059.label: retinopathy of prematurity zone i
HP_0500059.definition: Retinopathy which extends from the center of the optic disc to twice the distance from the center of the optic disc to the center of the macula.

HP_0500060.label: retinopathy of prematurity zone ii
HP_0500060.definition: Retinopathy which extends centrifugally from the edge of zone I to the nasal ora serrata.

HP_0500061.label: retinopathy of prematurity zone iii
HP_0500061.definition: Retinopathy which is a residual crescent of retina anterior to zone II.

HP_0500062.label: retinopathy of prematurity plus
HP_0500062.definition: Venous dilatation and arteriolar tortuosity of the posterior retinal vessels and may later increase in severity to include iris vascular engorgement, poor pupillary dilatation (rigid pupil), and vitreous haze. This definition has been further refined in the later clinical trials in which the diagnosis of plus disease could be made if sufficient vascular dilatation and tortuosity are present in at least 2 quadrants of the eye.
HP_0500062.UMLS synonyms: Retinopathy of Prematurity with Plus Disease

HP_0500063.label: retinopathy of prematurity pre - plus
HP_0500063.definition: As vascular abnormalities of the posterior pole that are insufficient for the diagnosis of plus disease but that demonstrate more arterial tortuosity and more venous dilatation than normal.

HP_0500064.label: retinopathy of prematurity threshold
HP_0500064.definition: A retinopathy with a 50% likelihood of progressing to retinal detachment. Threshold disease is considered to be present when stage 3 retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is present in either zone I or zone II, with at least 5 continuous or 8 total clock hours of disease, and the presence of plus disease.

HP_0500065.label: retinopathy of prematurity prethreshold
HP_0500065.definition: High risk patients who were in Zone 1 (no Plus or stage 3) or Zone 2 with Plus or stage 3 but not both.

HP_0500066.label: latent myopia
HP_0500066.definition: The difference between total and manifest myopia.

HP_0500069.label: paralytic ectropion
HP_0500069.definition: A type of ectropion associated with orbicularis muscle weakness caused by cranial nerve VII palsy.
HP_0500069.UMLS synonyms: paralytic ectropion | Paralytic ectropion of eyelid | Paralytic ectropion of left eyelid | Paralytic ectropion of right eyelid | paralytic ectropion of lower eyelid | paralytic ectropion of both eyelids | paralytic ectropion of upper eyelid | Paralytic ectropion of left lower eyelid | Paralytic ectropion of right lower eyelid | paralytic ectropion of left upper eyelid | paralytic ectropion of right upper eyelid | paralytic ectropion of both lower eyelids | paralytic ectropion of both upper eyelids | Paralytic ectropion of left eye, unspecified eyelid | Paralytic ectropion of right eye, unspecified eyelid | Paralytic ectropion of unspecified eye, unspecified eyelid | Identify the frequency and the type of the care according to the eyelid position in lagophthalmos (e.g., in comatose, under deep sedation and neuromuscular blockage, facial paralysis, Bell's palsy, thyrotoxic exophthalmos, paralytic ectropion)

HP_0500070.label: conjunctival dermolipoma
HP_0500070.definition: A conjuctival lesion composed of adipose tissue and dense connective tissue. Such choristomas of dermal elements are normally found at the outer canthus, and have a gelatinous appearance. Classically, there is an indistinct posterior border (with the lesion frequently extending into the orbit) and a well-demarcated anterior border several millimetres posterior to the limbus.

HP_0500072.label: absolute eccentric fixation
HP_0500072.definition: Eccentric fixation in which the angle of eccentricity equals the objective angle of deviation.

HP_0500073.label: abnormal ocular alignment
HP_0500073.definition: Any deviation from the normal ocular alignment.

HP_0500074.label: dissociated vertical deviation
HP_0500074.definition: An incomitant tendency for an occluded eye to elevate and extort which resolves on uncovering.
HP_0500074.UMLS synonyms: Dissociated vertical deviation | Esotropia with dissociated vertical deviation

HP_0500075.label: dissociated horizontal deviation
HP_0500075.definition: A change in horizontal ocular alignment, unrelated to accommodation, that is brought about solely by a change in the balance of visual input from the two eyes.

HP_0500076.label: alternating hypertropia
HP_0500076.definition: A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated upwards.

HP_0500077.label: alternating hyperphoria
HP_0500077.definition: A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates upwards.

HP_0500078.label: alternating hypotropia
HP_0500078.definition: A type of vertical tropia in which, when one eye is fixing, the other eye is deviated downwards.

HP_0500079.label: alternating hypophoria
HP_0500079.definition: A type of vertical phoria in which, in dissociation, the occluded eye deviates downwards.

HP_0500081.label: pseudophakia
HP_0500081.definition: The term pseudophakia refers to having an artificial lens implanted after the natural eye lens has been removed. During cataract surgery the natural cloudy lens is replaced by an pseudophakia intraocular lens (IOL).

HP_0500086.definition: Having a characteristic appearance of a slate gray area of pigmentation within the disc margins that commonly appears along the inferotemporal or temporal neuroretinal rim areas.

HP_0500087.label: peripapillary atrophy
HP_0500087.definition: Thinning in the layers of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium around the optic nerve.

HP_0500088.label: foveal depigmentation
HP_0500088.definition: Loss of pigment in the fovea centralis.

HP_0500089.label: optic nerve sheath meningioma
HP_0500089.definition: A benign tumor of meningothelial cells of the meninges that usually occurs in middle age. It is typically unilateral and there is an association with neurofibromatosis type 2.
HP_0500089.UMLS synonyms: Meningioma of optic nerve sheath | Primary optic nerve sheath meningioma | Secondary optic nerve sheath meningioma | Malignant meningioma of optic nerve sheath | Primary malignant meningioma of optic nerve sheath

HP_0500090.label: periocular capillary hemangioma
HP_0500090.definition: A capillary hemangioma surrounding the eyeball but within the orbit.

HP_0500091.label: lymphangioma of the orbit
HP_0500091.definition: A hamartoma of lymph vessels that usually presents in childhood. It tends to increase in size with head-down posture and with the Valsalva manoeuvre. Superficial lesions are visible as transilluminable cystic spaces of the lid or conjunctiva that may also contain blood. Deep lesions may cause gradual proptosis or present acutely with orbital pain and reduced vision due to haemorrhage.

HP_0500092.label: orbital rhabdomyosarcoma
HP_0500092.definition: A mesenchymal tumor that is considered to be the commonest primary orbital malignancy in children. Histologically, it may be differentiated into embryonal, alveolar, and pleomorphic types. It is usually intraconal or within the superior orbit.

HP_0500093.label: food allergy
HP_0500093.definition: Primary food allergies primarily occur as a result (most likely) of gastrointestinal sensitization to predominantly stable food allergens (glycoproteins). HP_4000001.label: abnormal cardiac magnetic resonance imaging finding
HP_4000001.definition: Abnormal finding by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which uses non-ionizing radiation via a strong magnetic field and radio frequency energy to generate three dimensional images. This term comprises findings that are specific to MRI. Findings such as ventricular spetum defect that can be detected by multiple modalities should be coded separately.

HP_4000003.label: elevated myocardial native t2
HP_4000003.definition: Increased duration of myocardial T2 time without gadolinium contrast. Elevated T2, which can detect myocardial edema.

HP_4000004.label: myocardial late gadolinium enhancement
HP_4000004.definition: Areas of high signal intensity in magnetic resonance imaging of the heart appearing 10 to 15 minutes after injection of the intercellular contrast agent gadolinium.
HP_4000004.UMLS synonyms: Myocardial late gadolinium enhancement MRI | Myocardial Injury by Late Gadolinium Enhancement of T1 Imaging

HP_4000005.label: pericardial late gadolinium enhancement
HP_4000005.definition: Areas of high signal intensity in magnetic resonance imaging of the pericardium appearing around 10 minutes after injection of the intercellular contrast agent gadolinium.

HP_4000006.label: elevated myocardial native t1
HP_4000006.definition: Increased duration of myocardial T1 time without gadolinium contrast. T1 mapping consists of quantifying the T1 relaxation time of a tissue by using analytical expressions of image-based signal intensities. A fundamental principle of MR imaging is that the signal intensity of pixels is based on the relaxation of hydrogen nuclei protons in a static magnetic field. The T1 relaxation times between two tissues vary substantially. Edema, fat infiltration, and fibrosis also cause differences in T1 relaxivity.

HP_4000007.label: bronchoconstriction
HP_4000007.definition: Tightening of smooth muscle surrounding the bronchi and bronchioles with consequent wheezing and shortness of breath.
HP_4000007.synonyms: bronchial constriction | constriction of the bronchi

HP_4000008.label: formation of multiple pronuclei during fertilization
HP_4000008.definition: Pronuclei formation is a critical process during fertilisation. Normally, there are two pronuclei (2PN), including the paternal pronucleus and the maternal pronucleus, in the zygote after fertilisation. It is generally accepted that multiple pronuclei (MPN) formation is due to the abnormal extrusion of the second polar body or to abnormal fertilisation with multiple sperm. The MPN therefore can cause infertility and recurrent failure of IVF/ICSI.

HP_4000009.label: kinesiophobia
HP_4000009.definition: An excessive, irrational, and debilitating fear of carrying out a physical movement due to a feeling of vulnerability to painful injury or reinjury.

HP_4000010.label: impaired renal tubular reabsorption of bicarbonate
HP_4000010.definition: Decreased renal tubular reabsorption of bicarbonate.

HP_4000011.label: history of congenital hpv infection
HP_4000011.definition: A congenital human papillomavirus (HPV) infection of the newborn. Congential HPV infection can manifest as condyloma cuminata in the newborn.

HP_4000023.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against laminin gamma-1.

HP_4000024.label: anti - laminin antibody positivity
HP_4000024.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against a laminin. Laminins are major components of the basement membrane.

HP_4000025.label: anti - integrin antibody positivity
HP_4000025.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against an integrin. Integrins are a family of cell adhesion molecules with 24 known integrin heterodimers. Integrins transduce mechanical and biochemical signals from fibrotic extracellular matrix into the cell, activate latent TGFbeta, and subsequently modulate fibroblast adhesion, migration, and growth.

HP_4000026.label: anti - transglutaminase 6 antibody
HP_4000026.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against transglutaminase 6.

HP_4000027.label: anti - lad - 1 antibody positivity
HP_4000027.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against LAD-1, which is the soluble 120 kDa ectodomain of BP180.

HP_4000028.label: anti - labd97 antibody positivity
HP_4000028.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against LABD97, which is structurally identical to a portion of the extracellular domain of BPAg2. BPAg2, a 180 kDa bullous pemphigoid antigen, is a transmembrane protein important for basement membrane cohesion.

HP_4000029.label: antigliadin antibody positivity
HP_4000029.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against gliadin.

HP_4000030.label: anti - reticulin antibody positivity

HP_4000031.label: anti - type vii collagen antibody
HP_4000031.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against collagen type VII.

HP_4000032.definition: A perception that one's body is moving or swaying despite lack of motion of the body.

HP_4000033.label: non - spinning vertigo
HP_4000033.definition: A perception of unsteadiness of dizziness that is not characterized bythe spinning sensation of classic vertigo, but rather by an oscillatory perception (rocking, bobbing, or swaying despite the fact that the subject is not moving).

HP_4000036.definition: A type of hydrocele testis in which both the proximal and distal portions of processus vaginalis get obliterated while the central portion remains patent and fluid accumulates within it.

HP_4000038.definition: Infantile Hydrocele is a type pf hydrocele in which the processus vaginalis gets obliterated at the level of the deep inguinal ring. However, the portion distal to it remains patent and allows fluid accumulation.
