HP_4000057.definition: A reduced amount of programmed cell death upon stimulation of the FAS receptor, which normally induces caspase-8 dependent apoptosis.

HP_4000058.label: glomerular proteinuria
HP_4000058.definition: A type of proteinuria characterized by increased permeability of the glomerular capillary wall to macromolecules (particularly albumin), whereby protein excretion can reach 20 g/24 h and consists mainly of albumin.
HP_4000058.UMLS synonyms: proteinuria; isolated, with glomerular lesion | Isolated proteinuria with minor glomerular abnormality | Isolated proteinuria with focal and segmental glomerular lesions

HP_4000059.label: abnormal lung development
HP_4000059.definition: A structural defect associated with abnormal development of the lung.

HP_4000061.label: pancreatic alpha - cell hyperplasia
HP_4000061.definition: A diffuse and specific increase in the number of alpha-cells.
HP_4000061.UMLS synonyms: pancreatic islet cells; hyperplasia, alpha cells | pancreatic islet cells; hyperplasia, alpha cells, with excess gastrin | pancreatic islet cells; hyperplasia, alpha cells, with excess glucagon | Hyperplasia of pancreatic alpha cells with gastrin excess | Hyperplasia of pancreatic islet alpha cells with glucagon excess

HP_4000062.label: 3 - 4 metacarpal synostosis
HP_4000062.definition: A congenital hand malformation characterized by the coalescence of the coalescence of third and fourth metacarpals (i.e., those corresponding to the middle and ring fingers).
HP_4000062.synonyms: fused third and fourth metacarpals | middle and ring finger metacarpal synostosis | synostosis of third and the fourth metacarpal bones

HP_4000066.label: abnormal iliac artery morphology
HP_4000066.definition: Any structural anomaly of the iliac artery.

HP_4000067.label: iliac artery aneurysm
HP_4000067.definition: Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the iliac artery.
HP_4000067.UMLS synonyms: Iliac Aneurysm | Iliac artery aneurysm enlargement | Aneurysm of right iliac artery | Aneurysm of left iliac artery | surgery for iliac artery aneurysm | Aneurysm of right common iliac artery | Aneurysm of left common iliac artery | Aneurysm of left internal iliac artery | Aneurysm of right internal iliac artery | Ligation of aneurysm of iliac artery | Aneurysm of right external iliac artery | Aneurysm of left external iliac artery | Ruptured aneurysm of common iliac artery | Ruptured aneurysm of internal iliac artery | History of aneurysm of iliac artery | Direct repair of iliac artery aneurysm | surgery for ruptured iliac artery aneurysm | Endovascular repair of aneurysm of iliac artery | Direct repair of ruptured iliac artery aneurysm | Direct repair of external iliac artery aneurysm | Direct repair of hypogastric iliac artery aneurysm | Direct repair of common iliac artery aneurysm | Repair of false aneurysm in iliac artery | Excision of iliac artery aneurysm and anastomosis of artery | computed tomography of abdomen: aneurysm of left internal iliac artery

HP_4000068.label: abnormal interest
HP_4000068.definition: Any deviation from normal intensity or subject of a person's interests, which can be defined as a state of giving selective attention to something.
HP_4000068.UMLS synonyms: abnormal preoccupation preoccupied with narrow and unusual interests | abnormal preoccupation only interested in same few toys or objects

HP_4000069.label: persistent preoccupation with parts of objects
HP_4000069.definition: A type of abnormal interest characterized by a persistent and intense focus on parts of a toy/object. For example, affected individuals may spin the wheels on a toy car rather than drive the toy car.
HP_4000069.synonyms: fixated interest in unusual objects | fixated interest with parts of objects | fixation with parts of objects

HP_4000070.label: fixated interests
HP_4000070.definition: Highly restricted, fixated interests that are abnormal in intensity or focus (e.g., strong attachment to or preoccupation with unusual objects, excessively circumscribed or perseverative interests).

HP_4000072.label: abnormal language feature
HP_4000072.definition: The presence of any atypical form of expressive language.

HP_4000073.label: pronoun reversal
HP_4000073.definition: Atypical language features characterized by first vs. second or third person pronoun errors such as using 'you' or 'he/she' in place of 'I'.

HP_4000074.label: idiosyncratic language
HP_4000074.definition: Consistent use of an unusual way of referring to something that is idiosyncratic to the individual.
HP_4000074.UMLS synonyms: idiosyncratic language | idiosyncratic language perseverative | idiosyncratic language self-stimulatory vocalizations | idiosyncratic language use of jargon or gibberish | idiosyncratic language refers to self by name only

HP_4000075.label: reduced frequency of facial expressions
HP_4000075.definition: The number of times facial expressions are produced in a given period is lower than expected given the social and cultural context.

HP_4000076.label: use of another person 's body to communicate
HP_4000076.definition: Moving another person's hand, body part, or body to communicate a desire, e.g. pushing or pulling someone toward a desired object or placing someone's hand on something.
HP_4000076.synonyms: hand - leading gesture | hand - taking gestures

HP_4000077.label: fixated interest with abnormal focus
HP_4000077.definition: A fixated interest in a specific topic that is atypical for the social context of the individual, such as topics of a non-social nature like fossils or vacuum cleaners.

HP_4000078.label: fixated interest with abnormal intensity
HP_4000078.definition: An abnormally intense interest in a topic or object that is not atypical for the social context of the affected person.

HP_4000079.label: sensory seeking
HP_4000079.definition: Unusual interest in sensory aspects of the environment.
HP_4000079.UMLS synonyms: Sensory Profile 2 quadrant score seeking/seeker | Sensory Profile 2 seeking/seeker quadrant percentile | sensory profile test infant-toddler sensation seeking raw score

HP_4000081.label: reduced production of gestures
HP_4000081.definition: Diminished use of typical non-verbal conversational gestures such as shaking the head to indicate no or nodding the head to indicate yes.

HP_4000082.label: reduced collaborative play
HP_4000082.definition: Impairment in a child's ability to be able to play in a way that involves peer collaboration. Collaborative play involves things such as verbal and non-verbal communication (e.g., self-initiated interactions), turn-taking, sharing, reciprocity, and collaborative problem-solving. It is often contrasted to parallel play, which involves a form of social play in which two children do similar activities near each other and often mimic each other. Typically developing children develop collaborative play between the ages of 4 and 5.

HP_4000083.label: ignores peers
HP_4000083.definition: Lack of interest in peers of comparable age and social groups is evident when an individual, such as a child, shows more interest in socializing with adults rather than children their own age.

HP_4000084.label: reduced sharing of interests
HP_4000084.definition: Decreased sharing of interests with others appropriate to culture and developmental level.

HP_4000085.label: reduced object sharing
HP_4000085.definition: An absence or reduction in object sharing. Object sharing is an early emerging social skill in which a child will share objects with parents or peers during object play. Object sharing typically develops within the first two years of life.

HP_4000087.label: abnormal communicative facial expressions
HP_4000087.definition: Abnormal expressions (movements or position of muscles of the face that convey the emotional state of an individual to observers during social interactions) comprising abnormalities of quantity, range, context-appropriateness, and quality.

HP_4000088.label: facial expressions that do not match the context
HP_4000088.definition: Production of facial expressions that are misaligned with the social context.

HP_4000089.label: abnormal quality of facial expression
HP_4000089.definition: Spontaneous production of communicative facial expressions that have poor quality or are exaggerated or muted.

HP_4000090.label: abnormal gesture use
HP_4000090.definition: Abnormality in the use of gestures defined as hand, shoulder, and head movements that convey a shared meaning within a culture that replace or supplement verbal communication.
HP_4000090.synonyms: abnormal communicative gesture use | abnormal communicative gestures | abnormal gestures

HP_4000092.label: poor conversational reciprocity
HP_4000092.definition: Reduced ability to conduct a reciprocal (back and forth) conversation, as expected for language level. May be characterized by deficits in the ability to make comments about discussion topics of others, failure to ask questions, and not building a conversation on comments of others. Affected persons may not know what to say next in a conversation, may not notice if others are bored with a given topic, may conduct a one-sided conversation (talking but not listening), or may veer off topic more than is socially acceptable.
HP_4000092.synonyms: failure of normal back - and - forth conversation

HP_4000093.label: ectopic tooth eruption
HP_4000093.definition: A condition in which the permanent teeth, because of deficiency of growth in the jaw or segment of jaw, assume a path of eruption that intercepts a primary tooth, causes its premature loss and produces a consequent malposition of the permanent tooth.
HP_4000093.UMLS synonyms: Tooth Eruption, Ectopic | Precocious exfoliation due to ectopic eruption of proximate tooth | Failure of exfoliation associated with ectopic eruption of succedaneous tooth | MALPOSITION OF TEETH WITH OR WITHOUT HYPODONTIA/OLIGODONTIA

HP_4000094.label: corpus cavernosum hypoplasia
HP_4000094.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by undergrowth of the corpus cavernosum.

HP_4000095.label: elevated circulating thymine concentration
HP_4000095.definition: Concentration of the nucleobase thymine in the blood circulation above the normal range.

HP_4000100.label: positive lactose hydrogen breath test
HP_4000100.definition: Elevated hydrogen gas level in exhaled breath following oral administration of lactose. In individuals with lactose intolerance, undigested lactose in the colon will be metabolized by colonic bacteria, releasing hydrogen gas.

HP_4000101.label: triggered by exposure to medication
HP_4000101.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to a medication.

HP_4000102.label: triggered by allopurinol
HP_4000102.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to allopurinol.

HP_4000103.label: ameliorated by oral zinc supplementation
HP_4000103.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by oral zinc supplementation.

HP_4000104.label: curved dental root
HP_4000104.definition: A root of a tooth that is more rounded than normal.
HP_4000104.UMLS synonyms: Curved form of root of tooth

HP_4000105.label: abnormal four chamber view of the fetal heart
HP_4000105.definition: The four-chamber (4Ch) view of the fetal heart is the most widely used screening examination for the detection of structural cardiac abnormalities during routine fetal ultrasonography. In the healthy normal fetus, the apical 4Ch view demonstrates four well-developed chambers, a concordant atrioventricular (AV) connection, unobstructed AV valves (mitral and tricuspid valves), the foramen ovale flap opening into left atrium (LA), and an intact interventricular septum. Additionally, the pulmonary venous opening can be visualized at the LA wall. Any structural deviations from normal anatomy may lead to congenital heart disease that can be determined by the 4Ch view of the fetal heart's ultrasound imaging.

HP_4000106.label: spleen hamartoma
HP_4000106.definition: A hamartomatous lesion (benign focal lesions composed of disorganized tissue elements) localized in the spleen.

HP_4000107.label: positive lupus band test
HP_4000107.definition: Deposits of immunoglobulins and complement components along the dermoepidermal junction.

HP_4000108.label: bone marrow erythroid vacuolization
HP_4000108.definition: Formation of vacuoles (a space within a cell that is empty of cytoplasm, lined with a membrane, and filled with fluid) in the cytoplasm of erythroid precursors in the bone marrow.

HP_4000109.label: triggered by electromagnetic field
HP_4000109.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to an electromagnetic field.

HP_4000110.label: exposure history
HP_4000110.definition: Information about current and past exposure to metals, dust, fibers, fumes, chemicals, biologic hazards, radiation, noise, and/or vibration at work or home.
HP_4000110.UMLS synonyms: exposure history | environmental exposure (history) | exposure to STD (history) | exposure to toluene (history) | History of radiation exposure | exposure to gonorrhea (history) | exposure to syphilis (history) | exposure to molds (history) | exposure to cholera (history) | exposure to polio (history) | exposure to alkalis (history) | Electronic cigarette exposure history | History of asbestos exposure | exposure to mumps (history) | exposure to radon (history) | exposure to Streptococcus (history) | exposure to xylene (history) | exposure to scabies (history) | exposure to hepatitis (history) | Chemical/Occupational Exposure History | Known exposure | Mother | History | Known exposure | Patient | History | exposure to methylene chloride (history)

HP_4000111.label: asbestos exposure
HP_4000111.definition: History of exposure to asbestos, a fibrous mineral with physical and chemical properties that make it resistant to heat and degradation.
HP_4000111.UMLS synonyms: Exposure to asbestos | History of asbestos exposure | exposure to asbestos dust | exposure to serpentine asbestos | Asbestos Exposure Mineral Type Indicator | Pulmonary Fibrosis - from Asbestos Exposure | Mesothelioma, malignant, after asbestos exposure | regular or heavy exposure to asbestos dust | occasional or light exposure to asbestos dust | work restrictions no exposure to asbestos | Encounter due to history of contact with and (suspected) exposure to asbestos

HP_4000112.label: medication history
HP_4000112.definition: Information about current or past medications taken by an individual.
HP_4000112.UMLS synonyms: medication history (history) | taking medication (history) | Medication history section | Medication history unavailable | Review medication history | postpartum history taking medication | Assesses medication use history | Concomitant Medication Medical History Number | History of noncompliance with medication regimen | History of therapy with ototoxic medication | Known History of Allergy to Medication | Obtain and document prescription medication history | Obtain and document nonprescription medication history | medication intolerance | medication intolerance anticoagulant medication | taking medication for high blood pressure (history) | medication history unobtainable due to patient refusal | Verify medication history with person and family | Determine past health history and medication use | History of ineffective health behaviors: medication regimen | Medication Nonadherence | H/O: regular medication | Medication use:Hx:Pt:^Patient:Nom | self-discontinued medication | recently stopped medication

HP_4000113.label: aminoglycoside exposure
HP_4000113.definition: History of having taken aminoglycoside antibiotics.

HP_4000114.label: statin exposure
HP_4000114.definition: History of having taken statins, also known as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors.

HP_4000115.label: potassium - sparing diuretic exposure
HP_4000115.definition: History of having taken a potassium-sparing diuretic exposure such as amiloride, eplerenone, spironolactone, and triamterene.

HP_4000117.label: valproate exposure
HP_4000117.definition: History of having taken valproate (valproic acid).

HP_4000119.label: calcium channel blocker exposure
HP_4000119.definition: History of having taken a calcium channel blocker such as amlodipine, nicardipine, nifedipine, verapamil, or diltiazem.

HP_4000121.label: triggered by poison ivy , poson oak , or sumac
HP_4000121.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure (cutaneous contact) to poison ivy, poison oak, and poison sumac. These three plants each contain urushiol. Contact with these plants is the most common causes of clinically diagnosed allergic contact dermatitis.
HP_4000121.synonyms: contact with poison ivy , poison oak , or sumac

HP_4000122.label: history of exclusive breast feeding
HP_4000122.definition: A past medical history of having been fed exclusively by breast feeding.

HP_4000123.label: nutrition history
HP_4000123.definition: A part of the past medical history consisting of information about the typical food intake of an individual.
HP_4000123.UMLS synonyms: Food and nutrition history panel | Food and nutrition history panel:-:Pt:^Patient:- | History of prescribed enteral nutrition feeding | food and nutrition-related knowledge deficit | caregiver improving level of nutrition support | History and physical note:Find:Pt:{Setting}:Doc:Nutrition and dietetics | current diet limited adherence to nutrition-related recommendations | has equipment for total parenteral nutrition at home | unable to manage one's own enteral or parenteral nutrition | History of nutritional deficiency | Personal history of nutritional deficiency | Family history of nutritional disorder | FH: Nutritional deficiency | H/O: nutritional disorder | history; disorder, disease or disorder, nutritional | Personal history of endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases | Family history of other endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases | Obtain the patient's social, family and nutritional history | At increased risk for imbalanced nutrition, less than body requirements (finding) | Personal history of other endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease | nutritional quality of current diet | Seeking and accepting physical, nutritional and chemical interventions known to be hazardous and harmful | Screen for health problems relevant to adolescent and suggested by history (e.g., anemia; hypertension; hearing and vision disorders; hyperlipidemia; oral health problems; abnormal sexual maturation; abnormal physical growth; body image disturbances; eating disorders; poor nutrition; alcohol, tobacco, or drug use; unhealthy sexual behavior; infectious disease; poor self-concept; low self-esteem; depression; difficult relationships; abuse; learning problems; work problems)

HP_4000124.label: high dietary oxalate intake
HP_4000124.definition: A history of ingestion of a relatively high amount of foods containing high levels of oxalate, such as green-leaf vegetables, tea, nuts, chocolate and rhubarb.
HP_4000124.synonyms: foods high in oxalate , high intake

HP_4000125.label: recent honey ingestion
HP_4000125.definition: A history of ingestion of honey in recent weeks.

HP_4000126.label: raw egg - white ingestion
HP_4000126.definition: A history of eating raw egg whites.

HP_4000127.label: exacerbated by sodium channel blocking agent exposure
HP_4000127.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by administration of sodium channel blocking agents such as phenytoin, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, lamotrigine, topiramate, and zonisamide.
HP_4000127.synonyms: sodium channel blocking drugs aggravate findings

HP_4000128.label: addictive nitrous oxide use
HP_4000128.definition: Addiction to inhaled nitrous oxide gas (N2O) is a growing concern.
HP_4000128.synonyms: nitrous oxide abuse | nitrous oxide addiction

HP_4000129.label: recent blood transfusion
HP_4000129.definition: A past medical history of a recent blood transfusion.

HP_4000130.label: ameliorated by colchicine
HP_4000130.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of colchizine.

HP_4000131.label: ameliorated by vitamin d
HP_4000131.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by administration of vitamin D.

HP_4000132.label: exacerbated by phenytoin exposure
HP_4000132.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by administration of phenytoin.

HP_4000133.label: triggered by angiotensin - converting enzyme inhibitor
HP_4000133.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is provoked or brought about by exposure to anngiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, and lisinopril.

HP_4000134.label: prostaglandin e1 exposure
HP_4000134.definition: History of having been treateed with prostaglandin E1.

HP_4000135.label: 5 - fluorouracil exposure
HP_4000135.definition: History of having been treated with 5-fluorouracil.

HP_4000136.label: 6 - mercaptopurine exposure
HP_4000136.definition: History of having been treateed with 6-mercaptopurine.

HP_4000137.label: isoniazid exposure
HP_4000137.definition: History of having been treateed with isoniazid.

HP_4000138.label: absent cavum septum pellucidum
HP_4000138.definition: The cavum septum pellucidum (CSP) is an important fetal midline forebrain landmark that is normally visible by prenatal sonography. This term refers to the lack of visiblity of the CSP on prenatal sonography. The CSP normally can be visualized between 18 and 37 weeks of gestation. Lack of visualization of the CSP in this time period generally requires follow up and may indicate the presence of underlying malformations such as malformations of the corpus callosum. The lack of CSP before 18 weeks or after 37 weeks of gestation (or postnatally) is considered a normal finding.

HP_4000139.label: fetal abdominal cyst
HP_4000139.definition: Fetal abdominal cysts are usually detected during the second trimester anomaly scan or discovered incidentally at later gestations. However, a definitive diagnosis is often not made until postnatal life. The most common etiologies of fetal abdominal cysts are: ovarian, gastrointestinal cystic duplication, liver and choledochal, meconium pseudocysts, mesenteric and adrenal. Following identification of a cyst, careful morphological assessment allows the prediction of their natural history and importantly, the likelihood of surgical intervention being required postnatally.
HP_4000139.synonyms: fetal cystic abdominal mass | foetal abdominal cyst | foetal cystic abdominal mass

HP_4000140.label: fetal bowel dilatation
HP_4000140.definition: Fetal bowel dilatation is characterized by fluid-filled intestinal loops which measure at least fifteen millimeters long or seven millimeters in diameter. Ultrasonographic image of dilated fetal bowel is a sign of intestinal mechanical or functional obstruction and its prevalence will depend on the underlying condition: bowel atresia or stenosis, malrotation with volvulus, meconium ileus, total colonic aganglionosis, and meconium plug syndrome. The etiology of fetal bowel dilatation is a difficult prenatal diagnosis since ultrasound has limited accuracy for bowel evaluation.
HP_4000140.synonyms: foetal bowel dilatation | prenatal ultrasound : bowel loops dilated

HP_4000141.label: left ventricular dilatation
HP_4000141.definition: Enlargement of the chamber of the left heart ventricle.
HP_4000141.UMLS synonyms: Left cardiac ventricular dilatation | Left ventricular or biventricular dilatation | Transient ischemic dilatation of left cardiac ventricular cavity | Transient ischemic dilatation ratio of left ventricular cavity | Balloon dilation of left ventricular outflow tract | Left ventricular dilation | Left ventricular dilation, mild | Left ventricular dilation, severe | Dilation of left ventricular chamber | Ventricular dilation, left or bilateral | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation | Cardiomyopathy, Dilated, with Left Ventricular Noncompaction | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation global | Acquired dilatation of left cardiac ventricle | CARDIOMYOPATHY, DILATED, 1C, WITH LEFT VENTRICULAR NONCOMPACTION | echocardiography: dilation of left ventricular outflow tract | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional diaphragmatic | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional anterior | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional posterobasal | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional anterobasal | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional anterolateral | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional posterolateral | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional apical | cardiac catheterization left ventricular dilation regional lateral

HP_4000142.label: fetal trigonocephaly
HP_4000142.definition: A fetal ultrasound finding defined by flattening of the occiput with pointing of the frontal bones and brachycephaly with an increased cephalic index. It is characterized by keel shaped deformity of forehead with midline ridge, bilateral fronto temporal constriction with compensatory biparietal expansion, supra orbital and lateral orbital retrusion and hypotelorism. This finding is said to resemble a strawberry.
HP_4000142.synonyms: foetal trigonocephaly | strawberry sign | strawberry skull | strawberry - shaped skull

HP_4000143.label: abnormal fetal heart outflow tract
HP_4000143.definition: A prenatal anomaly of the outflow tract. Fetal ultrasound may not always be able to easily and accurately describe the outflow anomaly, but can detect abnormal anatomy. Often, follow up with a fetal echo is recommended, but fetal ultrasound is limited.

HP_4000144.label: recent past medical history
HP_4000144.definition: History of events that precede the current presenting condition and are thought to be of potential relevance, having occurred in the hours, days, or weeks before the current condition.

HP_4000145.label: history of recent viral illness
HP_4000145.definition: Medical history of a viral illness in recent weeks.

HP_4000146.label: history of recent dental procedure
HP_4000146.definition: Medical history of a dental procedure in recent weeks.

HP_4000147.label: abnormal hepatic artery morphology
HP_4000147.definition: Any structural anomaly of the hepatic artery or its branches.

HP_4000148.label: hepatic artery hyperplasia
HP_4000148.definition: Abnormal increase in size of the hepatic arteries.

HP_4000149.label: lymph node necrosis
HP_4000149.definition: Areas of necrotic tissue within a lymph node.
HP_4000149.UMLS synonyms: Histology shows large regions of necrosis in lymph nodes, thymus, bone marrow, and spleen

HP_4000150.label: multinucleated neuron
HP_4000150.definition: Neurons that contain more than one nucleus.

HP_4000151.label: history of recent contralateral injury
HP_4000151.definition: A history of an injury that occurred several hours, days, or weeks before the current presenting complaint and is located on the other side of the body relative to the current presenting complaint.

HP_4000152.label: alternating laterality
HP_4000152.definition: Occuring on the left and right in succession. This term can refer to alternating sides of the body (e.g., Alternating hemiplegia) or alternative sides of the visual field (e.g., some migraine auras).

HP_4000153.label: cervical squamous cell papilloma
HP_4000153.definition: A benign tumor arising from the epithelial surface of the cervix and usually caused by Human Papillomavirus infection.
HP_4000153.UMLS synonyms: Human Papillomavirus-Related Cervical Squamous Cell Carcinoma

HP_4000154.label: liver leiomyoma
HP_4000154.definition: A benign smooth muscle neoplasm that arises in the liver.

HP_4000158.label: typified by high penetrance
HP_4000158.definition: Description of conditions in which only an incomplete but relatively high proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for incomplete, but high penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least 80 percent but less than 100 percent of individuals with the given genotype would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

HP_4000159.label: typified by moderate penetrance
HP_4000159.definition: Description of conditions in which only a moderate proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for moderate penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least 20 percent but less than 80 percent of individuals with the given genotype would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

HP_4000160.label: typified by low penetrance
HP_4000160.definition: Description of conditions in which only a low proportion of individuals with a given genotype exhibit the disease regardless of age assuming a full lifespan of 80 years. There is no commonly accepted definition for low penetrance, but we suggest that this term be applied if at least some but less than 20 percent of carriers would manifest the disease with a full lifespan.

HP_4000162.label: decreased succinyl - coa 3 - ketoacid coa transferase activity
HP_4000162.definition: Decreased activity of the enzyme succinyl-CoA 3-ketoacid CoA transferase.

HP_4000163.label: reduced phytanic acid oxidase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000163.definition: Activity of the enzyme phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase (PhyH; EC 1.14.11.18) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts. PhyH plays a role in the catabolism of phytanic acid, a branched-chain fatty acid that is a normal constituent of the human diet.
HP_4000163.synonyms: decreased phytanoyl - coa hydroxylase activity | phyh activity low in fibroblasts

HP_4000164.label: reduced bifunctional protein activity
HP_4000164.definition: Diminished activity of hydroxysteroid 17-beta dehydrogenase 4 (HSD17B4), also known as D-bifunctional protein (DBP), a peroxisomal enzyme that catalyzes multiple steps of beta-oxidation of very long chain fatty acids.

HP_4000165.label: decreased circulating plasmalogen concentration
HP_4000165.definition: Reduced plasmalogen concentration in the blood circulation.

HP_4000166.label: post - vaccination varicella zoster virus infection
HP_4000166.definition: Infection with live, attenuated varicella-zoster virus following vaccination. This is an extremely rare event that may indicate immunocompromise.
HP_4000166.synonyms: varicella zoster virus infection after vaccination

HP_4000167.label: recent steroid exposure
HP_4000167.definition: History of having been treated with corticosteroid medications in recent weeks.

HP_4000168.label: shark teeth
HP_4000168.definition: Eruption of permanent teeth behind deciduous (baby) teeth before they have fallen out, resulting in a double row of teeth. This phenomen is typically observed between the ages of 5 to 7 years.
HP_4000168.synonyms: cauliflower teeth | double - parked teeth | teeth : double row

HP_4000169.label: pontine t2 hypointensity
HP_4000169.definition: A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the pons.

HP_4000170.label: anti - platelet antigen antibody positivity
HP_4000170.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against antigens present on the surface of thrombocytes such as the glycoproteins GPIIb/IIIa, GPIb/IX, and GPIa/IIa.

HP_4000171.label: anti - voltage - gated potassium channel antibody positivity
HP_4000171.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the serum that react against a voltage-gated potassium channel.
HP_4000171.synonyms: voltage gated potassium channel antibodies in blood

HP_4000172.label: vegan diet
HP_4000172.definition: A history of following a vegan diet characterized by avoidance of food sourced from animals including meet, fish, and dairy products.
HP_4000172.UMLS synonyms: Vegan diet | Vegan diet (regime/therapy) | Vegan diet education | vegan diet including sprouts | vegan diet including fruit

HP_4000173.label: history of previous pregnancy with hydrops fetalis
HP_4000173.definition: One or more previous pregnancies in which the fetus developed hydrops fetalis.
HP_4000173.synonyms: history of hydrops fetalis in newborn offspring

HP_4000174.label: ameliorated by potassium supplements
HP_4000174.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by ingesting a potassium supplement.

HP_4000175.label: ameliorated by niacin
HP_4000175.definition: Applies to a sign or symptom that is improved or made more bearable by ingesting niacin (vitamin B3).
HP_4000175.synonyms: ameliorated by vitamin b3 | niacin reverses symptoms

HP_4000176.label: aggravated by exposure to medication
HP_4000176.definition: Applied to a sign or symptom that is worsened by treatment with a medication.

HP_4000177.label: bleeding ameliorated by vitamin k
HP_4000177.definition: Applies to bleeding that is significantly reduced by treatment with vitamin K.
HP_4000177.synonyms: vitamin k treatment reduces bleeding significantly

HP_4000178.label: anti - retroviral therapy exposure
HP_4000178.definition: History of having been treated with an antiretroviral agent.

HP_4000179.label: potassium - wasting diuretic exposure
HP_4000179.definition: History of having been treated with a potassium-wasting diuretic such as thiazide (chlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide, metolazone) and loop (bumetanide, ethacrynic acid, furosemide, torsemide) diuretics.

HP_4000180.label: tricyclic antidepressant exposure
HP_4000180.definition: History of having been treated with a tricyclic antidepressant medication.

HP_4000181.label: excessive dental attrition
HP_4000181.definition: A higher than expected amount of attrition of teeth, as menifested by loss of tooth characteristics including rounding or sharpening of incisal edges, loss of cusps, and fracturing of teeth, to an extent that is deemed more than would be expected at a given age.
HP_4000181.synonyms: excessive tooth attrition | excessive wear and tear on teeth
HP_4000181.UMLS synonyms: Excessive attrition of teeth | Excessive dental attrition [approximal wear] [occlusal wear]

HP_4000182.label: positionally dependent pain
HP_4000182.definition: Pain improves or worsens with changes in body position.

HP_4000183.label: abnormal erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
HP_4000183.definition: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) outside of the normal range.

HP_4000184.label: reduced erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
HP_4000184.definition: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) below the lower limit of normal.

HP_4000186.label: elevated erythrocyte adenosine triphosphate concentration
HP_4000186.definition: Concentration of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in red blood cells (erythrocytes) above the upper limit of normal.
HP_4000186.synonyms: adenosine triphosphate ( atp ) high in erythrocytes

HP_4000187.label: spermatogonial maturation arrest
HP_4000187.definition: A type of spermatogenesis maturation arrest in which the block of developmental occurs in the spermatogonial stage. Testicular histology shows seminiferous tubules with Sertoli cells and spermatogonial cells but no further differentiated cells like spermatocytes or round spermatids.

HP_4000189.label: elevated circulating neuron - specific enolase concentration
HP_4000189.definition: Concentration of neuron-specific enolase above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.
HP_4000189.synonyms: neuron - specific enolase high in blood

HP_4000190.label: reduced leukocyte alpha - mannosidase activity
HP_4000190.definition: Concentration or activity of an alpha-mannosidase as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.

HP_4000191.label: increased circulating alpha - mannosidase activity
HP_4000191.definition: Concentration or activity of alpha mannosidase above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

HP_4000192.label: reduced leukocyte cathepsin d activity
HP_4000192.definition: Concentration or activity of cathepsin D as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal. The reduction in cathepsin D activity can also be measured in fibroblasts.

HP_4000193.label: reduced leukocyte n - sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase activity
HP_4000193.definition: Concentration or activity of N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase as measured in leukocytes is below the limits of normal.
HP_4000193.synonyms: reduced leukocyte n - sulphoglucosamine sulphohydrolase activity

HP_4000194.label: pseudohyperkalemia
HP_4000194.definition: Pseudohyperkalemia describes a falsely elevated potassium level upon measurement of the serum electrolyte concentration due to disruption of cells during the collection or processing of the sample.
HP_4000194.UMLS synonyms: Pseudohyperkalemia Cardiff | Familial pseudohyperkalemia | Pseudohyperkalemia, Familial, 2, due to Red Cell Leak | DEHYDRATED HEREDITARY STOMATOCYTOSIS 1 WITH OR WITHOUT PSEUDOHYPERKALEMIA AND/OR PERINATAL EDEMA | DEHYDRATED HEREDITARY STOMATOCYTOSIS AND PSEUDOHYPERKALEMIA | Dehydrated Hereditary Stomatocytosis, Pseudohyperkalemia, and Perinatal Edema | DEHYDRATED HEREDITARY STOMATOCYTOSIS WITH PSEUDOHYPERKALEMIA AND PERINATAL EDEMA | In vitro hyperkalemia (pseudohyperkalemia) due to rupture of erythrocyte membranes | GLUT1 Deficiency Syndrome with Pseudohyperkalemia and Hemolysis Gene Anomaly Detection Reagents | Pseudohyperkalemia, due to ex vivo efflux of potassium from red cells | Cryohydrocytosis, Stomatin-Deficient, with Mental Retardation, Seizures, Cataracts, and Massive Hepatosplenomegaly | Xerocytosis

HP_4000195.label: abnormal enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000195.definition: Concentration or activity of an enzyme is above or below the limits of normal in cultured fibroblasts. Fibroblasts are easy to grow in culture and are the main cell type involved in producing extracellular matrix. They are used as a convenient model system for measuring enzyme activity for enzymes that are not expressed in blood cells. Usually, the test is done in fibroblasts for convenience rather than for the investigation of a pathophysiology specific to fibroblasts.

HP_4000196.label: reduced heparan - alpha - glucosaminide n - acetyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000196.definition: Concentration or activity of N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

HP_4000197.label: reduced n - acetylgalactosamine - 6 - sulfate sulfatase in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000197.definition: Concentration or activity of N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfate sulfatase as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

HP_4000198.label: reduced acetylglucosamine - 6 - sulfate sulfatase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000198.definition: Concentration or activity of N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase (EC 3.1.6.14) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal. N-acetylglucosamine-6-sulfatase hydrolyzes heparan sulfate and keratan sulfate.

HP_4000199.label: reduced erythrocyte porphobilinogen deaminase activity
HP_4000199.definition: Activity or concentration of in the level of porphobilinogen deaminase (EC 4.3.1.8) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

HP_4000200.label: reduced holocarboxylase synthetase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000200.definition: Concentration or activity of holocarboxylase synthetase (EC 6.3.4.10) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

HP_4000201.label: abnormal circulating alpha mannosidase activity
HP_4000201.definition: Concentration or activity of alpha mannosidase outside of the limits of normal in the blood circulation.

HP_4000202.label: reduced alpha - n - acetylgalactosaminidase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000202.definition: Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase (EC 3.2.1.49) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

HP_4000203.label: reduced erythrocyte arginase activity
HP_4000203.definition: Activity or concentration of arginase (EC 3.5.3.1) in red blood cells below the lower limit of normal. Arginase catalyzes the last step of the urea cycle.

HP_4000204.label: reduced mitochondrial acetyl - coa acetyltransferase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000204.definition: Concentration or activity of mitochondrial acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase (EC 2.3.1.9) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

HP_4000205.label: reduced beta - mannosidase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000205.definition: Concentration or activity of beta-mannosidase (EC 3.2.1.25) as measured in cultured fibroblasts is below the limits of normal.

HP_4000206.label: reduced 3 - methylcrotonyl coa carboxylase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000206.definition: Acitivity of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (EC 6.4.1.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.
HP_4000206.synonyms: 3 - methylcrotonyl coa carboxylase low in fibroblasts

HP_4000207.label: reduced branched - chain alpha - keto acid dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000207.definition: Acitivity of branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex (EC 1.2.4.4) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

HP_4000208.label: reduced erythrocyte galactose - 1 - phosphate uridylyltransferase activity
HP_4000208.definition: Activity or concentration of in the level of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase (GALT; EC 2.7.7.12) in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.

HP_4000209.label: abnormal erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity
HP_4000209.definition: Activity of adenosine deaminase in red blood cells outside the limits of normal.

HP_4000210.label: reduced isovaleryl coa dehydrogenase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000210.definition: Acitivity of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.99.10) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

HP_4000211.label: reduced glycerol kinase activity in cultured fibroblasts
HP_4000211.definition: Acitivity of glycerol kinase (EC 2.7.1.30) below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.

HP_4000212.label: increased circulating vitamin a concentration
HP_4000212.definition: Concentration of vitamin A above the upper limit of normal in the blood circulation.

HP_4000213.label: elevated circulating hyaluronic acid concentration
HP_4000213.definition: Concentration of hyaluronic acid in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.

HP_4000214.label: diminished breath sounds
HP_4000214.definition: A reduction in the intensity of the breath sound as ascertained by auscultation of the lung.

HP_5000000.label: anti - ak5 antibody positivity
HP_5000000.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-adenylate kinase 5 (AK5).

HP_5000001.label: anti - ampar antibody positivity
HP_5000001.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against anti-alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR).
HP_5000001.synonyms: anti - alpha - amino - 3 - hydroxy - 5 - methyl - 4 - isoxazolepropionic acid receptor antibody

HP_5000002.label: anti - amphiphysin antibody
HP_5000002.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Amphiphysin.

HP_5000003.label: anti - arhgap26 antibody
HP_5000003.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Rho GTPase-activating protein 26 (ARHGAP26).
HP_5000003.synonyms: anti - ca antibody | anti - rhogtpase - activating protein 26 antibody

HP_5000004.label: anti - carp viii antibody
HP_5000004.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Carbonic anhydrase-related protein VIII (CARPVIII).
HP_5000004.synonyms: anti carpviii antibody | anti - carbonic anhydrase - related protein viii antibody
HP_5000004.UMLS synonyms: Anti-CARP VIII antibody | Anti-CARP VIII antibody (finding)

HP_5000005.label: anti - caspr2
HP_5000005.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against contactin-associated protein-like 2 (CASPR2).
HP_5000005.synonyms: anti - caspr2 antibody | anti - contactin - associated protein - like 2 antibody

HP_5000006.label: anti - cv2 / crmp5 antibody positivity
HP_5000006.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against CV2/CRMP5. Anti-CV2/CRMP5 autoantibody is the most commonly detected anti-neuronal autoantibody. Patients with typical paraneoplastic chorea show fully developed chorea in the course of weeks to months with acute inflammation in the striatum.
HP_5000006.synonyms: anti - collapsin response - mediated protein 5 antibody | anti - cv2 antibody | anti - cv2 / collapsin response mediator protein ( crmp ) 5 antibody

HP_5000007.label: anti - dppx antibody
HP_5000007.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against dipeptidyl-peptidase-like protein 6 (DPPX).
HP_5000007.synonyms: anti - dipeptidyl - peptidase - like protein 6 antibody

HP_5000008.label: anti - fgfr3 antibody positivity
HP_5000008.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against FGFR3.
HP_5000008.synonyms: anti - fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 antibody

HP_5000009.label: anti - gaba ( a ) r antibody
HP_5000009.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against gamma-aminobutyric acid A receptor, i.e., GABA(A)R.
HP_5000009.synonyms: anti - gabaa r antibody | anti - gamma amino butyric acid type a receptors antibody

HP_5000010.label: anti - gaba ( b ) r antibody
HP_5000010.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against gamma-aminobutyric acid B receptor, i.e., GABA(B)R.
HP_5000010.synonyms: anti - gamma - aminobutyric acid b receptor antibody

HP_5000011.label: anti - gad65 antibody
HP_5000011.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 (GAD65).
HP_5000011.UMLS synonyms: Approximately 60% of patients have anti-GAD65 antibodies

HP_5000012.label: anti - gephyrin antibody
HP_5000012.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Gephyrin.

HP_5000013.label: anti - gfap antibody
HP_5000013.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP).
HP_5000013.synonyms: anti - glial fibrillary acidic protein antibody

HP_5000014.label: anti - glyr antibody
HP_5000014.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Glycine receptor (GlyR).

HP_5000015.label: anti - homer - 3 antibody
HP_5000015.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Homer-3.

HP_5000016.label: anti - hu antibody positivity
HP_5000016.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Hu.
HP_5000016.synonyms: anti - anna - 1 antibody | anti - neuronal nuclear antibody type - 1 antibody

HP_5000017.label: anti - iglon5 antibody
HP_5000017.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against immunoglobulin-like cell adhesion molecule 5 (IgLON5).
HP_5000017.synonyms: anti - immunoglobulin - like cell adhesion molecule 5 antibody

HP_5000018.label: anti - itpr1 antibody
HP_5000018.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor 1 (ITPR1).
HP_5000018.synonyms: anti - inositol 1,4,5 - trisphosphate receptor type 1 antibody

HP_5000019.label: anti - kelch like protein 11 antibody positivity
HP_5000019.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against kelch-like protein 11 (KLHL11).

HP_5000020.label: anti - lgi1 antibody
HP_5000020.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against leucine-rich glioma-inactivated 1 (LGI1).
HP_5000020.synonyms: anti - anti - leucine - rich glioma - inactivated 1 antibody

HP_5000021.label: anti - ma antibody positivity
HP_5000021.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma.

HP_5000022.label: anti - ma2 antibody positivity
HP_5000022.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma2.

HP_5000023.label: anti - ma1 antibody positivity
HP_5000023.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ma1.

HP_5000024.label: anti - mglur1 antibody
HP_5000024.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against metabotropic glutamate receptor 1 (mGluR1).

HP_5000025.label: anti - mglur5 antibody
HP_5000025.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5).
HP_5000025.synonyms: anti - metabotropic glutamate receptor type 5 antibody

HP_5000026.label: anti - neurexin - 3alpha antibody positivity
HP_5000026.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against neurexin-3alpha.

HP_5000027.label: anti - p / q - type vgcc antibody positivity
HP_5000027.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs).
HP_5000027.synonyms: anti - p / q - type voltage - gated calcium - channel antibody

HP_5000028.label: anti - map1b antibody
HP_5000028.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against microtubule-associated protein 1B (MAP1B).
HP_5000028.synonyms: anti - microtubule - associated protein 1b antibody | anti - purkinje cell cytoplasmic type - 2 antibody

HP_5000029.label: anti - pkcgamma antibody
HP_5000029.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against protein kinase Cgamma.
HP_5000029.synonyms: anti - protein kinase c gamma antibody

HP_5000030.label: anti - ri antibody
HP_5000030.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Ri, an antineuronal antibody.
HP_5000030.UMLS synonyms: Anti-Ri antibody positive | Anti-Ri antibody measurement | Anti-Ri Antibody Determination Reagents | ANNA-2 antibody, human | IVD Test Reagent/Kits, Immunoassay, Autoimmune, Neurologic, Anti-Ri Antibody

HP_5000031.label: anti - septin - 5 antibody
HP_5000031.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Septin-5.

HP_5000032.label: anti - sez6l2 antibody
HP_5000032.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against seizure-related 6 homolog like 2 (SEZ6L2).

HP_5000033.label: anti - sox1 antibody
HP_5000033.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against SOX1. Anti-SOX1 antibodies, also known as antiglial nuclear antibody (AGNA), are specifically found in paraneoplastic neurological disorders. Since SOX1 is expressed in neuronal precursor cells in the developing central nervous system, it has been used as an early marker of neural stem cells.
HP_5000033.synonyms: anti - sry - like high mobility group box ( sox ) 1 antibody

HP_5000034.label: anti - tr / dner antibody
HP_5000034.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Tr/DNER. Anti-Tr antibodies are directed against cerebellar Purkinje cells (termed anti-Tr or PCA-Tr). Anti-Tr autoantibodies are frequently associated with Hodgkin lymphoma (HL). Anti-Tr antibodies are defined by a specific staining pattern in cerebellar tissue that is characterized by punctate immunoreactivity in both the dendritic tree and soma of Purkinje cells but not in their axons. This characteristic pattern is indicative of the presence of anti-Tr antibodies. The Delta/Notch-like epidermal growth factor-related receptor (DNER) was identified as the target antigen of anti-Tr.
HP_5000034.synonyms: anti - delta / notch - like epidermal growth factor - related receptor antibody | pca - tr

HP_5000035.label: anti - trim46 antibody
HP_5000035.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the axon initial segment protein tripartite motif 46 (TRIM46).

HP_5000036.label: anti - trim9 / trim67 antibody
HP_5000036.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against TRIM9/TRIM67.

HP_5000037.label: anti - yo antibody positivity
HP_5000037.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Yo.

HP_5000038.label: anti - titin antibody positivity
HP_5000038.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against titin.

HP_5000039.label: anti - zic4 antibody positivity
HP_5000039.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Zic family member 4 (ZIC4).

HP_5000042.label: anti - sj / itpr1 antibody
HP_5000042.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against Sj/inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor.
HP_5000042.synonyms: anti - sj / inositol 1,4,5 - trisphosphate receptor antibody

HP_5000043.label: anti - d2 r antibody
HP_5000043.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against dopamine-2 receptor.

HP_5000044.label: anti - gluk2 antibody
HP_5000044.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against glutamate kainate receptor subunit 2 (GluK2).
HP_5000044.synonyms: anti - glutamate kainate receptor subunit 2 antibody

HP_5000046.label: anti - lrp4 antibody positivity
HP_5000046.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against low-density lipoprotein receptor (Lrp4).
HP_5000046.synonyms: anti - low - density lipoprotein receptor - related protein 4 antibody

HP_5000047.label: anti - ryanodine receptor antibody
HP_5000047.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against ryanodine receptor.
HP_5000047.UMLS synonyms: Anti-ryanodine receptor antibody positive | anti-ryanodine receptor autoantibody

HP_5000048.label: anti - kv1.4 antibody
HP_5000048.definition: The presence of autoantibodies (immunoglobulins) in the blood circulation that react against the voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.4.

HP_5200001.label: selective mutism
HP_5200001.definition: Voluntary failure to use spoken language (at whatever level attained) in selective social contexts over a period of time.
HP_5200001.UMLS synonyms: Selective Mutism | selective mutism of childhood | Selective mutism (in 2 sisters)

HP_5200002.label: limited repertoire of facial expression
HP_5200002.definition: An abnormally limited range of facial expressions demonstrated by a lack of nuance of facial expression to match specific social situations or an inability to demonstrate a normal range of emotions with one's face.

HP_5200003.label: excessive interest in others
HP_5200003.definition: An unusually strong interest in others in general or tendency to develop a strong interest in certain individuals.

HP_5200004.label: reduced response to another 's attempt to get direct attention
HP_5200004.definition: There is a diminished interest in all individuals, including both peers and non-peers.

HP_5200005.label: abnormal pitch
HP_5200005.definition: Abnormally high or low-pitched vocalization or speech.

HP_5200006.label: loose association
HP_5200006.definition: Speech characterized by weak (e.g. tangential/circumstantial) or absent (e.g. word salad) connections between ideas.

HP_5200007.label: neologism
HP_5200007.definition: Consistent use of an invented word that is unique to an individual.
HP_5200007.UMLS synonyms: Neologism | speech language uses neologisms literal | speech language uses neologisms verbal | speech language uses neologisms (paraphasic errors)

HP_5200008.label: overly formal / pedantic language
HP_5200008.definition: Use of language that is overly formal, precise, detailed, or pedantic for the social context.

HP_5200009.label: midline hand movements
HP_5200009.definition: Hand stereotypies within the medial plane of the body.
HP_5200009.UMLS synonyms: Arm and hand movements that grasp cloth, head in the midline. | INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER, X-LINKED 1 | Arm and hand movements that grasp cloth and uncover partially at least one eye, head in the midline.

HP_5200010.label: abnormal intonation
HP_5200010.definition: Abnormal rise and fall of the voice in speech and vocalization.

HP_5200011.label: abnormal speech rate
HP_5200011.definition: Speech that is abnormally fast or slow

HP_5200012.label: abnormal speech rhythm
HP_5200012.definition: Speech with abnormal rhythm or pattern

HP_5200013.label: ambiguous facial expression
HP_5200013.definition: Spontaneous production of communicative facial expressions that have poor quality or are perceived as odd or mechanical. This may include inaccurate mimicry of typical facial expressions. These expressions may be difficult to interpret for someone who is not familiar with the individual making the expression.

HP_5200014.label: exaggerated facial expression
HP_5200014.definition: A tendency to make facial expressions that are exaggerated and a failure to make subtle facial expressions in a social context when a subtle expression is more appropriate.

HP_5200015.label: muted facial expression
HP_5200015.definition: A tendency to produce facial expressions with decreased intensity or expressivity which appear muted or flat.

HP_5200016.label: abnormal peer relationships
HP_5200016.definition: The state of having abnormal relationships with others. This does not describe specific aspects of one's social aptitudes but rather a state which may come about from these aptitudes, such as lacking peer relationships or lacking close friends.

HP_5200017.label: abnormal movements of face and head
HP_5200017.definition: Abnormal movements of face and head.

HP_5200018.label: abnormal movements of the upper extremities
HP_5200018.definition: Abnormal movements of the upper extremities.

HP_5200019.label: abnormal movements of the whole body
HP_5200019.definition: Abnormal movements of the whole body.

HP_5200020.label: abnormal interest in others
HP_5200020.definition: A social interest in others that is abnormal given the social context. This can include an increased interest with another person or an abnormal lack of interest in other people.

HP_5200021.label: reduced social insight
HP_5200021.definition: A lack of awareness of social rules in multiple social settings, which are simple or intuitive to others in the same social setting.
HP_5200021.synonyms: abnormal social awareness | abnormal social understanding

HP_5200022.label: reduced awareness of convention
HP_5200022.definition: Reduced awareness of expected conventions, which are normal and expected for particular social settings or interactions.

HP_5200024.label: abnormal relationship
HP_5200024.definition: The state of having abnormal relationships with others. This does not describe specific aspects of one's social aptitudes but rather a state which may come about from these aptitudes, such as lacking peer relationships, lacking close friends, or having a relational network that is abnormal given one's cultural context.
HP_5200024.UMLS synonyms: Abnormal relationship of right ventricle to left ventricle | Abnormal relationship of aortic orifice to pulmonary orifice | echocardiography: great artery relationships | Overjet, Dental | Congenital abnormality of relationship of cardiac component | Screen for health problems relevant to adolescent and suggested by history (e.g., anemia; hypertension; hearing and vision disorders; hyperlipidemia; oral health problems; abnormal sexual maturation; abnormal physical growth; body image disturbances; eating disorders; poor nutrition; alcohol, tobacco, or drug use; unhealthy sexual behavior; infectious disease; poor self-concept; low self-esteem; depression; difficult relationships; abuse; learning problems; work problems)

HP_5200026.label: abnormal social imitation
HP_5200026.definition: A reduced ability to imitate a task or the movements of others.
HP_5200026.synonyms: deferred imitation of others | reduced immediate imitation of others

HP_5200027.label: reduced attempt to get or direct another 's attention
HP_5200027.definition: An abnormality in one's tendency to initiate social interactions.

HP_5200028.label: reduced response to social cues
HP_5200028.definition: Abnormality in the way one responds to social cues such as a verbal cue (which should cause one to shift attention) or someone sharing their emotions (which should elicit a sympathetic response).

HP_5200291.synonyms: rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder | rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder | rem sleep behavior disorder | rem sleep behaviour disorder

HP_5200292.label: non - restorative sleep
HP_5200292.definition: Perception of feeling unrefreshed after sleep.

HP_5200293.label: disturbance during transitions between sleep and wake states
HP_5200293.definition: A group of parasomnias that occur during the transition from wakefulness to sleep or from one sleep stage to another. Rhythmic Movement Disorder, Sleep Starts, Sleep Talking, and Nocturnal Leg Cramps - these four disorders belong to Sleep-Wake Transition Disorders in the International Classification of Sleep Disorders.
HP_5200293.synonyms: sleep state switching | sleep - wake transition disorders

HP_5200294.label: sexsomnia
HP_5200294.definition: Unintentional sexual behavior during sleep, such as masturbation, initiation of sex, or making sexual noises, is known as sexsomnia. Sexsomnia predominantly occurs during NREM sleep.
HP_5200294.synonyms: sexual behavior during sleep | sexual behaviour during sleep

HP_5200295.label: periodic limb movements
HP_5200295.definition: Repetitive limb movements during sleep can affect the quality of your sleep.
HP_5200295.UMLS synonyms: RESTLESS LEGS SYNDROME, SUSCEPTIBILITY TO, 6 | Conditions with periodic limb movement | Periodic limb movement sleep disorder | Nocturnal Myoclonus Syndrome | organic periodic limb movement sleep disorder | Family history of periodic limb movement disorder | Insomnia due to periodic limb movement disorder

HP_5200296.label: abnormal hypnagogia
HP_5200296.definition: Abnormal transition of consciousness from wakefulness to sleep.

HP_5200297.label: abnormal hypnopompia
HP_5200297.definition: Abnormal transition of consciousness from sleeping to wakefulness.

HP_5200298.label: abnormal sleep architecture
HP_5200298.definition: Interruptions during the various stages of sleep.
HP_5200298.synonyms: sleep architecture disturbances | sleep stage disturbances

HP_5200299.label: rem parasomnia
HP_5200299.synonyms: disturbance in rem | rapid eye movement parasomnia

HP_5200300.label: abnormal movement during sleep
HP_5200300.definition: Periodic Limb Movement Disorder, also known as Sleep-Related Myoclonus Syndrome or Nocturnal Myoclonus Syndrome, refers to the periodic and stereotypic movements of the legs or upper limbs during sleep.
HP_5200300.synonyms: nocturnal myoclonus syndrome | periodic limb movement disorder

HP_5200304.label: short n1 sleep
HP_5200304.definition: Disruptions in the first stage of NREM sleep can occur.

HP_5200305.label: paradoxical insomnia
HP_5200305.definition: Paradoxical insomnia is a condition in which individuals with a normal or near-normal sleep macrostructure tend to severely underestimate the quantity and quality of their sleep.
HP_5200305.synonyms: disturbance in perception related to sleep | sleep misperception | sleep state misperception

HP_5200307.label: short n2 sleep
HP_5200307.definition: Disruptions in the second stage of NREM sleep.

HP_5200309.label: short n3 sleep
HP_5200309.definition: Disruptions in the third stage of NREM sleep.

HP_5200310.label: decreased social interactions
HP_5200310.definition: A decrease in the frequency, intensity, or extent of social or personal exchanges between individuals.
HP_5200310.synonyms: reduced , declined or lessened social interactions

HP_5200311.label: increased interpersonal communication
HP_5200311.definition: An intensified exchange of information between individuals.
HP_5200311.synonyms: heightened , amplified social expression and social connectedness

HP_5200315.label: increased seeking of relationships
HP_5200315.definition: Increased frequency or duration in social outings and interactions as part of relationship-seeking or maintenance.

HP_5200316.label: decreased interpersonal communication
HP_5200316.synonyms: a decline or reduced social expression and social connectedness

HP_5200320.label: decreased seeking of relationships
HP_5200320.definition: A decrease in frequency or duration related to seeking or maintaining relationships may involve avoiding social outings or social interactions.

HP_5200321.label: increased sexual behavior
HP_5200321.definition: Engaging in riskier sexual practices, experiencing a significant increase in frequency, having multiple sexual partners, or spending excessive time on sexual activities can become disproportionate to other aspects of a person's life.

HP_5200322.label: increased emotional expression
HP_5200322.definition: Heightened emotional behaviors like crying, laughter, and smiling compared to the individual's baseline.

HP_5200323.label: increased emotional vulnerability
HP_5200323.definition: Increased emotional expression during interactions, involving personal emotion sharing or reciprocation.
HP_5200323.synonyms: empath | increased empathy | over - sharing | oversharing

HP_5200325.label: increased comfort with casual physical contact
HP_5200325.definition: An individual exhibits more physical contact with others than their usual behavior, seen as increased touch in platonic interactions or greater contact in romantic relationships.

HP_5200327.label: decreased sexual behavior
HP_5200327.definition: Absence of sexual attraction, behaviors, and interest that are different from the person's normal state.
HP_5200327.UMLS synonyms: Hyposexuality state | Limit physical mobility to decrease opportunity for socially unacceptable sexual behaviors, as needed

HP_5200328.label: decreased emotional expression
HP_5200328.definition: Reduced frequency or subdued emotional behaviors like crying, laughter, and smiling, making the individual appear apathetic or disinterested.

HP_5200329.label: problematic alcohol consumption
HP_5200329.definition: Impaired ability to stop or control alcohol use despite adverse social, occupational, or health consequences.
HP_5200329.UMLS synonyms: Alcohol intake above recommended sensible limits | Partner has problematic alcohol consumption

HP_5200331.label: addictive sedative use
HP_5200331.definition: Misuse and/or abuse of sedative drugs.

HP_5200332.label: addictive non - substance behaviors
HP_5200332.definition: Uncontrolled use or problematic behaviors of dependency without the use of drugs or substances can be detrimental.
HP_5200332.synonyms: addiction to a behavior | addiction to a behaviour | addiction to an activity | addictive activity

HP_5200333.label: addictive spending behavior
HP_5200333.definition: An uncontrollable urge to shop and spend money can lead to distress or impairment.

HP_5200334.label: addictive gambling behavior
HP_5200334.definition: The act of taking chances or engaging in behaviors without restraint, typically involving the wagering of something valuable, in pursuit of acquiring something of higher value.

HP_5200335.label: addictive sex behavior
HP_5200335.definition: Inability to control or manage sexual urges, fantasies, or behaviors that impair one's ability to function.

HP_5200336.label: addictive video game use
HP_5200336.definition: The inability to regulate persistent gaming behavior is characterized by a heightened prioritization of gaming activities over regular daily tasks and responsibilities.
HP_5200336.synonyms: excessive video game playing | video game addiction

HP_5200337.label: compulsive stealing
HP_5200337.definition: Irresistible impulses to take easily affordable items.

HP_5200338.label: excessive fire setting
HP_5200338.definition: The inability to control urges of deliberately setting fires for pleasure and gratification, without any criminal intent.

HP_5200339.label: self - cutting
HP_5200339.definition: Deliberate harm to one's body, in the form of cutting that results in tissue damage, without a conscious intent to die.
HP_5200339.synonyms: cutting | deliberate cutting of skin | self cutting
HP_5200339.UMLS synonyms: Cutting self | Deliberate self-cutting | Refrains from cutting self | self-mutilation by cutting (history) | Suicide and self-inflicted injury by cutting and piercing instrument | Irresistible urge to cut self

HP_5200341.label: addictive cannabis use
HP_5200341.definition: A persistent and compulsive need to use cannabis, despite negative consequences.
HP_5200341.synonyms: addictive marijuana use | cannabis addiction | marijuana addiction

HP_5200342.label: autophagia
HP_5200342.definition: The habitual action of inflicting pain upon oneself by biting and/or devouring portions of one's body.

HP_5200352.label: hypnagogic sleep paralysis
HP_5200352.definition: Sleep paralysis that occurs when falling asleep.
HP_5200352.synonyms: inability to move while falling asleep | predormital sleep paralysis

HP_5200353.label: hypnopompic sleep paralysis
HP_5200353.definition: Sleep paralysis that occurs when waking up from sleep.
HP_5200353.synonyms: inability to move while awakening | postdormital paralysis | postdormital sleep paralysis

HP_5200356.label: sleep onset rapid eye movement period
HP_5200356.definition: Entering REM sleep immediately upon falling asleep.
HP_5200356.synonyms: sleep - onset ( rem ) period | sleep - onset rapid eye movement ( rem ) period

HP_5200401.label: abnormal judgment
HP_5200401.definition: Beliefs that deviate from what is considered rational or within the range of normal human judgment and belief formation.

HP_5200402.label: overvalued idea
HP_5200402.definition: An unreasonable and an isolated sustained belief that is maintained with less than delusional intensity (i.e. the person is able is to acknowledge the possibility that the belief may or may not be true). The belief is not of one that is ordinarily accepted by other members of the person's culture or sub-culture.

HP_5200403.label: time agnosia
HP_5200403.definition: The inability to perceive the passage of time is usually due to a disorder involving the temporal area of the brain.

HP_5200405.label: olfactory agnosia
HP_5200405.definition: The inability to recognize certain smells or types of odors that you previously recognized.

HP_5200406.label: tactile agnosia
HP_5200406.definition: The inability to recognize objects by touch is called tactile agnosia.

HP_5200407.label: topographical agnosia
HP_5200407.definition: The inability to rely on visual cues to guide one's direction is due to the inability to recognize objects.

HP_5200409.label: delusional memory
HP_5200409.definition: A delusional interpretation of a normal memory.

HP_5200410.label: auditory agnosia
HP_5200410.definition: The condition is characterized by the inability to recognize spoken languages and/or nonverbal environmental sounds and music, despite having adequate hearing. However, spontaneous speech, reading, and writing abilities remain intact.
HP_5200410.UMLS synonyms: Auditory agnosia | Auditory Agnosia, Congenital | verbal; agnosia, auditory | verbal; agnosia, auditory, developmental

HP_5200411.label: gustatory agnosia
HP_5200411.definition: People cannot identify tastes, even though they can experience them.

HP_5200412.label: allesthesia
HP_5200412.definition: Referral of a sensory stimulus from one side of the body to the other.

HP_5200413.label: autotopagnosia
HP_5200413.definition: The loss of the ability to localize, recognize, or identify specific parts of one's body.

HP_5200415.label: delusion of persecution
HP_5200415.definition: False beliefs or perceptions in which a person believes that they are being treated with malicious intent, hostility, or harassment - despite significant evidence to suggest otherwise.

HP_5200416.label: delusion of infidelity
HP_5200416.definition: A false belief that a person is the victim of his or her partner's unfaithfulness.

HP_5200417.label: grandiose delusion
HP_5200417.definition: False beliefs relating to origin (aristocratic lineage, royal birth, being raised as a foster child), possessions (owning vast estates, castles, etc., which are withheld through intrigue), abilities (being great inventors, discoverers, artists, possessors of special wisdom, gifted with inspiration), and status (adviser to prominent diplomats, the true director of political destinies).
HP_5200417.UMLS synonyms: Grandiose delusions | Grandiose delusion disorder | Egomania | Delusion of grandiose identity | Delusion of grandiose ability | Grandiose delusions:Find:Pt:^Patient:Ord:DI-PAD CGP V 1.4

HP_5200418.label: folie à deux
HP_5200418.definition: Delusional beliefs are transmitted from one individual to another.

HP_5200419.label: delusion of control
HP_5200419.definition: A false belief that another person, group of people, or external force controls one's general thoughts, feelings, impulses, or behaviors.
HP_5200419.UMLS synonyms: Passivity of drive | Delusion of control of handwriting | Delusion of control of voice | Passivity of volitional acts | Thought alienation

HP_5200420.label: delusion of love
HP_5200420.definition: A delusion (a fixed false belief held despite evidence to the contrary) of being loved by another person, even though there is no evidence of this, and the person in question denies it.
HP_5200420.synonyms: de clérambault syndrome | erotomania | psychose passionelle
HP_5200420.UMLS synonyms: Kandinsky Syndrome | Delusion of being loved

HP_5200421.label: nihilistic delusion
HP_5200421.definition: A false belief associated with the nonexistence of the \"self,\
HP_5200421.UMLS synonyms: Nihilistic delusion | Nihilistic delusions:Find:Pt:^Patient:Ord:DI-PAD CGP V 1.4 | No nihilistic delusions

HP_5200422.label: cotard delusion
HP_5200422.definition: A false belief that you or your body parts are dead, dying, or do not exist.

HP_5200423.label: abnormal experience of reality
HP_5200423.definition: Subjective phenomena or perceptions that deviate from what is considered correct or are outside the range of normal human experiences.

HP_5200424.label: delusional perception
HP_5200424.definition: A true perception, to which a patient attributes a false meaning, ranges from experiencing some vague meaning to clear, delusional observations, and expresses delusions of reference.

HP_5200425.label: hypochondriac delusion
HP_5200425.definition: Bodily preoccupation, disease phobia, and a false fixed conviction of the presence of disease with no response to reassurance.

HP_5200426.label: delusions of infestation
HP_5200426.definition: A persistent belief that a person is infested with living or non-living pathogens, such as parasites, insects, or bugs, when no such infestation is present.

HP_5200427.label: delusional atmosphere
HP_5200427.definition: Experience everything around them as sinister, portentous, uncanny, and peculiar in an indefinable way. They know that they are personally involved but cannot tell how. They have a feeling of anticipation, sometimes even excitement, that soon all the separate parts of their experience will fit together to reveal something immensely significant.

HP_5200428.label: delusional misidentification
HP_5200428.definition: A group of complex, monothematic delusional phenomena in which subjects hold a belief that the identity of a familiar person, object, location, or self has been altered or replaced.

HP_5200429.label: religious delusion
HP_5200429.definition: Delusions are characterized by increased conviction and pervasiveness, permeating the individual's entire experience to a greater extent.

HP_5200430.label: abnormal psychotic pattern
HP_5200430.definition: Any abnormal pattern of psychotic experiences, where an individual has significant disturbances in their thoughts, perceptions, emotions, and behavior, resulting in a loss of touch with reality.

HP_5201000.label: incomplete unilateral cleft lip
HP_5201000.definition: Unilateral cleft lip cleft that starts from the bottom of the upper lip but does not reach the nasal cavity.
HP_5201000.UMLS synonyms: Cleft palate with cleft lip, unilateral, incomplete | Unilateral incomplete cleft lip and alveolus

HP_5201001.label: complete unilateral cleft lip
HP_5201001.definition: Unilateral cleft lip cleft that starts from the bottom of the upper lip and reaches the nasal cavity.
HP_5201001.UMLS synonyms: Cleft palate with cleft lip, unilateral, complete | Unilateral complete cleft lip and alveolus | Primary repair of cleft lip, unilateral, complete | Unilateral primary complete plastic repair of cleft lip | Unilateral primary complete plastic repair of cleft lip and nasal deformity | Plastic repair of cleft lip/nasal deformity; primary, partial or complete, unilateral

HP_5201002.label: microform unilateral cleft lip
HP_5201002.definition: Notch, groove, or scar of the upper lip without noticeable rupture of the lip. Microforms are sometimes associated with disruption of the continuity of the orbicularis oris muscle.

HP_5201003.label: complete cleft hard palate
HP_5201003.definition: Cleft hard palate in which the cleft goes through the entire length of the hard palate, ie. from the incisor foramen to the anterior border of the soft palate.
HP_5201003.UMLS synonyms: Complete cleft of hard palate | complete cleft hard palate with cleft soft palate | Complete cleft hard and soft palate | Complete cleft of right hard and soft palate | Complete cleft of left hard and soft palate

HP_5201004.label: incomplete cleft hard palate
HP_5201004.definition: Cleft hard palate in which the cleft does not go through the entire length of the hard palate, ie. the cleft does not go from the incisor foramen to the anterior border of the soft palate.
HP_5201004.UMLS synonyms: incomplete cleft hard palate with cleft soft palate | Incomplete cleft hard and soft palate

HP_5201005.label: complete cleft soft palate
